Abrahamsbergsskolan byggdes 1946 samtidi: Abrahamsbergsskolan school was built in 1946 at the same time as the housing area, and its yellow brick blends into the yellow town, as Abrahamsberg is sometimes called. A little way from here, in Riksby, is a much older sight: two Viking Age runic carvings on a flat rock. They had probably been hidden under soil and moss for several hundred years when children picking berries found them in 1904.
Affärsmannen Robert Ditzinger var en omt: The businessman Robert Ditzinger was a thoughtful father. In 1882 he had two identical main buildings built at Långsjö gård, one for each of his two sons. The estate later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö, bordered by Lake Långsjön towards Huddinge. Not far from here runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg, the historic main road to the south.
Ahlby säteri från 1620-talet är det älds: Ahlby säteri, a manor from the 1620s, is the oldest house in Lilla Alby. One of its owners was Clas Fredrik Horn, who was convicted of complicity in the murder of King Gustav III. Under the street, 28 metres down, lies Solna strand station with Takashi Naraha's artwork Himmelen av kub, Heaven of Cube, where the sky has been brought down to the platform.
Akallastråket passerar i närheten, ett p: Akallastråket passes nearby, a walking route of about 18 kilometres that follows the blue metro line from Akalla all the way to Stortorget in Gamla stan, the Old Town. The City of Stockholm has given the route the motto From 18th-century village to Stockholm's Silicon Valley. For the youngest there is Mulle Meckparken, a themed playground named after the children's book character Mulle Meck.
Alby är hemma för Cirkus Cirkör, som har: Alby is home to Cirkus Cirkör, which is based in the Subtopia cultural centre, and most people here live in one of Botkyrkabyggen's 3,000 flats. But people have been in the area much longer than that. Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist grave in the area, is dated to about 1800 BC – a type of grave from the late Stone Age that is very rare in the Lake Mälaren region.
Albykistan: Albykistan, a Stone Age stone cist
Alelyckan, området alldeles intill, har: Alelyckan, the area right next to here, is named after alders, or perhaps ale, a group of alders, and lyckan in the sense of an enclosed field. For a long time the name was associated with the waterworks, where water from the Göta älv river has been purified into drinking water since 1894. In 1990 the street Alelyckan changed its name to Alelyckegatan because of the risk of confusion.
Alelyckans sportcenter, alldeles intill,: Alelyckans sportcenter, right next to us, was born of a daily walk. Every day Vilhelm Björk passed the empty water basins at Alelyckan and got an idea. In 1974 he and Alva Björk founded the centre, which today has tennis courts, squash courts, 25 badminton courts and a floorball hall, where you can also play pickleball.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Långnäs gård,: Close by is Långnäs gård, which has its roots in a larger farm from the mid-14th century and is still privately owned. The residential area Sjövik, with villas and linked terraced houses, sits on a strip of shoreline along Kyrkviken bay that has been excluded from the Långängen-Elfvik nature reserve, and borders the Skogshem and Wijk conference centres.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Sköndalsskola: Close by is Sköndalsskolan, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and opened in 1953. On Mazarinvägen, architects lived in houses they had designed themselves: Eskil Sundahl built Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the married couple Hanna and Roy Victorson lived in one of their Sköndal villas. The couple also designed the flower kiosk at the northern entrance of Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Slagsta gård,: Right nearby is Slagsta gård, a venerable manor and former manorial estate. By Lake Mälaren, Slagstabadet beckons, a bathing spot laid out in the early 1970s on the site of one of Slagsta's two old brickworks, and terraces and house foundations can still be seen in the forest. Along the Hallunda heritage trail there is also a rock carving, discovered in 1971 and protected as an ancient monument.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Vallhamra ish: Very close by is Vallhamra ice rink, home arena of Partille HK. The rink was laid out in 1969, and in September 1981 it got a roof and walls and became an indoor arena. There's room for about 300 spectators, and besides ice hockey, the ice is used for figure skating and public skating. Both the hockey club and the figure skating club have their clubrooms here.
Alldeles i närheten ligger Vantörs kyrka: Close by is Vantör Church, the parish church of Vantör parish. The name carries a long history: the medieval parish of Vantör had a church that, after a fire in the 1400s, came to be called Brännkyrka, the Burnt Church. Högdalen's centre also used to have the Rondo cinema, which opened in January 1961 and showed films until May 1983.
Alldeles i närheten låg Hundra, ett av S: Very close by was Hundra, one of Salem's three soldier-sailor crofts. It bore the number 100, "hundra", hence the nickname, and the sailor who lived here was to be supported by the farms of his district to serve in the naval and coastal defence. The neighbouring croft Skyttorp got its name from a marksman, "skytt", who once lived there. It was one of the few cottages in the Stockholm area with its own kitchen, a building custom from southern Götaland.
Alldeles i närheten låg Härlanda fängels: Very close by was Härlanda prison, originally Härlanda Central Prison, which was in use from 1907 to 1997. It was designed by the court architect Gustaf Lindgren and has been a listed building since 1993. Since 2011 the area has been called Härlanda park. The Saga cinema was also in the area, and after it closed it became a grocery shop.
Alldeles i närheten låg Tuna gård, en gå: Right nearby was Tuna farm, a farm dating back to the Middle Ages, next to today's Hågelbyleden road. You can go even further back in time a little way off in Hogslaby, a reconstructed Iron Age village at Hågelby farm. All the children in the municipality get to come there for a day in the Iron Age, cooking food and forging in the smithy. Many of the buildings at Hågelby farm itself were built on the initiative of the telephone manufacturer Lars Magnus Ericsson.
Alldeles i närheten låg torpet Lugnet, b: Close by was the croft Lugnet, built in 1771 and demolished in 1962. A little way from here, Saltvägen winds through the part of Hökarängen unofficially called Kryddhyllan, the Spice Rack, and there, at Saltvägen 14, the troubadour Cornelis Vreeswijk once lived. Along Lingvägen is Farsta fire station, opened in October 1956.
Alldeles i närheten står Helige kung Ste: Right nearby stands the Church of Holy King Stefan Dečanski, Gothenburg's Serbian Orthodox church. It is dedicated to Stefan Uroš III Dečanski, King of Serbia from 1321 to 1331 and founder of the Visoki Dečani monastery in Kosovo, today an endangered World Heritage Site on UNESCO's list. Kortedala all around was Gothenburg's first suburb and was built in the 1950s.
Alldeles i närheten står Villa Brännugne: Right nearby stands Villa Brännugnen, a private villa designed by Gert Wingårdh, with a restaurant open to the public. It won Huddinge's architecture award in 2019. A little way off, Ågestabron bridge spans Lake Magelungen. The bridge has one foot in Stockholm and the other in Huddinge, because roughly half of it lies in each municipality.
Alldeles intill breder Sisjöns industrio: Right next to us spreads the Sisjön industrial area, directly south of the Söderleden road. The area came about in the 1960s for workshops and industry, but over the years it has turned into a retail area where there's more shopping than welding. A little way from here, at Askim's northern cemetery, a privateer captain in the service of Lars Gathenhielm is said to be buried, in the so-called privateer's grave.
Alldeles intill ligger Hovgårdsvallen, f: Right next to here is Hovgårdsvallen, the football pitch in Björlanda that is home ground for IK Zenith. It goes by several names, and anyone talking about Hovgården or Zenithgården means the same pitch. Maybe it's an advantage to have three names when the visiting team has to find its way?
Alldeles intill ligger Kungliga tennisha: Right next door is Kungliga tennishallen, the Royal Tennis Hall, opened in 1943 and designed by Sture Frölén. The Stockholm Open tennis tournament has been played here since its premiere in 1969, with one exception: between 1989 and 1994 the tournament moved to the Globe arena. In the pandemic year 2020 the tournament was cancelled altogether.
Alldeles intill ligger Livgardets Kavall: Right next door is the Life Guards' Cavalry Barracks, Kavkas, built from 1893 to 1898 to designs by Erik Josephson. Today the stables house the horses of the Life Guards' mounted royal guard and of the mounted police. A little further away is Armfeltsgatan, probably named after one of two gentlemen called Armfeldt, though neither of them had any close connection with the area. That is where Peter Celsing's Olaus Petri Church from 1959 stands.
Alldeles intill ligger Norra begravnings: Right next to us is Norra begravningsplatsen, the Northern Cemetery, one of Sweden's largest cemeteries, with paths called Aftonstjärnans väg, Sommarvindsvägen and Solregnsvägen, the Evening Star's Way, Summer Wind Road and Sun Rain Road. A little further away is Solna kyrkby, the old church village, where Solna Church has roots in the 12th century and the rectory dates from the 1720s. Along Solna kyrkväg there is also a terraced housing area designed by Dag Ribbing, counted among Solna's architectural gems.
Alldeles intill ligger Nya Solevi, ett s: Right next to us is Nya Solevi, a solar power plant that was called Säve Solcellspark while it was being built. Things moved fast: construction started on 11 September 2018 and the park opened as early as 14 December the same year. The plan is about 5.5 gigawatt hours of electricity a year. A little further away is Säve Airport, where today only police and rescue service helicopters fly.
Alldeles intill ligger Pepparred, ett av: Right next to us is Pepparred, one of the really old nature reserves, protected as far back as 1925. It is only 3.5 hectares in size and consists of old wooded pasture with broadleaf trees on a slope between the E6 motorway and the houses south of the Pepparred farm, which gave the reserve its name.
Alldeles intill ligger Röda Korsets Högs: Right next door is the Swedish Red Cross University, Sweden's oldest secular nursing school. It was founded in 1867 by Emmy Rappe, who had herself been trained by none other than Florence Nightingale in London. The school started in Uppsala and was long based at Sabbatsberg Hospital before ending up here. A short distance away is Flemingsberg church, consecrated in 1976.
Alldeles intill ligger Skrubbatriangeln,: Right next to us is Skrubbatriangeln, also called Skrubba Energicentrum, an industrial area opened in 1987 and named after its layout, which resembles a triangle. The Skrubba district borders Tyresö and Lake Drevviken, where the Strandkyrkogården cemetery lies a little way from here.
Alldeles intill ligger Täby Racketcenter: Right next to us is Täby Racketcenter, with twelve badminton courts, four squash courts, table tennis tables and a gym. A short walk away is Viggbyholm station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where the old station building is no longer needed for the trains and instead houses a café. Viggbyholm is divided by the E18 and the railway into Sjösidan, Stationssidan and Rönningesjösidan – the lake side, the station side and the Lake Rönningesjön side.
Alldeles intill ligger Viksjö gård, en h: Right next door is Viksjö gård, a manor and former noble estate that in the 17th century was held by, among others, the Skytte family. The farm sits on a hill, and modern Viksjö has spread out over the former fields around it. A little way off, in Jakobsberg, Järfällabadet opened in 2018, replacing the old swimming hall from 1971, which had a 48-metre water slide.
Alldeles intill ligger Västra Frölunda k: Right next door is Västra Frölunda cemetery, of medieval origin. The old Västra Frölunda church stood here until it was demolished in the 1860s, and in the wall there are iron rings where visitors once tied their horses. A grave slab inscribed Anno 1728 commemorates Olof Claeson, chief inspector at the Klippan customs station.
Alldeles intill ligger småorten Draget,: Right next door is the small village of Draget, on Vällingevägen north-west of Lake Aspen. A little further away is the neighbouring village of Fiskarhagen, which spreads out along Sankt Botvids väg between Lake Aspen and Lake Bornsjön. The road is part of the historic Göta landsväg, the old highway south, so the area has been a thoroughfare for a very long time.
Alldeles intill ligger Örvallen, Sverige: Right next to us is Örvallen, Sweden's national baseball arena and the country's only internationally approved baseball facility. It was completed in 2009 for the men's World Championship. The attendance record, 2,091 spectators, was set at the World Championship match between Canada and Sweden, which Canada won by a whopping 19 to 1. The home team is Sundbyberg Heat.
Alldeles intill lägger Kornhalls färja t: Right next to here, the Kornhall ferry docks – a cable ferry that crosses the Nordre älv river to Kornhall in Kungälv municipality. The crossing began in 1850 and was run by contractors until 1945, when the Swedish Road Administration took over. The shortcut to Gothenburg became so popular that the first motorised ferry was brought in in 1951. Today the route is served by M/S Gerd.
Alldeles intill låg torpet Månskär, som: Right next to us stood the croft Månskär, built when the new main road from Hornstull to Fittja was completed in 1673. Several crofts sprang up along the new road, among them Sadelmakartorp, which served as a schoolhouse after 1860. Today the area is dominated by Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen centrum is counted as the largest shopping destination in the Nordic countries.
Alldeles intill rinner Gudöån, som förbi: Right next to us flows the Gudöån stream, which connects Lake Drevviken with Lake Långsjön, and its centre line is the boundary between Haninge and Tyresö. Along the southern bank are traces of an almost extinct trade, the laundries. More well-preserved drying barns stand here than anywhere else in the county, reminders of the time when washing was an important source of income for smallholders. Today people would rather paddle a kayak here.
Alldeles intill stod Stuvsta gårds kvarn: Right next to us stood Stuvsta gård's mill, a windmill on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, which gave the Kvarnbergsplan area its name. A little further away, by Huddinge town hall, stands Bror Hjorth's bronze sculpture Girl with a Fruit Basket from 1951, life-sized, with a well-filled basket of apples. It was commissioned with money left over after the council chamber had been decorated with Sven X:et Erixson's large fresco.
Alldeles intill står Breviks kyrka, förs: Right next to us stands Brevik Church, a parish church in Lidingö parish. A short walk away is the Abenius Villa, also called Ljungströmshof, built in 1910 for Allan Abenius to designs by Ferdinand Boberg and Bror Almquist. The Stockholm County Museum has classed the house as culturally and historically irreplaceable.
Alldeles intill står Bräcke soldattorp f: Right next door stands Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft from the 1830s, a local history museum since 1965. From 1889 the soldier Sven Olof Emanuelsson Björk lived here. The croft has also moved: it used to stand north of the village of Bräcke. The home is no bigger than one room, a kitchen and an entrance hall – a modest soldier's home.
Alldeles intill står Kistastenen, runste: Right next door stands the Kista Stone, runestone U 75, at Kista gård. Even more runes have been hiding here: two Viking Age runestone fragments were walled into a cellar wall in Kista for a long time before being taken out in 1938, and today they are in the Swedish History Museum. A little further away you can see Kista fire station from 1980, with its distinctive concrete training tower.
Alldeles intill står Stensjökyrkan, och: Right next to us stands Stensjökyrkan, and a couple of hundred metres away, by Lake Stensjön, stood Mustad's margarine factory, in operation from 1897 to 1960. The lake has given its name to both the church and Stensjön parish, which also has Fågelbergskyrkan. Mölndal's upper station on the Borås line was also not far from here.
Alldeles intill står Västra Frölunda kyr: Right next to us stands Västra Frölunda church, the parish church of the old Västra Frölunda parish. The parish covered just over 32 square kilometres and was merged into the City of Gothenburg in 1945. A little way from here is something much newer: the Järnbrott bus depot, built exclusively for all-electric buses.
Alldeles intill, i Hagaparken vid Uppsal: Right nearby, in Haga Park on Uppsalavägen, is Haga tingshus, the old courthouse. Justice was dispensed here for the Södra Roslag district court right into the 1950s. A little further away rises the Wenner-Gren Center, the first high-rise in Sweden with a steel frame and, when it was completed, the tallest steel-framed building in Europe.
Alldeles intill, i hörnet av Litteraturg: Right next door, on the corner of Litteraturgatan and Skälltorpsvägen, is Friedländerska kyrkogården, the Friedländer cemetery. With just over twenty graves, it is Gothenburg's smallest cemetery – and privately owned as well. It belongs to Bäckebol Farm, a manor a little way off, and together with the farm it has been declared a listed monument.
Alldeles intill, vid Norra Kungsvägen, s: Right next to us, on Norra Kungsvägen, stands part of a runestone, Uppland runic inscription 172. It is one of only two runic inscriptions found on Lidingö; the other was discovered in 1984 near Bo gård. A little further away is Villa Backen, which Ivar Tengbom designed for August and Célie Brunius and which was completed in 1910.
Alldeles vid Bällsta bro, i hörnet av Bä: Right by Bällsta bro bridge, on the corner of Bällstavägen and Mariehällsvägen, is Mariehälls gård, a manor house that the Stockholm City Museum has blue-listed for its exceptionally high cultural and historical value. The house was built in 1790 and is named after Maria Elisabeth Wetterberg, wife of the tanner Melchior Eichhorn. The portico resembles a ship's stern, which is probably behind the legend that the shipbuilder af Chapman built the house.
Allmänna gränd ligger på Djurgården, mit: Allmänna gränd is on Djurgården, halfway between Gröna Lund and the Vasa Museum. From here you can reach the amusement park, museums and Skansen within a few minutes' walk.
Allmänna vägen var landsvägen västerut m: Allmänna vägen, the Public Road, was the country road west towards Klippan. It was the main street of Majorna until Karl Johansgatan was laid out in 1882. A devastating fire raged along the street in 1862, and the same year the villa on the Åhmansson estate was built. In 1919 Gothenburg's first vocational school was set up on the estate.
Allum, köpcentret ett stenkast bort, är: Allum, the shopping centre a stone's throw away, is big for real: 50,000 square metres, around 100 shops and about 1,700 parking spaces. Part of the building stretches right over the E20 motorway, and beneath the passage is a bus station. Partille church is also nearby, in the middle of the municipality's centre.
Allébron ser ut som en tunn skiva över S: Allébron looks like a thin slab over the Sickla canal. It was built in 2000 and carries pedestrians, cars and the Tvärbanan light rail trams on one and the same bridge. The bridge is in Hammarby sjöstad, was designed by Rundquist Arkitekter and links Lugnets allé between Sickla udde and Sickla kaj.
Alléparken, där Västerled möter Alviksvä: Alléparken, "the Avenue Park", where Västerled meets Alviksvägen, got its name in 1932, and in 1944 the author Gösta Langenfelt called it a monstrosity, since there was neither a park nor an avenue there. Later it turned out he was wrong: there actually was an avenue, which led to the croft Asplund, and some of the trees are still standing today.
Altartorp kan vara ett av traktens äldst: Altartorp may be one of the oldest crofts in the area, believed to date all the way back to 1540. According to folk tradition, the name Altaret, "the altar", comes from a place of prayer where soldiers held services before setting off for Europe's battlefields. A stone's throw away runs Smista allé, the street that has become known for the many car companies that have set up along it.
Altorps station öppnade 1910, när tågen: Altorp station opened in 1910, when trains began running here from Ösby. The line was extended to Lahäll in 1928 and to Näsbypark in 1937. Another branch was less lucky: from Eddavägen the track was extended to Svalnäs in 1912, but since the estate was never developed as planned, the stretch was closed as early as 1934. In the nearby cemetery is Altorp funeral chapel, where services are held over the All Saints' weekend.
Alvik är en knutpunkt där Tvärbanan och: Alvik is a hub where the Tvärbanan and Nockebybanan light rail lines meet the metro. From here you can reach Bromma, with its villa neighbourhoods and the shores of Lake Mälaren.
Alviks Torn fick bära titeln Västerorts: Alviks Torn, the Alvik Tower, held the title of the tallest residential building in Stockholm's western suburbs for about a year. It opened in December 2014 with 18 storeys and 56.7 metres, but as early as 2015 the record passed to Kista Torn. A bit of history in the neighbourhood: Tranebergs IP, a sports ground nicknamed Tranan, the Crane, was here from 1911 to 1935 and was leased by Djurgårdens IF before the club moved to Stockholm Olympic Stadium.
Alviks rättarbostad: Alviks rättarbostad, the Alvik farm foreman's house
Andalen, en bit härifrån, är liksom fler: Andalen, a little way from here, is, like several other places around Torslanda, a former summer cottage area that has grown into a villa area. The residents take care of a lot themselves: there's a road association, a private swimming spot run by Andals Badförening and a small harbour run by Andalens Båtförening, the local boat club.
Angered byggdes på 1970-talet och är i d: Angered was built in the 1970s and is today one of Gothenburg's most international districts. This is where the Blå Stället culture house is, and all around are large natural areas with lakes and forest.
Angered är en stadsdel på drygt 2 000 he: Angered is a district of just over 2,000 hectares that borders the Göta älv river to the west and Ale and Lerum to the north and east. Until 2015 Angered counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area, but since then the district has formed its own urban area, North-eastern Gothenburg. A little way off is Gunnared cemetery, opened in 2003.
Anundsvägen, en villagata en kort promen: Anundsvägen, a residential street a short walk from here, is known above all for one thing: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom paid a visit there in the 1950s. At about the same time Blackeberg was growing up, an area that even in the 1940s consisted mostly of forest and rock. The Kaskad cinema at Blackebergsplan has been there since 1957.
Apelsinlunden har fått sitt folkliga nam: Apelsinlunden, the Orange Grove, got its popular name from the orange-red colours of the buildings. The housing area was built in 1967 during the Million Programme housing drive to designs by Lars Bryde and is one of Stockholm's largest areas of low tower blocks. A little further on, the Götalandsviadukten viaduct crosses the railway tracks at Älvsjö station, where an early concrete arch bridge was built around 1910.
Arbetarrörelsens arkiv och bibliotek: The Labour Movement Archives and Library
Arbetarrörelsens torg är fullt av minnen: The labour movement's square is full of memories. The Branting Monument was commissioned from Carl Eldh as early as 1935, but was only unveiled in 1952 and became his largest and last completed work. Here you'll also find the Olof Palme memorial Mitt hjärta i världen, 'My Heart in the World'. LO-borgen, the trade union confederation's headquarters, designed by Ferdinand Boberg in 1899, was originally built for a timber merchant. And the fountain Maskrosbollen, the Dandelion, made for LO's centenary, has moved to Nacka.
Arendal är stort men nästan folktomt: på: Arendal is large but almost deserted: in 2012 only 90 people lived on its 890 hectares. Between 1963 and 1989 the Arendal shipyard was here. Today it is a large logistics and industrial area, with, among other things, the headquarters and development department of Volvo Buses and factories for several of Volvo's suppliers.
Arkitekten Jacob Gate ritade 1909 både V: In 1909 the architect Jacob Gate designed both Villa Höganloft, in Old Norse style, which has been a café, restaurant and Home Guard building, and the Trisshusen, an early form of terraced housing. A stone's throw away are the Canada Houses, considered among Sweden's very first terraced houses. The area is also home to Bo kvarn from 1816, one of the Stockholm area's oldest windmills still on its original site.
Arkitekten Ralph Erskine, som själv bodd: The architect Ralph Erskine, who himself lived on Lovön, dreamed of a lakeside town on Lake Mälaren at Tappström, and Ekerö centrum was the result. The area was completed in 1991, and Erskine himself was most pleased with this very project: it works as a complete community, he said in an interview, and he probably hadn't managed that in other places. Look out for the centre's landmark, a dot more than twenty metres high.
Arkitekturen i bostadsområdet Gretas bac: The architecture of the Gretas backe housing area, a short walk from here on Gamla Stockholmsvägen, won Huddinge's building award in 2017 – an award that had only just been created. The area belongs to Glömsta, a former noble estate that is today a residential area to the south, east and north of Lake Gömmaren.
Artillerigården har använts för artiller: Artillerigården, the Artillery Yard, has served the artillery's needs since the 1640s, and today Armémuseum, the Army Museum, is here. Beneath the yard hide two air-raid shelters from the Second World War, which are sometimes opened for tours. Round the corner at Artillerigatan 14 was the Michelin-starred restaurant Gastrologik, where guests got no menu and the chefs decided instead. Since 2024 the restaurant ergo has been in the same premises.
Artillerigården och Armémuseum: Artillerigården and the Army Museum, Armémuseum
Askim ligger vid Askimsfjorden, en del a: Askim lies on Askimsfjorden, part of the Kattegat, in hilly terrain where the villas crowd close to the coast. Askim is often pronounced 'Ashim'. In 1975 the Askim urban area grew together with Gothenburg's, and today the district counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. Askims torg, the square, is a short walk away.
Askim uttalas ”Ashim”, med ett sje-ljud,: Askim is pronounced 'Ashim', with a 'sh' sound, which tends to surprise visitors. The Askim parish has medieval origins and lies in the southern part of Gothenburg Municipality. A little way from here is the coastal area of Skintebo, which was farmland until the early 1970s.
Askims kyrka ligger inom promenadavstånd: Askim church is within walking distance of here. A bit further away is Sisjön, a lake for swimming and fishing in the Sandsjöbacka nature reserve, with both perch and pike. Curiously, the municipal border between Gothenburg and Mölndal runs straight through the middle of the lake, and a hiking trail winds around it.
Askims kyrka står bara ett par hundra me: Askim Church stands just a couple of hundred metres away, the parish church of a parish that stretches along the coast south of Gothenburg and became part of Gothenburg municipality in 1974. At the marina in Hovås there is also a sea rescue station, whose first boat, in 1983, was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson.
Askims kyrka, uttalas ”Ashim”, ligger al: Askim Church – pronounced "Ashim" – is right next door. The parish it serves is large, almost 37 square kilometres, and in 1974 it was merged into Gothenburg municipality. Within the parish boundaries are parts of Billdal, Gundal and Högås, the town of Hovås and, of course, the parish church itself.
Askims norra kyrkogård, bara några minut: Askim's northern cemetery, just a few minutes away, hides an exciting secret. The so-called privateer's grave is said to hold a privateer captain who served under Lars Gathenhielm. The cemetery has medieval origins, and the older part is surrounded by a stone wall with two lychgates.
Askims socken har vuxit rejält. Den 31 d: Askim parish has grown a lot. On 31 December 1888, 1,352 people lived here, but by 2000 the number had risen to 21,434. The parish belonged to Askim hundred, and in 1974 it became part of Gothenburg municipality. A short walk from here stands the parish church, Askim Church, and by the way, the name is pronounced "Ash-im".
Asperö är en liten ö i Göteborgs södra s: Asperö is a small island in Gothenburg's southern archipelago with just over four hundred permanent residents. The neighbouring island of Rivö is uninhabited, but the Asperö islanders' free-roaming sheep and horses graze there among hut foundations from the herring periods and two abandoned graveyards. On Brännö next door, the songwriter Lasse Dahlquist is buried, in a churchyard whose memorial grove is Gothenburg's smallest.
Aspnässkolan var Järfälla sockens första: Aspnässkolan was the first school of Järfälla parish and opened in 1846, in a manor house at the Aspnäs crossroads that had previously been a roadside tavern. The old school building was torn down in 1959, but it lives on in an unexpected way: today it serves as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor recreation centre. Right next door is the Pentecostal church Aspnäskyrkan.
Aspnässkolan, ett par minuter bort, var: Aspnässkolan, a couple of minutes away, was the very first school of Järfälla parish, opening in 1846 in a purchased manor house that had previously been a roadside inn. The oldest school building was demolished in 1959, but lives on in an unexpected way: today it serves as a wind shelter at Ängsjö friluftsgård, an outdoor recreation centre. The hospital itself is owned by Region Stockholm and houses, among other things, a health centre and a pharmacy.
Aspudden började byggas på 1910-talet, o: Aspudden began to be built in the 1910s, and many of the new homes had no bathroom. That made Aspudden's bathhouse on Schlytersvägen very popular, and it lasted from 1919 all the way to 2009. Even older is Villa Emmalund from 1885, where a farm slaughterhouse operated, mainly for horses, until 1912, when compulsory slaughter at the public abattoirs was introduced.
Aspuddsparken är en av Stockholms störst: Aspuddsparken is one of Stockholm's largest staffed playgrounds with animals, perfect if you'd like to say hello to a goat or two. Next to it is Aspuddens IP, a sports ground opened in 1913 and popularly called Linnéa, after a villa where the lads who founded the club IF Linnéa played football. On Manhemsgatan stands the fountain sculpture Fontändamm, created in 1912 by the architect Albin Brag, who also designed several of the area's Art Nouveau buildings.
Astrid Lindgrens berg: Astrid Lindgrens berg, Astrid Lindgren's hill
Backa Röd heter hyreshusområdet runt knu: Backa Röd is the name of the rental housing area round the corner, with its 1,500 apartments. And no, the name probably has nothing to do with a colour, even though röd means red. Here röd most likely means cleared land, land that was once cleared so it could be farmed. The district has the Backavallens IP sports ground and also Gothenburg's very first neighbourhood sports ground.
Backa socken i Bohuslän hörde en gång ti: Backa parish in Bohuslän once belonged to the Västra Hising hundred and was a rural municipality of its own. In 1948 the parish became part of the City of Gothenburg, and the old parish church, Backa church, is a little way from here. The parish covered almost fifteen square kilometres, and in 1988 more than 20,000 people lived here.
Backa, även kallat Hisings Backa, ligger: Backa, also called Hisings Backa, lies on the eastern side of Hisingen and stretches from Brunnsbo in the south to Skälltorp in the north. The old Backa parish became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1948. Backa Church, the parish church, is a little way from here, and a little further away is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, a square named after the Nobel Prize-winning author.
Bada på Husbybadet: Go for a swim at Husbybadet
Badkläderna med? En kort promenad bort l: Brought your swimming things? A short walk away is Stora Mölnesjön in eastern Rannebergen, with a swimming spot and jetty on the western side. A little further on is Lilla Mölnesjön, which belongs to the Vättlefjäll Natura 2000 area, and in the other direction the Lärjeån valley nature reserve begins.
Bagare by var förr namnet på Turebergs g: Bagare by, the Baker's Village, was once the name of Tureberg farm, and that's where the area's name comes from. For many years this was the site of Sollentunamässan, once Sweden's third-largest exhibition centre, which was demolished in 2017 to make way for housing. Today the area is dominated by Rättscentrum, the justice centre with a police station, district court and remand prison. Through the area runs Malmvägen, popularly known as Tian, 'the Ten', after its ten tower blocks, a Million Programme housing project that drew international attention when it opened in 1972.
Bagaregårdsskolan stod klar i april 1918: Bagaregårdsskolan was completed in April 1918, designed by Johan Jarlén, with a base of rustic grey stone and an ornate clock tower on the roof. Round the corner was the Saga cinema, which opened in 1942 and closed in 1964. The following year Bengt Johansson bought the premises and opened a grocery shop, Saga hemköp, which became the first shop in the Sagabutikerna chain. From cinema to checkout, in other words.
Baggeby blev plötsligt slutstation i jun: Baggeby suddenly became a terminus in June 2023. The old Lidingö Bridge was demolished, and the new Lilla Lidingöbron couldn't yet carry trains because of construction faults. So the Lidingöbanan trams turned here instead of continuing to Ropsten. Up in the villa suburb of Mosstorp, a short walk away, Hersby water tower stands at the end of Vattentornsvägen.
Bakom Lisebergs staket en bit härifrån l: Behind Liseberg's fence, a little way from here, lies Balders Hage, where the sports club Örgryte IS was founded in 1887 and where a skating oval opened on New Year's Day 1888. Today the Balder roller coaster races along nearby, one of the largest wooden roller coasters in the Nordic countries. And for those who want a fright, there's the Gasten haunted hotel, where visitors are met by live actors who scare them.
Bakom den trekantiga parken döljer sig e: Behind the triangular park lies one of Stockholm's most talked-about unsolved crimes. On 4 May 1932, Lilly Lindeström was found murdered in her flat at Sankt Eriksplan 11, in what is known as the Vampire Murder. There are brighter memories around the corner: the Capitol cinema from 1926 closed in 1985 but reopened in 2018 as Bio & Bistro Capitol.
Bakom granitmuren intill parken ligger V: Behind the granite wall next to the park is Västra kyrkogården, the Western Cemetery, on a slope in the middle of today's Kungälv. When it was completed in 1864 it lay just outside the town's buildings and was called Nya kyrkogården, the New Cemetery, to distinguish it from the old one. In the northern part stand mostly gravestones from the early 1900s, while the newer ones are gathered in the south. In other words, the town has grown past its own graves.
Bakom husen renar Käppalaverket avloppsv: Behind the houses, the Käppala plant, Käppalaverket, has been treating wastewater since 1969, and it is considered one of the world's most efficient treatment plants. A little way off is Käppalaställningen, an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War that was reopened in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defence, unique in Sweden. A bit further on is M/S Soya III, a tanker from 1936 built for soybean oil, today a conference ship.
Bakom hållplatsen ligger Östra Mölna rad: Behind the stop is the Östra Mölna terraced-house area, also called Vita staden, the White Town. The architect Nils Tesch designed the 52 terraced houses and eight villas as early as 1954, but they weren't built until between 1962 and 1972. The municipality has classed the area as culturally and historically irreplaceable. A little way off stands Villa Sjöstigen, which Ferdinand Boberg designed in 1911 as an experiment in cheap summer housing.
Bakom murarna i Härlanda satt fångar frå: Behind the walls at Härlanda, prisoners were held from 1907 to 1997. The old central prison is a listed building and is now called Härlanda park. The Saga cinema on Sofiagatan closed in 1964. The following year it became a grocery shop, Saga Hemköp, the first in the Sagabutikerna chain. In among the buildings there is also an old church ruin.
Bakom namnet Almedal finns ett litet bar: Behind the name Almedal is a little child. The area is named after Alma Buchholtz, who lived only in 1840–41 and was the daughter of an earlier owner of the Almedal country estate. The name then lived on through the linen factory that Hans Hemming Wesslau founded in 1848 by the Mölndalsån river, Almedahls fabriker. Almedalsvägen has existed since 1933.
Balltorp kan låta som en modern förort,: Balltorp may sound like a modern suburb, and the big expansion did happen in the 1980s. But the place was inhabited as long as 10,000 years ago! The district is in the southern part of Västra Mölndal, which corresponds to Fässberg district, and a little further away are both Västra and Östra Balltorp.
Bandhagens centrum invigdes 1954 tillsam: Bandhagen's centre opened in 1954 together with the metro station and is still owned by the housing cooperative HSB Bandhagen, with just over 500 apartments and around twenty shops. Above the centre rises the Murbruket block, an eleven-storey slab block from 1955. Both the building and the whole district are counted by the City Museum as culturally and historically valuable.
Bandhagens gymnasium vid Trollesundsväge: Bandhagens gymnasium, the upper secondary school on Trollesundsvägen, was built from 1957 to 1959, and the assembly hall came ten years later. The school housed various upper secondary programmes until 2002, and in the early 2000s the premises were converted into homes. So today people live in the old classrooms, and the property is marked green by the City Museum as particularly valuable.
Bara ett par hundra meter bort, nära Glö: Just a couple of hundred metres away, near Glömstavägen, is Glömstahällen, a runic rock in the Glömsta valley. Glömsta became a district of its own as late as 2018 and before that belonged to Flemingsberg. The houses surround Lake Gömmaren, and what was once an old holiday-cottage area is now slowly being filled in with new houses.
Bara ett par minuter bort ligger en sten: Just a couple of minutes away lies a stone that no one has really dared to live in: Dvärgahuset, the Dwarf House, a stone cist grave from the Late Neolithic that people believed was the home of dwarves. The grave was described in writing as early as the 17th century, was surely known to local people long before that, and was examined in 1899 by the archaeologist Oscar Montelius.
Bara ett par minuters promenad härifrån: Just a couple of minutes' walk from here are the ruins of Ytterby old church. It was built in the 12th century, when the area was Norwegian land, and according to legend it was Saint Olaf who built it. It was the parish church until 1870. The railway station itself, on the Bohus line, is much younger: it opened in 1907.

Just a couple of minutes' walk from here stands Kälvesta kvarn, a 17th-century windmill also known as Lilla Stampan and Lunda kvarn. The City Museum has blue-listed it, the highest cultural-heritage classification there is, because it is judged to have exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Not bad for a mill that started life on Observatoriegatan in the city centre.
Bara ett stenkast bort ligger Nilento St: Just a stone's throw away is Nilento Studio, a recording studio founded in 1993 by the musicians Lars Nilsson and Jenny Nilsson. It started as a mobile studio and is today popular for everything from jazz and big band to choirs, opera and symphony orchestras. Since 2013 they have also run their own record label.
Bara ett stenkast bort står Kummelbysten: Just a stone's throw away stands the Kummelby stone, a runestone carved in the late 11th century, almost a thousand years before the suburb grew up. It stands by Kummelby church, built where Kummelby farm once lay. The first church was so small that it was called Kummelby lillkyrka, the Little Church, with room for just 50 people. The new church was consecrated just before Christmas in 2000.
Bara ett stenkast bort står Villa Lundin: Just a stone's throw away stands Villa Lundin, built around 1911 and today one of the few well-preserved villas from that time. The house was often called “the Castle”, and the Lundin family who lived there are said to have owned one of Fagersjö's two cars in the 1930s. Real luxury in those days!
Bara några minuter bort reser sig Tyresö: Just a few minutes away rises Tyresö View, 82 metres tall with 23 floors, in 2016 the fourth tallest residential building in the whole of Stockholm County. About as close is Tyresö Centrum, a glazed-in shopping centre with 74 shops, the municipal offices and a library, where an exhibition hall constantly shows new exhibitions.
Bara några minuters promenad bort väntar: Just a few minutes' walk away is Kärna bokskog, a beech forest and nature reserve since 2008. Lichen lovers have a lot to enjoy, because there are several red-listed lichen species here, and the flora also includes the rare grass wood fescue. The reserve is about 18 hectares and is managed by the West Coast Foundation, with some parts adapted for accessibility.
Bara några steg härifrån porlar Sankt Bo: Just a few steps from here bubbles Saint Botvid's Spring, a cold-water spring at the south-eastern tip of Lake Bornsjön. About fifty metres away stands the Söderby Stone, a runestone next to the old Södertäljevägen road. A little further on is Söderby burial ground, one of the best preserved in the Mälaren Valley, with about 150 visible graves from the early Iron Age, and the farm Nedre Söderby from the 18th century.
Barkarby is a place in full transformation. The commuter train station got its current form on 10 October 2016, with four tracks and a ticket hall on the Barkarby bridge. At the same time a new metro station is being built underground, and a new entrance at the north end of the station is to become the main entrance when everything is finished.
Barken Viking vid kajen: The barque Viking at the quay
Barnet med käpphästen i Hagsätra centrum: Barnet med käpphästen, the Child with the Hobby Horse, in Hagsätra Centre
Beckbrukets chefsbostad: The tar works manager's house at Beckbruket
Begravningskapellet på Silverdals grifte: The funeral chapel at Silverdal Cemetery is built together with the crematorium. The whole Gärdestad family rests here. The cemetery itself was laid out in 1914 as a garrison cemetery for the Stockholm garrison. And the Silverdal area almost got a different name: when building plans began in 1989, the project was first called Margreteborg.
Bergshamras tunnelbanestation har en ova: Bergshamra metro station has an unusual design: Bergshamravägen runs on an underground bridge right on top of the passage between the southern entrance and the platform. The station opened in 1978. The area also has old houses by Stocksundet strait, such as the villa Fjällstugan from 1835 and Stocksundstorp farm, whose buildings were probably put up around 1753.
Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap: Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap, the Bergslagen Railway Company
Besök Akalla by med 4H-gård och kafé: Visit Akalla village with its 4H farm and café
Besök Kulturhuset Bergsjön: Visit Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house
Besök Sankta Birgitta kyrka: Visit Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Bridget's Church
Besök Sveriges VVS-museum: Visit the Swedish Plumbing Museum, Sveriges VVS-museum
Besök konsthallen Accelerator i det gaml: Visit the Accelerator art gallery in the old underground lab
Bilarna på Stuvstaleden försvinner in i: The cars on Stuvstaleden disappear into the Kungsklippan rock through the Stuvsta tunnel, 193 metres long and opened in 1994. Before that the road ran straight through Stuvsta, causing noise problems. The strangest thing is the tunnel's northern entrance: it is built into an apartment building that was constructed at the same time and straddles the entrance.
Billdal bjuder på både kyrka, park och h: Billdal offers church, park and sea all within walking distance. Billdal church is just a couple of hundred metres away, and right after that begins the nature area Billdals park, with Billdals gård, the manor. A bit further away, the Killingsholmen peninsula juts out into the water, with a municipal small-boat harbour and its own shipyard, Killingsholmens Varv.
Bio Capitol vid Skanstorget har visat fi: Bio Capitol on Skanstorget has been showing films since 1941 and since 1999 has been home to Cinemateket, the film archive cinema. A stone's throw away was the Sprängkullen activity centre, started in 1974, an important meeting place for the music movement and later the punk scene, where many well-known bands played. And Husargatan is named after the Crown Prince's Hussars, who were for a time quartered in a barracks at the end of the street.
Bio Kaskad, alldeles intill, öppnade 195: Bio Kaskad, right next door, opened in 1957, closed at the end of the 1990s and came back to life in 2018. Under the square, part of the metro platform lies inside the rock, with green, blue and yellow tiles. The collective housing block nearby was built in 1952 with 84 small flats for single people and young childless families, and Josephinahemmet is named after Queen Josefina, wife of Oscar I.
Biocafé Tellus vid Vattenledningsvägen ä: Biocafé Tellus on Vattenledningsvägen is one of the few remaining small cinemas from earlier times in Stockholm, with a café where all sorts of cultural events take place. A little further away is the Aspen cinema, which when it opened in 1952 was the first private cinema to be established in Stockholm since 1943. The auditorium had 300 seats but no balcony.
Biografen Bristol på Sturegatan invigdes: The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened on New Year's Eve 1939, and its owner at the time was Algot Myrgren. Today it is both a cinema and a cultural venue. A little further away is Folkets hus, the community hall, built as early as 1903, with rooms for meetings, conferences and parties, where the main hall holds up to 100 people. And the nearby Esplanaden is graced by a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström.
Biografen Vingen på Gamla Björlandavägen: The Vingen cinema at Gamla Björlandavägen 145 had a short but intense life. It was built and run by Leif Harald Winqvist and opened on 19 December 1957. Rolf Magnusson took over in 1960, but on 2 January 1962 the lights went out for good. Right next to the stop stands Toleredskyrkan, a church belonging to Lundby parish.
Biograferna har avlöst varandra här. Bio: Cinemas have come and gone here. Biografteatern on Sveagatan was already showing films in 1904–1908. Mignon on Linnégatan had 182 seats and was open from 1941 to 1982. At Sveaplan there was then Klappan, followed by Svea until 2008. The street is named after the Olivedal estate.
Björkhagen hörde under två korta år, 199: For two short years, 1997 and 1998, Björkhagen belonged to the Hammarby district, which was dissolved when the number of city districts was cut from 24 to 18. A stone's throw away rises Duggregnet 5, which was Stockholm's tallest residential building when it was built in 1957. And from the metro station starts Sörmlandsleden, a hiking trail that is part of the European long-distance path E6.
Björkhagens skola invigdes 1949, ritad a: Björkhagen School opened in 1949, designed by the architect Åke Lindqvist, and to the east the school grounds border the Nacka Reserve, Nackareservatet. The Taklampan block a little way off also lies right up against the reserve, and it was one of ten building projects nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2018. So here the deep forest is almost on your doorstep.
Björknäs nämns i skrift redan 1436 och h: Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436 and is named after Stora Björknäs gård, the farm. The area is at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where Skurusundet strait divides the provinces: west of the water is Södermanland, east of it Uppland. The bridges have been built in three rounds, in 1915, 1957 and 2023, and when the newest one opened it took over the name Skurubron, while the older ones became Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge.
Björkö, eller Bohus-Björkö som postorten: Björkö, or Bohus-Björkö as the postal town is called, has just over 1,500 permanent residents. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg Outdoor Association owns an area used as a naturist area with swimming and camping. Near Bovik is also Pjonken, known for the large number of hepaticas, blue anemones, that flower there every spring.

Björkö, or Bohus-Björkö as the postal town is called, has a few more secrets than you might think. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg outdoor association owns an area used as a naturist area with swimming and camping. The island has around 1,500 permanent residents and an area of just under five and a half square kilometres.
Björlanda kyrka, en bit härifrån, står p: Björlanda Church, a little way from here, stands on north-western Hisingen and since 2010 has belonged to Torslanda-Björlanda parish. The old Björlanda parish was counted as part of the province of Bohuslän and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000, just over 10,000 people lived in the parish. The parish is large, almost 44 square kilometres, and in 2000 just over 5,000 inhabitants lived here.
Björlanda, kyrkbyn i Björlanda socken, h: Björlanda, the church village of Björlanda parish, has had trouble making up its mind about what it is. Before 2015 it was a locality of its own, then part of Torslanda, from 2018 a locality of its own again, and from 2023 it counts as part of Gothenburg. The houses are next to the church and were mainly built during the 1990s.
Blockhusudden är Djurgårdens östligaste: Blockhusudden is the easternmost point of Djurgården, and this is where Stora Sjötullen, the great sea customs house, stood, mentioned as early as 1623. It charged a toll on all sea traffic coming in from the archipelago, so this is where boats had to pay before reaching the city. Along Blockhusringen are several fine villas, among them Johannisberg, whose summer salon has been a listed building since 1935, and a little further on the art treasures of Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, await.
Bollmora var faktiskt en egen tätort åre: Bollmora was actually a locality of its own from 1965 to 1974, but today the area is mostly called Tyresö centrum. There's a glazed shopping centre with 74 shops and a library with its own exhibition hall. Above it all rises Tyresö View, 82 metres and 23 storeys tall, which in 2016 was the fourth-tallest residential building in the whole of Stockholm County.
Bollmora var åren 1965–1974 en egen täto: From 1965 to 1974 Bollmora was a separate built-up locality, but today the area is mostly called Tyresö centrum. Here you'll find the glazed shopping centre with 74 shops, the municipal hall and a library with its own exhibition room. A little further away is Tyresövallen, formerly Bollmoravallen, home ground of both Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators.
Bollmora, som Tyresö centrum egentligen: Bollmora, which is the real name of Tyresö centrum, was a town in its own right in 1965–1974 and had 16,566 inhabitants in 2010. A few minutes away is Bollmoradalen church, the parish church of Tyresö parish, which covers the whole municipality. And a little further on, Tyresö View stretches up 82 metres as one of the tallest residential buildings in the county.
Boo breder ut sig på västra delen av ön: Boo spreads out over the western part of the island of Värmdö, east of the Skurusundet strait. Until 2015 Boo was a town of its own, but since then its buildings have merged with the Stockholm urban area, so the big city has in practice made its way across the strait. A little way from here glitters Kocktorpssjön, a small lake in the district.
Bostadshuset 79&Park, alldeles intill, ä: The residential building 79&Park, right next door, was designed by the Danish architecture firm Bjarke Ingels Group and was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2019. A little way off, in a 1920s warehouse in Frihamnen, the free port, the financier Robert Weil and museum director David Neuman founded in 1987 what became the art museum Magasin III. Since May 2024 the museum has closed its public activities in Stockholm.
Bostadsområdet Alphyddan byggdes 1960 ti: The Alphyddan housing area was built from 1960 to 1965 to designs by the architects Backström and Reinius, with the Svindersberg nature area as a green neighbour to the east. A little further away is Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, where Atlas Diesel made diesel engines until 1951 and which today houses a cultural centre, library and cinema. Sickla Köpkvarter next door has around 160 shops and restaurants.
Bostadsområdet Annedal vid Bällstaån har: The Annedal housing area by the Bällstaån stream is named after a plot owned in the 1880s by Anna Augusta Wickman-Olsson. Between 2008 and 2013 around 2,000 flats went up here, and to the north-west the area ends with the Mattisborgen block and its tower. On the other side of Ulvsundavägen lies Solvalla, the trotting track.
Bostadsområdet Krusboda, i området här o: The Krusboda housing area, around here, grew up in the first half of the 1970s, between 1970 and 1975, and has its own school, Krusboda skola. A longer walk away is Barnsjön, a small forest lake just under nine metres deep with a public swimming spot. It belongs to the Tyresån river catchment, so the water here eventually makes its way through the Tyresån river.
Bostadsområdet Myrängen-Högmora ligger i: The residential area of Myrängen-Högmora is nestled into Kynäsberget hill, between western Magelungen and lake Trehörningen. Högmora consists mostly of holiday homes with some permanent housing and became a district of its own in 2018, while Myrängen has terraced houses and a school for the youngest children. All around, the forest and hill area takes over, of national interest for outdoor recreation.
Botkyrkahallen, några minuter härifrån,: Botkyrkahallen, a few minutes from here, was opened in the summer of 2000 by King Carl XVI Gustaf and is the home ground of Balrog IK's men's team. A little way off is S:t Botvids gymnasium, an upper secondary school best known for its contemporary circus programme together with Cirkus Cirkör. Among the school's former pupils are the artist Dogge Doggelito and the politician Ibrahim Baylan.
Bredäng är ordentligt kuperat: Bredängss: Bredäng is properly hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, is 62 metres above sea level and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken next to the centre is one of the district's largest parks, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because it used to be rowdy. Bredäng Church isn't a building of its own but is housed in a parish hall at one end of the centre.
Bremnäs är en liten by med ett lite förv: Bremnäs is a small village with a slightly confusing statistical life. Statistics Sweden counted it as a small locality for fifteen years, until its neighbour Stora Lycke had grown together with it and both suddenly became one urban area with the double name Lycke och Bremnäs. The area belongs to Lycke parish on the coast south-east of Marstrand, and a little way from here stands the parish church, Lycke Church.
Breviks gård, som gav området sitt namn,: Breviks gård, the manor that gave the area its name, dated back to the 14th century. The last main building was demolished in 1987, and Brevik centre now stands there. Next to it is Blocket, from 1914–1915, one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings. In 1905 the estate's owner offered to pay for a small primary school, today Banvägen 7. A little way off is the Abenius Villa, Abeniuska villan, designed by Ferdinand Boberg.
Bromma flygplats invigdes den 13 maj 193: Bromma Airport was opened on 13 May 1936 by King Gustaf V and was the first airport in Europe with asphalt runways. The old hangars were in their day the largest in Northern Europe, and today they house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. The first hypermarket moved in there as early as 1972.
Brommadepån, som stod klar 1944, byggdes: Brommadepån, the tram depot completed in 1944, was built where there had previously been emergency housing from 1917, and trams from the Ängbybanan, Nockebybanan and Tvärbanan lines have all been parked here. Not far from here, in the summer of 1927, no fewer than 29 newly built villas along Ekorrvägen were shown at the housing exhibition Bygge och Bo in Äppelviken. Ulvsunda garden city next door was originally called Kungsholms villastad.
Brostugan på Kärsön har anor från 1700-t: The Bridge Cottage, Brostugan, on Kärsön dates back to the 18th century and stands by Nockebybron, a swing bridge over Lake Mälaren. The bridge has recently been given a new lease of life: the Swedish Transport Administration has moved the footpath and cycle path to the other side and built a reversible lane that can change direction according to the traffic. The work is linked to the construction of the Stockholm Bypass, Förbifart Stockholm.
Brotorp är Sundbybergs ytmässigt minsta: Brotorp is Sundbyberg's smallest district by area, just three per cent of the municipality. The land was long used by the military, and not far from here was Järva skjutfält, a military training ground on Järvafältet. Today Brotorp is Sundbyberg's part of the large urban development project Järvastaden, which it shares with Solna.
Brunnsparken är stadens hjärta för kolle: Brunnsparken is the heart of the city's public transport. Almost all the tram lines run from here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, the square with the statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that's why Gothenburg has canals. The Dutch knew how to build on clay.
Brunnstorpsnäs är en liten ort vid Nordr: Brunnstorpsnäs is a small village on the shore of the Nordre älv river on Hisingen, with only 87 residents in 2023. Small but important, because from here the Kornhall ferry crosses the river to Kornhall in Kungälv municipality. The village is in the former parish of Säve, around two kilometres north-west of Säve.
Bräcke by ligger i Torsby socken, fyra k: The village of Bräcke lies in Torsby parish, four kilometres from the Kattegat coast and seven kilometres north of the mouth of the Nordre älv river. At the Råckeröd pass, about 700 metres east of the village, stands Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft from the 1830s. It is now a local heritage museum, and the croft was actually moved there from a site north of the village.
Bräcke cemetery has a grim history. When cholera hit Sweden hard in the 19th century, the disease entered the country via Gothenburg, and this cemetery was established in connection with the epidemic of 1834. It was used until 1886, when Lundby church was completed with its own churchyard, and today it is classed as a protected ancient monument. Since 2017 it has been a memorial grove for ashes.
Bråvallavägens station, en bit härifrån,: Bråvallavägen station, a little way from here, opened in 1909 and is a small station with about 150 people boarding on an ordinary winter weekday. Two trains collided there in 2013 while carriages were being coupled. In the other direction is Altorp station, which came into use in 1910 and is a passing station on the single-track section towards Näsbypark.
Bussarna mot Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsu: The buses to Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsund and Tjörn pull in at the travel centre, and right next door is Kongahälla Center, with around a hundred shops and restaurants, opened in 2019. The E6 motorway rushes past right alongside. A little further away is Oasen, a swimming pool and ice rink built after the old swimming baths burned down. It has both a 25-metre pool and a rehab pool with warmer water.
Bygden här på sydöstra Färingsö har gaml: The countryside here in southeastern Färingsö goes back a long way. The development of Mörby village can be traced from the mid-1400s, and the neighbouring village of Ekeby is mentioned as early as 1342, when Eskil Petersson and his wife Cecilia exchanged land with Vårfruberga convent. At Troxhammar stands a Viking Age granite runestone a full 2.2 metres tall.
Byn bjuder på ett litet vikingatida gall: The village offers a small Viking Age gallery. One runestone, U 44, signed by the carver Snare, disappeared some time between about 1795 and 1850 and only turned up again in 1981, in pieces that were then fitted back together. It is more than two metres tall. Another stone, U 43, has stood at the entrance to a farm since 1937, and on an embedded boulder, Saxe had runes carved in memory of his mother.
Bysten av Carl Michael Bellman avtäcktes: The bust of Carl Michael Bellman was unveiled in 1829. The year before, the court confectioner Carlmark had opened a café here, which was named Bellmansro, Bellman's Rest, after the bust. The restaurant burned down in 1955, but the place still has the name. Its neighbour is the Oakhill mansion, which Ferdinand Boberg designed for Prince Wilhelm in 1910. Since 1926 it has been the Italian Embassy.
Bäckahagens skola byggdes i etapper mell: Bäckahagen school was built in stages between 1953 and 1968 to designs by the architect David Dahl, and the school included both a home for the caretaker and its own dental clinic. All of Bandhagen is a good example of "folkhem" architecture, the style of Sweden's post-war welfare state, with low-rise buildings forming leafy courtyards and point-block towers that break things up and give the area a varied character.
Bäckebol Center är ett av Hisingens stor: Bäckebol Center is one of Hisingen's big retail areas, with around twenty shops on a whole 95,000 square metres. Shops come and go, and one shop left the area in 2010 only to come back three years later. A little way off flows the Lärjeån river, which starts north of Gråbo and flows into the Göta älv river at Lärjeholm.
Bäckebols gård, en bit härifrån, är en h: Bäckebols gård, a little way from here, is a manor house and former manorial estate by a stream. Construction in stone was begun in 1764 by the weighmaster and ironworks owner Johan Oliveholm, and the house was restored in 1943–1944. Since 9 January 1969 it has been a listed building, and the estate also includes Gothenburg's smallest churchyard.
Bällsta är en trädgårdsstad av små trähu: Bällsta is a garden suburb of small wooden houses from the 1940s, where around 200 cottages were self-built: the owners built them themselves, with materials and instructions from the City of Stockholm's small-cottage office. A little further away is Solvalla, Sweden's national arena for harness racing, with room for 35,000 guests and home to Elitloppet, one of the world's biggest trotting races. On a hill nearby stands the radar tower popularly known as Golfbollen, the Golf Ball.
Bänk vid vattnet med utsikt mot Långholm: A bench by the water with a view towards Långholmen
Bärby Korsväg är bara cirka 650 meter lå: Bärby Korsväg is only about 650 metres long and runs between Kongahällavägen and Svensbyvägen in the small village of Bärby. But the village has a grander history than the road: between 1824 and 1887 Bärby was the court site for the Västra and Östra Hising districts, where trials for large parts of Hisingen were held.
Bö herrgård omnämns redan 1485, och 1746: Bö manor is mentioned as early as 1485, and in 1746 none other than Carl Linnaeus came to visit and described the manor and its garden. A pear tree on the site is said to have been planted by him. Closer by rises Örgryte New Church in neo-Gothic style, with a tower of nearly 60 metres. The church got electric lighting in 1908, the same year as its neighbour, Bö School.
Canonhuset, några minuter härifrån, bygg: Canonhuset, the Canon Building, a few minutes from here, was built for the electronics company Canon and houses offices, a warehouse and a workshop. The building is one of the few examples of Swedish high-tech architecture and is blue-listed by the City Museum. A little further away is Sätra pistol shooting range, which despite its name is in Bredäng and is the only range of its kind in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Carl Milles Flöjtspelande ängel, ett av: Carl Milles's Flöjtspelande ängel, the Flute-Playing Angel, one of his late works and originally intended for the Saint Martin Fountain, can be found in several places, including by Lidingöbron, the Lidingö Bridge. At the landing of the old Lidingö Bridge also stands a small building by Ivar Tengbom, opened in 1925 and used as a waiting shelter until 1967. The windy spot earned it the popular name Vindarnas tempel, the Temple of the Winds.
Carlanderska sjukhuset intill uppfördes: Carlanderska sjukhuset, the hospital next door, was built in 1927 to designs by Arvid Bjerke and was originally called Carlanderska sjukhemmet, the Carlander nursing home. A little way off, in Renströmsparken, stands Solringen, the Sun Ring, a 4.4-metre-high ring by Claes Hake. It has a twin: a version in patinated bronze was put up the same year, 1993, in Hjørring in Denmark.
Chalmers tekniska högskola grundades 182: Chalmers University of Technology was founded in 1829 with money bequeathed by William Chalmers. He had worked for the Swedish East India Company. All around is the Johanneberg campus, where thousands of engineers are trained every year.
Chapmans torg fick sitt namn 1939 efter: Chapmans torg got its name in 1939 after the legendary sea captain Charles Chapman, who was active here in Majorna in the 18th century. Many of the people who lived here in Majorna used to work in the shipyards and the harbour.
Choklad, konst och plask! Marabouparken: Chocolate, art and splashing! Marabouparken is open to everyone, with a sculpture collection that had grown to sixteen works by the 1970s and a paddling pool that attracts families with children. The art gallery opened in 2010 and is built underground, next to the old cocoa laboratory building. Nearby, Sundbyberg Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb and displays burnt bones from a Viking Age grave.
Dalens sjukhus från 1977 är ett välbevar: Dalen Hospital from 1977 is a well-preserved example of late modernist architecture typical of its time, with value for the history of urban planning. A little way off, on the Nytorp field, was the croft Nytorp, belonging to Hammarby Farm, which disappeared in the early 1960s when the Nytorpsbadet pool was built on its site. The Dalen residential area consists of 14 courtyard blocks and is green-listed by the City Museum in its entirety.
Danderyds gymnasium: Danderyd gymnasium, an upper secondary school
Danderyds kyrka ligger ett par minuter b: Danderyd church is a couple of minutes away, next to the busy E18 towards Norrtälje. By the gate stands the runestone U 127, one of the Jarlabanke stones, and south of the churchyard lies Berga gård, which probably dates back to the Viking Age, with a manor house from the 18th century. Next to the church there is also Klockare Malm's Chapel, used for smaller christenings, weddings and funerals.
Danderyds kyrka, en bit härifrån, gömmer: Danderyd Church, a little way from here, hides several Viking Age runestone fragments. One of them, the top of a sandstone stone, was found as late as 1938 in the Banér family burial vault during a restoration and is now fixed to the church's western inner wall. Just west of the church stands runestone U 131, between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall.
De eleganta villorna i Lärkstaden byggde: The elegant villas of Lärkstaden were built around 1912. In Tofslärkan 3, Prime Minister Karl Staaff lived between 1912 and 1915. The neighbouring villa, Tofslärkan 6, has housed the Embassy of Latvia since 1995. The plots were small: Tofslärkan 3 measured just 292 square metres, including a nine-metre-wide strip for the garden.
De gamla trähusen runt berget: The old wooden houses around the hill
De tre vingarna: De tre vingarna, the Three Wings
Delvis under Södertäljevägen, en bit här: Partly under Södertäljevägen, a little way from here, lies Svarta Löt – one of the best-known medieval assembly sites in the area, where courts were held as early as when Stockholm was founded. It is thought to have been by the croft Eriksberg, formerly called Tingsta, at Kumla gård. Even older is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist grave from the late Stone Age, dated to around 1800 BC. Only seven such graves are known in the whole of Stockholm County.
Den 14 april 1993 rasade marken vid Agne: On 14 April 1993 the ground collapsed at the Agnesberg industrial area, on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, a little way from here. It was a pilot on board a ship who spotted the landslide at nine o'clock, and by then an area of about 20 by 50 metres had already slid out into the river. The slide reached right up to an industrial building, and several smaller slides followed the same day.
Den 3 april 1973 öppnade OBS i Bäckebol,: On 3 April 1973, OBS opened in Bäckebol, 30,000 square metres in size and at the time the country's largest hypermarket. Long before that there was Bäckebol farm. The manor house began to be built in stone in 1764 by the weighmaster Johan Oliveholm and has been a listed building since 1969. The owners of the estate even have their own burial ground, in use since the mid-18th century.
Den 3 mars 1957 beslöt magistraten i Göt: On 3 March 1957, Gothenburg's city magistrates decided to split Arendal into two districts, Arendal and Syrhåla. Arendal became a purely industrial area where only 90 people lived in 2012, with Volvo Buses' headquarters among other things. Syrhåla kept its old name from 1550, which means a swampy place or sour ground.
Den del av Hagsätra som ligger sydväst o: The part of Hagsätra south-west of Huddingevägen has a name of its own: Ormkärr. A little further away is Hagsätra Centre, which opened in 1960 after a year of construction, the same year the metro reached Hagsätra. The centre's trademark is Barnet med käpphästen, 'The Child with the Hobby Horse', a copper sculpture designed by Marie Stenqvist.
Den del av Ånäsvägen som går mellan Redb: The part of Ånäsvägen that runs between Redbergsplatsen and Ejdergatan once had a lovely name: Nyfikeliden, or simply Nyfiken and Nyfika – ‘nyfiken’ meaning curious. ‘Liden’ means a slope, and the name probably comes from a house called Nyfika on a map from 1790. Ånäsvägen itself was named in 1883 after the Ånäs country estate and is just over a kilometre long.
Den gamla Spånga socken var stor. Fram t: The old Spånga parish was big. Until 1949 it included Hässelby Palace, the estates of Akalla, Bromsten, Rinkeby and Tensta, and the parish church, Spånga kyrka. In 1948 about 21,000 people lived here, before the parish was dissolved and divided between Stockholm, Sollentuna and Sundbyberg.
Den gamla elverksbyggnaden intill har ha: The old power station building next door has had a colourful life. It was built in 1893 to supply electricity to Djursholmsbanan, the Djursholm railway, and later became a film studio for, among others, Film AB Imago and Svensk TV-produktion. Today it is used by Marina läroverket, a school with a marine theme which, among other things, has a programme called Archipelago Captain, even though no such title exists.
Den gamla gården Gåshaga gav namn åt hel: The old Gåshaga farm gave its name to the whole district, but the last of the farm's buildings was demolished in 1971. The shore at the very tip of southern Lidingö, facing the Hustegafjärden and Höggarnsfjärden bays, was long reserved for industry and boatyards with quays for larger ships. When the companies disappeared, the area was built up instead with apartment blocks, terraced houses and villas.
Den gröna Tuvanparken har en dramatisk h: The green Tuvanparken park has a dramatic history. In 1892 Tuvans hem, a home for people with nervous disorders, was built here, later called Solna sjukhem. In a fire in 1940 three patients died and the home was closed, but the building was later used for things like housing soldiers before it was demolished in 1960 and became a park. Nearby stands Alby Church, a listed church that was taken out of use in 2013.
Den här delen av Hökarängen kallas inoff: This part of Hökarängen is unofficially called Kryddhyllan, the Spice Rack, and the street names explain why. At Saltvägen 14 the troubadour Cornelis Vreeswijk once lived. Right next to it is Skönstaholm, terraced and linked houses from 1949 to 1952 designed by Nils Sterner and Erik F. Dahl, and nearby was the croft Lugnet, which stood here from 1771 to 1962.
Den jättelika postterminalen räknades so: The gigantic postal terminal was counted as one of Sweden's largest single buildings, and mail was sorted here from 1983. After the operation closed, others moved in, and in 2021 SL, Stockholm's public transport authority, opened the largest bus depot in the Nordic countries in parts of the building. On the grounds of Tomtebodaskolan, two fragments of a Viking Age runestone were found. One was found in 1903 but probably disappeared before 1911.
Den kupolformade byggnaden är Volvohalle: The dome-shaped building is Volvohallen, an exhibition hall that Volvo Cars put up in 1975 to designs by Lund & Valentin architects. Volvo's Torslandaverken factory began to be built in the district of Sörred, a village name recorded as early as 1388 in the form Surfua rudi. Sörred belonged to Björlanda parish until it was incorporated into Gothenburg in 1967.
Den lilla bäcken Flabäck har varit en ri: The little Flabäck stream has been a national border! It separates Kållered from Lindome, and thus the province of Västergötland from Halland, and when Halland belonged to Denmark, right up until the Peace of Brömsebro in 1645, the border with Sweden ran right here. The name comes from Flaksjö, and in the 17th century it was written, among other ways, as Flaksjöbäcken.
Den lilla kyrkan i närheten heter Älvsbo: The little church nearby is called Älvsborgs kyrka but used to be Hagens kapell, Hagen Chapel. Underground a little further away, traffic roars through the Gnistängstunneln tunnel, part of the Västerleden ring road. It is 712 metres long and carries about 55,000 vehicles a day. Originally the tunnel was a single tube, but the exhaust fumes became such a problem that in 1996 a concrete wall was built dividing it in two.
Den lilla orten Fiskarhagen ligger klämd: The little village of Fiskarhagen is squeezed between two lakes, Aspen and Bornsjön, south-west of Norsborg. The houses line both sides of Sankt Botvids väg, which is part of the historic Göta landsväg highway – so travellers passed through here long before the buses came. A little way off, the Männö udd peninsula juts out into Bornsjön, divided between Botkyrka and Salem and part of the Bornsjön nature reserve.
Den lilla villagatan Anundsvägen, alldel: The little villa street Anundsvägen, right next to us, has a royal claim to fame: Britain's Queen Elizabeth II paid a visit here in the 1950s. Much older is Björklunds hage a little further away, a burial ground from the early and late Iron Age and the second largest in Bromma. It was the burial site of Viking Age Ängby, and the graves are clearly visible south of Bällstavägen.
Den låga raden av hus längs vägen kallas: The low row of houses along the road is called Långa raden, the Long Row, and was laid out in the 1780s on the initiative of Gustav III. The Cavaliers' House was home to the court's gentlemen, the Pharmacy House held the palace pharmacy, and in the Chancellery House from 1787 the county governor, the king's favourite Adolf Fredrik Munck, held sway. Since 1991 it has all been part of the Drottningholm World Heritage Site.
Den röda trävillan Villa Bellona från 19: The red wooden Villa Bellona from 1907 is the only one left of the seven professors' villas at Experimentalfältet. The others were demolished when Södra huset was built, and Bellona was actually meant to be demolished too before the decision was changed. The architect Ralph Erskine left his mark on the campus with, among other things, the student union building Allhuset, which won the Kasper Salin Prize, and the lecture hall Aula Magna, where Nobel lectures have also been held.
Den stora arenan här är Scandinavium, in: The big arena here is Scandinavium, opened in 1971. Ice hockey has been played here, concerts held and world championships staged. Right next to it is Nya Ullevi.
Den stora byggnaden här är Handelshögsko: The large building here is the School of Business, Economics and Law at the University of Gothenburg. The surrounding blocks are Vasastaden, one of the city's best-preserved turn-of-the-century neighbourhoods.
Den stora halvcirkelformade byggnaden ru: The big semicircular building around Fatbursparken is called Bofills båge, Bofill's Arch, after the Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill. It was completed in 1992. Where the park is today there used to be Fatburssjön, a lake that was filled in during the 1800s when the railway came.
Den stora kvarnen vid farleden byggdes 1: The large mill by the shipping lane was built in 1888–1890 by Holmberg & Möllers Qvarn AB, and the location by the shipping lane was part of the point. The mill kept grinding until the late 1980s, when the owner, Kungsörnen, closed it down. The core building has been preserved and now houses flats and a hotel. Up on Bageriberget there's a viewpoint.
Den vackra byggnaden här är Riddarhuset: The beautiful building here is Riddarhuset, the House of Nobility, from the 1600s, where the nobility used to gather. Right next to it is Riddarholmen with Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, where Swedish kings have been buried for several hundred years.
Den vita byggnaden intill är Bergslagsba: The white building next door is the old station building of the Bergslagsbanan railway, popularly known as Vita huset, the White House, since 1923, designed by the brothers Axel and Hjalmar Kumlien and opened in 1881. Today it is part of Regionens hus, the headquarters of Region Västra Götaland. The Nils Ericson bus terminal won the Kasper Salin Prize in 1996, and at Hotel G on top of the central station you can take a sauna with a view over the railway tracks.
