Den vita kupolen är Avicii Arena, som ti: The white dome is Avicii Arena, which used to be called the Globe. It opened in 1989 and is the world's largest spherical building. On the outside, you can ride the SkyView glass gondolas up to the top.
Det entomologiska kvinnorovet: The Entomological Rape of Women, the sculpture
Det finns en vägkrog i Aspnässkolans his: There's a roadside tavern in Aspnäs School's history. When Järfälla parish's first school of its own opened in 1846, a manor house at the Aspnäs crossroads was bought, which had previously been a tavern. That house was demolished in 1959, but the school still has buildings from 1901 and 1945. And the old schoolhouse? It now serves as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
Det gamla huset på Hornsgatan 82 kallas: The old house at Hornsgatan 82 is called Bysis. It was Stockholm's jail for debtors from 1782 to 1872. Next door was the Rixi cinema, which became a music studio in 1971. Parts of ABBA's Ring Ring and Carola's debut album Främling were recorded there. Today it's called the Ingrid studio, and artists such as Lykke Li and Peter Bjorn and John have recorded here.
Det gamla torpet Islinge gård har gett n: The old croft of Islinge gård has given its name to the whole district of Islinge in north-western Lidingö. By Lilla Värtan, south of Islingeviken bay, stands Torsvik lighthouse, also known as the Islinge lighthouse, which was built in 1950 and switched off in 1980 but still serves as the reference point for the finish line in the Lidingö Runt sailing race. The area is also home to the art school Nyckelviksskolan, offering programmes in art, crafts, architecture and design.
Det gamla torpet Tussmötet har gett namn: The old croft Tussmötet has given its name to Tussmötevägen, a city block and Tussmöteparken park. Even the local cinema was called Tusse-Bio when it opened in March 1938 on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen. Later it changed its name to Corso, and in December 1969 it closed for good.
Det gula tornet byggde AGA 1943 för att: AGA built the yellow tower in 1943 to test and manufacture things like periscopes for Swedish submarines. Inside the rock behind it, production continued until 1987. The area is today called Dalénum after the inventor Gustaf Dalén, who worked here from 1912 until his death in 1937. The ice rink next door became known to a wide audience through the TV series HCZ.
Det gula tornet en bit härifrån har ett: The yellow tower a little way from here has an exciting past. AGA's optics tower was built in 1943, and in the rock factory behind it AGA tested and manufactured, among other things, periscopes for Swedish submarines. Production continued in various forms until 1987, and the tower was renovated in 2022.
Det går inte att missa Karlatornet: med: You can't miss Karlatornet: at 246 metres and 73 storeys, it's the tallest building in Sweden and the Nordic countries, completed on the outside in 2024. Around the tower, Karlastaden is taking shape with about 2,000 homes. The area has a long industrial history, because the shipbuilding and industrial group Götaverken was based on Lundbyvassen from 1841. The last part of the shipyard closed in 2015.
Det här var en gång gurkland. Axel Svens: This was once cucumber country. Axel Svensson's market garden operated from 1907 until the 1970s, specialising in growing cucumbers. Where the greenhouses stood is today the garden suburb of Hildedal. Svensson's two-storey villa from 1919 still stands at Växthusvägen 60, a reminder of the time when market gardens were common here.
Det här är ett hörn fullt av unika saker: This is a corner full of one-of-a-kind things. Sätra indoor athletics hall from 1998 is the only hall in the municipality adapted for youth athletics competitions, Sätra pistol shooting range is the only one of its kind in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs, and Pingstkyrkan Bredäng is the only Pentecostal church in Stockholm's south-western suburbs. A little further away is the Church of Saint Maroun, which used to be called Sätra Church.
Det höga betongtornet i närheten hör til: The tall concrete tower nearby belongs to Kista fire station from 1980. It is a training tower for the firefighters and a well-known local landmark. At Kista farm there is also Kistastenen, a runestone that shows Järvafältet was inhabited long before Kista became an IT city.
Det höga huset på berget är Fyrtornet Da: The tall building on the hill is Fyrtornet Dalénum, the Lighthouse Tower, designed by Wingårdh and completed in 2020. At 68 metres above sea level, it is Lidingö's highest building. Down by the shore stands the Larsberg bridge cottage from around 1803. It was built for the bridge that, that same year, linked Larsberg with Kaknäs on the Stockholm side. The whole area used to be the factories of AGA, where Gustaf Dalén worked.
Det höga huset som syns på långt håll he: The tall building you can see from far away is called Tyresö View. It's 82 metres high with 23 storeys, and in 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Under the roof of the glazed shopping centre are some 70 shops, the municipal hall and a library with its own exhibition hall.
Det lugna radhusområdet Kälvesta bär på: The quiet terraced-house area of Kälvesta holds a sad chapter in Swedish aviation history. On 15 January 1977 a Skyline plane, flying for Linjeflyg as Flight 618, crashed into the residential area. All 22 people on board were killed, and the event is now known as the Kälvesta air disaster.
Det lustiga namnet Pungpinan kommer från: The funny name Pungpinan comes from a tavern that stood here from the 17th century until the 19th century. The Pungpinan croft, built in 1763 under the Skarpnäck estate, was named after the tavern and in 1933 became a meeting place for young people in the then newly built cottage area. Later the youth organisation Unga Örnar also met here, and since 2000 the croft has been privately owned.
Det långa, slingrande skivhuset Ormen Lå: The long, winding slab block Ormen Långe, a short walk away, together with six tower blocks on Botkyrkavägen, had the honour of being the first modern suburban development in these parts. Right next to it is Fittjanäset, a peninsula between Lake Mälaren and Lake Albysjön. Fittja bridge crosses the narrow strait to Fittja, and right up until the end of the 1950s the main traffic heading south from Stockholm rolled across exactly there.
Det stora kontorshuset alldeles i närhet: The big office building close by is called Bankhus 90, now Ursvik Entré, and it was built from 1989 to 1992 for Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken after an architecture competition. A short distance away stands something much older: the Stora Stampan windmill, probably one of the oldest preserved windmills in Greater Stockholm.
Det tornprydda huset vid farleden kallas: The house with the tower by the shipping lane is called the Smugglers' Villa, Smugglarvillan. The Bremer Villa was built in 1912 and bears witness to fortunes made from herring fishing around the turn of the century and from liquor smuggling in the 1920s. On the island's highest point, 31 metres above sea level, stands the sea mark Valen, the Whale. Beneath it, a compass rose is carved into the rock, with the year 1684.
Det var bolaget Lidingö villastad, under: It was the company Lidingö villastad, under Hjalmar Arwin, that from 1906 transformed Lidingö from farmland and a summer haunt for well-off Stockholmers into a modern suburb. The company's very first acquisition and first office was Vattängen farm on Stockholmsvägen. In the middle of the villa town you will also find Centralpalatset from 1912 to 1913 and Vasaborgen, which was planned as early as 1913 but not built until 1923.
Det är inte varje dag man ser en soffgru: It's not every day you see a sofa suite on a roof. But you do here: the furniture store that Skinngruppen founded in 1975 has become a landmark thanks to the giant sofa on top. Krokslätt used to be an industrial area with the Krokslätt factories, and the first owner-built family homes in the Gothenburg area were built here.
Dieselverkstaden hette ursprungligen Sam: Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, was originally called the Assembly Hall, and Atlas Diesel built diesel engines here right up until 1951. Since 2002 the old industrial hall has been filled with culture instead: a culture house, a library, a climbing centre and a cinema with five screens. And beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter there is a test mine where rock drills and mining machines are tested.
Djupt inne i berget under bostadsområdet: Deep inside the rock beneath the Eriksberg residential area, the red line's metro trains sleep: Norsborg depot lies 18 to 37 metres down in Aspberget and the Eriksbergsåsen ridge and connects to the metro at Norsborg. Norsborg station itself, a couple of minutes from here, is the westernmost in the entire metro network and opened in 1975.
Djupt inne i ett bergrum i Edsberg finns: Deep inside a rock cavern in Edsberg is Elefanten, the Elephant, a nuclear-bomb-proof command centre built in 1972–1977 for 200 people. It was meant to protect the leadership of Stockholm and Sollentuna municipalities if war came. After standing unused for 19 years, it was bought in 2017 by the Swedish Armed Forces, which modernised it and brought it back into use. Above ground things are more peaceful, with Edsberg church, a red wooden church.
Djupt under campus forskade man en gång: Deep beneath the campus, research was once done in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the laboratory has been the Accelerator art gallery, inaugurated by the artist Tino Sehgal. The laboratory bears the name of Manne Siegbahn, who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1924. Ralph Erskine designed the Law Building as a semicircle around an old oak, and the same idea of saving the oaks can be found at Aula Magna.
Djupt under fötterna, 27 till 36 meter n: Deep beneath your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, is the metro station, which opened in 1975. Above it awaits one of the Stockholm region's largest shopping centres, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen is Eric Grate's Park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. His bronze sculptures Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God, stand there.
Djursholm är villornas rike, och i närhe: Djursholm is the realm of villas, and nearby stands Villa Snellman, one of Gunnar Asplund's early works. Strandvägen in Djursholm, along Lilla and Stora Värtan, is often counted among Sweden's most exclusive residential areas. The Djursholmsbanan railway used to run past, and on the narrow platform at the Bragevägen stop there was for a long time a sweet and newspaper kiosk.
Djursholms slott ägdes av ätten Banér i: Djursholm Castle was owned by the Banér family for more than 300 years, from 1508 to 1813, and contains parts from the late Middle Ages. Today it's the municipal hall, where you can also rent the banqueting rooms for weddings. On the hill next to it stands the water tower from 1890, built beside a small Dutch-style windmill that was demolished shortly afterwards. And Djursholm's co-educational school, founded in 1891, was right nearby.
Domkyrkan, ofta öppen dagtid: Gothenburg Cathedral, often open during the day
Donsö är en levande skärgårdsö med Donsö: Donsö is a lively archipelago island with Donsö church and more than 1,500 permanent residents. A little to the south lies tiny Kårholmen, with a wonderful story: on 7 May 1933, twenty people hired a motorboat, formed the association Workers to the Sea, and were allowed to take possession of the island. The members were poor workers, and today the island is almost completely covered with just over 80 summer cottages.
Drottningtorget ligger mitt framför Cent: Drottningtorget lies right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Large parts of the biggest tram network in the Nordic countries start from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and the city chose to keep its trams when many other Swedish cities got rid of theirs.
Du är nu i Majorna, strax väster om Mast: You are now in Majorna, just west of Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914, one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square are the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and the Sailors' Tower, Sjömanstornet, with the statue of the sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Du är nu i Masthugget, där fartygens mas: You are now in Masthugget, where ships' masts were once hewn. Up on the hill stands Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church from 1914, one of the city's best-known landmarks. By the square are the Maritime Museum and Aquarium and the Sailors' Tower, Sjömanstornet, with the statue of the sailor's wife gazing out over the river for ships that never came home.
Duggregnet 5 vid Björkhagsplan ritades a: Duggregnet 5 at Björkhagsplan was designed by the architect Georg Varhelyi, and anyone who knows Le Corbusier's famous Unité d'Habitation in Marseille will see the family resemblance at once. The building was Stockholm's tallest residential building when it went up in 1957 and is today marked blue, the City Museum's highest class. In the metro station there are artworks by Lenka Jonesson, unveiled in 1991.
Duvnäs nämns i skrift redan 1436, men vi: Duvnäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436, but the villas only came when the Saltsjöbanan railway station opened in 1893. At Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, the Manor Villa, built in 1910 to 1911 as a show home to attract buyers to the new villa plots, and in the park is Ringparksstugan, a cottage where the neighbours celebrate annual festivities. A little further away, Kvarngården, the miller's house from the mid-1700s, recalls the old watermill at Duvnäsviken bay.
Där Alviks gamla industriområde en gång: Where Alvik's old industrial area once lay by Lake Mälaren, there are now mostly offices and a few restaurants. In Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, an event venue nearby, the competition show Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail disappears into the rock through the roughly 250-metre-long Alvik tunnel and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the Alvik bridge, which is 400 metres long and was completed in 2000.
Där Husby står i dag övade militären änd: Where Husby stands today, the military trained right up to 1965, since Järvafältet was a military training ground. The district was created in 1971 and was first called Husby gård. Today it has Husbybadet, a swimming centre with an adventure pool, a 25-metre pool and a diving tower with 1- and 3-metre platforms.
Där Obs! Stormarknad slog upp portarna 1: Where Obs! Stormarknad, a hypermarket, opened its doors in 1963, there was once Haga gård, an outlying farm of Vårby gård that was demolished in the early 20th century. The store building still stands, but Obs! disappeared in 1998 and furniture shops moved in. Right next door is Fittjanäset, and over the narrow strait to Fittja ran Fittja bro, the Fittja bridge – the main road south from Stockholm until the end of the 1950s.
Där Skärholmens centrum ligger i dag fan: Where Skärholmen centrum stands today there was once Smista gård, a farm dating back at least to the 800s, and people lived nearby as early as the 200s, in the Roman Iron Age. In the 1700s and 1800s Smista was an outlying farm of Vårby gård. Today you'll find here, among other things, the Red Cross folk high school, where some courses even travel abroad, and the Skärisbiografen cinema, which opened in 2017.
Där Stockholmsmässan står i dag låg en g: Where Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, stands today, there was once a lake. Brännkyrkasjön, also called Kyrksjön, lay south of Brännkyrka church and was drained in stages, from the 1870s right up to the 1950s. Since 1971 the exhibition buildings and car parks have stood on the western side of the former lake, while the eastern side is still largely undeveloped.
Där Ulriksdals Golfklubb ligger i dag gi: Where Ulriksdal Golf Club is today, things used to move really fast: the area was once the site of Ulriksdal racecourse. The commuter train station itself is 7.1 kilometres from Stockholm Central on the branch towards Märsta, and got its current design in 1990, with a ticket hall on the platform and an entrance from a pedestrian tunnel.
Där bostadsområdet Minneberg ligger låg: Where the Minneberg housing area stands today was once the Stockholm Bonemeal Factory, which made glue, bone oil, chicken feed and even the washing powder Pärlglans. The foul-smelling business moved in 1968, and Minneberg was built in the 1980s. Its neighbour is Tranebergs gård, a farm dating back to a ferryman's croft in the 1670s. The croft was named Traneberg after its owner, Bengt Trana.
Där bostadsområdet Rissne ligger i dag h: Where the Rissne housing area stands today, the military was once based. The Svea Artillery Regiment had its barracks here until 1963, and after that the Ordnance Administration School was in the area until 1977. The apartment buildings weren't built until 1982 to 1988. Fittingly, the square was called Dragonplan, Dragoon Square, before it was renamed Rissne torg.
Where the sun shines on Hisingen, electricity is harvested. The solar park Nya Solevi, in Säve north-west of Gothenburg, is planned to produce about 5.5 gigawatt hours a year. Construction was record-fast, from the first sod being turned in September 2018 to the opening in December the same year. During planning the facility was called Säve Solcellspark.
Där villorna står i dag låg förr åkrar s: Where the villas stand today there were once fields belonging to Viksjö gård, a farm dating back to prehistoric times. The farm was sold in 1921 to Viksjö AB, which farmed here, but in 1963 a building consortium began developing the area. The result was villas and terraced houses from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s, with pockets of nature in between.
Edsbacka krog vid Edsviken blev den förs: Edsbacka krog by Edsviken bay became the first restaurant in Sweden with two Michelin stars, under the restaurateur Christer Lingström. The stars disappeared when it changed hands in 2010, but since spring 2021 the restaurant is once again called Edsbacka krog. North of the restaurant, in the 17th century, lay a toppled runestone, and its base now stands just south of the avenue leading to Edsberg Palace.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och fick: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and got a facelift around 2004, including a new multi-storey car park. Here you'll find a library, a pharmacy, an Ica supermarket and two grills, Oscar and Ló Mero Kök och Bar. Right next door stands Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church that belongs to Sollentuna parish. The district also includes Edsberg Castle, Rudbecksskolan school and the Edsbacka krog restaurant.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och har b: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and has a library, shops and a couple of grill bars. Right next to it stands Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church. And somewhere in the rock a little way off lies Elefanten, the Elephant, a nuclear-bomb-proof command centre built in the 1970s and today back in use by the Swedish Armed Forces.
Edsbergs slott stod färdigt 1760 vid Eds: Edsberg Palace was completed in 1760 on the northern shore of Edsviken bay, built on the initiative of Thure Gustaf Rudbeck, and the Rudbeck family owned it for almost 200 years. Today part of the Royal College of Music's chamber music programme is based here, and the palace has a wedding room. A stone's throw away is Edsbacka krog, Sweden's first restaurant with two Michelin stars.
Edsängens gravfält, ett par hundra meter: The Edsängen burial ground, a couple of hundred metres away, has around 125 Viking Age burial mounds and is one of Sollentuna's largest burial grounds. Not far from there is something completely different: Elefanten, the Elephant, a nuclear-bomb-proof command centre blasted into the rock. Closest of all is Rudbecksskolan, one of Sweden's largest upper secondary schools, with around 2,400 students and a national athletics programme.
Efter badet: The sculpture Efter badet, After the Swim
Ekebyhovskyrkan, en bit härifrån, är mer: Ekebyhovskyrkan, Ekebyhov Church, a little way from here, is more than a church: it is part of a church centre with a parish office for all the parishes in the Ekerö pastorate, and it even has a full-time preschool. A little further away is the Tappström strait, about one and a half kilometres long and only just over three metres deep, which marks the border between the islands of Lovön and Ekerön.
Ekensberg har fått sitt namn efter värds: Ekensberg takes its name from the Ekensberg inn, built in the early 18th century and still standing at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, Ekensberg was the name of most of what is now called Gröndal. The headland lies between Mörtviken bay and the Essingesundet strait.
Ekerö centrum, en bit härifrån vid Tapps: Ekerö centrum, a little way from here at Tappström, is recognised by its navigation marker, more than twenty metres tall. The area was designed by Ralph Erskine, who lived on Lovön himself, and his idea was to create a town on Lake Mälaren. Erskine was most pleased with this particular area and felt that it works as a whole community. From Tappström, the commuter boat 89 also runs all the way to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay, in Stockholm.
Ekerö är främst en bostadsort, och den s: Ekerö is mainly a place to live, and commuters usually travel into Stockholm. Until 1990, the village of Träkvista, a little way from here, was the centre of the municipality. That year Ekerö centrum opened, designed by the architect Ralph Erskine, and took over that role. At Träkvista torg, though, there is still a grocery shop, a pizzeria and a restaurant.
Ekerö, inte att förväxla med åländska Ec: Ekerö, not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland, is on Ekerön island in eastern Lake Mälaren and is the main town of Ekerö municipality. Ekerö centrum was designed by the well-known architect Ralph Erskine and opened in 1990. Before that, Träkvista was the town's centre. The island itself is in eastern Lake Mälaren, and the largest employer is the municipality.

Ekerö, not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland, is the main town of Ekerö municipality and mainly a residential town, where most people commute into Stockholm. Ekerö centrum at Tappström was designed by Ralph Erskine, and its hallmark is a dot more than twenty metres tall, like a navigation marker among the shops. In the past it was Träkvista that was the centre of the town.
Eklanda är en ung stadsdel med gamla röt: Eklanda is a young district with old roots. For a long time there was only a small core of older buildings here, but from 1993 houses began to spring up, and now there are about 700. The Änggårdsbergen nature reserve is next door, which makes the area a playground for the many families with children who live here.
Eklanda är stadsdelen där barnfamiljerna: Eklanda is the district where families with children have taken over. Since building got under way in 1993, about 700 houses have sprung up with around 3,100 residents, next to the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. A little way from here, in Åby, is Åbytravet, Sweden's second largest trotting track.
Elektraparken har fått sitt namn efter E: Elektraparken is named after Elektraverken, which from 1917 made electrical measuring instruments nearby, and between 1915 and 1944 the site was home to Södra folkparken, a people's park. In 1939 the master builder Olle Engkvist had a very lavish villa built for himself and his wife Signhild on Västberga allé, but Villa Engkvist was demolished as early as 1967–68 to make way for an industrial building.
En biograf blev början på en hel butiksk: A cinema became the start of a whole chain of shops. Saga on Sofiagatan showed films from 1942 to 1964, and when Bengt Johansson bought the closed cinema he opened a grocery shop: Saga hemköp, the first of the Sagabutikerna. Right next door was Härlanda prison, in operation from 1907 to 1997. The walls still stand as a listed building, and since 2011 the area has been called Härlanda park.
En bit bort breder Ryssbergen ut sig, en: A little way off stretch the Ryssbergen hills, about 30 hectares of rocky pine forest reaching 60 metres above sea level. Below, in Ryssviken, is Marinstaden, a residential area where people live on the water in an old harbour facility. In the other direction lies the villa area Birka, one of Nacka's oldest, where the first houses were built in the 1880s for industrial workers.
En bit bort går Kongahällavägen, Hisinge: A little way off runs Kongahällavägen, Hisingen's oldest country road, about 23 kilometres long from Torslanda to Eriksdal south of Kungälv fortress. Until 1970 it was called Kungälvsvägen. The new name is the old spelling of the royal estate Kungahälla, which lay roughly at Ragnhildsholmen by the Nordre älv river.
En bit bort ligger Angereds Centrum, knu: A little way off is Angereds Centrum, the hub with around sixty shops and restaurants and the terminus of three tram lines. The decision to build the centre was taken by a unanimous municipal executive board in 1975. On Angereds torg stands the culture house Blå Stället, with a library, cinema, theatre and restaurant, and by the terminal is Angered Local Hospital, opened in 2015.
En bit bort ligger Glose, sydväst om Kär: A little way off is Glose, south-west of Kärna in Kungälv municipality. The shore meadows by the Ryskärsfjorden inlet are so rich in birds and plants that Swedish Radio has broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from there. The area is both a nature reserve and a Natura 2000 site, and the county administrative board singles it out as one of the most valuable in the county.
En bit bort ligger Kästadalsparken, en l: A little further away is Kästadalsparken, a playground in the Kästa villa area where everything is inspired by the world of fairy tales. Flemingsberg Church was built in 1975–1976 to designs by Gunnar Cedervall and was consecrated by Bishop Ingmar Ström in August 1976. Nearby also stood Hagstaeken, the Hagsta oak, Huddinge's largest oak protected as a natural monument, until it was felled in December 2025.
En bit bort ligger Preemraff Göteborg, e: A little way off is Preemraff Göteborg, a refinery that can process about six million tonnes of crude oil a year. The oil comes mostly from the North Sea and is stored in large rock caverns. At the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen, even ULCC-class ships have docked, the world's largest tankers, 333 metres long and 60 metres wide.
En bit bort ligger pingstkyrkan Aspnäsky: A little further away is the Pentecostal church Aspnäskyrkan, with the vision Discover faith, share hope, grow deeper in love. In the same area is Aspnäs school, Järfälla parish's first school of its own, from 1846. It started in an old roadside inn, and the first school building now serves as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
En bit bort svävar Angeredsbron, cirka 5: A little further away, Angeredsbron bridge soars, about 50 metres high and 930 metres long, over the E6, Göta älv river, the E45 and the railway. Ships have 47 metres of clearance beneath it, and the spans between the pillars are about 130 metres long. The bridge continues into the Gårdsten tunnel, built in 1978 and 235 metres long, with three lanes and a footpath and cycle path.
En bit bort, på Göta älvs östra strand,: A little way off, on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, lies Agnesberg. Travellers have stopped there for several hundred years, as it was a coaching inn stop long before the railway station came in 1880. After that, industries moved in, including a paint manufacturer and a milling company. On the other side of the river is Kärra, which in postal addresses is called Hisings Kärra.
En bit härifrån breder Gunnestorps mosse: A little way from here spreads Gunnestorps mosse, a bog with plants such as bulrushes, water lilies, cranberries and sundews. East of the bog, down towards Tuvevägen, there is a strip of meadows and deciduous woodland. And on the northern edge of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården playground.
En bit härifrån breder Kvibergs kyrkogår: A little way from here spreads Kviberg cemetery, which at 130 hectares is Sweden's largest cemetery and the second largest by area in northern Europe. It has over 24,000 graves, and there's capacity for 30,000 coffins and 50,000 urns. Gamlestadsvägen, which passes very close, has had its name since 1883.
En bit härifrån breder Trångsundsskogens: A little way from here, the Trångsundsskogen nature reserve stretches along the western shore of Lake Drevviken, from the bathing spot at Mörtviken to just north of Trångsund manor. The reserve was formed in 2006 and covers 53 hectares, ten of them water. The manor itself and its immediate grounds are not included, though. Mörtviks gård is also at Mörtviken.
En bit härifrån breder naturreservatet V: A little way from here stretches the Välen nature reserve, a wetland area at the far end of Askimsviken bay. Since 1992, shaggy Highland cattle have been grazing the shore meadows, and the reserve contains two ancient remains from the Bronze Age. In the other direction is Opaltorget, the terminus of the Tynnered tram line.
En bit härifrån breder villaområdet Nora: A little way from here stretches the villa area of Nora, about ten kilometres north of Stockholm. It used to be farmland, but in 1926 the lands of Nora gård began to be divided into villa plots. In the same area is Lake Nora träsk, whose water belongs to the Åkerström-Norrström coastal catchment.
En bit härifrån byggs tunnelbanestatione: A little way from here, the metro station Barkarbystaden is being built, in the middle of the urban development project of the same name. In the other direction is Järfälla Church, where in 1728 Olof Celsius wrote about a runestone outside the porch door. He called it lost and worn, and sure enough it has been missing ever since. Further away is Kyrkbyn, which used to be called Järfälla gård.
En bit härifrån börjar Eklanda, en stads: A little way from here begins Eklanda, a district in western Mölndal bordering the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. Apart from a small core of older buildings, the area wasn't developed until 1993, and today around 3,100 people live here, many of them families with children. The plan is for Eklanda to grow together with Fässberg village through new houses on the farmland to the east.
En bit härifrån börjar Görvälns naturres: A little way from here begins the Görväln nature reserve, which stretches almost eight kilometres along the undeveloped shore of Lake Mälaren, from Hässelby to Kallhäll. There you'll find the croft Baset, privately owned since 2021. But under an easement, the path down to the swimming spot must be kept open to the public, so a dip in Mälaren is still free for all.
En bit härifrån börjar Pixbo, ett bostad: A little way from here begins Pixbo, a residential area on the southern side of Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo is very hilly, because it's built on and around a height called Björnåsen. The area is in Härryda municipality, apart from a small number of properties that belong to Mölndal, and has its own postal town.
En bit härifrån börjar Rågsveds friområd: A little way from here begins the Rågsved open space, or Kräppladalen, just over 100 hectares of nature with at times dramatic terrain of hills, valleys and steep slopes. In the middle of it is the Snösätra storage area, which since 2014 has become a centre for graffiti and street art; facades and walls have been painted with the property owners' permission. Nature and spray cans, side by side.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet J: A little way from here begins the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve, which follows the Säveån river valley from the bridge in Kåhög to Lake Aspen. Mixed broadleaf forest with a rich variety of fungi grows here, including the red-listed smoky finger fungus. Look out for grey wagtails, kingfishers and dippers, birds that thrive by flowing water.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet Ä: A little way from here begins the Älta mosse–Strålsjön nature reserve, created in 1995 and covering 52 hectares. Together with the Strålsjön–Erstavik reserve, it forms a large recreation area with little Lake Strålsjön in the middle. The lake's water is dark because it flows in from the humus-rich Älta mosse bog, and the lake is home to pike, perch and roach.
En bit härifrån finns ett unikt minne fr: A little way from here there is a unique memento of the Second World War. Käppalaställningen is an anti-aircraft position with several foxholes and three gun emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a protected monument to Stockholm's air defence, something that exists nowhere else in Sweden.
En bit härifrån gick förr den numera ned: A little way from here ran the now closed Djursholm railway, and on Valevägen was the Bragevägen stop from 1924, with a sweet and newspaper kiosk on its narrow platform. It closed in 1976. Until the 1920s the train ran across open fields here. Not far away, at Hildingavägen 26, stands the Laurin Villa, designed in 1910 by the architect Karl Güettler.
En bit härifrån går Bullegummans gata, m: A little way from here runs Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, which has a sweet story. In the 1930s a Mrs Liljegren lived here who baked such good buns that the children on their way to Påvelundsskolan couldn't resist them. She cut a hatch in the wall of her house and sold buns through it, and became known locally as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. The house still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there as late as 2011.
En bit härifrån går Marieholmsbron, en b: A little way from here runs Marieholmsbron, a bridge for rail, pedestrian and cycle traffic from Gamlestaden over the Säveån and Göta älv rivers to Tingstad on Hisingen. The section over the Göta älv is a swing bridge that can turn to let boats through. The bridge is part of the Bohusbanan railway and links Gothenburg's harbour railway with the rest of the rail network.
En bit härifrån gömmer sig något unikt:: A little way from here hides something unique: the Hammarkullen stop, the only fully underground tram stop in Sweden. It lies 25 metres below ground and was built with Stockholm's metro stations as its model, since in the 1970s there were plans for a metro to Angered. The platforms are built for 120-metre trains but today only 70 metres of them are used.
En bit härifrån höll Sollentunamässan ti: A little way from here, Sollentunamässan, the Sollentuna exhibition centre, operated from 1973. With just over 17,000 square metres of exhibition space, it was Sweden's third largest trade fair venue, until it closed in 2008 and Kistamässan took over. Demolition began on 24 May 2017, and homes are now being built where the exhibition halls stood.
En bit härifrån korsar Gamlestadsbron Sä: A little way from here, Gamlestadsbron, the Gamlestaden bridge, crosses the Säveån river, and there has been a bridge here for more than 500 years. When Nya Lödöse was founded in 1473, traffic was busy, because the main road to Norway passed by. In the summer of 1723, the city architect Johan Eberhard Carlberg was allowed to build a completely new wooden bridge, but as early as January 1724 it was destroyed by a strong flood and timber.
En bit härifrån ligger Akalla, en stadsd: A little way from here lies Akalla, a district on Järvafältet built between 1972 and 1977, at the same time as its neighbours Husby and Kista. Through the district runs Sibeliusgången, a 900-metre walkway named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius. Along it bubble fountains by the artist Bertil Johnson, put up in 1976, including the Akalla fountain in a little square.
En bit härifrån ligger Angereds sporthal: A little way from here is the Angered sports hall by Angered Centrum, with room for 400 people. The hall is home ground for the handball club GIK Wasaiterna, but also for the roller derby team Dock City Rollers, whose players race around the track on roller skates. Next door are Angered Arena and the Angeredsvallen sports ground.
En bit härifrån ligger Arendalsbanan, sp: A little way from here is Arendalsbanan, the speedway arena that was the home track of Kaparna. The attendance record, 5,940 spectators, was set in September 2002 at a match between Kaparna and Rospiggarna. The track record, a time of 60.1, was set by none other than Tony Rickardsson, then riding for Masarna, in September 2004.
En bit härifrån ligger Arken kombitermin: A little way from here is the Arken combi terminal, where semi-trailers are lifted between ships and rail. It was built because the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and the Central Station had to move when the Västlänken rail tunnel was to be built. Construction began in 2018 and it opened in 2019. Arendal itself used to have a large shipyard, Arendalsvarvet, between 1963 and 1989.
En bit härifrån ligger Askims norra kyrk: A little way from here is Askim's northern churchyard, and just north of it is an Iron Age burial ground with some eighty burial mounds. In the early Middle Ages the parish church was built on the site, but it burned down in 1876. A memorial stone in the churchyard recalls the old church.
En bit härifrån ligger Bandhagens tunnel: A little way from here is Bandhagen metro station, which opened on 22 November 1954 and was designed by Magnus Ahlgren. From there it's six and a half kilometres to Slussen. By Bandhagen's centre also rises the Murbruket block, an eleven-storey slab block from 1955 that the Stockholm City Museum has green-listed.
En bit härifrån ligger Bastusjön, en lit: A little way from here is Bastusjön, a small lake in Skuru that's good for swimming. It's almost six metres deep, and perch, roach and two kinds of freshwater mussel thrive there. A little further away is Solsunda, which until 1922 was called Skuru gård. In the 16th century King Gustav Vasa gave the estate to Danvik's Hospital, and since the early 20th century the main building has been a rest and treatment home.
En bit härifrån ligger Beckomberga, där: A little way from here is Beckomberga, where the psychiatric hospital Beckomberga sjukhus was from the 1930s until it closed in 1995. The hospital was built in 1930–1932, and in the mid-2000s the old hospital buildings began to be converted into homes. Bromma hospital in Beckomberga has been a care home since 2020.
En bit härifrån ligger Benareby, inklämt: A little way from here is Benareby, squeezed in between the lakes Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. The village was once known for making wooden barrels, mainly for the fish processing industry, and the coopering tradition has lived on right into our own time. Closest to the stop is the small lake Abborrtjärnen.
En bit härifrån ligger Benareby, mellan: A little way from here is Benareby, between the lakes Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. Benareby used to be known for its wooden barrels, which mainly went to the fish-processing industry, and the coopering tradition lives on to this day. There are also many old holiday cottages here that are now permanent homes.
En bit härifrån ligger Biskopsgårdens ky: A little way from here is Biskopsgården Church, consecrated in 1961 by Bishop Bo Giertz. At the consecration he himself burned in the cross that you can see on the church door facing Vårvädersgatan. At first only a small chapel was planned, but when the parish was formed it became the parish church. It was originally called Södra Biskopsgården Church, but changed its name when Norra Biskopsgården Church was deconsecrated in 2004.
En bit härifrån ligger Björlanda, den ga: A little way from here is Björlanda, the old church village of Björlanda parish on Hisingen. The place has had trouble making up its mind: first its own town, then part of Torslanda, then on its own again from 2018, and from 2023 it is counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area. The houses cluster around the church, and most were built in the 1990s.
En bit härifrån ligger Bäckebols gård, e: A little way from here is Bäckebols gård, a manor whose stone building was begun in 1764, and today a listed building. The manor comes with an odd curiosity: Friedländerska kyrkogården, a privately owned cemetery with just over twenty grave plots. It is Gothenburg's smallest cemetery.
En bit härifrån ligger Dammträsket, i fo: A little way from here is Dammträsket, popularly known as Dammkärr, a small lake recently converted into a stormwater facility. On its shore lies Mellanberg, an old croft and smallholding where the surroundings still bear witness to laundering and farming. A little further away is Kvarntorp, which has its roots in a watermill and appears on maps as early as 1638.
En bit härifrån ligger Danderyds gymnasi: A little way from here is Danderyds gymnasium, an upper secondary school that opened in 1982 and is one of the largest in Stockholm County, with 1,390 students in 2024. The area around it is called Rinkeby, but that's a farm and residential area in Danderyd, not to be confused with the district of the same name in northern Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Djupedal, med mån: A little way from here is Djupedal, with many stables and two hill forts above the village. Just a few kilometres north stood the Norwegian king Håkon the Old's castle on Ragnhildsholmen in the Nordre älv river. Closer at hand is Klareberg, where bus drivers take a break and riders and dog owners train.
En bit härifrån ligger Drottning Silvias: A little way from here is the Queen Silvia Children's Hospital, Sweden's largest children's hospital, with about 1,900 employees and around 45,000 patient visits a year. Since 1997 it has been based at the old Östra sjukhuset hospital. Children come here from the whole Gothenburg area, and for the most specialised care from all over the country.
En bit härifrån ligger Fredrikshamns ska: A little way from here is Fredrikshamn's redoubt, a reminder of 1645. In the final stages of the Hannibal Controversy, a war between Sweden and Denmark-Norway, Hannibal Sehested tried to attack Gothenburg, and Norwegian troops threw a temporary bridge across the river to the Swedish east bank. The redoubt was built to protect the bridgehead here on Hisingen.
En bit härifrån ligger Fridhems kyrkogår: A little way from here is Fridhem Cemetery, a burial ground covering a full 87 hectares, consecrated in 1968. It contains one of the Church of Sweden's three Islamic burial grounds in Gothenburg. For the first fourteen years, a travelling church served as a temporary chapel, until the present chapel was consecrated in 1982. Closer to the stop, the Bäckebol Center shopping area spreads out.
En bit härifrån ligger Frölunda torg, ri: A little way from here is Frölunda torg, designed by the architects Hjalmar Klemming, Lars Grönlund and Erik Thelaus and built over seven years for 80 million kronor. When Olof Palme opened it in 1966, it was the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries. Gothenburgers, famous for their puns, have a long tradition of giving buildings witty nicknames, by the way.
En bit härifrån ligger Gaisgården, Gais: A little way from here is Gaisgården, the training ground of the football club Gais, which has a dramatic history. It was hit by fire one morning in June 1996 but was rebuilt. Before the 2009 derby against IFK Göteborg, someone painted a gable wall in IFK's blue and white, and the club's chairman reported it to the police. A bit further away is Lake Stora Delsjön, up to 22.5 metres deep.
En bit härifrån ligger Gothia Arena, hem: A little way from here is Gothia Arena, home ground of Högsbo Basket. The hall has three courts and is the only club-owned hall in Gothenburg, and one of the largest club-owned basketball halls in Sweden. The fixed stand holds around 500 people, and with retractable seating and extra chairs the hall can take 1,000 spectators for matches.
En bit härifrån ligger Gunnestorps mosse: A little way from here is Gunnestorps mosse, a bog that is part of S.A. Hedlund's park and Hisingsparken. North of the bog are the ruins of an old croft called Mosstorpet. The ruin has become part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground, so today children play where a croft once stood.
En bit härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget: A little way from here is Hammarkulletorget, built in 1971. During a renovation in 1997 the square got both new colours and a new shape. You get there by tram and get off at what is called Gothenburg's only underground station. Closer to the stop lies Eriksbo, part of the Hjällbo district.
En bit härifrån ligger Hässelby slott, u: A little way from here is Hässelby slott, Hässelby Palace, built in the 1650s, possibly to designs by Simon de la Vallée, and one of Stockholm's oldest surviving secular buildings. The former noble estate was only called a palace when the Hässelby gård district was formed, to avoid confusion. At the entrance stands a runestone on a Viking Age burial mound, moved there in the 1860s from Skesta backe, about three kilometres away.
En bit härifrån ligger Högsbo pegmatitbr: A little way from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, two old quarries about 200 metres apart. Feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined here from 1945 until the late 1950s, and rare minerals such as monazite, columbite and bismuthinite were found too. Since 2016 the area has been part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve.
En bit härifrån ligger Imam Ali-moskén,: A little way from here is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in all of the Nordic countries, with activities in several languages. All around spreads Jakobsberg, Järfälla's commercial and administrative centre, just over 15 kilometres north of central Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Isolda, en tremas: A little way from here lies Isolda, a three-masted schooner built in 1902 at the Lödöse shipyard. She was the last Swedish sailing merchant ship in ocean trade and sailed to the West Indies, Mexico, South America and West Africa. The same skipper, Carl Julius Ahlgren, was in command for just over fifty years, from 1909 to 1960. Only in 1928 did she get a diesel engine to help.
En bit härifrån ligger Järnbrottsmotet,: A little way from here is Järnbrottsmotet, an unusual so-called double trumpet interchange that works like a real motorway interchange, although none of the roads is signposted as a motorway. It was built in the 1990s where the Europa roundabout used to be, an unusually large roundabout that the Söderleden road cut straight through with traffic lights.
En bit härifrån ligger Klare mosse, en l: A little way from here is Klare mosse, a small pond that is one of Hisingen's best waters for frogs and newts. Among others, the rare great crested newt lives there, thriving among all the little ponds and hollows. The pond was overgrown for a long time, but thanks to the Osbäck project the environment has become much better.
En bit härifrån ligger Komettorget, där: A little way from here is Komettorget, where the tram turns and two bus routes connect. Around the square is a centre building with shops and a restaurant, as well as well-used allotments. A footpath with steps leads up to a hilltop with the large housing areas on Kosmosgatan and Universumsgatan.
En bit härifrån ligger Kornhall, en hamn: A little way from here lies Kornhall, a harbour and small village on the Nordre älv river, just inside the Nordre älv estuary. There is a small shipyard and a marina, but the village is best known for Kornhallsleden, a ferry crossing with a long history that cuts the travel time to Gothenburg considerably. The name refers to the place where grain, korn, was loaded and unloaded.
En bit härifrån ligger Kungshamn, en ham: A little way from here is Kungshamn, a harbour that existed back in the Middle Ages and is mentioned in the 13th century in Bjärköarätten, an old town law. This is where the king of the Svear gathered his ledung, the people's fleet, before it sailed out towards other lands or the enemy. Just outside lies Sveriges holme, Sweden's Islet, and further off Danmarks holme, Denmark's Islet. Sveriges holme was donated to the state in 1937 and is today a protected nature reserve.
En bit härifrån ligger Kvastekulla grift: A little way from here is Kvastekulla griftegård, a cemetery designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander after a Nordic architecture competition. The idea was to preserve the beautiful landscape with as little intervention in nature as possible. The cemetery opened in 1959, and the chapel, with walls of untreated concrete and a copper roof, four years later.
En bit härifrån ligger Kvastekulla kapel: A little way from here is Kvastekulla chapel, a building that stands out. The walls are of untreated concrete, the roofs are clad in copper and above the chancel rises a tower-like lantern. The chapel was consecrated four years after the cemetery, which in turn was finished in 1959 and designed to blend into the landscape.
En bit härifrån ligger Kåhög, ett litet: A little way from here is Kåhög, a small villa community by the Säveån river north of the E20, close to both Gothenburg and Lake Aspen. A little further away is Lexby, where the actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up. She has written about growing up there in her autobiography CV. Livets gång.
En bit härifrån ligger Lilla Varholmen,: A little way from here is Lilla Varholmen, an island next to Hjuvik that is connected to Hisingen by a bridge. From there, car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality, and there are also buses all the way into the Nils Ericson terminal in central Gothenburg. The island has a long lighthouse history, and the leading lights standing there today date from 1927.
En bit härifrån ligger Lillhagsparkens s: A little way from here is Lillhagsparkens sjukhus, originally Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. No care is provided there any more; the forensic psychiatry unit moved out in 2013. Closer to the stop was Hökälla säteri, an old estate in Skogome.
En bit härifrån ligger Lundadepån, en av: A little way from here is Lundadepån, one of SL's bus depots, which came into use in 2009. It has room for 75 buses plus workshops, and since August 2024 the services from there have been run by Keolis. A little closer stands something much older: Kälvesta kvarn, a windmill from the 1600s that was moved here from Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm.
En bit härifrån ligger Långsjön, en grun: A little way from here is Långsjön, a shallow lake just three metres deep that forms the border between Stockholm and Huddinge, between the villa areas of Herrängen and Segeltorp. Along the north side of the lake is Långsjö gård, dating back to the 17th century, when it was a croft under Långbro gård. The farm has given its name to the whole Långsjö district.
En bit härifrån ligger Lövsta sopstation: A little way from here is the Lövsta waste station, which for much of the 20th century was the central station for handling Stockholm's household waste and later became a pioneer in district heating from waste. And a little curiosity: the district area of Hässelby existed only in 1997 and 1998, before it was merged with Vällingby.
En bit härifrån ligger Malmvik, en herrg: A little way from here is Malmvik, a manor dating back to the 14th century. On a wooded hillock south of Ekerövägen is the Wallenberg family's burial ground, the so-called Wallenberg Mausoleum. Lindö, by the way, was once an island of its own, but because of post-glacial land uplift it has joined up with Lovön via a 200-metre-wide isthmus at Lindöbro.
En bit härifrån ligger Novum Forskningsp: A little way from here is Novum Research Park, whose white concrete buildings with window frames in different colours are meant as a transition between the hospital's concrete and the high-rises of Flemingsberg. The idea is for researchers' discoveries to be taken further by companies. All around spreads Campus Flemingsberg, with about 17,000 students from five universities and colleges.
En bit härifrån ligger Partille Arena, i: A little way from here is Partille Arena, opened in September 2016. Swedish Radio has held the P3 Guldgalan music awards there several years in a row, and in April 2018 the attendance record was broken when Bryan Adams played to 5,503 people. The arena is also home ground for the women's and men's teams of the handball club IK Sävehof.
En bit härifrån ligger Pinntorp, en lite: A little way from here is Pinntorp, a small village in Landvetter parish near Tahult. Next to the village is a forest called Pinntorpaberg, and it grows mostly on, yes, a hill, a 'berg'. The village also has a famous face in its history: the road racing rider Kent Andersson has lived in Pinntorp. Since 2023 the village has been counted as part of the Landvetter urban area.
En bit härifrån ligger Rissne torg, som: A little way from here is Rissne torg, the square that used to be called Dragonplan, where an octagonal building has become the district's landmark. Deep beneath it, 25 to 40 metres down in the bedrock, lies Rissne metro station, whose artwork is a lettered timeline of historical events from 3000 BC up to 1985, the year the station opened. The artwork was made by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
En bit härifrån ligger Rågsveds tunnelba: A little way from here is Rågsved metro station, which opened on 14 November 1959 and was the terminus until 1960, when the tracks were extended to Hagsätra. The platform is outdoors, and on it stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Green Bird, by the artist Björn Selder. The district is cut right in two by the metro, with the iconic horseshoe-shaped centre on one side.
En bit härifrån ligger Råtjärnen, en rik: A little way from here is Råtjärnen, a true miniature lake of just 0.012 square kilometres, 75 metres above sea level. A bit further away, by Lake Finnsjön, is the small village of Lahall, where for a long time there were only two farms. Holiday homes were later built on their land, and many of them have become permanent homes.
En bit härifrån ligger Selma Lagerlöfs t: A little way from here is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, where Bäckebol's church hall once was. It belonged to Bäckebol parish, which merged into Backa parish in 2010. The name Bäckebol still lives on, today as a district of its own in northern Gothenburg on Hisingen. The square, built in 1971, is named after the Nobel laureate Selma Lagerlöf.
En bit härifrån ligger Skarpnäcksfältet,: A little way from here lies Skarpnäcksfältet, which was once an airfield. For many years the Skarpnäcksloppet motor race was held here, and the last air show took place in August 1980. Since then the field has gained a residential area. Closer at hand is the Gubbängen business area, also called the Norra Sköndal industrial area, one of the city's smallest.
En bit härifrån ligger Skintebo, ett kus: A little way from here is Skintebo, a coastal residential area that even has a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion. In the other direction is Stora Svindal, about a kilometre northeast of Billdal. Before 2015 it counted as a small village of its own, but since then it has grown together with Billdal.
En bit härifrån ligger Skrubbatriangeln,: A little way from here is Skrubbatriangeln, an industrial area in the district of Skrubba that opened in 1987. The name isn't hard to work out, because the area is shaped like a triangle. The district of Skrubba borders lake Drevviken to the west and south, and Trollbäcken in Tyresö to the east. Further away, on the shore of Drevviken, is the Strandkyrkogården cemetery.
En bit härifrån ligger Sollentuna sjukhu: A little way from here is Sollentuna hospital, opened on 15 November 1978. The building has a special shape: an eight-storey slab surrounded by nine lower, single-storey sections. The hospital was completely renovated from 2015 to 2020, and in connection with that it took over the urgent care centre from Löwenströmska hospital.
En bit härifrån ligger Sophie Elkans gat: A little way from here is Sophie Elkans gata, named in 1992 after the Gothenburg-born author Sophie Elkan, better known as Selma Lagerlöf's close friend. Nearby is also Gothia Park Academy, BK Häcken's clubhouse and training ground, with three full-size football pitches.
En bit härifrån ligger Storkällans kapel: A little way from here is Storkällan Chapel at Storkällan Cemetery in Nacka. The name has a lovely background: it comes from an open spring, storkällan meaning the big spring, which to this day provides the forest animals with fresh water. A peaceful place, where the forest animals have their very own drinking fountain.
En bit härifrån ligger Strålsjön, en lit: A little way from here is Strålsjön, a small, nutrient-poor forest lake hidden in the nature reserves east of Älta. The water is dark because it flows in from the humus-rich Älta bog. Even though the lake is so small, pike, perch and roach all swim here, and in the south-west bog myrtle, among other plants, grows along the shore.
En bit härifrån ligger Tyresös centrum,: A little way from here is Tyresö's centre, where the tower block Tyresö View rises 82 metres with 23 storeys – in 2016 the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Next to it is the glazed shopping arcade Tyresö Centrum, with 74 shops, the municipal hall and a library with its own exhibition hall, and Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church for the whole municipality.
En bit härifrån ligger Vidja, vid östra: A little way from here is Vidja, on the eastern shore of Lake Orlången. The village is something of a dead end: the only road in comes from the north, through Ågesta. Since 2018 the two together have formed the district of Vidja-Ågesta. In the forests around Lissma lies Kvarnsjön, a long, narrow and shallow lake protected as a Natura 2000 site.
En bit härifrån ligger Villa Finedal, up: A little way from here is Villa Finedal, built in 1886 as a summer residence for the fireworks maker Adolf Rickard Törner. The villa has great cultural and historical value and has been a listed building since 1979. Closer by is the old folk high school, to which Missionsskolan, the mission school, moved in 1908 from Högbergsgatan on Södermalm, and where people trained in mission work, development aid and music, among other things.
En bit härifrån ligger Wendelsbergs folk: A little way from here is Wendelsbergs folkhögskola, Sweden's oldest folk high school run by a popular movement, which started in 1908. The wooden buildings were put up at the end of the 19th century by Bruno Wendel, who wanted a place where he and his wife could retire in their old age. Instead it became a school, after the temperance movement bought the house in 1907.
En bit härifrån ligger byn Skändla, vars: A little way from here is the village of Skändla, whose name comes from Skinhälla, ‘the rock slab the sun shines on’. Like many other wooded hills on northern Hisingen, Skändla was once an island in an archipelago. When land uplift made the water recede, it became fertile land that is still used for grazing and farming today. Closer to the stop, the little lake Holmdammen glitters.
En bit härifrån ligger ett område som he: A short distance from here is an area called Ingenting – which means 'Nothing'. The name comes from the manor farm Ingenting, which belonged to Karlberg Palace, where the sculptor Johan Tobias Sergel spent several summers and where Carl Michael Bellman is also said to have stayed. Legend has it that Bellman or Gustav III jokingly came up with the odd name, but its origin is disputed. The farm was demolished in the early 1980s.
En bit härifrån ligger rondellen vid Skr: A little way from here is the roundabout at Skra Bro, an invisible border in the road network. Here, responsibility for Kongahällavägen passes from the state's Swedish Transport Administration, to the north, to Gothenburg's municipal Traffic Office, to the south. Skra bro itself, an old bridge over the Osbäcken stream, has given its name to the whole area.
En bit härifrån ligger ruinen av Ytterby: A little way from here are the ruins of Ytterby Old Church, built in the 12th century in Romanesque style on what was then Norwegian land. Legend has it that Saint Olaf himself had it built. The church was rebuilt in 1699 and was the parish church right up until 1870. The countryside around Ytterby has been settled since the Iron Age and is rich in ancient remains.
En bit härifrån ligger villagatan Anunds: A little way from here is the residential street Anundsvägen, which is best known for a royal visit: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom was here during the 1950s. Closer by is Snabba hus Råcksta, with 247 flats, which was one of ten finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year 2020.
En bit härifrån ligger Åkermyntans centr: A little way from here is Åkermyntan Centre, opened in November 1977 and mentioned in one of the comedy group Killinggänget's sketches, in which the character Fred Asp, known for partying with his ferret Göran, lives nearby. The whole of Hässelby takes its name from Hässelby Palace, whose lands once covered large parts of today's three Hässelby districts, and Hässelby Villastad is Stockholm's westernmost district.
En bit härifrån ligger Öringesjön, en my: A little way from here is Lake Öringesjön, a very shallow and nutrient-rich lake with an average depth of only about two metres. Even so, it's one of the richest lakes in Södertörn for aquatic plants, with 29 species, and several of them are so rare they're on the national red list. In Alby nature reserve are also Kolardammarna, ponds built in 1997 and 1998 to clean stormwater before it reaches the lakes.
En bit härifrån låg Filmstaden i Råsunda: A little way from here was Filmstaden in Råsunda, the film studios where nearly 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973, a place associated not least with Ingmar Bergman. Even closer was the tramway's Råsunda depot from around 1910, with staff housing in the Boken and Björken blocks. Incidentally, Näckrosen metro station is the only one with exits in two municipalities.
En bit härifrån låg Hundhamra, en gård s: Not far from here lay Hundhamra, a farm mentioned as early as Erikskrönikan, the medieval Chronicle of Eric, but which has since disappeared. What remains is a hillfort and a burial ground, and a runestone is also said to have stood here, about a man who died on Ingvar the Far-Travelled's ill-fated Viking expedition to the east. During the Second World War, the Norsborg anti-aircraft position was built in the area, one of the more powerful in Stockholm's defences, to protect the city and the Norsborg waterworks from air raids.
En bit härifrån låg LM Ericssons central: A little way from here was LM Ericsson's central warehouse, built between 1965 and 1975. The goods handling was so automated that the warehouse became a sight in its own right. In the other direction you can see Grantorp, where the colourful tower blocks from the early 1970s of the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, have become a familiar feature of the townscape. The municipality today classifies them as a particularly valuable cultural environment.
En bit härifrån låg Stockholm-Barkarby f: A short distance from here was Stockholm-Barkarby airport, also called Hägerstalund airfield, where planes flew all the way from 1913 to 2010. In the Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, one of the old runways still crosses the stream. Igelbäcken itself winds about 10.5 kilometres from Säbysjön lake all the way to Edsviken bay by Ulriksdal Palace. Closer by is Hästa klack, a nature reserve since 2026.
En bit härifrån låg Täby Galopp, Skandin: A little way from here was Täby Galopp, Scandinavia's largest gallop racecourse. King Gustaf VI Adolf opened it on 28 August 1960, and the last race day was held on 18 May 2016, before racing moved to Bro Park. Right next to it is the Grindtorp residential area, between Näsbydal, the old racecourse and Täby centrum.
En bit härifrån låg torpet Parken, anlag: A little way from here was the croft Parken, established in 1839 and demolished in the mid-1950s, around the time Bagarmossen grew up as a suburb. Today the district is a well-preserved 1950s suburb, known for its many footpaths and pedestrian underpasses that keep walkers and cars apart, and for low-rise blocks of flats, small houses and terraced houses that follow the landscape well.
En bit härifrån reser sig Hummelmoraberg: A little way from here, Hummelmoraberget rises in Görväln nature reserve, with a slope down towards Lake Mälaren. There you can see traces from the time after the Ice Age: beach ridges of gravel and stone once washed up by the waves of the sea, so the sea level actually reached all the way up here. South of the hill are Hummelmora hage, a wooded pasture, and Hummelmora torp, a croft.
En bit härifrån rinner Forsån, en bara 1: A little way from here flows Forsån, a stream just 1.4 kilometres long that connects the lakes Magelungen and Drevviken and forms the border between Stockholm and Huddinge. The total drop is 0.7 metres, and most of it is in the first hundred metres. By Forsån stood Forsen farm from the 18th century; today only the foundation remains, about 25 metres from the bridge over the stream.
En bit härifrån rinner Forsån, knappt en: A little way from here flows Forsån, a stream just under one and a half kilometres long that links Lake Magelungen with Lake Drevviken and forms the boundary between Stockholm and Huddinge. Almost its entire drop, 0.7 metres, is in the first hundred metres. The rest of the way it flows calmly. By the stream stood Forsens gård, an 18th-century farm. Today only the foundations remain, about 25 metres from the bridge.
En bit härifrån rinner Glose å, sex kilo: A little way from here, the six-kilometre Glose å stream flows into Ryskärsfjorden. The inlet has shallow beds and grazed shore meadows with rich plant and bird life, and the area is part of the Nordre älv estuary, a vast nature reserve counted among the most valuable natural areas in the county.
En bit härifrån rinner Vendelsån, en lit: A little way from here flows Vendelsån, a small river that gets its water from three lakes with lovely names: Svartsjön, Ramsjön and Lycksjön – the Black Lake, the Ramsons Lake and the Lucky Lake. It winds its way through Gudö and Vendelsö and flows into Lake Drevviken, near the spot where the Gudöån river begins. To the east, the Vendelsö-Gudö district borders the deep forests of Tyresta National Park.
En bit härifrån slingrar sig Osbäcken, e: A little way from here winds Osbäcken, a small stream with a big distinction: it's the only stream with sea trout on the whole of Hisingen. It runs from the Klare mosse bog, along Björlandavägen and out at Björlanda kile. To improve the water quality, part of the stream's flow has been rerouted in an EU-funded project, which also created a pond.
En bit härifrån slingrar sig Söderån, et: A little way from here winds Söderån, a stream just over a kilometre long between the lakes Orlången and Ågestasjön. It starts in Orlången's northern bay with the lovely name Fräkenbotten and then flows through a wetland called Pumphusängen. It all belongs to the Orlången nature reserve. A little further away is Ågestaverket, Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers.
En bit härifrån sticker Tyresö View upp: A little way from here, Tyresö View sticks up above the rooftops, an 82-metre-tall residential building with 23 storeys which in 2016 was the fourth-tallest in Stockholm County. At its foot is Tyresö centrum, a glazed shopping centre with 74 shops, the municipal hall and a library that constantly shows new exhibitions.

A little way from here, Tyresö View sticks up above the rooftops: an 82-metre-tall residential building with 23 storeys, designed by Archus arkitektur. In 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County, after Kista Torn and Skatteskrapan, among others. All around is Bollmora, which was a locality of its own from 1965 to 1974 and where Tyresö municipality's administration is based.
En bit härifrån sticker halvön Männö udd: A little way from here, the peninsula Männö udd juts out into Lake Bornsjön. It has something of a split identity: the northern part belongs to Botkyrka and the southern part to Salem, but the whole headland is part of Bornsjön nature reserve. The area is also home to Söderby burial ground, one of the best preserved in the Lake Mälaren valley, with around 150 visible graves from the early Iron Age.
En bit härifrån stod Hagstaeken, en grov: A little way from here stood Hagstaeken, a massive oak that, by trunk circumference, was the largest of Huddinge's ten oaks protected as natural monuments. Despite protests, it was felled for safety reasons on the night of 3 December 2025, following a government decision. The area is also home to Flemingsberg manor, whose history goes back to the 15th century and which gave the whole district its name.
En bit härifrån står Bjurslättskyrkan, s: A little way from here stands Bjurslätt church, which has changed tradition: it used to be a church in what is now Lundby parish, but since 1998 it has belonged to the Greek Orthodox Church. Further away, at Vågmästareplatsen, is Kville saluhall, a food hall opened in 2013, with meat, fish and seafood, a bakery, a café and a wide range of restaurants.
En bit härifrån står Högenskolan, som nä: A little way from here stands Högenskolan, which when it was built in 1930 was called a “rural school palace”. The old Högenskolan burned down, perhaps because the children themselves were allowed to light the stove before the schoolmaster arrived in the morning. The new one was designed by Ivar Burman in 1920s Classicism.
En bit härifrån står Högenskolan, uppför: A little way from here stands Högenskolan, built in 1930 for the children of Högen, Fiskebäck, Önnered and Tynnered. When it was new, it was called a rural school palace. The older school had burned down, possibly because the children looked after the heating themselves before the schoolmaster arrived in the morning, so perhaps it's no surprise that the new one got a slate roof.
En bit härifrån står Nasirmoskén, som in: A little way from here stands the Nasir Mosque, which opened in 1976 and became the first building in Sweden built to be a mosque. It belongs to the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community. The hilltop housing area of Högsbohöjd has a charming detail: several of its courtyards bear women's names, such as Elin, Gerda and Fredrika. The Högsboleden road was built in 1966 at the same time as the area.
En bit härifrån står Villa Korndal, uppf: A little way from here stands Villa Korndal, built in 1870 for David Otto Francke, the entrepreneur who made Korndal paper mill Sweden's largest. Later the villa came into the ownership of the Wallenberg family, and after that it became the managing director's residence for the head of the Papyrus company. Paper mills, financial dynasties and directors, all in one and the same villa.
En bit härifrån står en gammal lada som: A little way from here stands an old barn that has become a theatre. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is the stage for six amateur theatre societies. Since 1998 it has put on revues and comedies, mainly by young people, and there is even an English theatre group in the building.
En bit härifrån står en lada som bytt hö: A little way from here stands a barn that has swapped hay bales for spotlights. Teaterhuset Mölndal is a former barn converted into a theatre with 150 seats, and several amateur theatre groups perform here, mostly revues and comedies made by young people. There's even an English theatre group in the building.
En bit härifrån tar Partille kommun vid,: A little way from here, Partille municipality begins, and the closest part is Sävedalen. The name says exactly what it is: the valley of the Säveån river. Sävedalen borders Gothenburg municipality and counts as a close suburb of Gothenburg; in fact it's even part of the Gothenburg urban area, despite belonging to another municipality.
En bit härifrån tar naturreservatet Älta: A little way from here begins the Älta mosse – Strålsjön nature reserve, 52 hectares of nature established in 1995. Together with the neighbouring Strålsjön – Erstavik reserve, it forms one large continuous outdoor area, with the small lake Strålsjön in the middle. Perfect if you want to swap asphalt for bog and forest lake.
En bit härifrån tränar BK Häcken. Gothia: A little way from here, BK Häcken trains. Gothia Park Academy is the football club's clubhouse and training ground on Hisingen, with a 1,300-square-metre clubhouse and three full-size pitches, two of them with artificial turf and floodlights. On top of those three there is also a grass pitch, so there's rarely a shortage of grass to kick a ball on here.
En bit härifrån, i Biskopsgården, ligger: A little way from here, in Biskopsgården, is Biskopsgården Church. When Bishop Bo Giertz consecrated it in 1961, he also burned in the cross that can still be seen on the church door facing Vårvädersgatan. At first only a small church was planned. By the Älvsborgsfjorden inlet is the Rödjan district, mostly an industrial area but also home to the Rya forest.
En bit härifrån, i Hansta naturreservat: A little way from here, in Hansta nature reserve at the very northern tip of Stockholm municipality, is Astrid Lindgrens berg, Astrid Lindgren's Hill. It got its name in 1989 as thanks for the author's efforts to preserve Hansta's natural and cultural heritage. The reserve was created in 1999, covers about 270 hectares and borders the Järvafältet nature reserve.
En bit härifrån, i Hässelbygårdsskolan,: A little way from here, in Hässelbygårdsskolan, was the Prisma cinema, which opened in 1960 and was a public cinema until 1984. The first film shown was Let's Make Love with Marilyn Monroe, and the auditorium had 375 blue armchairs. In the neighbouring district of Vinsta, which the City of Stockholm bought from Spånga in 1949, there are terraced houses and villas in the north and the hill Johannelundstoppen in the south-west.
En bit härifrån, i Orlångens naturreserv: A little way from here, in the Orlången nature reserve, is the forest lake Mörtsjön. On its shore is the croft Charlottendal, where Prince Eugen painted the picture Spring. The lake is unusually nutrient-rich for a forest lake, so crucian carp and rudd thrive, and someone has also introduced carp. In the other direction is the old croft Sjötorp by Flemingsbergsviken bay.
En bit härifrån, i Sjöängen, låg en gång: A little way from here, in Sjöängen, there was once a lake called Brännkyrkasjön, also known as Kyrksjön. The lake was drained in stages, but it may make a small comeback. In 2009 the Älvsjö district council made a decision in principle that Sjöängen would become a park with an artificial lake, recreating a small part of the vanished lake.
En bit härifrån, i Skälby, står runstene: A little way from here, in Skälby, stands the runestone U 89, a finely carved stone of coarse-grained granite, 132 centimetres tall. It has fired people's imaginations: Olof Rudbeck the Elder presented a fanciful reading of the inscription in his work Atlantica. The piece missing from the stone was already missing in the oldest drawings from the 17th century.
En bit härifrån, i Tyresö strand, ligger: A little way from here, in Tyresö strand, is the small pond Karptjärnen, which is barely two metres deep. It hides a curious story: both medicinal leeches and horse leeches live in the lake, believed to have been introduced back when Stockholm's pharmacies released and caught leeches to treat various ailments. In spring, the pond also teems with tadpoles.
En bit härifrån, i Vinsta industriområde: A little way from here, in the Vinsta industrial area, is Vällingby fire station, which came into service in December 1964. The firefighters there have an unusual speciality: they are specially trained in roof blasting and rappelling, that is, climbing at great heights. Their district stretches all the way from Abrahamsberg in the south up to Lövsta in the north.
En bit härifrån, i hörnet Telefonvägen o: A little way from here, on the corner of Telefonvägen and Mikrofonvägen, Tellus Towers were once planned, two residential skyscrapers of 82 and 62 storeys. The project was presented in 2013, but in 2020 it emerged that the city planning office no longer supported it. The name came from the Tellusborg area. At Telefonplan you will also find Midsommargården, one of Stockholm's six community centres, which has offered culture since 1946.
En bit härifrån, i området Gunnared, lig: A little way from here, in the Gunnared area, lies Titteridamm, and the name has a charming legend behind it. On Saturday evenings, the girls are said to have gone down to the pond to look at their reflections in the still water and make themselves pretty before the dance. They simply peeked into the pond, 'tittade i dammen'. The area also has Gunnared cemetery, opened in June 2003 and a full 80 hectares in size.
En bit härifrån, i slutet av Kumla allé: A little way from here, at the end of Kumla allé on a peninsula in Lake Drevviken, lies Kumla Manor, Kumla herrgård. The estate has roots in the Middle Ages and is the original property for large parts of western Tyresö. It was in fact Kumla that changed its name to Trollbäcken in 1947. Since 2013 food has been served here, and the manor also hosts conferences.
En bit härifrån, inne i Alby naturreserv: A little way from here, inside Alby nature reserve, are the Kolardammarna ponds, a water purification project built in 1997 and 1998 on the old Kolarängarna meadows. The ponds receive water from the delightfully named Fnyskbäcken stream, which mostly carries stormwater from Bollmora. First an oil separator catches the worst of it, then the particles are left to sink to the bottom before the water flows on towards the lakes of the Tyresån river.
En bit härifrån, mellan Övre och Nedre R: A little way from here, between the lakes Övre and Nedre Rudasjön, is Rudans gård, an old 17th-century croft that is today the heart of the Rudan recreation area and nature reserve. In the other direction, in front of Haninge Culture House on Poseidons torg, stands the runestone Sö 269. It originally stood on Söderbymalm and has given its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, in the middle of Handen.
En bit härifrån, nära gränsen till Tyres: A little way from here, near the border with Tyresö, bubbles Storkällan, a cold-water spring at the edge of Storkällan chapel and cemetery. It's the spring that gave its name to both the chapel and the burial ground, and it still provides the forest's animals with fresh water.
En bit härifrån, på Elektronvägen, finns: A little way from here, on Elektronvägen, are the Labour Movement Archives and Library, Arbetarrörelsens arkiv och bibliotek. It was founded in 1902 and is the oldest of its kind in the world. It holds documents from most of the parties and organisations in the labour movement and over 600 personal archives. The archive used to be on Upplandsgatan in Stockholm, near Folkets hus and the LO trade union headquarters, but in 2012 it moved here.
En bit härifrån, på Järfällasidan, ligge: A little way from here, on the Järfälla side, is Hummelmoraberget in the Görväln nature reserve.
