There are traces there from the time after the Ice Age: beach ridges of gravel and stone, washed up by the waves of the sea, show that the sea level once reached all the way up here. And a little trivia: the Hässelby district administration area existed only in 1997 and 1998.
En bit härifrån, på Kalvsund, står Breme: A little way from here, on Kalvsund, stands Bremerska villan, popularly known as the Smugglers' Villa. It was built in 1912 and bears witness to fortunes made from herring fishing and from liquor smuggling in the 1920s. With its towers, it is a landmark by the shipping lane. At the highest point of the island stands the pole beacon Valen, and beneath it a compass rose with the year 1684 is carved into the rock.
En bit härifrån, på Klockargårdens skola: A short distance from here, in the schoolyard of Klockargården school, Carl Milles' elephants are at play: the sculpture group Playing Elephants has stood there since 1947. The school itself is the oldest one still in use in the municipality, dating back to 1843. Along Stockholmsvägen in Näset you'll also find Näsets krog, a preserved 18th-century roadside inn, and Villa Nynäs, where Lidingö's first general store opened in the late 19th century.
En bit härifrån, på Kofferdalsvägen 37,: A little way from here, at Kofferdalsvägen 37, is Villa Dalfrid. It is a privately owned home, but not just any home: on 24 September 1979 the villa became a listed building under the Swedish Cultural Environment Act. The area belongs to Askim parish, whose roots go all the way back to the Middle Ages.
En bit härifrån, på andra sidan Göta älv: A little way from here, on the other side of the Göta älv river, is Villa Ellesbo. Gothenburg's city architect Carl Wilhelm Carlberg designed the manor house and garden in 1795 in an Italian-inspired style, with terraces down towards the river. Rare trees and huge old oaks grow in the garden. Just south of the manor is Rösbo, with one of the largest beech forests in the Gothenburg area.
En bit härifrån, på en kulle i Glöskär,: A little way from here, on a hill in Glöskär, stands Burås mill. It was built in 1892 to 1893, on three floors, by the master builder Emanuel Andréasson, but wind power has old roots here: there have been windmills on the site since the 18th century. The mill became a listed building in 2004.
En bit härifrån, på en udde söder om Bor: A little way from here, on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, is Salem church, nestled among large oaks, limes, alders and birches, with the old Södertäljevägen road beside it. The area is full of ancient remains. And here's a curiosity: for a few years in the 1970s and 80s, Salem parish was part of Botkyrka municipality, and since 1983 it has formed the main part of Salem municipality.
En bit härifrån, strax öster om E18 i hö: A little way from here, just east of the E18 at Kallhäll, is Lake Översjön. It's a rift-valley lake, 4.1 metres deep and 22.1 metres above sea level, shared between Järfälla and Sollentuna. Around it spreads an open cultural landscape, together with coniferous forest and bare rock.
En bit härifrån, ungefär nio kilometer n: A little way from here, about nine kilometres north-east of central Gothenburg, is Lärjeholm manor. It became a listed building in 1973, and the main building stands only 150 metres from the Göta älv river. Around the buildings are remains of the old garden, and to the south the Lärjeån stream forms the edge of the grounds.
En bit härifrån, vid Askims norra kyrkog: A little way from here, at Askim's northern cemetery, history rests in several layers. North of the cemetery is an Iron Age burial ground with around eighty burial mounds, and Askim's medieval parish church stood on the site until it burned down in 1876. Most exciting of all is the so-called privateer's grave, where a privateer captain in the service of Lars Gathenhielm is said to be buried.
En bit härifrån, vid Drevvikens västra s: A little way from here, on the western shore of Drevviken lake, is Trångsunds gård, traditionally called the pearl of Drevviken. The manor has roots in the mid-1700s, and the main building was designed by none other than the Surveyor of the Royal Office of Works, Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz. The name Trångsund comes from the narrowest strait in Drevviken, the largest lake in the Tyresån lake system.
En bit härifrån, vid Elisedal i nuvarand: A little way from here, at Elisedal in present-day Kallebäck, matches were made. From 1907 Eric Holmberg moved his production here from Södertälje, and the factory was called Södertelje Tändsticksfabrik, the Södertälje Match Factory, right up until 1917, even though it was in Gothenburg. After that it became Göteborgs Tändsticksfabrik, and most of the matches were exported.
En bit härifrån, vid Göta älv, låg Sverr: A little way from here, by the Göta älv river, was Sverres Varv, which started out as a factory for ship models. The company was founded in 1915 and built models for Gothenburg's shipyards and for the maritime museum, including one of the East Indiaman Finland. For the Jubilee Exhibition of 1923, a long series of models of ships, shipyards and harbours was made. When demand fell, they started making toys instead.
En bit härifrån, vid Idrottsvägen i Åbyo: A little way from here, on Idrottsvägen in the Åby area, is Åbybadet, a swimming centre that opened its doors on 16 June 2023. The baths cost a whole 500 million kronor to build, so every splash is quite an exclusive experience. A bit further away, hooves thunder at Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track.
En bit härifrån, vid Nordsjön, ligger by: A little way from here, by Lake Nordsjön, lies the village of Bolås, five kilometres south-east of Mölnlycke. The village has changed parish: historically it belonged to Landvetter parish, but in 1949 it was transferred to Råda parish. Closer to the stop is the small forest lake Slättebacketjärnen.
En bit härifrån, vid Rådasjön, ligger Rå: A little way from here, by Lake Rådasjön, is Råda säteri, a manor with a main building, wings and farm buildings. The estate became a listed building on 3 June 1969. Rådasjön itself is 23 metres deep and is the drinking water source for Mölndal municipality, and the Mölndalsån river flows through the lake, changing its name further downstream to Gullbergsån.
En bit härifrån, vid Stubbåkersgatan, li: A little way from here, on Stubbåkersgatan, lies Fässberg Cemetery, a large area of 116,000 square metres with 4,800 graves, natural land included. Since 1936 there has been Fässberg Chapel and an old mortuary here, and in 1982 a memorial grove opened in the middle of the area. In the other direction is the new Åbybadet swimming centre, opened in 2023.
En bit härifrån, vid fritidsbåtshamnen i: A little way from here, at the marina in Hovås, is one of the Swedish Sea Rescue Society's rescue stations. It was set up in 1983 and today has 25 volunteer sea rescuers. One of the first boats, Pernilla, turned out to be too slow, so it was rebuilt with a new engine and propeller.
En bit härifrån, öster om E4:an och väst: A little way from here, east of the E4 and west of the Edsviken bay, is Silverdal, which was once a croft. When plans to build here began in 1989, the project was first named Margreteborg, before it was changed to Silverdal. In the other direction stretches Sörentorp, an area of Solna that runs down towards the grounds of Ulriksdal Palace.
En bit härifrån, öster om sjön Trehörnin: A little way from here, east of Lake Trehörningen, is Solbacken, a distinctly small-house community. The area is part of the Högmora district, formed in 2018. Holiday homes have long dominated there, but now they are being converted into permanent homes. The whole area lies in Kynäsberget, a forest and hill area covering most of central Huddinge.
En bit ut i skärgården ligger Grötö, där: A little way out in the archipelago lies Grötö, where only 84 people live all year round. At the northern end of the island is a nature reserve with one of Bohuslän's few sandy beaches, and along the west coast runs an esker, a ridge of rounded boulders. The passenger ferry leaves from Björkö, and in the main harbour there is a kiosk open in summer and a guest harbour.
En gångväg knyter ihop hållplatsen med Å: A footpath links the stop with Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, northern Kortedala's square with a café-bakery, a pizzeria and a health centre. A little further away a time machine awaits: Kortedala museum, a flat of about 50 square metres that shows what a working-class home could look like in the 1950s, filled out with original fittings from other flats in the area.
En kort bit bort ligger Svensbydösen, äv: A short distance away is Svensbydösen, also known as Queen Hacka's Grave, Gothenburg's only known long dolmen – a Stone Age tomb – and the municipality's oldest structure. According to legend, a gold ring forged by a giant lies in the grave, and treasure hunters have badly damaged the dolmen searching for it. When the Norrleden road was being planned in 1978, archaeologists excavated the grave and were able to establish that it really was a dolmen.
En kort bit bort står Centrumkyrkan, en: A short distance away stands Centrumkyrkan, a church that changed hands in an unusual way. The Methodists had used it since 1996, but when their numbers became too few, the building was handed over to the Church of Sweden in 2023. In November 2025 it was consecrated as the new church for Kållered parish in the Mölndal pastorate.
En kort promenad bort fanns Hallinge, en: A short walk away was Hallinge, a small locality designated by Statistics Sweden in 1990, with temporary housing just south-west of the croft Smedstorp. The name was borrowed from Hallinge gård, a farm one and a half kilometres away. Today only the Smedstorp croft remains, so the locality became a brief footnote in the statistics.
En kort promenad bort korsar Linnarhults: A short walk away, the Linnarhult Bridge, Linnarhultsbron, crosses the Lärjeån river. The bridge was built in the early 1970s and replaced an old stone arch bridge, but the old bridge wasn't demolished – it still stands next to the new one. Two bridges side by side, one from the age of the car and one from a slower time.
En kort promenad bort ligger Ahlby säter: A short walk away lies Ahlby säteri, a stone-built manor from the 1620s and the oldest surviving building in Lilla Alby. Among its owners was Clas Fredrik Horn af Åminne, who was convicted of complicity in the murder of King Gustav III. Landsvägen, the Country Road, has kept its rural name because it was once part of the main road from Stockholm. That is also where you will find Swedbank's head office, shaped like a double V.
En kort promenad bort ligger Annelunds g: A short walk away is Annelund farm, where the "father of gymnastics" Per Henrik Ling lived between 1822 and 1839. The main building and the gymnastics wing are listed buildings. An old tall tale says that Gustav III gave the farm to his favourite Elis Schröderheim, but it isn't true. Schröderheim lived on another farm, now vanished.
En kort promenad bort ligger Kärra kyrka: A short walk away is Kärra Church, which was a chapel until 2001 and since 2010 has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish. On the other side of the Göta älv river is Agnesberg, where travellers have been given food and lodging for several hundred years, since the place was a coaching inn stop long before the railway arrived in 1880.
En kort promenad bort ligger Lundby Kolo: A short walk away are the Lundby allotment gardens, Lundby Koloniträdgårdar, originally Lundby kolonien, although in 1972 the association had to give up about half the area for a football pitch and parking. Nearby runs Hjalmar Brantingsgatan, one of the city's longest streets at almost 4,400 metres. At Frihamnen is also Gothenburg's lowest point along the street, two metres below mean water level.
En kort promenad bort ligger Park Studio: A short walk away is Park Studios, a music studio where Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander, among others, recorded during the 1990s, and which from 2004 to 2016 was owned by the band Kent and their producer. Park-Bio, the cinema in Örby's Folkets hus community centre from 1928, showed films until 1968, and since 2021 the films are rolling there again. And Örby Palace is today let to the Embassy of Vietnam.
En kort promenad bort ligger Skändla rös: A short walk away is Skändla rös, a Bronze Age burial cairn, 18 metres wide and just over two metres high. It lies on the boundary between Bohuslän and Västergötland, which before the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658 was the border between Sweden and Norway. Every year a mowing day is held in the meadows next to it, where the grass is cut by hand, including with scythes.
En kort promenad bort ligger Sköndalssko: A short walk away is Sköndalsskolan school, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and opened in 1953. According to the Swedish National Heritage Board, it has unusual design for its time and many interesting architectural details. In the other direction is Gubbängen's business area, also called the Norra Sköndal industrial area, one of the city's very smallest industrial areas.
En kort promenad bort ligger Vällingby c: A short walk away is Vällingby centre, the model for the 1950s suburban vision known as the ‘ABC town’. There stands the Trappan civic centre from 1956, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius and built in terraces between a lower and an upper square, with theatre, music and a library. Right next to it is the brick church of St Thomas, S:t Tomas kyrka, by Peter Celsing, consecrated in 1960, with a wooden crucifix by the artist Bror Hjorth.
En kort promenad bort ligger Västra Fröl: A short walk away is Västra Frölunda churchyard, of medieval origin. The old Västra Frölunda church stood here until it was demolished in the 1860s. Look for the iron rings in the churchyard wall – they were for tethering horses. The oldest gravestones are from 1680 and 1729.
En kort promenad bort ligger herrgården: A short walk away is the manor Stora Frösunda, built in 1783 and given its palace-like appearance in the 1890s. Today it is owned by SAS Institute. By the manor also stands the runestone U 121. Nearby rises Hagahuset, built from 1954 to 1957 to house the entire administration of Stockholm County Council.
En kort promenad bort ligger kulturhuset: A short walk away is the Cyklopen cultural centre, self-run and non-profit, with music, art and adult education. The first building burned down in an arson attack in 2008 but was rebuilt. Just below Högdalen centre is Högdalen skatepark, which with about 5,500 square metres of concrete is the largest in Stockholm and almost as big as Stapelbäddsparken in Malmö.
En kort promenad bort ligger tjärnen Kla: A short walk away is the pond Klare mosse, one of Hisingen's best waters for frogs and newts. Among others, the uncommon great crested newt lives here, thriving among all the little ponds and hollows. The pond had become overgrown but has been given new life through the Osbäck project, and from here the Osbäcken stream flows down towards Björlanda kile.
En kort promenad bort står De tre vingar: A short walk away stands De tre vingarna, The Three Wings, a monumental steel sculpture by the American Alexander Calder. The city bought it in the early 1960s, but Angered was delayed, so the sculpture stood temporarily on Götaplatsen from 1967. Only in 1979 did it move out to Angered. Nearby is Angered Arena, with an ice rink and swimming pool, where there's a special focus on teaching children to swim.
En kort promenad bort, längs Solvädersby: A short walk away, along Solvädersbyn, stand 124 houses with a really sporty background. They were originally built for the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer, reused at the 1995 World Athletics Championships and found their final home here in 1996. That's why the streets there have athletics names instead of weather names. On the same site, what was then Europe's longest building was built in 1954; it was demolished in 1995.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Bräcke: A short walk from here is Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft built in the 1830s and a local heritage museum since 1965. From 1889 the soldier Sven Olof Emanuelsson Björk lived here. The croft has not always stood where it is now; it used to be north of Bräcke village. Inside there is room for just one room, a kitchen and an entrance hall.
En kort promenad härifrån ligger Dvärgah: A short walk from here is Dvärgahuset, the Dwarf House, a stone cist grave from the late Neolithic. People used to believe the grave was a home for dwarfs, hence the name. Three large blocks form a roof over the burial chamber, and in one of the end slabs there is a round, ground-out hole that nobody knows the purpose of.
En kort promenad härifrån står Torslanda: A short walk from here stands Torslanda church, considered one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. It is the parish church of Torslanda parish, which until 1967 lay outside the City of Gothenburg, in the Västra Hising hundred in the province of Bohuslän. Since 2010 it has belonged to the Torslanda-Björlanda parish.
En kort promenad härifrån, bredvid Bromm: A short walk from here, next to Bromma Church, is Stockholm's smallest and oldest school, Bromma kyrkskola, from 1864. Around the mid-1890s, a primary school teacher taught here who was at the same time parish clerk, organist and vaccinator. Before that, children had learned to read and write in a small room in Gamla Klockargården, the old parish clerk's house next door, because the parish clerk had had that duty since the mid-1600s.
En kyrka som slutat vara kyrka finns en: A church that has stopped being a church is a short walk from here. Lövgärdet Church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016, meaning it was formally taken out of religious use. Before that it managed to change parishes: from 1973 it belonged to Gunnared parish and in its final years to Angered. Lövgärdet itself is a neighbourhood in the Gårdsten district in north-eastern Gothenburg.
En promenad bort ligger Slätta damm, som: A short walk away is Slätta damm, a pond that was formed around 1860 in S.A. Hedlund's park. By the pond there's a barbecue area and a waffle café, and in cold winters people skate on the ice. It's mostly ducks and goldeneyes swimming here. The park is part of Hisingsparken, Gothenburg's largest park area.
En riktig kuriosa: på J. Sigfrid Edström: A real curiosity: on J. Sigfrid Edströms gata, traffic drives on the left, even though the rest of Sweden drives on the right. That's because of the way the tracks into and out of the Vagnhallen Rantorget tram depot are built. The street is named after the first director of Gothenburg's tramways. In Gårdahallen next door, the tram society Spårvägssällskapet Ringlinien keeps the city's vintage trams and vintage buses.
En väderkvarn som har flyttat två gånger: A windmill that has moved twice! Kälvesta kvarn, also called Lilla Stampan, was built in the 1600s and first stood on a hill by Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm. In 1884 it was moved to Lunda, and in 1892 it came to its current spot on Skestavägen in Solhem, a short walk from here.
Enebyberg är ett villasamhälle med cirka: Enebyberg is a villa community of about 5,000 residents, characterised by houses from the first half of the 20th century. The district belongs to Danderyd but borders both Täby and Sollentuna. A couple of blocks away is Eneby Church on Eneby torg, where the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden share the same church.
Enligt legenden växte helgonet Sankt Bot: According to legend, the saint Sankt Botvid grew up at Hammarby gård, a little way from here by Prästviken bay on Lake Aspen – and it is after him that Botkyrka is named. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main building from 1804 served as the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument by the church.
Eriksberg var ett av Göteborgs stora var: Eriksberg was one of Gothenburg's big shipyards. The gigantic gantry crane that still stands here is a reminder of that time and has become a landmark for the whole riverside.
Essingeleden svävar förbi här på Blommen: The Essingeleden motorway glides past here on the Blommensberg viaduct, which spans the Vinterviken valley and almost passes over the roofs of Blommensberg school. The bridge opened on 21 August 1966. Just a stone's throw away is Stora Fågelsången, an 18th-century farm by the lake Trekanten, where the garden has become allotments without cabins. A little further on stands Sankt Sigfrid's church, a red wooden church that was moved here from Vasastaden in 1904.
Ett hotell man bor i på riktigt! Hässelb: A hotel people actually live in! When it opened in 1955, Hässelby familjehotell, the family hotel, was the builder Olle Engkvist's largest co-housing block. The professional services were discontinued in 1976, but the residents still run some activities on a voluntary basis. Its neighbour, Hässelby ungdomshotell, the youth hotel, originally contained flats for young people, flats for pensioners, art studios and a day nursery.
Ett litet namnskämt: tunnelbanestationen: A little naming joke: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg, but in Riksby. Before the metro arrived, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals of glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are inspired by the tiled stations of the tram era. Nearby is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955.
Ett lokstall som heter Sundbyberg fast d: An engine shed called Sundbyberg, even though it's in Solna! The old steam locomotive shed and the water tower building were put up in 1904 by the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen Railway, and SJ named them Sundbyberg because they were close to that station. The buildings are well preserved and of very high cultural and historical value. The nearby Huvudstaleden road was meant to be part of an urban motorway, but was only partly built.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Kvarnto: A couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a runic rock slab discovered in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård. It bears the word "stepsons", unusual in runic inscriptions. Nearby is the Näsbydal housing area, shaped like an egg, with 900 flats ranging from one room to seven rooms on two floors. The neighbouring area of Grindtorp lies by Täby's former horse-racing track.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Tacksäg: A couple of hundred metres away is Tacksägelsekyrkan, the Church of Thanksgiving, also called Trångsund Church. It was designed by the architect Sture Frölén and consecrated in 1957, when Trångsund grew into a town. It was the parish church until Mariakyrkan in Skogås took over the role in 1987. By the church there's a memorial grove and a small burial ground.
Ett par hundra meter bort står Tibble ky: A couple of hundred metres away stands Tibble Church, which has been called the cathedral of Roslagen and is both a church and the administrative centre of Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby centrum, and its library keeps two Viking Age runestone fragments found in Lissby in 1930. One of them measures only 47 by 46 centimetres.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån ligger Hög: A couple of hundred metres from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined after 1945 until the late 1950s. The rock also hid rare minerals such as monazite and columbite. Today the quarries are part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve, where the small lake Axlemossen also lies.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån låg Hörnin: A couple of hundred metres from here stood Hörningsnäs gård, a manor and large estate in Huddinge parish, by today's Parkhemsvägen. The farm buildings burned down in the 1950s, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further away is Lake Trehörningen, where you may spot bats and protected frogs and toads.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån stod Hagst: A couple of hundred metres from here stood Hagstaeken, a huge oak in Glömsta. Measured by trunk circumference, it was the largest of the ten oaks protected as natural monuments in Huddinge municipality. On the night of 3 December 2025 it was felled for safety reasons, following a government decision and despite protests. A little further away opens up Glömstadalen, a valley that is of cultural-heritage interest in the municipality.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån står Stens: A couple of hundred metres from here stands Stensjö church, one of two churches in Stensjön parish. A little further away, at the very top of Kvarnbygatan's steep hill, the so-called Mölndals kråka, is the Mölndal City Museum. It has a café serving lunch on weekdays and coffee with pastries at weekends, a well-deserved reward after that hill.
Ett par kvarter bort ligger Atlantisområ: A couple of blocks away is the Atlantis area, a terraced-house village from the 1950s that drew international attention and where Olof Palme lived with his family between 1968 and 1983. Further away, in Beckomberga, stood the mental hospital Beckomberga sjukhus, built between 1930 and 1932 and in operation until it closed in 1995. Since the mid-2000s the old hospital buildings have been converted into homes.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Filmstaden H: A couple of minutes away is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's largest cinema, with eighteen screens and a total of 4,166 seats. It is part of Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen Centre attracts 30 million visitors a year. Long before the popcorn arrived, this was the site of the croft Sadelmakartorp, the saddler's croft, with roots in the late 17th century, which became a schoolhouse after 1860.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Högdalens sk: A couple of minutes away is Högdalen skatepark, also called Highvalley Skateworld, a whole skate world in concrete with a freestyle area, a children's area, the Mega Ditch and a bowl ride. At around 5,500 square metres, it is Stockholm's largest. Its neighbour is the Cyklopen culture house, run entirely by volunteers, and a little further on is Högdalen centre, planned with Vällingby centre as its model.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Skärisbiogra: A couple of minutes away is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is part of Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, Stockholm's culture house and city theatre. Its neighbours are the Red Cross folk high school, with courses with an international and humanitarian focus, and the old Skärholmen upper secondary school from 1974. Beneath it all are traces of Smista gård, a farm dating back to the 800s in the Viking Age.
Ett par minuter bort snurrar Vridande mo: A couple of minutes away turns Vridande moment, "Torque", also known as Skruven, the Screw, the steel sculpture by Aston Forsberg that has become the signature of Skärholmen centrum. It won first prize in an ideas competition in 1968. Skärholmen centrum had 15 million visitors in 2013, and nearby is Kungens kurva with the world's second-largest IKEA store, which together make the area the largest out-of-town shopping area in the Nordic countries.
Ett par minuter härifrån börjar Ulriksda: A couple of minutes from here, Ulriksdal nature reserve begins, about 32 hectares between Brunnsviken and Edsviken bays, created in 1988. It also contains Mellanjärva burial ground with its ancient graves. In the palace park stands Villa Beylon, a pink-rendered brick villa from 1803 next to Ulriksdal Palace Theatre, a state listed building since 1935.
Ett par minuter härifrån ligger Björkäng: A couple of minutes from here is Björkängen sports ground, with a football pitch and two ice rinks where Huddinge IK play their home ice hockey matches. One of the rinks used to be called Nickehallen, after the club stalwart Bengt "Nicke" Nilsson. Until 2018 the area belonged to the municipal district of Stuvsta-Snättringe, which was then split so that Stuvsta and Snättringe became districts of their own.
Ett par minuter härifrån står runstenarn: A couple of minutes from here are the runestones on Häradsvägen, a Viking Age pair. One of them has had an adventurous life: in the 1800s it was used as a doorstep in Lindal, disappeared for a while and was found again in 1938 lying on a burial mound at Skälby gård. The other was given a fanciful interpretation by Olof Rudbeck the Elder in his work Atlantica.
Ett par minuter härifrån, längs Hallunda: A couple of minutes from here, along the Hallunda cultural trail opposite Slagsta motel, is a rock carving that was only discovered in 1971. Nearby is Slagsta gård, a historic manor, and down by Lake Mälaren is Slagstabadet, an EU-designated bathing site with excellent water quality. One of Slagsta's two brickworks used to be there, and in the forest you can still see terraces and remains of house foundations.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Lå: A couple of minutes' walk away is Långsjö farm, on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön. It has two identical main buildings, and there's a touching explanation: the businessman Robert Ditzinger had them built in 1882, one house for each of his two sons. The farm dates back to the 17th century and has given its name to the whole district of Långsjö.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Ty: A couple of minutes' walk away is Tyresövallen, which used to be called Bollmoravallen. It is the home ground of Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns and holds about 2,700 spectators. Tyresö ice rink is in the same area, and a little further away the glazed Tyresö centrum awaits, with the municipal hall and library.
Ett par stenkast bort, i Sundby, ligger: A couple of stone's throws away, in Sundby, are two runic rock slabs side by side: U 80, a large and elaborate one, and U 81, which was never finished. The Sundby district counts as part of Old Spånga, and the name has been known since 1312, even though the district itself was only formed in 1953, on land that the City of Stockholm had bought from Spånga in 1949.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Hagsätra centru: A stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local centre, opened in 1960, the same year the metro reached here. Keep an eye out for "Barnet med käpphästen", the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further away there's also an outdoor pool with a funny name: Älvsjöbadet, which despite its name isn't in Älvsjö at all but here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Älta kyrka, int: A stone's throw away is Älta Church, next to Ältavägen. The road was built in 1934 and winds just over eight kilometres through the undeveloped landscape between Älta and Nackanäs. The neighbouring area of Stensö bears a memory of the water: the peninsula was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip Stensö bathing beach beckons.
Ett stenkast bort står Vårby gårds kyrka: A stone's throw away stands Vårby gård church, regarded as one of Sweden's first postmodern buildings, colourful and imaginative. It was consecrated on 25 May 1975 and sits on a slope facing Lake Mälaren, next to a Viking Age burial ground. And just south-west of the church, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard, a silver treasure, was found in 1871.
Ett stenkast härifrån breder Rålambshovs: A stone's throw from here, Rålambshovsparken spreads out, known locally as Rålis, named after the old Rålambshov estate. The park was laid out around the same time as Västerbron, the Western Bridge, in the 1930s, and Lilla Västerbron, the Little Western Bridge, spans right across it. By the square is also Riksarkivet, the National Archives, whose main building was completed in 1968 when the archives moved here from Gamla Riksarkivet, the Old National Archives, on Riddarholmen.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Albykistan,: A stone's throw from here is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist, a type of grave from the late Stone Age that is very rare in the Lake Mälaren region. Only seven are known in the whole of Stockholm County, and this one has been dated to around 1800 BC. From the Stone Age to the circus: Alby is also home to Subtopia, where Cirkus Cirkör is based.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Bullegumman: A stone's throw from here is Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, named after Mrs Liljegren, who in the 1930s sold home-baked buns through a hatch in the wall of her house to the children on their way to Påvelundsskolan. The house was later used for a time as a reception centre for refugees and still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there in 2011.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Kristineber: A stone's throw from here is Kristineberg Castle, a castle-like manor that was once a malmgård, a country house on the city's outskirts, and still preserves much of its 18th-century character. People have lived privately in the main building since the 1930s, and in the wings the children attend Kristinebergsskolan school. By Fredhällsparken park was the Tranan cinema, where films were shown from 1933 to 1961.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger en teater s: A stone's throw from here is a theatre that was once a barn. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is the stage for six different amateur theatre societies, gathered under a joint umbrella organisation. These days it mostly offers revues and comedies created by young people, and the building also has an English theatre group.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Ågestaverke: A stone's throw from here is the Ågesta plant, Ågestaverket, also called R3 or Adam – Sweden's first nuclear power plant to supply energy to consumers. It mostly provided district heating to Farsta, so it was called the nuclear heating plant. The reactor used heavy water and natural uranium. The plant closed in 1974 but largely remains standing and has found a new life as a training ground for Stockholm's fire service.
Ett stenkast härifrån låg Råsunda fotbol: A stone's throw from here stood Råsunda football stadium. The World Cup final was played there on 29 June 1958, when Brazil beat Sweden 5–2 in front of almost 50,000 spectators. The stadium closed in 2012, when the new national arena in Arenastaden was completed, and the site has since been redeveloped into homes and offices.
Ett stenkast härifrån står Ängbystenen,: A stone's throw from here stands Ängbystenen, runestone U 60, on a small hill in the middle of the residential area. It's the stone that gave its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, and the surrounding streets also have names linked to runes and the Viking Age. A little further away is Björklunds hage, Bromma's best-preserved burial ground from the early Viking Age, and the manor Stora Ängby, whose main building was put up in the last years of the 1600s.
Ett stycke härifrån slingrar sig Bällsta: Not far from here winds the Bällstaån stream, which in its upper reaches is also called Spångaån. It starts on a hill in Viksjö and has a really adventurous journey: under Spånga it runs through a tunnel about 1.4 kilometres long, and further on it crosses the Solvalla trotting track lengthwise, right through the track's green infield.
Fagersjö började som en del av Södertörn: Fagersjö began as part of Södertörns villastad, a planned villa town. A little way from here stands Villa Edvardshäll, the very first villa in the Fagersjö part, built in 1903 just north of the then-new Nynäs railway line. The builder, the machine worker Axel Edvard Samuelsson, named the house after himself, and it became something of a custom among the pioneers in Fagersjö to give their villa their own name.
Fagersjö ligger utmed sjön Magelungens n: Fagersjö lies along the northern shore of Lake Magelungen, and here you'll find Högdalstoppen, two of Stockholm's highest points, with sweeping views over southern Stockholm. The street also has a little story of its own: Villa Lundin, known as "the Castle", once had the address Vildandsvägen 14. The Lundin family is said to have owned one of Fagersjö's two cars in the 1930s.
Faggens krog är en nästan musealt bevara: Faggens krog is an almost museum-like preserved 18th-century townhouse that Carl Michael Bellman sang about, and it has housed both a tavern and a cloth factory. Just below the music pavilion on Vita bergen stood Ceders Café, where the Ceder family served summer fika – coffee and cake – from the 1910s. Later the youth movement Vitabergsklubben, led by the author Per Anders Fogelström, used the building, before it was destroyed by arson in 1969 and 1970.
Falutorget fick 1883 sitt namn efter Fal: Falutorget got its name in 1883 after Falun, the end point of the Bergslagsbanan railway, and the ground here was reed marsh in the Göta älv river right up until the 1860s. For a long time the square was dominated by Gasklockan, the gasholder, an 86-metre-tall round structure visible over large parts of Gothenburg. It was taken out of service in 1993 and demolished in 2017, after delays caused partly by peregrine falcons.
Falutorget fick sitt namn 1883 efter Fal: Falutorget got its name in 1883 after Falun, the end point of the Bergslagsbanan railway, whose station building was nearby. Until the 1860s the land was reeds and part of the Göta älv river, until dredging created new land. For a long time, the Gasklockan gasholder rose here, 86 metres tall and visible from large parts of the city. It was taken out of service in 1993, and its demolition in 2017 was delayed by, among other things, peregrine falcons.
Farsta centrum invigdes den 23 oktober 1: Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was big for its time, escalators and all. The car park was one of Europe's largest, with space for 4,000 cars. To shorten the walk to the shops, moving walkways were installed to carry customers from their cars. Farsta was called the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby.
Farsta gård och Farstastenen: Farsta gård and the Farsta runestone
Farsta gård vid Magelungen har rötter än: Farsta gård by Lake Magelungen has roots going all the way back to the 14th century, and today the Farsta association council, with around 70 member associations, runs the activities at the farm. There you'll also find Farstastenen, the only surviving runestone in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. The stone was re-erected in 1875 and stands by the footpath from the farm down towards Farstabadet.
Farsta torg, ett par minuter härifrån, a: Farsta torg, a couple of minutes from here, was laid out as an Italian piazza and opened on 23 October 1960. The long, narrow square, 180 by 100 metres, has a convex shape that may have been inspired by Piazza delle Erbe in Verona, and there is a market with fruit and flowers here most days. Its neighbour is the former Farsta gymnasium, a secondary school where the Adolf Fredrik music classes are now based.
Farstaviken sträcker sig från Baggensfjä: Farstaviken bay stretches from Baggensfjärden in towards Gustavsberg, the main town of Värmdö municipality, about 20 kilometres east of Stockholm. Here nature itself has redrawn the map: because of post-glacial land uplift, the islands of Farstalandet and Ormingelandet have grown together. At the same time, places like Mörtnäs, Hemmesta and Torsby have merged with Gustavsberg.
Feskekôrka, räkmacka vid vattnet: Feskekôrka fish market, and a prawn sandwich by the water
Filmhuset: Filmhuset, the Swedish Film Institute building
Filmstaden i Råsunda: Filmstaden in Råsunda, the old film studios
Finansmannen Ernest Thiel lät Ferdinand: The financier Ernest Thiel had Ferdinand Boberg design a villa in Viennese Art Nouveau style, and since 1924 it has been the art museum Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery. Here hang works by Bruno Liljefors, Ernst Josephson, Carl Larsson, August Strindberg and Anders Zorn, among others, but also Edvard Munch, Paul Gauguin and Toulouse-Lautrec. Right next to it, on a south-facing slope by Blockhusudden, is the memorial to the victims of the 2004 tsunami disaster, Gravitational Ripples by Lea Porsager.
Finnboda varv anlades 1874 som filial ti: The Finnboda shipyard was founded in 1874 as a branch of the Bergsund shipyard. The shipyard area has since become a mixed district. The old workshops, such as the joinery, the steam-engine workshop and the canteen, now house homes, offices and shops. The yard's workers used to live on Finnbodaberget, Skatberget and Finnberget, among other places.
Fiskebäck är stadsdelen där Göteborg möt: Fiskebäck is the district where Gothenburg meets the sea at the southern archipelago. It covers 561 hectares and borders Hinsholmen and Långedrag to the north and Önnered to the south. The name, "fish brook", gives away what was once most important here, and the closeness to the water still shapes the area.
Fisksätra, inklämt mellan Lännerstasunde: Fisksätra, squeezed between Lännerstasundet strait and the Nacka forests, is Sweden's most densely populated urban area, with 7,724 residents per square kilometre. Lännerstasundet is a strait of the Baltic Sea on the border between the Boo and Nacka districts. Fisksätra is also home to the Toy and Collectors' Museum, a museum devoted entirely to toys and play.
Flatenbadet är stadens största friluftsb: Flatenbadet is the city's largest outdoor bathing spot, and Stockholm Vatten, the water company, considers Lake Flaten to be Stockholm's cleanest lake. The buildings were designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist, and the facility opened on 23 June 1934. All around stretches the Flaten nature reserve, Stockholm's largest, which even has a racing track for radio-controlled model cars.
Flemingsbergs industriområde anlades på: Flemingsberg's industrial area was laid out in the 1960s, and Billman-Regulator's factory from the early 1960s is still here. The street name Regulatorvägen remembers the electronics company. Now there may be real culture: the municipality is planning space for activities that the Royal Swedish Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, have in Nacka. This is also home to the Labour Movement Archives and Library, the oldest of its kind in the world.
Flera gator i trakten har fått sina namn: Several streets in the area are named after a sawmill. Sörensens gata honours the sawmill master Nils Georg Sörensen, whose sawmill company, Säfveåns AB, also gave its name to Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget. On a hill by Stabbetorget stands Björkekärr Church. A little further away is Queen Silvia Children's Hospital, Sweden's largest children's hospital.
Flysta är i huvudsak en villastadsdel, m: Flysta is mainly a villa district, but it holds a little mystery. There was once a Viking Age runestone here, known as Uppland runic inscription 70, and it has been searched for several times without being found. It has probably been lost. The neighbouring district of Sundby counts as part of Old Spånga, and its name is known all the way back to 1312.
Fontänen Elementens kamp: The fountain Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements
Fontänen Tors fiske: The Tors fiske fountain, Thor's Fishing
Forsån, en bit härifrån, är en liten å m: Forsån, a little way from here, is a small river with a big job: in just 1.4 kilometres it links lakes Magelungen and Drevviken and is part of the Tyresån lake system. It flows mostly calmly and marks the boundary between the City of Stockholm and Huddinge municipality. North of Drevviken is Orhem, a district that consists mostly of nature in the Flaten nature reserve.
Fotbollsplanen ligger på mark som förr h: The football pitch lies on land that used to be called Söderlingska ängen, Söderling's Meadow, after the organ builder Johan Nikolaus Söderling. He was the first to suggest that Slottsskogen should become a park. Majvallen was built as relief work from 1946 and opened on 5 June 1949, at a cost of just over 327,000 kronor. Today Göteborgs FF, among others, play their home matches here.
Fotbollsstadion Råsunda fick en smygprem: Råsunda football stadium had a soft opening in April 1937 with a match between AIK and Malmö FF, and was then Sweden's largest sports facility. The official opening was performed in May of the same year by King Gustaf V, at a match between Sweden and England. The stadium was the national arena for the men's national team and AIK's home ground up to and including 2012. As early as 1910, Råsunda IP sports ground had opened nearby, and AIK also played some matches there.
Fotografiska vid Stadsgårdskajen: Fotografiska, the photography museum, on Stadsgårdskajen
Fotö är en liten ö i Göteborgs norra skä: Fotö is a small island in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, just 0.70 square kilometres in size but with just over six hundred permanent residents. Yew grows here, which the islanders call barlind. On the east side there's a swimming spot, and the south side has a sheltered harbour. Climb up to the island's higher parts on a clear day and you can see all the way to Vinga.
Fotö är en riktig miniatyrvärld: 621 bof: Fotö is a real miniature world: 621 permanent residents share an area of just 0.70 square kilometres. The south side has a sheltered harbour and on the east side there's an inviting bathing spot. The island is also known for its yew, locally called "barlind", and from the higher rocks you can see Vinga when the weather is clear.
Framför biblioteket en bit härifrån står: In front of the library a little way from here stand nine granite animals. This is Fredens rike, the Peaceable Kingdom, a play sculpture by Pye Engström, who lived in the area for a whole month to get to know the place. The title comes from the Book of Isaiah, about a kingdom of peace where former enemies will live side by side. The animals are carved in black, red and grey granite, and the whole group is made as a play sculpture.
Fredens rike: Fredens rike, the Kingdom of Peace
Frescati hage vid Brunnsviken hette tidi: Frescati hage, the meadow by Brunnsviken bay, used to be called Norrbrunnshagen, after the Norra Brunn tavern, and in 1897 the State Entomological Institute was built here, researching insect pests in agriculture. On the shore, Brunnsviken Canoe Club paddles, founded in 1909. A little further away is Södra huset, the university's building complex, which because of its sky-blue facade is sometimes called the Blue Houses.
Fridhems kyrkogård, alldeles intill, rym: Fridhem Cemetery, right next to us, has about 5,627 Christian grave plots. It is also home to one of the Church of Sweden's three Islamic burial grounds in Gothenburg. The cemetery opened in 1968, and until 1982 a mobile church had to serve as its chapel. A little further away is the manor Bäckebols gård.
Fridhems kyrkogård, en bit härifrån, inv: Fridhem cemetery, a little way from here, opened on 20 November 1968. For fourteen whole years a portable church had to serve as a temporary chapel, before the current chapel was consecrated in 1982 by Bishop Bertil Gärtner. The cemetery covers a full 87 hectares and holds about 5,627 grave plots.
Fridhemsplan är en av Kungsholmens stora: Fridhemsplan is one of Kungsholmen's major hubs, with the metro, buses and shops. In the 16th century, Kungsholmen was called Munklägret, 'the Monks' Camp', after the monks who owned land here.
Friedländerska kyrkogården: Friedländerska kyrkogården, the Friedländer Jewish cemetery
Frihamnen var förr en hamn där varor kun: Frihamnen, the Free Port, used to be a harbour where goods could be stored without customs duty. Now a new district is growing up here. Shortly we'll cross Göta älv on Hisingsbron, a lift bridge that opened in 2021 and replaced the old Götaälvbron.
Frihetens port: Frihetens port, the Gate of Freedom
Frimurarhemmet, ritat av arkitekten Ludw: Frimurarhemmet, the Freemasons' Home, designed by the architect Ludwig Peterson, consists of eleven buildings, the first of which was ready to move into in 1912. Elderly Freemasons and their relatives from all over Sweden could apply for a home here, and since 2007 the buildings have been owned by a housing cooperative. The neighbouring district of Gångsätra, like so much on Lidingö, began as a farm and is mentioned in writing as early as 1379.
Fritidshusområdet Kungshättan på östra d: The holiday-home area of Kungshättan, on the eastern part of the island of Kungshatt, had a full 87 holiday homes on 30 hectares in 2010. The island has a long history: in 1531 the Crown acquired an outlying plot on the island, then probably called Serszöön, from the village of Norrby on Lovön. The neighbouring island of Fågelön is also in eastern Lake Mälaren.
Fruängen blev egen stadsdel den 1 februa: Fruängen became a district of its own on 1 February 1948, when it was split off from the district of Västberga. The buildings of Fruängen School were built between 1956 and 1960 to designs by the architect Ture Ryberg and have been given a green listing by the City Museum. Much earlier, around 1650, the croft Istorp appeared, also known as Komöte. It no longer exists today.
Fruängens station är den högst belägna i: Fruängen station is the highest in the entire metro network, 46.8 metres above sea level. Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady, has an unusual history: the church centre opened in 1963, but the actual church hall shown on the drawings only began to be built in 2004 and was consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent in 2005. A block away stands Triangelhuset, the Triangle House, from 1955, named after its unique triangular floor plan.
Fräntorp bebyggdes under 1930-talet med: Fräntorp was built up in the 1930s with prefabricated small houses, which the future homeowners put up together. Stone was quarried on the rocky hills of Valåsen and Källeberget from the mid-19th century to the early 20th century, and on the high ground above the motorway there are ancient remains. The People's House, Folkets hus, stands where the main building of the Fräntorp estate once was.
Från 1895 till 1994 marscherade soldater: From 1895 to 1994 soldiers marched in the barracks area. Today the buildings are listed, with a restaurant, a market and museums. The Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, holds over 15,000 objects, and since 2005 also the boxer Ingemar Johansson's collection of prizes. The former horse hospital has housed a military history museum.
Från Burö färjeläge på Hälsö går Nordöle: From Burö ferry terminal on Hälsö, the Nordöleden ferry route runs out to the islands of Knippla, Hyppeln and Rörö, furthest out in the Kattegat. It is served by the ferries Nordö III, Ulrika and Linda, and it's the only one of the Swedish Transport Administration's ferry routes that runs between more than two ferry terminals. Hälsö itself is a small island of 1.28 square kilometres.
Från Kärrtorp når man ända bort till Nac: From Kärrtorp you can reach all the way to the Nacka Reserve, Nackareservatet, in Nacka municipality, so the forest is never far away. Closer at hand is the Reflexen cinema, which has been showing films since 1961, and the Kärrtorp sports hall, Kärrtorpshallen, from the early 1960s, designed by Kjell Ödeen and given a green listing by the City Museum. Kärrtorp Park only got its current name in 2009, but in its southern part stands the old crofter's cottage that gave the district its name.
Från Ropsten går Lidingöbanan över Lidin: From Ropsten, the Lidingöbanan light rail runs across the Lidingö Bridge out to Lidingö. The bridge opened in 1925 and was for a long time the only land link to the island.
Från Tappström går pendelbåten linje 89: From Tappström, commuter boat line 89 runs all the way to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay in Stockholm, with boats including M/S Lux. In the Tappström strait, where the boundary between the islands of Lovön and Ekerön runs, there's also a guest harbour for leisure boats. A little further away was Tappsund brickworks, founded in the late 19th century and closed in 1959.
Från slutet av 1800-talet och under 1900: From the late 19th century and through the 20th century, Albano was an industrial area. Today it is instead dominated by Campus Albano, the joint campus of Stockholm University and KTH Royal Institute of Technology, which opened in September 2023, with around 1,000 student flats. The area is also home to Nordita, the Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics, which was created in 1957 on the initiative of Niels Bohr among others, and which moved from Copenhagen to Stockholm in 2006.
Från toppen av Väsjöbacken, en bit bort,: From the top of Väsjöbacken, a little way off, on a clear day you can see Stockholm's inner city and the Globe arena to the south, and far to the north the Arlanda control tower. The ski slope has four runs and a vertical drop of 82 metres. A little further still, in Rösjö nature reserve, stands Jarlabanke's stone from the late 1000s, along an ancient path towards Täby.
Frölunda Torg öppnade 1966 och var ett a: Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 and was one of Sweden's first large suburban shopping centres. All around lies Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin.
Frölundaborg invigdes 12 september 1967: Frölundaborg opened on 12 September 1967 with a shock result: Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. The arena holds just over 6,000 spectators and is still used by Frölunda HC. Next to it runs Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way. It used to be called Viljo Nousiainens Gångväg, after the coach who took Patrik Sjöberg, Stefan Holm and Christian Olsson to great success at Slottsskogsvallen stadium.
Fullersta gård, några minuter härifrån,: Fullersta gård, a few minutes from here, is a former noble estate that since 2009 has been run as an art gallery, with a permanent exhibition including works by Peter Dahl and Ewert Karlsson – and a café. Even closer is Fullersta bio, where an old cinema and former Konsum co-op shops have become an art gallery and theatre.
Furulundskyrkan är lite ovanlig: den är: Furulundskyrkan is a little unusual: it is a joint church shared by EFS, a revival movement within the Church of Sweden, and the Furulund-Öjersjö parish. A little way from here hides Prästtjärnen, a small lake which, despite its modest size, is a full 14 metres deep. It lies just over 108 metres above sea level and is part of the main Göta älv drainage basin.
Furåsens kyrka ligger alldeles intill, m: Furåsen church is right next door, but a little way from here is a street with a sweet story. In the 1930s a Mrs Liljegren lived around here and baked buns that the children on their way to Påvelundsskolan school couldn't resist. She opened a hatch in the wall of her house and sold the buns from there, and so she became Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. Today the street bears her nickname.
Fynda på Bellevue marknad: Hunt for bargains at Bellevue market
Fynda på Kvibergs marknad: Hunt for bargains at Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market
Fyra vägar möts vid Bellevue i Gamlestad: Four roads meet at Bellevue in Gamlestaden: Generalgatan, Artillerigatan, Kvibergsvägen and Kortedalavägen. Around the junction there are kiosks, hairdressers and restaurants, and at Bellevue market people hunt for bargains among second-hand goods. At the nearby country estate Mariedal, the ball-bearing giant SKF had its office from 1910 to 1914.
Färingsö är runstenarnas land. En bit hä: Färingsö is the land of runestones. A short distance from here, in Eneby, stands a Viking Age runestone whose carver, according to the experts, was not a skilled rune artist, but the pattern resembles another stone, so perhaps the same man was behind both. In Törnby there is a runic inscription on an embedded boulder of reddish granite, which a man named Saxe had carved in memory of his mother, but sadly the mother's name has been lost.
Färjan Älvsnabben över älven: The Älvsnabben ferry across the river
Fässbergs kyrka ligger strax intill, och: Fässberg Church is right next to us, and between 1922 and 1976 it was actually called Mölndal Church. Fässberg district has the largest population of any district in both the province and the county. Very close by is also Fässbergs Bio, a cinema with 400 seats in the old secondary school assembly hall, which has been converted into an event venue.
Få byggnader har bytt skepnad som Hammar: Few buildings have changed shape like Hammarkullen church. It was a parish church in Angered parish but was deconsecrated in 2011 and became a preschool. After that the building was transformed once more, and today it houses Hammarkullen mosque.
Fåfängan, kafé med utsikt: Fåfängan, a café with a view
Författaren Gösta Langenfelt kallade nam: In 1944 the writer Gösta Langenfelt called the name Alléparken, the Avenue Park, “a monstrosity”, because there was neither a park nor an avenue here. It later turned out that an avenue really had led to the croft Asplund, and a few trees still stand. Next door are the “English terraced houses”, 43 terraced houses from 1919–1920. Up on Alviksberget, Elfvinggården was built in 1939–1940, a collective housing block for single, educated women.
Förr reste sig Tyskbagarbergen på platse: The Tyskbagarbergen hills once rose here, named after the baker Martin Kammecker from Mecklenburg, who built windmills on his land in the 1600s. One of them stood at the far end of Jungfrugatan. The hills were in the way of traffic, so the passage Karl XV:s port was blasted through so that Nybrogatan could reach up to Valhallavägen. That is where you now find the monumental red-brick building of the Swedish Patent and Registration Office, designed by Ragnar Östberg.
Förr slingrade sig Ekerövägen genom skar: Ekerövägen used to wind through sharp, narrow bends right here, between Tillflykten and Lindö lada. In 1994 they blasted straight through the rock instead: the Lindö tunnel is 178 metres long. The result was fewer accidents and shorter queues at rush hour.
Gallhålans naturreservat bildades 1988 o: The Gallhålan nature reserve was formed in 1988 and expanded in 2013 to 96 hectares. Besides oak woodland, there are alder swamps, rocky pine forest and a hay meadow, and among the shrubs hazel, guelder rose and alder buckthorn. The reserve lies on the eastern slope of the Tahult drumlin, a long glacial ridge that drops steeply down to the small lake Agntjärnen, and the birdlife is rich.
Gamla Boråsvägen en bit härifrån var en: The old Gamla Boråsvägen road, a little way from here, was once Gothenburg's main way in and out, part of national road 5 from 1945 to the 1950s. The narrow, steep and winding stretch was called Kallebäcks lider and was feared by both motorists and horse drivers. Just south of the road, Örgryte IS train at ÖIS-gården, where one of the pitches has been called Hammarviken Arena since 2013.
Gamla Danderyds socken var en gång rätt: The old parish of Danderyd was once rather sparsely populated: in 1905, 3,605 people lived here, in an area that today holds Djursholm, Stocksund, Enebyberg, Mörby and Nora. The parish church, Danderyd Church, is a little way from here next to the E18. And in nearby Rinkeby there was once a runestone fragment, U 132, which disappeared in the second half of the 19th century.
Gamla Filmstaden: Gamla Filmstaden, the old film studios
Gamla Huddingevägen var en gång en del a: Gamla Huddingevägen was once part of the real Huddingevägen road. But through traffic straight through the villa suburb of Örby got so heavy that the road was rerouted in 1971, north of the district. A little way from here is Stockholmsmässan, Sweden's largest exhibition and congress centre, and the Scandic Talk Hotel, regarded as the trademark of the exhibition centre.
Gamla Kungälv i trä omger hållplatsen. R: Old wooden Kungälv surrounds the stop. The town hall on Gamla torget, the Old Square, has become a symbol of the old town, and along Västra gatan stand several of the town's oldest houses. Zetterlöfska huset was built in 1762, and Strandska huset, with its gateways, double staircase and cobbled courtyard, was built by the merchant David Werming. Thorildska huset has been both a school and a telegraph station.
Gamla Kvibergs regemente har fått nya li: The old Kviberg regiment has been given new lives. In the former horse stables is Kvibergs marknad, a market with 160 stalls full of antiques, curiosities, books and toys. And just north of the barracks rises Prioritet Serneke Arena, the Nordic region's largest multi-sport complex, with an indoor ski slope and a 1.2-kilometre ski track.
Gamla Stockholmsvägen, alldeles i närhet: Gamla Stockholmsvägen, the old Stockholm road close by, links Snättringe and Glömsta. Further along the same road is Nytorp, a former croft dating back to the mid-1600s, where coffee is served today: an old croft cottage that has become a café.
Gamla flygfältet kallas det också, Torsl: It's also called the old airfield: Torslanda airfield, which was laid out in 1923 a little way from here on the west side of Hisingen, about 15 kilometres from central Gothenburg. For more than fifty years it was the city's airport, until Landvetter replaced it in 1977. Today Torslanda is known above all for Volvo's car factory, the Torslanda Works.
Gamla stans gränder: The alleys of Gamla stan, the Old Town
Gamlestaden är just det, den gamla stade: Gamlestaden is exactly that – the old town. Nya Lödöse was founded here in 1473, long before today's Gothenburg was laid out in 1621. Later the area became industrial, and this is where the ball-bearing company SKF grew up.
Gamlestadens fabriker, mat och design: Gamlestadens fabriker – food and design in the old factories
Gamlestadsvägen, en bit härifrån, är en: Gamlestadsvägen, a little way from here, is a major road running parallel to the E45 through Bagaregården, Gamlestaden and Olskroken. It got its name in 1883, after the Gamlestaden district. The road crosses the Säveån river on the Gamlestad bridge, passes Nylöse Church and continues towards the Lärje interchange. Fredrikshamn redoubt, from 1645, is also nearby.
Gamlestadsvägen, som löper alldeles inti: Gamlestadsvägen, which runs right next to us, got its name as early as 1883, after the district of Gamlestaden. A little further away is Hospitalskyrkogården, also called Nylöse hospital cemetery, which was the cemetery of the hospital parish from as far back as the late 16th century. The gravestones are almost gone, but a Franciscan friary also once stood on the same spot.
Gatan fick sitt namn 1888 efter Albert L: The street got its name in 1888 after Albert Lindhagen, the man behind Stockholm's great street-planning schemes. Nearby was Gamla Stadshagen, sometimes called Guldgrävarlägret, the Gold Diggers' Camp, with about 350 emergency homes for working-class families from 1917 to 1965. And Thorildsplan is named after the writer Thomas Thorild, who described in his letters how he sought out the Kungsholmen parks to enjoy the view.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter Johannisd: The street is named after Johannisdalsgården, a croft recorded in writing since the 1770s and demolished in the 1940s. Much of today's Mälarhöjden grew up on the farm's land, and the Johannisgården block also recalls the old property. A little way off is Fruängen centre, opened in 1962 and given a green listing by the City Museum.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter markland,: The street is named after markland, an old unit for valuing land. Right next to it is the Frölundaborg ice stadium. It opened in 1967 with a friendly match in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. By Slottsskogsvallen, where high jumpers such as Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, winds Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way.
Gatan minns adelsätten Eketrä, som från: The street remembers the noble Eketrä family, who from the 18th century owned the Västra Pilegården estate right up until 1875, just where the asphalt is today. This is also where the Bräcke tram line turned off southwards. The line was closed in 1968 and dismantled in the 1980s, but the embankment remains almost untouched, like a trace from another time.
Gatan är en bit av en riktig kungsväg. G: This street is part of a real royal road. Gustav III opened his own road to Drottningholm Palace on 19 August 1787, and it ran from the Royal Palace across Bromma roughly where Gustav III:s väg runs today. The surroundings, though, are 20th century: Abrahamsberg is one of Stockholm's larger areas of narrow slab blocks and is sometimes called the yellow town, after all the yellow brick.
Gatorna här har väder i blodet. Väderils: The streets here have weather in their blood. Väderilsgatan, a little way off, got its name in 1958 as part of a group of street names on the theme of weather and meteorology, and that's where tram line 2 turns in a loop. Near the stop is Länsmanstorget, an indoor square built in 1966. Länsmansgården Church held its last service in April 2024 and is to become an activity centre for all.
Gatorna på Södra Guldheden är uppkallade: The streets of Södra Guldheden are named after doctors. Doktor Liborius gata honours Johan August Liborius, chief surgeon at Sahlgrenska Hospital from 1845 to 1870 and regarded as the hospital's first modern surgeon. Doktor Bex gata remembers Abraham Bex, the town physician of Gothenburg around 1685. At the very top of that street are unusual shop buildings from 1951, where the Konsum co-op became the first tenant.
Gatunamnen här doftar häst, och det är i: The street names here smell of horses, and that's no coincidence. A few hundred metres away is Åbytravet, Sweden's second largest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. Its neighbour, the Åbybadet swimming baths, opened in 2023, so here both people and horses can get their pulse up.
Gatunamnen här doftar sågspån. Sågmästar: The street names here smell of sawdust. The master sawyer Nils Georg Sörensen ran the Säfveåns AB sawmill, which has given its name to several streets in Björkekärr: Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget itself, all named after sawmill terms. Sörensen even got a street of his own. On a hill by the square stands Björkekärr Church, and the area borders the Delsjön nature reserve.
Gatunamnen här är ingen slump, Biskopsgå: The street names here are no coincidence – Biskopsgården is full of weather-themed names. At Vårväderstorget, Spring Weather Square, a short walk away, is the Biskopsgården library, which opened in 1964 and is now one of the city's most popular, with 700 to 800 visitors on an ordinary day. In 2020 the Swedish Arts Council named it a Romani reading embassy.
Gatunamnet ljuger inte: ett par hundra m: The street name doesn't lie: a couple of hundred metres away, Kållered Church stands on a rise in the village. It is not only the parish church of Kållered parish but also the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. Kållered was farming country for a long time, before the superstores took over the western part of the town.
Gatunamnet passar bra, för en kort prome: The street name fits well, because a short walk away is Skansberget, one of Huddinge municipality's eight ancient hillforts. Even closer, the Smista bridge spans the E4/E20 motorway. The steel footbridge and cycle bridge opened in 2008 and stretches in a single span between Segeltorp and Sätra, to make it easier to get between the two areas.
Gatunamnet passar perfekt. På Tullinge g: The street name fits perfectly. At Tullinge gymnasium, the upper secondary school a couple of hundred metres away, it is a tradition for a Nobel laureate to visit every year, usually someone from the natural sciences. In 2014 the chemistry laureates Eric Betzig and William Moerner came, and in 2017 Michael W. Young. Not many schools can boast guest lecturers like that.
Gatunamnet påminner om Svenska Ostindisk: The street name recalls the Swedish East India Company, which was based in Gothenburg between 1731 and 1813. The company's ships sailed to China and came home laden with tea, porcelain and silk.
Gatunamnet är ingen slump. Strax intill: The street name is no coincidence. Right next door is Stora Sköndal, which began as a deaconry institution. It was founded in 1898 in Gävle to train deacons and moved here in 1905, when Stora Sköndal was bought. And funnily enough, the blue-listed Terrasshuset, the Terrace House, designed by Axel Kandell, stands in a block called Predikanten, the Preacher, on a steep, south-facing plot.
Gatunamnet är inte taget ur luften. Inge: The street name wasn't plucked out of thin air. In 1885 the engineer Gerhard Arehn started a factory here on Kungsholmen to make matchboxes, and machines that made matchboxes. The company eventually ended up with Svenska Tändsticksaktiebolaget, the Swedish Match Company. Nearby was also Tullmuseum, the Customs Museum, which from 1927 displayed the Swedish Customs' collected objects, and the old Jewish cemetery Aronsberg.
Genom Henriksdalsberget går Saltsjöbanan: Through the Henriksdal hill runs the Saltsjöbanan railway's 337-metre tunnel, where trains have rolled since 1893. The area around Henriksborg used to be industrial land, and from 1882 until the late 1950s the Rylander and Rudolph factory made, among other things, batteries for crank telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps. In 1987 the office building Danvikcenter received a European award for its steel structures.
Gibraltargatan en bit härifrån fick sitt: Gibraltargatan, a little way from here, got its name in 1886 after the Gibraltar estate. In 1923 the street-naming committee wanted to change it to Gibraltarsgatan, but the city council said no. On the street was the Gibraltarvallen sports ground from 1922, until it was replaced by Mossen sports ground in 1959 and became mostly a car park. The footpath Syster Bojans backe, Sister Bojan's Hill, is named after Ingeborg Kastman.
Gillar du bröllop? Tuve kyrka, några min: Do you like weddings? Tuve Church, a few minutes away, is one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. The church is the parish church of Tuve parish, which belonged to Östra Hising hundred in Västergötland and was merged into the city of Gothenburg in 1967. Since 2010 the church has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish.
Glose gränsar till Ryskärsfjorden, där g: Glose borders Ryskärsfjorden, where shallow waters and grazed shore meadows attract a rich plant and bird life. The meadows are part of the Nordre älv estuary, a nature reserve and Natura 2000 site counted among the county's most valuable natural areas. The spot has even been featured in a live broadcast of Sveriges Radio's nature programme Naturmorgon. A little further away also stands Burås mill from the 1890s.
Golfhistoria i grannskapet! Lidingö golf: Golf history in the neighbourhood! Lidingö Golf Club's parkland and forest course at Sticklinge opened in 1927 and was then Sweden's first 18-hole course. If you'd rather swim, there's Sticklingebadet, also called Sandviksbadet, a small beach on Stora Värtan bay. And the trail of Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, also runs through Sticklinge.
Gothia Arena, Högsbo Baskets hemmahall,: Gothia Arena, Högsbo Basket's home court, is just a couple of hundred metres away. The whole area belongs to the old parish of Västra Frölunda, which in 1944 had about 13,500 inhabitants and the following year was merged into the City of Gothenburg. The parish church, Västra Frölunda Church, is today in the district of Järnbrott.
Granne med Frölunda torg, som Olof Palme: Next to Frölunda torg, which Olof Palme opened in 1966 as the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries, it seems fitting to talk about Gothenburg humour. Kal and Ada, "Kal å Ada", are the main characters in the classic Gothenburg jokes, and tradition has it that Oscar II's court photographer Aron Jonason was one of the founders of the Gothenburg pun. Next to the square is Frölunda Culture House, with a library, theatre and swimming pool.
Granne med gymnasieskolan ligger Svandam: Next to the upper secondary school is Svandammen, a park and bathing spot that is a popular meeting place for both young people and families with children. A little further away is Spånga station on the Mälaren line, 11.3 kilometres from Stockholm Central Station. On an ordinary winter weekday, about 7,900 people board the trains there.
Granne med tenniscentret växer Råstapark: Next to the tennis centre, Råstapark is taking shape, AIK's future training facility and clubhouse for the men's team. It is due to be finished in autumn 2028 and will replace Karlberg, where the team has trained since 1999. A short walk away is Lake Råstasjön, Solna municipality's only lake if you don't count Mälaren.
Granne med värdshuset gömmer sig en rikt: Next to the inn hides a real gem: Confidencen, the Ulriksdal Palace theatre, Sweden's oldest rococo theatre. It was fitted out in 1753 by the architect Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz and was renovated in stages in the 1990s and 2000s. The inn building itself is younger; it was built in 1868 on the initiative of King Karl XV.
Grannkommundelen Viksjö i Järfälla har e: The neighbouring district of Viksjö in Järfälla has a name with a long history. It comes from Viksjö farm and is a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which already appears on a runestone from the 11th century. The farm was sold in 1921, and in 1963 development of the area began; today it's dominated by small houses.
Grevegårdens kyrka ligger några hundra m: Grevegården Church is a few hundred metres away, but a little further away, in Älvsborg, one of the area's sweetest stories awaits. In the 1930s Mrs Liljegren baked buns that she sold through a hatch in the wall of her house to schoolchildren on their way to Påvelundsskolan school. She became known as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady, and the street was named after her in 1965.
Groens malmgård: Groen's malmgård, a traditional town estate
Groens malmgård är en riktig överlevare:: Groens malmgård is a real survivor: its main building in Carolean style is the only remaining one of its kind in Stockholm, and the garden has been cultivated without interruption for more than 300 years. A malmgård is an old country house on the outskirts of the city. The street outside has had names including Stadsträdgårdsgatan and Wintertullsgatan, and from 1885 Vermdögatan, a name considered misleading that was changed in 1939 to Malmgårdsvägen. In the 1600s a windmill also turned here, Bengt Bagares kvarn, Bengt the Baker's mill.
Grynkvarnsparken har fått sitt namn efte: Grynkvarnsparken is named after a groats mill that once ground grain here, and the farm next to it was demolished in the 1940s. In the southern part of the park, at what is now Bolidenvägen 2, lay the croft Linde, which was both a coaching station and a tavern for travellers. The park was designed in the 1950s by the city gardener Holger Blom and Erik Glemme, and today Talltunneln, one of the slip roads to the Södra länken ring road, runs beneath the lawns.
Grädde och ost, det passar ju ihop. Alld: Cream and cheese – they go together, don't they? Right next to Gräddgatan, Cream Street, rises Ostkupan, the Cheese Dome, the nickname of a 14-storey apartment building from 1964 that mostly houses students in corridor rooms with shared kitchens. The Kallebäck district itself has an even older name: it means the stream with the kettle and is mentioned as early as 1496.
Gräsbacken Sjöbacken, som i folkmun kall: The grassy slope Sjöbacken, popularly known as Tippen, 'the Tip', was once a shallow sea bay. When Frölunda torg was built, the excavated soil was dumped here, and the result became a popular spot for picnics and kite flying, with skating ice in cold winters. Down in Fiskebäck harbour there is also a fishing museum with a café, opened in 1999.
Gröna Lund öppnade 1883 och är Sveriges: Gröna Lund opened in 1883 and is Sweden's oldest amusement park. In summer the screams from the roller coasters can be heard far out across the water. Opposite is the Liljevalchs art gallery.
Gröndal växte fram som en tidig arbetar-: Gröndal grew up as an early working-class and factory suburb when the Western Main Line was built past Liljeholmen in the 1860s. In the famous Gröndal terrace house, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, the Galjonen cinema operated between 1952 and 1962. The Riggen apartment building at Fågelsångsvägen 13 is much younger and was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2016.
Gröndal är känt för stjärnhusen, och här: Gröndal is known for its star-shaped houses, and Sweden's first ones were built here. The architects Sven Backström and Leif Reinius designed them, and the master builder Olle Engkvist drove the project. The houses have become internationally known. Between 1926 and 1934 the district was called Ekensberg, and it got its current name from the Gröndal estate.
Gubbängens IP hette ursprungligen Bandha: Gubbängen sports ground, Gubbängens IP, was originally called Bandhagen sports ground and has a colourful history. In summer, the speedway bikes of Hammarby Speedway and Getingarna roared here, and in the old days the place was even known for car speedway. Today bandy and field hockey are played here, and since 2020, when Stockholm's first indoor bandy hall was completed, so is IK Tellus.
Guldrummet i Historiska museet: The Gold Room at the Swedish History Museum
Gullmarsplan har fått sitt namn efter Gu: Gullmarsplan is named after Gullmarn, the fjord at Lysekil in Bohuslän. The square was built in the 1940s at the same time as the surrounding district, and the metro station opened on 1 October 1950. Before that, trams stopped here. Today it's one of Stockholm's biggest hubs, where the metro, the Tvärbanan light rail and buses meet.
Gunnareds kyrka ligger bara några minute: Gunnared church is only a few minutes away and has belonged to Angered parish since 2014. A little further away is Titteridamm pond, surrounded by roads like Titteridammsvägen and Titteridammsstigen. According to legend, the name comes from girls who looked at their reflections in the pond's shiny water before the Saturday dance – "titta" means to look.
Gunnareds kyrkogård, en kort promenad bo: Gunnared Cemetery, a short walk away, has a long backstory. Plans for a new cemetery in north-eastern Gothenburg began as early as the 1980s, the land was acquired through a land swap with the city, and at the end of the 1990s an architectural competition was held. The cemetery opened in 2003 and covers 80 hectares. Next to it stands Gunnared Church.
Gustaf Adolfs torg och Stora Hamnkanalen: Gustaf Adolfs torg square and the Stora Hamnkanalen canal
Gustav III ritade i stor utsträckning sj: Gustav III largely designed his own English park at Drottningholm, but he never lived to see it finished. A memorial temple to the king was to be built on Monumentholmen, but only the foundation was ever made. Next to it is Svanholmen, Swan Island, with a swan house resembling a Chinese pagoda, where the park's wing-clipped mute swans lived in winter. And the Gothic Tower, begun in 1792, was never fully completed inside.
Gustav Vasa skänkte en gång Skuru gård t: King Gustav Vasa once gave Skuru gård, the Skuru estate, to Danvik's Hospital, so that the rent would help pay the hospital's expenses. The estate, a short walk from here, was bought in 1922 by the matron Mathilda Sundelin, who renamed it Solsunda. Since the early 20th century, the manor-like main building has been a rest and treatment home. In little Bastusjön lake next to it, perch and roach swim.
Gustavi domkyrka har brunnit två gånger,: Gothenburg Cathedral, Gustavi domkyrka, has burned down twice, in 1721 and 1802. The building you see was completed in 1815. The streets around it are the grid from the city's first years, and Kungsgatan, one of Sweden's longest pedestrian streets, is just a block away.
