Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån har lek: The upper secondary students a little way from here have lessons in an old weaving mill. Krokslättsgymnasiet started as a healthcare upper secondary school in 1992 and rents premises in the Krokslätt factories, a textile mill built in the 1890s. The buildings were declared listed in 1991 and are today protected in the local plan, even though they have been rebuilt inside.
Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån pluggar: The upper secondary students a little way from here study in a real piece of industrial history. Hulebäcksgymnasiet opened in 1995 in the converted and extended Hulebäck factory from 1878, which was a branch of Mölnlycke fabriker. The railway has moved too: Mölnlycke station opened in 1894, but back then it was about 350 metres east of where it is today, and in 2003 it was moved to its current location, where the Västtågen regional trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop.
Gäddviken var förr namnet på hela Svinde: Gäddviken used to be the name of the whole of Svindersviken bay, and there have been industries on the shore ever since the mid-1600s, including a superphosphate factory from the 1870s. In the old coffee roastery, the Royal Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, now store their things, so there may be both stage sets and costumes behind the walls. A little further away is the manager's residence of Beckbruket, the old pitch works, from the 1830s, the oldest preserved building in Finnboda.
Gärdesgården, byggd 1940 till 1941, pres: Gärdesgården, built in 1940 to 1941, was presented in the newspaper Svenska Dagbladet as a modern residential hotel, with a shared restaurant, a sun terrace and even a Finnish sauna for the tenants. In Tessinparken next door stands the sculpture Husmorssemester, 'Housewife's Holiday', from 1973: a granite woman in a summer dress with a suitcase. It recalls the state grant that housewives could receive to go on holiday between 1946 and 1979.

Gå ner i tunnelbanan och det känns som a: Go down into the metro and it feels like stepping into a child's drawing. The artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark decorated the station with motifs that look like children's drawings, inspired by their own childhoods. The station opened on 31 August 1975, with the blue line's first section between T-Centralen and Hjulsta.

Gå uppför Kvastmakarbacken till trähusen: Walk up Kvastmakarbacken to the wooden houses on Åsöberget
Gå ut på Allébron över Sickla kanal: Walk out on Allébron bridge over Sickla canal
Gå ut på Mariebergsbron och titta över M: Walk out onto Mariebergsbron bridge and look out over the Mariebergssundet strait
Gården Stora Fågelsången är från 1700-ta: The farm Stora Fågelsången dates from the 18th century and sits on the western side of the little lake Trekanten. Since 1963 it has been owned by the City of Stockholm, and the old garden has become allotments, though without any allotment cottages. The City Museum has blue-listed the farm, which means it is considered to have exceptionally high cultural and historical value. A little further away, the Essingeleden motorway whooshes past on the Blommensberg viaduct, almost over the roofs of Blommensbergsskolan school.
Gården och värdshuset Sandsborg har gett: The farm and inn Sandsborg has given its name to both a cemetery and a metro station here in Gamla Enskede. A little further away is the Museum of the Visually Impaired, housed in premises that once belonged to De blindas tekniska fabrik, a workshop for the blind, with collections on the history of visually impaired people in Sweden going back to the late 18th century. And inside Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, Almhöjden awaits: a hill of weeping elms that recalls a painting by Caspar David Friedrich.
Gårdsten har vänt en trend. När det komm: Gårdsten has turned a trend around. When the municipal housing company Gårdstensbostäder was formed in 1997, more than 800 of about 2,200 apartments stood empty. The company set up its office in the middle of the area to work close to the tenants. The renovation of eastern Gårdsten won the Stora Samhällsbyggarpriset, a major Swedish urban development award, in 2006, and in 2019 Gårdsten became the first area to be removed from the police list of particularly vulnerable areas.
Görvälns griftegård ritades av landskaps: Görväln cemetery was designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg and laid out in 1966–1977 on old farmland and a wooded hill. Here a 300-metre waterway with eleven waterfalls runs down towards a large reflecting pool. In 2017 a Muslim burial section with 220 coffin graves was opened. Nearby also stands Görväln school, which was in use between 1896 and 1939, and the school building is still there.
Göteborgs botaniska trädgård öppnade 192: Gothenburg Botanical Garden opened in 1923 and is one of Europe's larger botanical gardens. There's a rock garden, a Japanese valley and greenhouses with thousands of plants. On the other side of the road is Slottsskogen, the city's big park.
Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri: Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery
Göteborgs stad tackade 1874 nej till att: In 1874 the City of Gothenburg declined to buy the Tingstadsvassen reed beds for ten öre per square foot, but two years later it decided to acquire the area for 300,000 kronor. Nearby there are two veteran vessels: the sailing ship Isolda from 1902, the last Swedish sailing merchant ship in ocean trade, and the tug Sven from 1897, built as an icebreaking steam tug.
Göteborgs stadsmuseum i Ostindiska huset: Gothenburg City Museum in Ostindiska huset, the East India House
Göteborgsoperan står ungefär där länscel: The Gothenburg Opera stands roughly where the county jail was, a prison that opened in 1857. From the Lilla Bommen harbour, cargo and passenger boats once sailed via the Göta älv river, the Göta Canal and the lakes all the way to Stockholm and Norrköping. Outside the opera house, water runs down Bård Breivik's stone sculpture Källan, the Spring, from 1994.
Haga Nygata och jättekanelbullar: Haga Nygata and giant cinnamon buns
Haga parkmuseum i Koppartälten: Haga Park Museum in the Copper Tents
Hagakyrkan invigdes 1859 och ligger vid: Hagakyrkan, the Haga Church, was consecrated in 1859 and stands by Haga, one of Gothenburg's oldest districts. Along Haga Nygata, Haga's main street, there are small shops and cafés. This is where they sell the famous giant cinnamon buns, as big as a side plate.
Hagaparken börjar nästan här. Gustav III: Hagaparken park almost starts here. Gustav III had Övre Haga built as an inn in 1788–1789, with two kitchens and three dining rooms. Haga Trädgård is known from Bellman's song 'Fjäriln vingad syns på Haga', 'The winged butterfly is seen at Haga', and in 1989 the Butterfly House moved into one of the greenhouses. If you want a view, you can climb Frösundatoppen, about 72 metres above sea level.
Hagsätra centrum invigdes 1960 efter bar: Hagsätra centrum opened in 1960 after just one year of construction, the same year the metro arrived, and cost 25 million kronor in the money of the day. The centre's signature is 'Barnet med käpphästen', 'The Child with the Hobby Horse', a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist. If you need some greenery, Hagsätraskogen forest is close by; in 2021 it became Stockholm's eleventh nature reserve.
Hallunda Folkets hus: Hallunda Folkets hus, the community centre
Hallunda var en levande jordbruksbygd än: Hallunda was a thriving farming area right up until the Million Programme arrived in the early 1970s and Botkyrkastaden was built on the farm's land. Hallunda manor itself, an 18th-century manor house a little way from here, was however left out of the town plan and is still privately owned, one of the few old manor estates in the Stockholm area where that is the case. Next to the manor is a large Iron Age burial ground.
Hammargården ligger på sydöstra Färingsö: Hammargården lies in south-eastern Färingsö, and the small houses here were once staff housing for the youth reform school that stood on the site. A little to the south, Lullehovsbron bridge spans Lullehovssundet, a strait in Lake Mälaren just over 200 metres wide and about seven metres deep in the middle. In the southern part of the strait lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island, and both the bridge and the strait are named after the settlement of Lullehov on Lindö.
Hammarkullen är känt för sin karneval, s: Hammarkullen is known for its carnival, which every year fills the district with music, dance and colourful costumes. The stop lies deep inside the rock and is reached by a long escalator.
Handelshögskolan grundades 1909 som Sver: Handelshögskolan, the Stockholm School of Economics, was founded in 1909 as Sweden's first business school, and the main building on Sveavägen was designed by Ivar Tengbom in 1925. Among other things, its researchers have contributed to the Stockholm School of economics. Around the corner is Betlehemskyrkan, Bethlehem Church, whose predecessor from 1840 was Sweden's first free-church building. It stood near Hötorget but was demolished in 1953, and the new church was consecrated here in 1956.
Haninge kulturpark: Haninge kulturpark, the Haninge culture park
Harestads kyrka ligger ett stenkast häri: Harestad Church is a stone's throw from here, in the church village of Kyrkeby. The village was classified as a small locality in 1995, but since then it has had fewer than 50 inhabitants and so lost that status. A church village so small that the statistics no longer count it, but the church still stands in Harestad parish, which has belonged to Kungälv municipality since 1971.
Harestads socken ligger vid kusten sydvä: Harestad parish lies on the coast south-west of Kungälv and includes small villages such as Flateby, Toreby and Kornhall. In 2000, 951 people lived here. The parish church, Harestad Church, stands in the church village of Kyrkeby a little way off. The parish used to belong to Inland Södre hundred and since 1971 has been part of Kungälv municipality.
Havsguden Poseidon av Carl Milles har va: The sea god Poseidon by Carl Milles has watched over the square since 1931 and is one of Gothenburg's best-known landmarks. Crowded around him are the art museum, the Concert Hall, the City Theatre and the City Library, the city's most visited cultural institution. In Götapalatset the cinema Göta opened in 1936, closed in 1997 and got a new lease of life in 2015. Don't miss Peter Linde's bronze statue of the writer Karin Boye, either.
Hela Bergshamra ligger i Nationalstadspa: The whole of Bergshamra lies within the Royal National City Park. The land for the Kungshamra student area was donated by King Gustaf VI Adolf, hence the name, "King's Hamra". The water tower from 1951 by Edsviken bay is a landmark seen from far away, and on Pipers väg stands Övre Karlsro, also called Carl Malmsten's house.
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn efte: The whole district takes its name from Breviks gård, a manor with roots going back to the 14th century. The last main building was demolished in 1987, and Brevik centre with its Lidingöbanan light rail stop stands there today. Its neighbour is Blocket, one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings, built in 1914 to 1915. And in 1905 the owner of the manor offered to pay for a small primary school in the area himself.
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn från: The whole district has taken its name from the farm a couple of hundred metres away. Flemingsbergs gård, once spelt Flemmingsbergs gård, is a manor and former estate with a history going back to the 15th century. On the other side is the industrial area, where LM Ericsson's central warehouse was in its day a sight worth seeing thanks to its automation.
Helige Savas serbisk-ortodoxa kyrka är h: The Serbian Orthodox Church of Saint Sava is dedicated to Serbia's national saint, Sava, who founded the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1219, and it is the cathedral of the eparchy, or diocese, of Scandinavia. Nearby is the Skagers House, Skagershuset, an apartment building with a wooden facade that was named Stockholm Building of the Year in 2014. The building takes its name from Skagersvägen, which in turn is named after Lake Skagern, on the border between Värmland and Västergötland.
Helige kung Stefan Dečanskis kyrka, Göte: Church of the Holy King Stefan Dečanski, Gothenburg
Hellasgården är en frisksportanläggning: Hellasgården is an outdoor sports facility and clubhouse by Lake Källtorpssjön, in the middle of the Nacka Reserve. This is the start and finish of Källtorpssjön runt, the yellow trail, a five-kilometre walking route marked with yellow dots and arrows. On the north-western shore of the lake is Stengärdet, old farmland enclosed by a stone wall protected as an ancient monument.
Hemgården på Östermalmsgatan blev 1906 S: In 1906, Hemgården on Östermalmsgatan became Sweden's first collective housing block. With a shared central kitchen, young women in particular would have time to go out to work. The building went up where the 18th-century Brandel sugar refinery had stood, a building that had also served as a cholera hospital. Nearby was Palmgrenska samskolan, the first school in Scandinavia where girls and boys were taught together all the way to the upper secondary leaving exam.
Herrgården Lilla Frösunda från 1700-tale: The 18th-century manor Lilla Frösunda has been owned by, among others, the gardener Anders Lundström, and the Swedish state used the main building as an officers' mess until the end of the 1980s. When Canon moved to Frösunda in 2001, the company called in the architects Tengboms, who gave the office building on Gustav III:s boulevard an architecture that reflected the company's high technology.
Herrgården Riddersvik ligger vid Mälaren: The Riddersvik manor house stands on the shore of Lake Mälaren next to Lövstafjärden bay, and here you can still find Tempeludden and the English Park, also called the Star Park. The garden cottage, probably from the 18th century, has been home to estate labourers and crofter families, and every year the manor holds a Christmas market. The garden suburb also had a station on the Spånga–Lövsta railway, where passenger services ran from 1889 to 1956.
Herrgården Stensjöhill vid Stensjöns väs: The manor house Stensjöhill on the western shore of Stensjön lake has had a varied life. It was built in 1917 for the manager of the nearby margarine factory, became offices in the 1980s, and was then taken over by the Hare Krishna movement. After that it became a hotel and conference centre, and at the end of 2012 it was sold to become a residential care home. Closest by is the ridge Kikås, with Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel.
Herrgården och det tidigare säteriet Säb: The manor and former noble estate Säby gård has been a state listed building since 1983 and lies in the Järvafältet nature reserve. It is now owned by Järfälla Municipality, and the main building houses a Waldorf preschool, so the youngest children have unusually fine premises. South of the farm is the rune slab U 90, a Viking Age carving made directly in the bedrock.
Herrgården Ålstens gård står på en grund: The manor house Ålstens gård stands on a foundation from the 16th century, and the enormous stone walls in the cellar bear witness to its age. In 1936 it was bought by Axel Gauffin, director general of the Nationalmuseum, who restored the house and lived here until 1957. Below stretches Ålstensängen, an old field belonging to the estate that is now an open meadow ending at a sandy beach on Lake Mälaren.
Herrängens gård har anor från 1600-talet: Herrängen farm dates back to the 17th century, when the place was a croft called Isbergatorpet, belonging to Långbro farm. The farm lies on the north side of Lake Långsjön and has given its name to the whole district of Herrängen. The City Museum has marked it blue, which means the buildings are judged to have exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Hersby gymnasium: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Hersby gymnasium, som tidigare hette Lid: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school formerly called Lidingö högre allmänna läroverk, got its first school building in 1914 and was rebuilt and extended until 1957. A stone's throw away are the terraced houses of the Tegen större and mindre blocks, built as early as 1908–1909 to designs by Jacob Gate and today classed as culturally and historically valuable. All of Hersby forms the core of Lidingö villastad, the villa town founded in 1906.
Hisingen är stor, cirka 199 kvadratkilom: Hisingen is big, about 199 square kilometres, roughly half the area of Gothenburg municipality, and about a quarter of the inhabitants live here. The island is framed by Göta älv to the south and east, Nordre älv to the north and the Kattegat to the west. The area includes the small settlement of Holm in Tuve parish.
Hisingen, ön vi befinner oss på, är till: Hisingen, the island we're on, is Sweden's fifth-largest island by area, after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust, and also the second most populous. The island is bounded by Göta älv river to the south and east, Nordre älv to the north and the Kattegat to the west. With its 199 square kilometres it makes up roughly half of Gothenburg municipality.
Hitta Calles klimp vid vattnet: Find Calles klimp, Calle's Lump, by the water
Hitta Emotrappan i Nordstan: Find the Emo stairs, Emotrappan, in Nordstan
Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen är Hisingens st: Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen is the main transport hub of Hisingen. Hisingen is Sweden's fourth-largest island, and both ships and cars were once built here. Volvo was founded in Gothenburg in 1927, and its head office is still on Hisingen.
Hjorthagen var ursprungligen ett hägn fö: Hjorthagen was originally an enclosure for the king's deer, before the area became an industrial suburb in the late 19th century, with the Värta gasworks and the Värta power plant as landmarks. The headland Ropsten has a lovely name: the stone where people called out for the ferry from the other side. At the end of the Lidingö Bridge, the Stockholmsfyren skyscraper, with 54 storeys and 187 metres high, was once planned, but the project never went ahead.
Hjulsta, den västra delen av Tensta, är: Hjulsta, the western part of Tensta, is a textbook example of the Million Programme's traffic separation, from Sweden's big 1960s and 70s housing drive. A ring road surrounds the residential area, which is more or less car-free, and footbridges link it together over sunken streets. The metro station, terminus of line 10, was blasted out of the rock beneath Hjulstaskolan, the school.
Hjällbo centrum byggdes 1969 och fick et: Hjällbo centrum was built in 1969 and got a new look during a rebuild in 2001. On the square there's a market hall with fruit and vegetables, and in the shopping building an oriental grocery, a gift shop and a pizzeria. A library, pharmacy and church are here too, so most of everyday life fits around one and the same square.
Hjällbo är en stadsdel på hela 927 hekta: Hjällbo is a district covering a full 927 hectares in north-eastern Gothenburg, and within it lies the area of Eriksbo. A little further away begins Nordöstra Göteborg, North-East Gothenburg, an urban area consisting mainly of Hammarkullen and Gunnared with Gårdsten, Lövgärdet, Rannebergen and Angered centre. It is the largest urban area in Sweden that isn't the main town of its municipality.
Hornstull har fått sitt namn efter tulle: Hornstull is named after the toll gate, the ‘tull’, that stood here at the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood. Today it's one of Södermalm's liveliest spots, with restaurants along Hornstulls strand and views over the water.

Hornstull takes its name from the toll gate that stood here at the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood. Today it's one of the liveliest places on Södermalm, with restaurants along the Hornstulls strand waterfront and views over the water. To the south is Tantolunden park, with allotments and big lawns.
Hotell The Weaver reser sig 22 våningar,: Hotel The Weaver rises 22 storeys, with 370 rooms and conference space for 600 people. The name is a nod to Krokslätts fabriker, the Krokslätt mills, which were a complete weaving business right into the 1970s. Where the looms once stood, business travellers now sleep.
Huddinge centrum ligger mitt i en villas: Huddinge centrum lies in the middle of a garden suburb that never happened. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård began selling plots for Huddinge villastad. Selling building plots close to Stockholm was more profitable than carrying on farming. Only a few of the old villas remain.
Humlegården och Kungliga biblioteket: Humlegården park and the National Library of Sweden
Hungrig? Kville saluhall öppnade 2013 me: Hungry? Kville saluhall, the food hall, opened in 2013 with meat, fish, seafood, a bakery and lots of restaurants. A little further away was the Gnistan cinema. Its opening film in 1938 was the military farce Kamrater i vapenrocken, and in 1968 the curtain fell for good after Django Shoots First. On Kvilletorget stands Carl Milles' statue Susanna, also called Girl with a Shell.
Husby, en bit härifrån, är byggt på norr: Husby, a little way from here, is built on the northern part of Järvafältet, which the military used as a training ground right up until 1965. Between 1971 and 1980 the district was actually called Husby gård. Here you'll also find Husby Church, designed by Karl Erik Hjalmarson and consecrated in 1976, given a green listing by the City Museum, and the Husby baths, with an adventure pool and diving tower.
Husbybadet öppnade kring millennieskifte: Husbybadet opened around the turn of the millennium and tempts you with a water park, jacuzzi and sauna. A little further away is Akalla church, with an unusual history: consecrated in 1976, it was sold by the Church of Sweden in 2020 to the Catholic Diocese of Stockholm. Today it's the home church of the Syriac Catholic Church.
Husen glesnar och villor tar över. Snart: The buildings thin out and villas take over. Soon you'll see the sea.
Huvudgatan Sturegatan hette från början: The main street, Sturegatan, was originally called Storgatan, but at the end of the 1800s it was renamed after Sten Sture the Elder. Along the street there are shops, restaurants, Folkets hus, the community hall, and Sundbybergs köksbryggeri, a brewery, and there used to be a cinema here as well. The cultural centre Allaktivitetshuset opened in 2013.
Huvudsta har fler slott än man kanske tr: Huvudsta has more palaces than you might think. The district has Karlberg Palace, Huvudsta gård and Huvudsta Old Palace, and by Lake Ulvsundasjön there's the popular Huvudstabadet pool. Beneath your feet, 25 metres down in the rock, is the metro station with Per Holmberg's artwork Hängande trädgårdar, Hanging Gardens, from 1985.
Huvudstråket genom Akalla heter Sibelius: The main walkway through Akalla is called Sibeliusgången, after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius, and it's 900 metres long. Along the way, Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubble away. But the name Akalla has been known since the Middle Ages: in Akalla village stands Storgården from the 17th century, in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area, with a 4-H farm and a café.
Hägerstens gård är en herrgård vars mang: Hägerstens gård is a manor whose main building with wings still stands, but since 1997 it has been a housing cooperative with just five flats. At Hägerstens torg, also called Axelsbergs centrum, the centre building is modernist with façades clad in dark red ceramic tiles. And at night the trees on Axelsbergs torg square are lit from below by a spotlight.
Häggvikstunneln är den kortaste av Norro: The Häggvik tunnel is the shortest of the three road tunnels on the Norrortsleden road, just 289 metres long, and a park has been laid out on its roof. A little further away is Klasro School, built in 1804 and until 1871 Sollentuna's only school. It was placed by the parish's most famous spring, where travellers watered their horses, and which Malla Silfverstolpe called la bonne fontaine. Today it is a school museum.
Hällsvik vid Hälleviken var förr en lite: Hällsvik by the Hälleviken bay used to be a small fishing village, where fishing and eventually farming provided a living, and parts of the original buildings still remain. During the heyday of the shipyards, many shipyard workers got themselves summer cottages here. Over time the plots have been divided up, and the cottages have been demolished or rebuilt as villas.
Hälsa på Bellmansbysten: Say hello to the Bellman bust
Hälsa på bronskvinnan Väntan: Say hello to the bronze woman Väntan, Waiting
Hälsö är en liten ö i Göteborgs norra sk: Hälsö is a small island in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, just 1.28 square kilometres in size, with around 590 permanent residents. On the south side of the island you cross the bridge to Öckerö and can then continue to Hönö to take the ferry to Hisingen and the mainland. The islands hang together like pearls on a string.
Här bjuds på namnförvirring: Skarpnäcks: Here's some name confusion for you: Skarpnäck's old school from 1928 is in Enskededalen, while Skarpnäck school from 1952 is opposite, in Kärrtorp. The younger one has been called both Nya skolan, the New School, and Skarpnäcks nya skola before getting its old name back, and since 1992 it has been an annex to its older neighbour. Both school buildings are green-listed by the Stockholm City Museum.
Här doftar det konspiration. En bit bort: There's a whiff of conspiracy here. A little way off is Huvudsta gamla slott, Huvudsta Old Palace, a wooden building from 1750 rumoured to be where the murder of Gustav III was planned. The house was originally the main building of Huvudsta Farm but was moved in 1834. Down by the water you may also spot the schooner Constantia, built in Denmark in 1908 and today a sail training ship for young people and adults alike.
Här fanns en gång Vårby gård, även kalla: Here once stood Vårby gård, also called Vårby Castle, an estate bought by the City of Stockholm in 1931. The main building burned down on 5 May 1975, and today the site is mostly park and allotment gardens. Right nearby, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard, a silver treasure, was found in 1871. In the manor park stands Myrstugan, a boatswain's croft from the early 1700s that was moved here in 1986.
Här finns ett av Stockholms mer udda mus: Here you'll find one of Stockholm's odder museums: Sveriges VVS-museum, the Swedish Plumbing and Heating Museum. The collection was first in Katrineholm and reopened in Bromma in 2016. Further away, in Tuvanparken, was Tuvan's home for nervous disorders in the 1890s. In a fire in 1940, three patients died, and the building was demolished in 1960. Where the nursing home stood there is now a park.
Här finns gott om skolbänkar: Nacka gymn: There are plenty of school desks here: Nacka gymnasium is one of Sweden's largest schools, and its neighbour, Eklidens skola, is one of the country's largest lower secondary schools, with an ice rink and a swimming pool right next door. The name Järla comes from the title jarl, or earl. In nearby Vikdalen, Stockholm families built summer villas in the late 19th century and arrived by steamboat, but when the car engine factory in Augustendal came, workers moved in and the villas became workers' housing.
Här gick en gång Göteborgs gräns. Område: This is where Gothenburg's boundary once ran. The area of Kungssten used to be called Stadsgränsen, the City Limit, and the Oden cinema on Långedragsvägen was just outside the city limit when it opened in 1919. Under the hill runs the Gnistäng tunnel, 712 metres long and one of Sweden's longer road tunnels, with about 55,000 vehicles a day.
Här har flyghistoria skrivits. En bit bo: Aviation history has been written here. A little way off is Säve Airport, which for a period was called Göteborg City Airport and was Sweden's eighth largest, busy with low-cost flights. After 2015 the airlines moved to Landvetter, and since 2026 only police and rescue service helicopters fly from here. Closer to the stop, the Nya Solevi solar park glitters; it was built in just three months in 2018.
Här i Amhult, några hundra meter bort, l: Here in Amhult, a few hundred metres away, was Torslanda airfield, Gothenburg's airport from 1923 right up until 1977, when Landvetter took over. Originally it was called Göteborgs Flyghamn and also had a seaplane harbour. When it closed, it was one of Europe's oldest airfields with scheduled traffic.
Här i Högdalens industriområde ligger Hö: Here in Högdalen's industrial area is Högdalsdepån, one of the metro's depots, where the trains get to rest and be serviced. A little further away rises Högdalstoppen, three artificial hills, and on one of them a disc golf course opened in 2005. From the tops in Fagersjö you get a sweeping view over southern Stockholm.
Här i Skälltorp, norra Backa, finns en b: Here in Skälltorp, northern Backa, there's a piece of Swedish music history. The music theatre group Nationalteatern moved in 1970 to Backa Fritidsgård, the youth centre at Selma Lagerlöfs torg. Nearby is also the Friedländer cemetery, which with just over twenty graves is Gothenburg's smallest.
Här i Västra Frölunda har gatorna musika: Here in Västra Frölunda the streets have musical names, such as Musikvägen and Positivgatan – Music Road and Barrel Organ Street. The district was built in the 1960s, when Gothenburg was growing rapidly southwards.
Här i de gamla AGA-fabrikerna var uppfin: Here in the old AGA factories, the inventor Gustaf Dalén worked from 1912 until his death in 1937, hence the name Dalénum. Next door is Stillerska Filmgymnasiet, a film upper secondary school named after the director Mauritz Stiller, who began his career in the 1910s in Svenska Biografteatern's film studio here on Lidingö. A little further away you can see AGA's yellow optics tower, where submarine periscopes were developed.
Här i närheten låg Galgbacken, Stockholm: Near here was Galgbacken, Gallows Hill, Stockholm's largest and last public execution site, and a few stones by Solandergatan still mark the spot, which is now a protected ancient monument. The street itself is named after the botanist Daniel Solander, a pupil of Carl Linnaeus. And on a happier note: in an old cinema right next door, EMI built a recording studio modelled on Abbey Road, where Anni-Frid Lyngstad recorded her first solo album before Abba was formed.
Här i trakten fanns en gång en ort som h: Around here there was once a place called Backen och Hultet. In 1990 it counted as a small locality with buildings in Kållered parish, but it then grew together with both Kållered and Lindome, and after that there's no longer any settlement unit by that name. A little further away is Lake Tulebosjön, eight metres deep.
Här i trakten stod slaget vid Brännkyrka: Around here the Battle of Brännkyrka was fought on 27 July 1518, in the final phase of the union wars, between union troops and Swedish rebel forces, and the Swedes won. Far more peaceful was Enskedemejeriet, one of the Mjölkcentralen dairy cooperative's dairies, which operated here from 1943 to 1992. A little further away is Valla torg, named after Valla gård with roots in the Middle Ages, with the Vallafontänen fountain by Bertil Johnson.
Här ligger Sahlgrenska universitetssjukh: This is Sahlgrenska University Hospital, one of the largest hospitals in Northern Europe. It is named after Niclas Sahlgren, yet another of the wealthy directors of the Swedish East India Company, whose money laid the foundation for the hospital.
Här ligger Skinnarviksberget, den högsta: This is Skinnarviksberget, the highest natural point in central Stockholm. Climb up and you'll get a wide view over Riddarfjärden bay, the City Hall and Kungsholmen. The name comes from the skinners who once prepared hides and leather by the cove.
Här ligger två av Stockholms mest besökt: Two of Stockholm's most visited museums are here. The palace-like building is the Nordic Museum. Behind it is the Vasa Museum, with the warship Vasa, which sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 and was salvaged in 1961.
Här ligger Östermalms saluhall från 1888: This is Östermalms saluhall from 1888, one of the most beautiful food halls in Europe. Inside the old brick building, fish, cheese and delicacies are sold.
Här låg Råsunda fotbollsstadion, en gång: This was the site of Råsunda football stadium, once the national arena with room for 37,285 spectators. It had a soft opening in April 1937 with AIK against Malmö FF, and in May that year King Gustaf V officially opened it during the match between Sweden and England. A stone's throw away is Charlottenburg, Solna's local heritage centre, with a local history museum and a small park to play in.
Här låg en gång Sveriges största mentals: Sweden's largest psychiatric hospital once stood here. Beckomberga Hospital was in use from 1932 to 1995, and in the mid-20th century it had 2,000 patients, making it one of the largest in Europe. When it closed, around 250 beds remained. Since the mid-2000s, the old hospital buildings have been converted into homes.
Här mäter gatunamnen jord. Marklandsgata: Here the street names measure land. Marklandsgatan got its name in 1959 from 'markland', a unit for valuing land. At the Marklandsgatan stop, tram line 3 turns around, while lines 1, 2, 7 and 8 pass through on their way to Frölunda torg and Tynnered. Right next to it runs Dag Hammarskjöldsleden, five kilometres long from Linnéplatsen.
Här passerar Hagsätrastråket, ett promen: This is where Hagsätrastråket passes, a walking route of about 12 kilometres that runs all the way from Hagsätra to Stortorget, the main square in Gamla stan, the Old Town, past Enskede gård and across the Skansbron bridge to Södermalm. The name Enskede gård comes from the old manor and large estate, mentioned as early as the 1390s. Right next to it is Enskedeparken, which got its name in 1979.
Här på västra Södermalm snurrade förr vä: Here in western Södermalm, the windmill Brinckan once turned. It was documented from the 1670s and disappeared in 1884, but it lives on in Josabeth Sjöberg's watercolours from the 1850s. The surrounding area is called Södra stationsområdet, the South Station area, because Stockholm's first railway station, with a large rail yard, stood here before the city bought the land in 1979 to build housing. Up on the hill is the park Bergsgruvan.
Här pågår en liten stavningsstrid. Torge: A small spelling dispute is going on here. The square got its name in 1963 after Villa Brunsbo, by the nearby level crossing, which was owned by the Brundin family. The family therefore insists that the spelling with two n's is wrong. The centre building, designed by Sven Brolid's architectural firm, was built during the 1960s, and today the square is a hub for buses.
Here the road literally stands on a landslide. The name Jordfallsbron comes from "jordfall", an old word for landslide, which around the year 1150 caused parts of the ground at what is now Källarliden to collapse into the Göta älv river. The eastern part of the bridge and the E45 now stand on the landslide debris. The bridge is about 700 metres long and can open, with a 49.5-metre bascule span.
Här tar innerstaden slut och vallgraven: This is where the inner city ends and Vallgraven, the old moat, begins. The winding canal is what's left of the fortifications that once surrounded Gothenburg. Along the water is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks like a church, and the people of Gothenburg have called it the fish church ever since.
Här är en klurig geografifråga: centrala: Here's a tricky geography question: central Spånga, with the commuter train station and town centre, is in the district of Solhem, while Spånga Church itself is in the district of Tensta. Spånga is not an official area, you see, but a name that lives on from the old parish. In the other direction stretches Nälsta, with a mix of villas, terraced houses and blocks of flats.
Här är ett ortnamnsmysterium som löser s: Here's a place-name mystery that solves itself: the historic farm Råsta and its neighbour Frösunda together gave rise to the name Råsunda – Råsta plus Frösunda. And the neighbouring district of Hallonbergen? It's on a rocky hill and was probably named after the area, which used to be rich in raspberry thickets – "hallon" means raspberry.
Här, på Campus Solna, utses varje år mot: Here, at Campus Solna, the winners of the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine are chosen every year by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet. Its neighbour Biomedicum is one of Europe's largest laboratories, with just over 82,000 square metres on eleven floors. Also check out Aula Medica, designed by Gert Wingårdh and named Building of the Year 2014.
Här, vid idrottsplatsen Yttern strax syd: Here, at the Yttern sports ground just south-west of the Rollsbo industrial area, Kungälv Arena is taking shape. The plan is a bandy hall for around 2,500 spectators and an ice rink for around 1,500, with room for bandy teams, ice hockey players and figure skaters alike. The arena will replace the historic bandy ground Skarpe Nord and at the same time take pressure off Oasen, the town's old ice rink.
Häradsvägen, som slutar en bit härifrån: Häradsvägen, which ends a little way from here at the Stuvsta tunnel, was laid out in the mid-1920s as relief work by the Svartlösa hundred's road association, which is where the name, 'Hundred Road', comes from. Forest had to be cleared to get through, and villas sprang up along the road. The tunnel itself is unusual: its northern entrance is built into a block of flats that straddles the road.
Härifrån kan man vandra riktigt långt, f: From here you can hike a really long way, because at Björkhagen metro station the first stage of Sörmlandsleden begins, a looping network of hiking trails totalling about 1,000 kilometres through the province of Södermanland. Markuskyrkan, St Mark's Church, next door is built on an old lakebed, in the birch grove that gave the district its name.
Härifrån ser du Älvsborgsbron spänna öve: From here you can see the Älvsborg Bridge spanning Göta älv, Gothenburg's river. When it opened in 1966, it was Sweden's longest suspension bridge. Out in the river mouth lies the New Älvsborg Fortress, Nya Älvsborgs fästning, from the 17th century. It protected the city against the Danes for over a hundred years.
Härifrån är det 10,9 kilometer med pende: From here it is 10.9 kilometres by commuter train to Stockholm Central, and on an ordinary winter weekday about 5,400 people board here. The neighbour is Eriksberg, a narrow strip between the E4 motorway and the railway, named after the Eriksberg croft from 1819. A little further away is Silverdal cemetery, laid out in 1914 as the garrison cemetery for the Stockholm garrison.
Härifrån är det cirka 14,5 kilometer in: From here it's about 14.5 kilometres into Stockholm Central Station, and the commuter train station has four tracks so that freight trains and long-distance trains can whizz past. In Järfälla Church, Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone in 1728 that was probably lying as a step. It then disappeared, but in 1939 seven fragments turned up, and they are kept today at the Swedish History Museum.
Härifrån är det nära till Fåfängan, ett: From here it's not far to Fåfängan, a small café up on a cliff with one of Stockholm's best views over the harbour entrance, Djurgården and Gamla stan, the Old Town.

From here it's not far to Fåfängan, a small café up on a cliff with one of Stockholm's best views over the harbour entrance, Djurgården and Gamla stan, the Old Town. Along Fjällgatan, a little to the west, there's another classic viewpoint with old houses and cobblestones.
Härifrån är det nära till Götaplatsen, s: From here it's not far to Götaplatsen, the city's cultural square. That's where you'll find the Gothenburg Museum of Art, which opened in 1923, and around the square are also the City Theatre and the Concert Hall. In the middle stands Poseidon, Carl Milles's powerful sea god.
Härifrån är det nära till Rågsveds friom: From here it's not far to Rågsved's open area, or Kräppladalen, just over 100 hectares of rift valley landscape with ridges, plateaus and steep slopes. Part of the area became a nature reserve in September 2018. In the middle of it is the Snösätra storage area, which since 2014 has become a centre for graffiti and street art, where the walls are painted with the property owners' permission.
Härryda kommun har en kuriös detalj: en: Härryda municipality has a curious detail: a small part in the west, Helenedal, actually counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. A little north-east of Mölnlycke is Stora Bråta, just nine kilometres from central Gothenburg, which is the city's nearest small village. The municipality's main town is Mölnlycke.
Hässelby har fått sitt namn från Hässelb: Hässelby is named after Hässelby Castle, whose lands once covered large parts of today's Hässelby gård, Hässelby strand and Hässelby villastad. Many farms and crofts on the estate have given their names to places in the neighbourhood. And a funny detail: the castle is in the district of Hässelby gård, but in the postal town of Vällingby.
Hässelby slott uppfördes på 1650-talet,: Hässelby Palace was built in the 1650s, possibly to designs by Simon de la Vallée, and is counted among the oldest surviving secular buildings in Stockholm. Its tower-topped wings are angled slightly inwards. Just east of the entrance, the runestone U 79 stands on top of a Viking Age burial mound, but it originally stood below Skesta backe, about three kilometres away, and was moved here in the 1860s. In its marketing today the palace is spelled Hesselby, using the older spelling.
Hässelby strand bildades som stadsdel 19: Hässelby strand was formed as a district in 1954, and here by Lake Mälaren stands Hässelbyverket, a combined heat and power plant that started operating in 1959 and produces both electricity and district heating. The buildings are classified green by the City Museum, meaning especially valuable. When the metro reached here on 18 November 1958, the first train left Bagarmossen at 13.28, decorated with flags both front and back.
Hässelby trädgårds- och hembygdsmuseum: Hässelby garden and local history museum
Hässelby villastad är Stockholms västlig: Hässelby villastad is Stockholm's westernmost and, by area, largest district. A little way from here is Åkermyntan's shopping centre from 1977, which has the odd honour of being mentioned in one of the comedy group Killinggänget's sketches. Further away, outside the Hässelby garden and local heritage museum, stands a runestone of grey granite that was found in Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved to the museum in 1988.

Hässelby villastad is Stockholm's westernmost district and also the largest by area, and it was once a municipality of its own, the market town of Hässelby villastad. A little way from here, outside the Hässelby garden and local history museum, stands a runestone of grey granite that was found at Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved to the museum in 1988. The whole Hässelby area takes its name from Hässelby Palace.
Hässelbygårdsskolan byggdes med det mest: Hässelbygårdsskolan was built with just about everything: a doctor's surgery, two dining halls, a swimming pool and an assembly hall that was also the Prisma cinema. The cinema opened in 1960 and showed films to the public until 1984. The nearby metro station sits on a viaduct above Hässelby torg, the square.
Hästa klack är ett av Järfällas allra ny: Hästa klack is one of Järfälla's very newest nature reserves, protected since 2026, with 14 hectares of conifer forest and open forest edges. In the other direction is Kyrkbyn, which used to be called Järfälla gård and was one of the historic farms of the parish. Today it has given its name to a housing area in the culturally and historically valuable garden suburb of Barkarby villastad.
Hästarna är stjärnorna i Åby. Strax inti: The horses are the stars in Åby. Right next to us is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track, which is home to Åby Travgymnasium, one of the country's oldest trotting upper secondary schools, where students get a B trainer's licence. Very close to the stop is also Åbybadet, the swimming baths opened in 2023. And the name Mölndal? It comes from the mills that stood by the rapids of the Mölndalsån river since the Middle Ages.
Hästskosömsfabriken: Hästskosömsfabriken, the old horseshoe nail factory
Hågelby gård har medeltida rötter, men d: Hågelby farm has medieval roots, but most of today's buildings and park were created in the 1910s on the initiative of the telephone manufacturer Lars Magnus Ericsson and his wife Hilda. Several buildings were made of reinforced concrete, a novelty in Sweden at the time. By the farm stands a runestone from the mid-11th century, and from here the Aspen nature trail runs just over seven kilometres around the lake.
Håll i dig i rulltrappan! På tunnelbanes: Hold on tight on the escalator! Västra skogen metro station has Sweden's longest escalator, 66 metres long with a rise of 33 metres. The record is set to be beaten, though, by an escalator at Nacka metro station on the blue line, which is expected to be 82 metres long. A little way from here is Arken, the head office of Posten AB, the Swedish postal service.
Håll utkik efter de rödlysande neonglasö: Keep an eye out for the glowing red neon glasses above Ringdahls Optik at Fleminggatan 36. The signs are from the 1950s and 1960s, and in 2017 the City Museum nominated them for the competition Lysande skylt, Brilliant Sign. Celsiusgatan nearby is named after Anders Celsius, even though he had no particular connection to Kungsholmen.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter Långetjä: The stop is named after Långetjärnen, a forest lake right nearby that is eight metres deep and lies 93.5 metres above sea level. Nearby are also the two tiny Kroppedammarna ponds, the eastern and the western one. The water from here flows via the Finnebäcken stream towards the Kungsbackaån river.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter Näsets k: The stop is named after Näsets kvarn, one of only two windmills left on Lidingö. In the 1840s there were seven. Next to it is Kvarnskolan from 1875, a school that at first took only girls. On Stockholmsvägen stands Näsets krog, a roadside inn from the 18th century, and Villa Nynäs, where Lidingö's probably first general store stood.
Hållplatsen har fått namn efter SKF, som: The stop is named after SKF, which was founded in Gothenburg in 1907 and became the world's leading maker of ball bearings. The factory area here in Gamlestaden has been the company's home for over a hundred years.
Hållplatsen har fått sitt namn efter Bil: The stop is named after Billdals gård, the manor just a stone's throw away in the Billdals park nature area in southern Gothenburg. A little northeast of Billdal is also Stora Svindal, a settlement that until 2015 counted as a small village of its own but has now been swallowed up by the town of Billdal.
Hållplatsen ligger vid Volvos bilfabrik,: The stop is at Volvo's car factory, Torslandaverken. Digging began on 4 November 1957, and on 24 April 1964 the factory was opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf. The first car to leave the line was a Volvo Amazon, and the sporty P1800 was also built here from the start. Today models including the XC90 are made in Torslanda.
Högdalens centrum planerades med Välling: Högdalen centre was planned with Vällingby centre as its model and was completed in 1959. The Rondo cinema was also here between 1961 and 1983. Right next door is Högdalshallen from 1971, which closed for four years for a major renovation and reopened its swimming pool in June 2022. And at the metro, the middle track leads into SL's train depot.
Högdalens industriområde har av Stockhol: Högdalen industrial area has been named by the City of Stockholm as the city's most important technical supply area. In the middle of it stands Högdalenverket, which burns waste and turns it into electricity and district heating. When it started operating in 1970 it produced only electricity; the district heating came in 1979. A little way off is Gubbängens IP sports ground, which was once known for car speedway.
Högdalshallen har haft en händelserik hi: Högdalshallen has had an eventful history. The swimming and sports hall was completed in 1971, and between 2012 and 2018 it was operated by a private company. Because of mismanagement, the City of Stockholm took back control, and the hall was then closed for four years for extensive renovations before the swimming pool could reopen in June 2022.
Höghusen i Granängsringen, en bit härifr: The tower blocks of Granängsringen, a little way from here, were built in 1968–1969 and are a textbook example of the Million Programme's housing planning, Sweden's big push to build a million homes, with no fewer than 932 flats. Bollmora, where the area lies, was actually a separate built-up locality from 1965 to 1974 and is now usually called Tyresö centrum. Further south in the municipality, Storskogen takes over, with patches of genuine old-growth forest in Tyresta National Park.
Höghusen i kvarteren här omkring hör til: The high-rises in the blocks around here belong to Granängsringen, built in just two years, 1968–1969, with 932 flats – a textbook example of the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive of the 1960s and 70s. The area is in Bollmora, which had 16,566 residents in 2010 and is home to Tyresö municipality's central administration. Bollmora was once a separate urban area, but today it counts as part of the Stockholm urban area.
Höghusen runt omkring utgör Granängsring: The tower blocks all around make up Granängsringen, built in record time in 1968–1969 with 932 apartments – a typical example of housing planning under the Million Programme, Sweden's big post-war housing drive. A short walk away is Tyresö centrum, which is really called Bollmora, with the municipal offices, a glazed shopping arcade and Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church for all of Tyresö.
Höghuset Hagahuset, ritat av Stig Annerf: The high-rise Hagahuset, designed by Stig Annerfelt, was built in 1954–1957 as the County Council Building and housed the entire administration of Stockholm County Council until the early 1970s. A short walk into Haga Park rises Frösundatoppen, also called Haga kulle, one of the county's highest man-made hills at about 72 metres above sea level. In the Copper Tents, Haga Park Museum displays a large wooden model of Stora Haga Palace, which Gustav III had planned.
Höghuset och marmorintarsian på torget: The tower block and the marble inlay on the square
Höjden Stigberget var Stockholms avrättn: The hill Stigberget was Stockholm's place of execution for most of the 16th and 17th centuries, and the old block name Justitia still recalls it. The mood is more cheerful today: on Stigbergsgatan you'll find Blockmakarens hus, the Blockmaker's House, a museum flat furnished as in the early 20th century. On Tjärhovsgatan, Kafé 44 has been based since 1984 in the old Swedish bottle-cap factory, and Cornelisparken, dedicated to the singer Cornelis Vreeswijk, is right next door.
Höjden här, Strömmensberg, har kallats b: The hill here, Strömmensberg, has been called Bagaregårdshöjden, Kristinedalshöjden and the Kristinedal plateau. The name probably comes from Olof Ström, the ironworks owner of the Sävenäs estate, a cousin of Niclas Sahlgren and one of the biggest stakeholders in the Swedish East India Company. In his day, in the 18th century, the hill was completely undeveloped. Today the average age here is lower than in the rest of Gothenburg.
Hökarängen var en av de första förortern: Hökarängen was one of the first suburbs to grow up along the new metro after the Second World War, and its car-free centre, designed by David Helldén, became a model for suburbs all over Sweden. Right next to it is Farsta fire station, which was originally called Enskede fire station. And the light, arched roof of Gubbängshallen can be seen from far across Gubbängsfältet, the Gubbängen fields.
Hökarängen växte fram i rasande takt: 19: Hökarängen grew at a furious pace: in 1946 there were 45 people living here, and just six years later there were 16,000. The car-free town centre, designed by David Helldén, set the style for suburbs across the whole Swedish welfare state. Helldén also designed the Tobaksområdet area with its 16 slab blocks, one of which bears the delightful name Sjöskumspipan 4, the Meerschaum Pipe. And the metro station was the terminus of the city's very first metro line.
Hökarängens tunnelbanestation har en pla: Hökarängen metro station has a place in the history books. It opened on 1 October 1950 as the terminus of Stockholm's very first metro line from Slussen and remained the terminus until November 1958. The station was designed by Peter Celsing. Right nearby, at Lingvägen and Örbyleden, stands Söderledskyrkan, a red-brick church opened in 1960 and since 1990 a legally protected listed building.
Hökmossens gård från 1750-talet var ursp: Hökmossen farm from the 1750s was originally a croft under Västberga gård, and since the mid-1990s a cultural association has run activities in the house. A little way off runs Älvsjövägen, with a curious comparison: its 22,000 vehicles a day are as many as all the daily border traffic between Norway and Sweden along the E6 and E18.
Hönö har fått sitt namn av själva berget: Hönö got its name from the rock itself. It comes from the Old West Norse word ‘hein’, meaning whetstone, and refers to the island's round, smoothly polished rock slabs. The island has the most residents in the whole of Öckerö municipality, and since 2018 its built-up area has grown together with Öckerö's. A little way off is Hönö Church.
Hönö är den folkrikaste ön i Öckerö komm: Hönö is the most populous island in Öckerö municipality, with more than 5,500 permanent residents on just over five and a half square kilometres. In 2018 the town grew together with neighbouring Öckerö and is now called Hönö-Öckerö. The round, polished rock gave the island its name, from an old word for whetstone. A little way from here is Hönö Church.
Hönö är kommunens folkrikaste ö, och nam: Hönö is the municipality's most populous island, and the name is really old. It's based on the Old West Norse word hein, whetstone, and refers to the round, smoothly polished rocks. The neighbouring island of Fotö is much smaller, but yew grows there, locally called barlind, and from the higher parts you can see Vinga on a clear day.
Hönöleden är Sveriges mest trafikerade f: Hönöleden is Sweden's busiest ferry route counted in motor vehicles, with just over 2.3 million vehicles in 2009. The ferries run between Lilla Varholmen, by Hisingen island, and Hönö, a distance of 2,500 metres that takes twelve minutes. The route counts as part of county road 155 and is therefore free. Among the ferries are M/S Ada, M/S Beda, M/S Göta and M/S Marie.
Hösten 2006 brann den gamla stationskure: In autumn 2006 the old shelter at Östberga station burned down, and today a glass shelter stands in its place. The station itself has been here since 1910. A couple of hundred metres away is the Laurin villa at Hildingavägen 26, designed in 1910 by Karl Güettler, and at the Djursholm cemetery in Altorp is the funeral chapel where services are held around All Saints' Day.
I Backa Folkets hus, byggt 1924 och om-: Backa Folkets hus, the community hall built in 1924 and rebuilt and extended in functionalist style in 1939, once housed the Rex cinema. It opened in September 1940 and closed in June 1958. But the screen made a comeback: in 1992 Folkets Hus Backa bio opened in the same premises. The building is included in the municipality's conservation programme and has five rooms for between 30 and 200 people.
I Backlura, den nordöstligaste delen av: In Backlura, the north-easternmost part of the Hässelby villa town near the border with Järfälla, all the streets are named after flowers and plants. A couple of minutes from here stands One Tonne Life, also known as Villa Bright Living, an experimental low-energy house for one family, designed by Wingårdh Architects with A-hus as the developer.
I Bergsjön har gatorna fått namn efter r: In Bergsjön the streets are named after space and the universe, hence Teleskopgatan, Telescope Street, and Stjärnbildsgatan, Constellation Street. On Stjärnbildsgatan in the 1980s, something unusual was done with empty apartments: the upper floors of the four-storey buildings were simply lifted off, leaving terraced houses around spacious courtyards. Nearby is also Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the Nordic region's first folk high school for Roma students, opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
In Bergsjön, outer space is never far away. Teleskopgatan, Telescope Street, got its name in 1967 and belongs to a whole group of street names on the theme of space and the universe. The district lies about 8 kilometres from the centre and had just over 16,000 inhabitants in 2013. Keep an eye out for more celestial bodies on the signs along the way.
I Bromstens industriområde fanns en gång: Bromsten's industrial area was once home to Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large graffiti painting. It was a piece of living street-art history, but in early December 2021 the wall was demolished, and the painting disappeared with it. The Bromsten district belongs to the Järva city district, and the Bällstaån stream runs through it.
I Danderyd startade 2011 tennisakademin: In 2011 the Good to Great tennis academy started in Danderyd, founded by the former tennis pros Magnus Norman, Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillström. Among the students were the brothers Mikael and Elias Ymer. All around lies Enebyberg, a villa community largely characterised by buildings from the first half of the 20th century.
I Eriksbergshallen, där Eriksbergs Mekan: In Eriksbergshallen, where the Eriksberg shipyard, Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad, once operated, the Melodifestivalen song contest was held in 1997. The shipyard buildings have found new roles: the neighbouring Quality Hotel 11 used to be called Blå Hallen, the Blue Hall. And in a converted service building for the floating docks, the restaurant Westra Piren opened in 1990 and won a Michelin star as early as 1992.
I Fructushuset på Ulvsundavägen tillverk: In the Fructus Building on Ulvsundavägen, the soft drink Pommac was once made. The factory was built in 1939–1940, and the long white building is considered a fine example of a modern, functional factory. By the canal towards Lake Ulvsundasjön stands the Dairy Villa, Mejerivillan, from 1905, the only building left of the Ulvsunda farm.
I Gamla Filmstaden i Råsunda producerade: At Gamla Filmstaden, the Old Film City in Råsunda, a significant share of Swedish cinema was produced – nearly 400 feature films between 1920 and 1973 – and the place is associated above all with Ingmar Bergman. The last film, En liten julsaga, A Little Christmas Story, was shot in 1999. Näckrosen station got its name from Näckrosdammen, the Water Lily Pond, because the name Råsunda was not considered suitable when Råsunda Stadium was by another station.
I Glömstadalen, en bit härifrån, finns G: In Glömstadalen, a little way from here, is Glömstahällen – a rock slab with runes carved directly into the bedrock. Glömsta used to be a noble estate and is today a residential area around Lake Gömmaren and the Gömmaren nature reserve. Much of the area used to be holiday cottages, which have slowly been joined by newly built family homes.
I Hagaparkens sydöstra del ligger Finnst: In the southeast of Hagaparken, Haga Park, are Finnstugorna, the Finnish Cottages. The log house Stora Finnstugan was already there when Gustav III bought Haga in 1771; back then the place was called Finntorpet, and it's said the king enjoyed himself here even as crown prince. Not far away is Stallgrunden, the remains of Gustav III's Great Stables, where excavation began in 1789. The stables were meant as a counterpart to Stora Haga slott, the Great Haga Palace, but were never finished.
I Hammarbyverket utvinns värme och kyla: At Hammarbyverket, heat and cooling are extracted from treated wastewater. The plant went into operation in 1986, and in 2013 it was counted as the world's largest heat pump plant of its kind. Its neighbour is Fryshuset, the youth centre that aims to help young people change the world through their passions. By the quay, from 2017 to December 2024, the Swedish Internet Foundation ran Goto 10, a free meeting place for internet ideas.
I Hanneberg, en bit härifrån, har parken: In Hanneberg, a little way from here, the park has two rabbit houses where children and young people can keep and look after their own rabbits. The area also has a youth centre with a café and three villas from the early 20th century. At Storgatan 27 is Löftets kyrka, a former church building.
I Historiska museets Guldrum glänser for: In the Gold Room of the Swedish History Museum, ancient times really do glitter. The collections hold a total of 52 kilos of gold and over 200 kilos of silver, including three unique gold collars from the Migration Period and the Timboholm Hoard, Sweden's largest gold treasure found in one place. Since 2020 the museum has shared its building with the Economic Museum, the Royal Coin Cabinet. Next door stood Fredrikshov, which managed to be a royal palace, a prison and an arsenal.
I Härlandaparken ligger resterna av en g: In Härlandaparken park lie the remains of an old church. The parish was merged into Nylöse as early as 1528, and what remained was the Härlanda church ruin, next door to the new church. Munkebäckstorget nearby is named after the Munkebäcken stream. The monks in the name – munkar in Swedish – were probably monks from Nya Lödöse.
I Hässelby villastad står ett experiment: In Hässelby Villastad stands an experimental house with the telling name One Tonne Life, a climate-smart low-energy house designed by Wingårdh Architects. It was one of five finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year 2011. A little further away towards Lake Mälaren is Lövsta, an area that has been settled for at least 2,000 years.
I Hässelbygårdsskolans aula fanns biogra: The assembly hall of Hässelbygård School housed the Prisma cinema, which opened in November 1960 and showed films to the public until December 1984. The school also got both a doctor's surgery and a swimming pool. A little further away is Hässelby familjehotell, which when it opened in 1955 was the master builder Olle Engkvist's largest collective housing block. The professional services were discontinued in 1976, but the residents still run some activities on a voluntary basis.
I Inverness låg bryggeriet Inverness bru: In Inverness, the brewery Inverness brunn operated between 1929 and 1945. Among other things, Sweden's first club soda was made here. The spring is still there on the shore of Stocksundet, but the water is unfit to drink and tastes salty. Closer to the stop was the 18th-century farm Mörby gård, which gave the area its name. It became a listed building in 1944 but burned down in 1976.
I Kulturum huserar delar av Partille gym: Kulturum houses parts of Partille gymnasium, an upper secondary school that used to be called Porthälla gymnasium. A little further away stood Partillebohallen, opened in 1967 as Porthällaskolan's sports hall, with a handball hall, a bowling alley and stands for about 1,800 spectators. The hall hosted everything from badminton and basketball to table tennis, and IK Sävehof played here up to and including spring 2016.
I Kvarnparken, vid bäcken som rinner frå: In Kvarnparken, the Mill Park, by the stream that flows from Lake Ekebysjön to the Edsviken bay, is the rune carving Norahällen, cut directly into a smooth slab of bedrock. There is also the old mill cottage from the 18th century, which once had a water mill and a water-powered sawmill and is now used as a weaving workshop. And if you fancy a dip, there's Kvarnparksbadet, a bathing spot run by dedicated volunteers.
I Lilleby finns Sillviks Havskoloni, som: In Lilleby you'll find Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside cottage colony formed when the Burgården colony in central Gothenburg was demolished to make way for the Valhallabadet swimming baths. The colony has just over 120 cottages, a shared clubhouse and a beach café, and its genuine 1950s style has been preserved. So a swimming baths in town gave rise to a whole cottage village by the sea.
I Lundas arbets- och industriområde finn: Lunda's business and industrial area has a surprising amount of green technology. Ferroamp, a Swedish greentech company founded by Björn Jernström in 2010, has its development and production in Spånga. The company's systems optimise electricity in buildings with solar panels, small-scale wind power, energy storage and charging of vehicle batteries.
I Mölnlycke utbildas bland annat tullspe: In Mölnlycke, among other things, customs specialists are trained. Yrkeshögskolan i Mölnlycke, a higher vocational college run by Härryda Municipality, started in 1998 and has about 200 students, who can also become payroll specialists or work with information security. A little way off, in the middle of central Mölnlycke, lies the little lake Massetjärnen.
I Nackareservatet, en bit härifrån, står: In the Nacka nature reserve, a little way from here, stands the croft Brotorp, a small single cottage measuring eight by five metres, which today is an ancient monument and the clubhouse of the orienteering club Skogsluffarnas OK. Right next to it flows the Ältaån stream, which long-distance skaters and canoeists like to call the Brotorp Canal. Closer by was the croft Parken, established in 1839 and demolished in the mid-1950s.
I Nobelparken, ett stenkast härifrån, sk: In Nobelparken, a stone's throw from here, a monumental Nobel Palace in memory of Alfred Nobel was supposed to stand. Ferdinand Boberg worked on the designs between 1906 and 1911, but it was never built. The only reminders of the grand plans are the names Nobelparken and Nobelgatan, decided in 1912. Today the street leads through Diplomatstaden, the Diplomat Town, an exclusive villa area.
I Nockeby, en bit härifrån, ligger Villa: In Nockeby, a little way from here on Grönviksvägen, is Villa Markelius, the architect Sven Markelius' own functionalist home between 1930 and 1938. Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church, was built on the land where the old terminus of the Nockebybanan tram line used to be and was consecrated in 1962. Winding past the villas is Hässelbystråket, a walking trail of about 19 kilometres that runs all the way from Hässelby strand to Gamla stan, the Old Town.
I Nordre älv, en bit härifrån, finns Orm: In the Nordre älv river, a little way from here, is the Ormo barrier, an adjustable dam that can choke the flow in the Nordre älv when needed. The water is then diverted instead into the Gothenburg branch of the Göta älv. The structure lies between the Nordre älv railway bridge and the Kornhall ferry – a kind of tap that controls how the river divides.
I Restaurang Barnvagnsfabrikens gamla lo: In the old premises of Restaurang Barnvagnsfabriken, the old pram factory, on Sockenvägen, the exclusive restaurant Mistral was based between 2009 and 2012, serving local seasonal produce and often biodynamic wines. The restaurant came from Gamla stan, the Old Town, where it had held a Michelin star. Right next door is the Mursmäckan block, named after the women who carried mortar to the bricklayers on building sites, and its urban terraced houses were named Stockholm Building of the Year in 2012.
I Roslags Näsby finns en runhäll med en: In Roslags Näsby there is a rune-carved rock with a literary discovery story. The Kvarntorp rock was found in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård, who was living in Täby at the time. The carving is indistinct and partly worn away, but it contains the word for stepsons, which is known from only a handful of runic inscriptions. Roslags Näsby is about one kilometre south of Täby centrum.
I Troxhammar på södra Färingsö ligger Tr: In Troxhammar on southern Färingsö is Troxhammar Golf Club, but the area has much older traces than golf balls. A little further away stands a 2.2-metre-tall Viking Age runestone of granite, and the village of Ekeby is mentioned as early as 1342, when land was exchanged with Vårfruberga convent. In the 1400s the Crown took over a long-abandoned Crown farm in Ekeby.
I Vinsta industriområde ligger Vällingby: In the Vinsta industrial area is Vällingby fire station, designed by Mårten J. Larsson and opened in January 1965, where the firefighters are specially trained in roof ventilation and high-altitude climbing. Hässelby kvarn also once stood nearby, a windmill belonging to the Hässelby manor estate, known since the mid-1600s but gone by the 1820s. When the metro provisionally reached Hässelby gård in 1956, it took just one month before passenger services on the Spånga–Lövsta railway ended.
I berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig Nybo: Hidden in the rock a little way from here is Nybohovshissen, an inclined lift in a rock tunnel nicknamed Klumpen, the Lump. It is 230 metres long, climbs 37 metres, and the ride takes 2 minutes and 16 seconds between Liljeholmen metro station and Nybohovsberget hill. The Nyboda tunnels also run through Nybodaberget, and the oldest of them became Sweden's very first railway tunnel when the Western Main Line was brought to Stockholm in 1860.
I byn Bärby skipades rätt under 1800-tal: Justice was dispensed in the village of Bärby in the 1800s. This was the court site for the Western and Eastern Hising court district, formed in 1824 and covering both the Västra and Östra Hising hundreds. The court district lasted until 1888, when it was merged into the Askim, Hising and Sävedal court district. Today Bärby is a quiet small village west of Säve.
I byn Törnby på södra Färingsö, en bit h: In the village of Törnby on southern Färingsö, a little way from here, there were in 1541 two farms owned by the nobility and one taxpaying farm, and in 1544 Karin Axelsdotter Tott sold both noble farms to none other than Gustav Vasa. The village is mentioned as early as 1342 and has now grown together with Stenhamra, while its neighbour Söderberga has become part of the Tureholm urban area.
I den lilla Karptjärnen, en bit härifrån: In the little pond Karptjärnen, a short distance from here, live both medicinal leeches and horse leeches – and they are believed to have been introduced back when Stockholm's pharmacies released and collected leeches used to treat various ailments. In spring the pond teems with tadpoles. The area around Tyresö Strand has grown with detached, semi-detached and terraced houses since the mid-1990s, but the same district is also home to Tyresö Palace and church from the 17th century.
I det före detta Långbro sjukhuset fanns: For several years the former Långbro hospital housed Långbro Folk High School. Among other things, it was home to the Linnea art school, a three-year post-secondary art programme for people with intellectual disabilities. In 2007 the programme moved to Södra Stockholms folkhögskola in Skärholmen. The hospital's old core area is today Långbroparken park.
I det här industriområdet forskade state: In this industrial area, the state once did research on aircraft. The Aeronautical Research Institute was in the Ulvsunda industrial area and carried out research and tests in aeronautics, until at the turn of 2000/2001 the agency became part of the Swedish Defence Research Agency. A little way from here, the Huvudsta bridge crosses over to Solna, popularly known as the Pripps bridge.
I det här området finns något så ovanlig: In this area there's something as unusual as a prison exclusively for women, Anstalten Sagsjön in Lindome. Not far from there is Lindome station, which has had a real roller-coaster history: opened in 1888, closed to passenger traffic in 1970 and shut down completely in 1989, only to get a new lease of life with the commuter trains in 1992.
I det informella området Vasalund ligger: In the informal area of Vasalund are Solna's only municipal upper secondary school and the Vasalundshallen sports hall. This is also where you find Södra Långgatan, which became the Lyckliga gatan, the Happy Street, of the song sung by Anna-Lena Löfgren, although the part of the street in the song was actually in Hagalund. The area also has Charlottenburg, Solna's local heritage farmstead with Solna local history museum.
I en gammal konsumbyggnad i villaområdet: In an old Konsum co-op building in the villa area was the restaurant Aloë, which existed from 2015 to 2025. The restaurateurs Daniel Höglander and Niclas Jönsson were awarded a Michelin star in 2018, and two years later it became two. There was room for only 35 guests, and the name Aloë is Latin for unknown origin.
I en trädgård vid gamla Råsta gård, en k: In a garden at the old Råsta gård, a short walk from here, stands Råstastenen, a runestone from the time when Råsta belonged to Spånga parish. Another runestone used to stand here, but only a fragment of it remains, which since 1976 has been kept at the Sundbyberg museum. Råsta gård lies at the north-western corner of Lake Råstasjön.
I grannskapet öppnade 1907 landets först: In 1907, the country's first home for patients with skin tuberculosis opened in this neighbourhood. They were treated with Finsen light, ultraviolet light, a method invented by the Danish physician Niels Ryberg Finsen, who received the Nobel Prize for it in 1903. Right next door was also Vattenborgen, the Water Castle, one of the city's early water reservoirs, demolished in 1934. Stadshagsplan stands on the site today.
I hamnbyn Kornhall en bit härifrån gömme: In the harbour village of Kornhall, a little way from here, hides a name with a whiff of grain. According to place-name researchers, it refers to the cereal barley, "korn", and to "hall", a place where barley was loaded or unloaded, and the name is recorded as early as 1774. The village is best known, though, for the ferry over the Nordre älv river, a crossing with a long history that cuts the journey to Gothenburg considerably.
I huset Ryttaren 15 vid Valhallavägen in: In the Ryttaren 15 building on Valhallavägen, the first rubbish chutes were installed, using the architect Sven Wallander's own patent. From the start, the building was also managed so that tenants gradually bought shares in the property company, a forerunner of housing cooperatives and of HSB, which Wallander helped found in 1923. Wittstocksgatan next door commemorates Johan Banér's victory at Wittstock in 1636.
I hörnet av Kronobergsparken finns en ju: In a corner of Kronoberg Park is a Jewish cemetery that came about because of a quarrel. Some members of the city's Jewish congregation felt that one of its leading figures, Aaron Isaac, was far too authoritarian, so they got themselves a cemetery of their own. It was laid out in 1787, the last burial took place in 1857, and 209 people rest here. A little further away shone the Sörman sign, one of Stockholm's classic neon signs.
I kvarteren runt Skälby gård har folk hå: People have been living in the blocks around Skälby gård for a long time: the manor and former estate have existed since the 16th century, and the current main building from 1802 sits among no fewer than four burial grounds. A little way from here there is also a pair of Viking Age runestones, U 88 and U 89, known as the runestones by Häradsvägen, which already in the 17th century stood inside a circle of smaller, round stones.
I norra delen av Rissne, inte långt häri: In the northern part of Rissne, not far from here, the whole blue line goes to sleep. All the metro trains that run on the blue line are parked in the Rissne depot, on underground tracks. Between 1975 and 1985, the connecting track there was also used by ordinary passengers, because the stretch via Huvudsta and Rissne wasn't yet finished.
I närheten har skonaren Ingo sin hemmaha: Nearby, the schooner Ingo has her home port, a three-masted vessel built in 1922 that carries on the west coast's tradition of sailing traditional ships. A short walk away stands Kanalhuset, where SVT, Sveriges Radio and Utbildningsradion, Sweden's public television, radio and educational broadcaster, have their operations. The building was actually built for the camera company Hasselblad, which however moved out after a short time. And on Jägaregatan there used to be the cinema Lundby Bio.
I närheten ligger Backa Folkets hus, upp: Nearby is Backa Folkets hus, a community hall built in 1924 and rebuilt and extended in 1939 in functionalist style by Sven Wedenmark. The Rex cinema opened here on 13 September 1940 and showed films right up to 1958. But that wasn't the end of the screen: in 1992 Folkets Hus Backa bio opened in the same premises.
I närheten ligger Näsbydal, ett bostadso: Nearby is Näsbydal, a housing area shaped like an egg, with 900 flats ranging from studios with a sleeping alcove to seven-room flats on two floors. The association has its own tennis court, basketball court, boules court and barbecue area. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, an indistinct and partly worn-away runic rock slab that the author Jan Fridegård found in 1943.
I närheten låg Fjällbohemmet, ett vårdhe: Nearby was Fjällbohemmet, a care home in Utby between 1939 and 1983. After that it became sheltered housing for the elderly, before it was closed down around 1990. Utby also has a much older history: the old Utby parish was merged into Partille parish as early as 1571, after its church was destroyed in 1566.
I området Kristinedal en bit härifrån ka: In the Kristinedal area a little way from here, you can see the 1960s dream of a house of your own. Around a hundred villas, terraced and linked houses were finished in 1964, with single-storey and split-level houses in facing brick. It was in this kind of small-house area that the carport was introduced. The neighbouring area of Sjövalla is older and began to be built up with villas as early as the 1920s and 1930s.
I området Kummelby låg förr en gård, och: In the Kummelby area there was once a farm, and on its site the first Kummelby Church was built in 1956–1957. It was so small that only 50 people could fit inside, so it was sometimes called Kummelby's little church. Just before Christmas 2000 a new church was consecrated. By the church also stands the Kummelby Stone, a runestone from the late 11th century.
I området finns Mariakyrkan i Hammarkull: In the area is Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, in Hammarkullen, formerly called Tomaskyrkan, which unusually is shared by two denominations: the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. In the other direction is Hjällbo centrum, built in 1969, with a market hall for fruit and vegetables, a library and a church around the square.
I området ligger Atlantisområdet, en rad: The area includes Atlantisområdet, a terraced-house village designed by the architects Bertil Karlén, Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist in the early 1950s. The terraced houses attracted international attention and are today classed blue by the City Museum, the highest class. Lisbeth and Olof Palme lived in one of them with their three sons between 1968 and 1983.
I området ligger Glose, där betade stran: The area includes Glose, where grazed shore meadows meet the shallow waters of Ryskärsfjorden.
