Both birds and plants thrive here, and the fjord with Glose's shore meadows is part of the Nordre älv estuary, a vast nature reserve. The six-kilometre Glose å stream also flows out into the fjord.
I området ligger Gunnestorps mosse, en b: The area includes Gunnestorps mosse, a mix of lake, fen and bog in Hisingsparken, the Hisingen park. Reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow here side by side with cranberries, sundew and cotton grass. North of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, which is now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground.
I området ligger Helgered, med drygt 240: The area includes Helgered, with just over 240 households on both sides of Björlandavägen. In its north-eastern part is the beautiful walking area Klare mosse, where the Osbäcken stream has its source. Helgered also borders the nature areas Hisingsparken and Svarte mosse, so forest and bogland are close at hand from here.
I området ligger Hisingsparken, Göteborg: The area is home to Hisingsparken, Gothenburg's largest park area at about 320 hectares, which only got park status in 1980. The oldest part is S.A. Hedlund's park from the late 19th century. Joggers can choose between four trails, from the blue one at 2.8 kilometres to the green one at a full 11.1 kilometres. In the northern part is Kättilsröd 4-H farm.
I området ligger Mölnlycke, centralorten: This area includes Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda municipality, about ten kilometres south-east of central Gothenburg. The Mölndalsån river flows through the centre on its way from Lake Landvettersjön to Lake Rådasjön. Since 2023 even the village of Öjersjö in the neighbouring municipality of Partille counts as part of the same urban area, so Mölnlycke has grown across the municipal border.
I området ligger Vidkärr, som under mång: The area includes Vidkärr, which for many years was the terminus of tram line 1, until the line was extended to Östra sjukhuset hospital in 1982. On 24 January 1922 the first two houses in Vidkärr's garden suburb were completed. Right next to it is Sävenäs station, where commuter trains stood still between December 2024 and August 2026 because of the works on the Western Main Line.
I området ligger den lilla sjön Skåtte m: The area includes the small lake Skåtte mosse, about 55 metres above sea level, whose water flows on through the Glose å stream. A little way off is Kärna bokskog, a beech forest that has been a nature reserve since 2008, where the rare grass wood fescue and several red-listed lichens thrive. Parts of the beech forest are adapted for accessibility.
I området runt omkring, ett par kilomete: In the area around here, a couple of kilometres south of central Mölndal, is the residential area of Rävekärr. It's known for its grey, square terraced houses, which have been given the fitting nickname "lådhus", box houses. South-east of the houses glitter two lakes, Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten.
I området, vid Agnesbergs industriområde: In this area, by the Agnesberg industrial estate, the riverbank gave way on 14 April 1993. The Agnesberg landslide covered an area of about 80 by 30 metres along the Göta älv river. A few hours after the first slide came an eight-metre-wide retrogressive slide, and several small slides followed during the day. It was one of the many post-war landslides in western Sweden.
I parken vid Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, e: In the park by Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school a little way from here, stand two runestones that originally stood on the lands of Vibble gård, the old name for Jakobsberg. They have stood there since 1926. On one of them you can read that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised. Nearby also stood Jakobsberg mill from the 1840s, a windmill that burned no fewer than three times: in 1980, 1997 and 2005.
I postala sammanhang heter stadsdelen Hi: For postal purposes the district is called Hisings Kärra, and it covers 1,438 hectares. A little further away is Larsered, whose name is something of a mystery. That it refers to a Lars is clear, but nobody knows who he was. The ending -red means cleared woodland, so perhaps it was Lars who once cleared the land.
I rondellen vid infarten till Lidingö st: In the roundabout at the entrance to Lidingö stands the sculpture Till en annan värld, To Another World, cast only in 2008 from a bronze sketch just 66 centimetres high by Carl Milles that was never made full-size in his lifetime. The municipality commissioned it as a symbol of Lidingö's health profile, and the 240-centimetre copy was produced by computer-scanning the original. A little further on is Lidingö town hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson.
I skogarna en bit härifrån ligger Natura: In the forests a little way from here is the Natura 2000 site Maderna-Haketjärn, with small lakes such as Haketjärnen and Långevatten. Haketjärnen is shared between Härryda and Partille municipalities and is just over seven metres deep. Lilla Långevatten covers only 0.03 square kilometres but is almost ten metres deep. Partille is also home to Partille SC, Sweden's oldest field hockey club still in action.
I skogen en bit härifrån ligger Södra Lu: In the forest a little way from here is Södra Lundtjärnen, a small lake with a curious detail: the coordinates given for it actually point to a nameless lake just south of the real pond. In the other direction is the village of Pinntorp, near Tahult, where the road racing rider Kent Andersson has lived.
I skogen en kort promenad härifrån låg s: In the woods a short walk from here stood the summer villa Kappsta, also called Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. The villa burned down in 1931, but the foundations remain in Kappsta nature reserve, with the memorial Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W., by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz. Nearby also stand Villa Ekbacken, built in 1912 to 1913 for Gustaf Dalén, and Skärsätra water tower from 1912.
I skogen mellan Fisksätra och Igelboda,: In the woods between Fisksätra and Igelboda, just south of the Saltsjöbanan railway, the stone foundation remains of Vinterbrinken, a lineman's cottage where a railway worker lived with his family. The last to live here were the Nordgrens: first Ludvig with his wife Kristina and five children, then their son Ragnar, a station hand, with his family until the end of the 1920s. The name lives on in Vinterbrinksvägen.
I trakten finns gott om natur. En bit hä: There's plenty of nature around here. A little way from here is the Älta mosse – Strålsjön reserve, created in 1995 and owned and run by Nacka municipality. In the other direction is Stensö, named after the peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, with a swimming spot at its tip.
I trakten finns gott om runor. Vid Sundb: There are plenty of runes in this area. At Sundby is U 80, a large and elaborate rune-inscribed rock slab, and right next to it an unfinished one, U 81. Flysta also had a Viking Age runestone, but it has been searched for several times and has probably been lost. In the Bromsten industrial area was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large graffiti painting, until the wall was demolished in early December 2021.
I trakten flyter Lärjeån, som börjar nor: The Lärjeån river flows through the area, starting north of Gråbo and flowing into the Göta älv river at Lärjeholm. Along the eastern bank of the Göta älv, by the E45 road and the Bergslagsbanan railway, is Agnesberg, an old coaching inn stop that belonged to Angered municipality until 1967. The railway station came in 1880, and soon industries began to set up here.
I trakten ligger Långsjö gård, som på 16: In this area is Långsjö gård, which in the 17th century was a croft under Långbro Farm and later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö. A little way from here also runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg, the highway along which travellers once journeyed south from Stockholm.
I trähuset i backen har Djurgårdsskolan: Djurgårdsskolan has been in the wooden house on the slope since 1878, and it's one of Stockholm's oldest schools. A little way off stand Karl Johans-ekarna, the Karl Johan oaks, where, according to tradition, the king rested in the 1820s. Slätten, the meadow here, used to draw a colourful crowd, and according to the national librarian Rydqvist, Gustav III came here incognito. The poet Bellman is said to have sat under an oak improvising songs to his mandolin.
I vattenvaktarstugan bodde förr en vakt: The water keeper's cottage was once home to a guard whose job was to make sure Stockholm's main water pipeline between Norsborg waterworks and Nybohov reservoir worked without disruption. The first pipeline was built in 1902 to 1904 and is still one of the city's most important drinking water mains. In Gömmaren nature reserve, a little way off, there are also remains of a farm from the middle Iron Age.
I Årsta har gatorna fått namn efter sven: In Årsta the streets are named after Swedish lakes, such as Skagern and Hjälmaren, so a walk here is almost a geography lesson. Vättersparken used to have a supervised playground, Vättersdälden, which closed in 1992, but the paddling pool, swings and sandpits are still there. A little further away stands Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm Building of the Year in 2014.
Idrottsplatsen vid Kyrkvikens inre del h: The sports ground at the inner end of Kyrkviken bay has everything from athletics to ice hockey. But walk a little way and you'll find Lidingö's oldest farm: Bo gård, with a history going all the way back to the late Iron Age. Right next to it stand the Trisshusen from 1909, an early form of terraced housing designed by Jacob Gate.
Igelbäcken rinner förbi alldeles i närhe: The Igelbäcken stream flows past close by, around 10.5 kilometres from Lake Säbysjön all the way to Edsviken bay, and its valley is one of Stockholm's green wedges. A little way off is Akalla village, a name known since the Middle Ages. The oldest house is Storgården from the 17th century, and today there's a 4H farm, a café and bike hire in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area.
Ikeas andra svenska varuhus, efter det i: IKEA's second Swedish store, after the one in Älmhult, opened here on 18 June 1965. The round original part was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York, and after rebuilding and extension the store became the world's second largest IKEA by floor area. Among the very first neighbours was Esso Motorhotell from 1968, which today is Scandic Kungens Kurva.
Ingemarsgatan har troligen fått sitt nam: Ingemarsgatan street is probably named after the wine tapster Ingemar Frodbom, who ran an inn at the Ingemarshof country house in the 1700s. On his death he left a plot of land to his loyal head waiter Clas Browall, who in 1731 opened the inn Browallshof, today Clas på Hörnet. The surrounding area, by the way, got the nickname Siberia, because moving so far out felt like being sent into exile.
Ingen säger Köpstadsö. I dagligt tal het: Nobody says Köpstadsö. In everyday speech the island is called Kössö, and it is known for its wheelbarrows. Just over one square kilometre in size, with 129 permanent residents in 2020, it belongs to Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Keep an eye out for the wheelbarrows when you step ashore; they are the island's trademark.
Inloppet till Göteborg har länge bevakat: The approach to Gothenburg has long been guarded from this area. On Lilla Billingen, a headland a little way off, you can still see an angular fortification from 1741 to 1742, and in 1789 a four-sided redoubt with batteries facing the river was built. Gothenburg's saluting station was also here. The neighbouring hill, Stora Billingen, has military spaces blasted into the rock.
Innan Frösunda började bebyggas på 1990-: Before Frösunda began to be built up in the 1990s, the area was dominated by military activity, with the Signal Regiment and the Svea Engineer Regiment. Towards the end it was called the Frösunda detachment and was used, among other things, as quarters for the units doing royal guard duty. A little further away is Annelunds gård, where Per Henrik Ling, the father of Swedish gymnastics, lived between 1822 and 1839.
Innan tunnelbanan kom stannade spårvagns: Before the metro arrived, tram line 19 stopped here, at the Enskedefältet stop. On 9 September 1951 it was replaced by the metro station, and today the trains pass on a viaduct over Sockenvägen. The neighbour is Enskedefältets skola, a school designed by Paul Hedqvist and built in 1933. A little way off was the Enskede ski jump, where in 2016 the district council decided to build a viewpoint.
Inne i Fredhällsberget, alldeles intill,: Inside Fredhällsberget hill, right next to us, the traffic of the Essingeleden motorway roars through the Fredhäll tunnel, and right after that the Fredhäll bridge takes over, 270 metres long across the Mariebergssundet strait. Above ground it is calmer. The leafy Rudbecksparken park is full of oak trees, and Fredhäll elementary school, designed by Paul Hedqvist and opened in 1938, is today green-listed by the City Museum.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån döljer sig: Hidden inside the rock a little way from here is Aeroseum, an aviation experience centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing, one of only five built for the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000 visitors have been able to step down into the bunker and experience aviation history up close.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig: Inside the rock a little way from here hides Vargen, the Wolf, a secret, nuclear-bomb-proof command centre from the 1970s with room for 200 people. It was meant as a shelter for the leadership of Stockholm and Huddinge if war came, but was decommissioned and eventually became a data centre. North of Stockholm there's an almost identical twin, Elefanten, the Elephant. Nearby Lake Lissmasjön has shrunk to a third of its former size after several lake-lowering projects.
Insekterna har det lyxigt i Kikås. Vid K: The insects live in luxury in Kikås. By Kikås Långvatten lake is Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel, built to increase biodiversity, with a focus on wild bees, butterflies and birds. Kikås is the name of the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and a little way from here is Fågelberg church.
Inte långt härifrån ligger Anstalten Sag: Not far from here is Anstalten Sagsjön, a prison for women in Lindome. It got its name from Sagsjön a little further away, a very shallow little lake just 1.5 metres deep that lies 20 metres above sea level and drains into the Kungsbackaån river basin.
Inte långt härifrån reser sig tre konstg: Not far from here rise three artificial hills made of demolition rubble and bulky waste. The first, Högdalstoppen, was finished in 1964, and the hill there was previously the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the peaks are a recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still being topped up with excavated soil from road construction.
Interkulturella folkhögskolan: Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the intercultural folk high school
Invalidkyrkogården: Invalidkyrkogården, the old military veterans' cemetery
Ishallen en bit härifrån blev känd i hel: The ice rink a little way from here became famous throughout the country through the TV series HCZ. It has changed its name several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club plays here, and figure skaters train here.
Islandstorget fick sitt namn 1936, men d: Islandstorget, Iceland Square, got its name in 1936, but it was neither exiled Icelanders nor fishmongers who gave the place its name. The link to Iceland is vaguer: when the streets and squares of Norra Ängby were to be named, the planners took their cue from the ancient remains in the area. The trams on the Ängby line, route 11, turned here from the autumn of 1944. A short walk away is Björklunds hage, the burial ground of Viking Age Ängby.
Jakobs stege är en trappa med 187 granit: Jakobs stege, Jacob's Ladder, is a staircase of 187 granite steps down towards Lake Mälaren, named after the patriarch Jacob's dream of a ladder between earth and heaven. Nearby bubbles Bellmanskällan, which according to local tradition is the spring Bellman writes about in Fredman's Epistle No. 82, Vila vid denna källa. The water still flows, if slowly, and you can drink it.
Jakobsbergs Centrum, alldeles intill, är: Jakobsbergs Centrum, right next to here, is Järfälla's big shopping centre with around sixty shops, but also homes and offices under the same roof. A couple of minutes away stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, the old station building from 1876, and at the junction of Vasavägen and Ynglingavägen is Maria kyrka, St Mary's Church.
Jakobsbergs folkhögskola: Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the Jakobsberg folk high school
Jakobsbergs gård var från början ett tor: Jakobsbergs gård was originally a croft under Sätra gård, dating back to the early 17th century. The manor-like building was added in the 1750s, when the farm had become a summer retreat for well-to-do Stockholmers, and today it is blue-listed by the city museum. Down by the water is Mälarhöjdsbadet, a municipal beach that, despite its name, is not in Mälarhöjden but in Bredäng.
Jakobsbergs kvarn från 1840-talet hade o: Jakobsberg's windmill from the 1840s was unlucky with fire: it burned in 1980, 1997 and 2005, and after the third fire it was never rebuilt. Next to it is Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, a folk high school for adult education, in the buildings of the old manor. In the park stand two runestones moved there from the lands of Vibble farm, and on one of them you can read that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised.
Jakobsbergs sporthall stod klar 1967 och: Jakobsberg sports hall was completed in 1967 and is the home ground of, among others, Järfälla Basket, which was founded in 1973 and whose men's team made its debut in the top league, Elitserien, as early as 1981. The women's team went up the year after. After a refurbishment in 2009, the main hall holds about 1,100 people. A stone's throw away is Järfällabadet, the swimming centre that opened in 2018.
Jarlabergs vattentorn är 47,5 meter högt: Jarlaberg's water tower is 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-eastern Stockholm since it was completed in 1987. A little further away, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899 to build a car factory. But car development moved too fast, so paraffin engines were made instead under the name Avance, and they soon became a success.
Johannebergs vattentorn från 1924 byggde: The Johanneberg water tower from 1924 was converted into housing in 1995, with just two flats per floor. The top floor is 134 metres above sea level, and for a long time these were Gothenburg's highest-lying homes, until Karlatornet took the record in 2023. All around spreads Chalmers, a university of technology founded as early as 1829.
Jonsered var ett säteri som från 1830-ta: Jonsered was a noble estate that from the 1830s grew into a mill town under the Gibson family. The brick buildings from the mill era still define the place, and the Swedish National Heritage Board has designated Jonsered a cultural environment of national interest. Nearby is also Göta Bio, where the cinema society Götas Vänner has run the film screenings since 1996.
Jubileumsparken anlades till Göteborgs 4: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park, was created for Gothenburg's 400th anniversary. There's a public sauna and a place to swim in the river, and the park is used to try out ideas for the new district to be built around Frihamnen.
Jubileumsparken i Frihamnen växte fram i: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park in Frihamnen, grew up ahead of Gothenburg's 400th anniversary as an experiment in urban development. Here you'll find Hamnbadet, also called Pöl Harbour, with saltwater pools and a diving tower, and Allmänna bastun, the public sauna. The sauna is built from recycled materials, with changing rooms made of 12,000 glass bottles, and sits four metres above the water. On Bananpiren, the Banana Pier nearby, 5,000 homes were planned, but they were scrapped in 2020 because the ground was too poor.
Jubileumsparken med bastu och bad: Jubileumsparken park with sauna and swimming
Jungfruplatsen, några hundra meter bort,: Jungfruplatsen, a few hundred metres away, was named after the constellation Virgo, Jungfrun in Swedish, in 1958 and opened on 6 December 1959. It was Mölndal's first real shopping centre, built by Wallenstam. It is also where Mölndal's first outdoor artwork stands, Bossanova by Bertil Lundgren, unveiled in 1964. The streets of Bifrost all around have names connected to farming.
Jungfrusund är både bostadsområde och ha: Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour by the Vårbyfjärden bay on the east side of the island of Ekerön. Offshore lie the Jungfruholmarna, two islands that are the club islets of the Göta Sailing Society. The society began leasing the islets in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built its own clubhouse there in 1955. The islets are about six nautical miles into Lake Mälaren from Stockholm.

Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden, on the east side of Ekerön. Out in the water lie the Jungfruholmarna, two islands that are the club islands of Göta sailing club. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse in 1955. The Ekerö ferry route also crosses the bay.
Juringe gård var en gång utgård till det: Juringe gård was once an outlying farm of the large Vårby estate. The old main building was demolished in 2001 and replaced by a new one of similar appearance, which now houses a preschool. Remaining from the farm's time are the storehouse, a laundry and dairy shed, and the workers' house Väderluven. The croft Nytorp was also in the area, by the new route from 1673 that replaced the old Götha vägen road.
Järfälla gymnasium har funnits här nära: Järfälla gymnasium, an upper secondary school, has been here near Jakobsberg centre since 1962, under various names, and in 2020 it had just over 1,000 students. Among other schools, the SAM-gymnasiet used to be here, offering social sciences with specialisations ranging all the way to football. A little way off is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in the Nordic countries.
Järfälla är en kommun där det mesta är b: Järfälla is a municipality where most of the land is built up, and that has led to creative ways of preserving nature. Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, for example, contains an old airfield, and a metro line is being built under it. Otherwise the municipality is mostly associated with shopping, thanks to the Barkarby retail park.
Järfälla är rikt på runor. I Skylsta fin: Järfälla is rich in runes. In Skylsta there is a Viking Age runic inscription carved directly into the rock, while a runestone fragment that, according to Richard Dybeck, stood on the same hill has vanished without trace. A little further away, on the Stockholm side, is Backlura, where all the streets are named after flowers and plants.
Järfällabadet, en bit härifrån, invigdes: Järfällabadet, a little way from here, opened on 14 April 2018 and has a 50-by-25-metre swimming pool, two water slides and pools with a floor that can be raised and lowered. It replaced Jakobsberg swimming hall, which opened on a Monday in August 1971 and had a 48-metre-long water slide. The old building was at first going to be demolished, but will instead become premises for leisure activities.
Järfällas sydligaste kommundel heter Bar: Järfälla's southernmost district is called Barkarby-Skälby and had about 12,000 inhabitants in 2011. Among other things, it has Kyrkbyn, the church village, with the Gästgivargården coaching inn, in recent years known as Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja, and the old courthouse. Closer to the sports ground is the manor Skälby gård, whose current main building dates from 1802.
Järla gård är en riktigt anrik herrgård:: Järla gård is a truly venerable manor: the first farm named Järla is thought to have been built around the year 900. It is mentioned in the Stockholm city court records in 1453, and its location on the northern shore of Lake Järlasjön is shown on a map from 1690. Industry later grew up all around, and from Saltsjö-Järla station there were once branch lines to both a yeast factory and De Laval's steam turbine factory.
Järnbrottsmotet i närheten är en ovanlig: The nearby Järnbrottsmotet is an unusual kind of motorway interchange, a so-called double trumpet interchange. It was built in the 1990s where the Europa roundabout used to be, a gigantic roundabout that the Söderleden road cut straight through with traffic lights. In the wall of Västra Frölunda cemetery next door there are still iron rings, meant for churchgoers' horses.
Järntorget har fått sitt namn av järnet: Järntorget, Iron Square, is named after the iron that was weighed and shipped from here. The fountain in the middle is from 1927 and depicts the earth's five continents. This is where the working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga with its cafés and landshövdingehus, the typical Gothenburg houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors, and to the west run the Långgatorna streets with vintage shops and bars.
Järva krog var en vägkrog cirka 3,5 kilo: Järva krog was a roadside inn about 3.5 kilometres north of Norrtull, Stockholm's northern entrance, along the Uppsala road. The name lives on in the motorway junction. A short walk away is something much older: Mellanjärva burial ground, which with its roughly 175 visible graves is one of the largest farm burial grounds in the Stockholm area.
Järvastaden är ett stadsbyggnadsprojekt: Järvastaden is an urban development project that's taking its time. The first residents moved in in September 2007, and when everything is complete the plan is for more than 15,000 residents. The last, ninth phase will have to wait until after 2030, though, because a high-voltage power line must first be moved. The neighbour to the east is the residential area Agnesberg.
Kallhäll ligger intill Mälaren i Järfäll: Kallhäll lies by Lake Mälaren in the northern part of Järfälla, and in the centre is the Folkets hus community centre with a cinema and a library. A little further away is Stockholm Mejeri, Arla Foods' large dairy, which started production in 1984. Beneath the library in Kallhäll is the Bolinder Museum, showing items made by Bolinders Mekaniska Verkstad, the Bolinder engineering works.
Kanske skrevs svensk kungahistoria i när: Perhaps Swedish royal history was written nearby. Korseberget, a small village on the northern bank of the Nordre älv river near its mouth, is possibly the same place as Horsaberg. That is where King Magnus Ladulås held peace negotiations with his brother Valdemar on 26 June 1274. A small community with a possibly big place in the history books.
Kanton var en liten hantverksby som Lovi: Kanton was a small craft village that Queen Lovisa Ulrika and King Adolf Fredrik had built next to the Chinese Pavilion, Kina slott. Ironwork and lace were made here, and silk ribbons were woven. The queen even started silk farming, but the mulberry trees didn't like the cold and the project lasted only about ten years. The houses are private homes today and are regarded as a model for the Swedish garden city.
Kapplandsgatan intill känns igen på sina: Kapplandsgatan next door is recognisable by its red three-storey buildings, and at the southern end of the street lies Högsbo Hospital. The nearest square is Axel Dahlströms torg, which stands out with a 16-storey high-rise from 1956 and a marble inlay by Endre Nemes on the community centre. Along Marklandsgatan there's a pizzeria, a bakery and a grill.
Karl XII står i brons och pekar mot Ryss: Karl XII stands in bronze, pointing towards Russia, as a reminder of his wars. The statue by Johan Peter Molin was unveiled on 30 November 1868, on the 150th anniversary of the king's death. It was cast on Kungsholmen and weighs two and a half tonnes. The mortars around the base are spoils of war from Riga. The Green Party has put forward a motion to move the statue.

Kika in på Malmstens möbelskola: Peek into Malmstens möbelskola, the furniture school
Kikås är den höga åsen vid Stensjöns söd: Kikås is the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and here you'll find Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel, where wild bees and butterflies check in. A little way from here is Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow clear-water lake surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges. It's a popular lake for swimming, but if you want to fish, you need a fishing licence.
Kista Nod, alldeles intill, kostade 700: Kista Nod, right next door, cost 700 million kronor and was completed in 2014. Stockholm University does research there in computer and systems sciences. The area is also home to the Electrum laboratory, with a complete production line for semiconductor chips, and, a little more secretively, Försvarsunderrättelsedomstolen, the Defence Intelligence Court, which rules on permits for signals intelligence and has its premises in Kista.
Kista tunnelbanestation är den enda på b: Kista metro station is the only one on the blue line that's above ground. It rests on a viaduct 1,120 metres long, the longest in the whole metro network. When the station was to be named, the naming committee first wanted to add "Gård", meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a likkista, a coffin. Above the shopping mall rises Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall.
Kista är fullt av forskning. Rise SICS,: Kista is full of research. Rise SICS, formerly the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, carries out non-profit computer science research to strengthen the competitiveness of Swedish companies. The Electrum Laboratory, part of the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, has a complete production line for semiconductor circuits and does research in micro- and nanotechnology.
Kistas tunnelbanestation är den enda på: Kista's metro station is the only one on the blue line that is above ground. The trains glide in on a viaduct 1,120 metres long, the longest bridge in the entire metro network. Near the centre is also Kista Church with its octagonal shape, and at Kista torg is Kista folkhögskola, Sweden's first folk high school with a Muslim profile.
Klareberg i Kärra är en plats där bussar: Klareberg in Kärra is a place where the buses take a breather. Bus drivers like to take a break here, and the large bus stop is used for journeys to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also known among riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and to train their dogs.
Klingska huset, i hörnet av Älvsjövägen: Klingska huset, on the corner of Älvsjövägen and Johan Skyttes väg, is the oldest surviving rental apartment building in Solberga. This urban-style apartment block was built from 1923 to 1925 and was Älvsjö's first town-centre development. A couple of hundred metres away is Älvkvarnstenen, an old cup-marked stone that has been moved twice and since 1994 has rested next to Lerkrogen.
Klippan är en av Göteborgs äldsta miljöe: Klippan is one of Gothenburg's oldest settings, with old seamen's houses and the remains of the older Älvsborg fortress. Right next to it rises the Älvsborg bridge, and under the bridge is the Röda Sten art centre.
Klippan är fullt av historia. Här låg Ga: Klippan is full of history. Here stood Gamla Älvsborg, a mighty fortress from the 14th to the 17th century, now a ruin. The old Sugar Refinery, Sockerbruket, housed 24 kvadrat, Sweden's smallest dance stage, and the Klippan Inn from 1762 became famous through the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg's book Min son på galejan, My Son on the Galley. The trams sleep in the Majorna tram depot next door.
Kliv ner i Rinkeby tunnelbanestation och: Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg has enlarged small Viking Age finds, dug up in the area, into large wall mosaics on brick-red walls with gold inlays and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was inaugurated.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet! Ett stenkast: Step straight into the 1950s! A stone's throw away is Kortedala museum, a perfectly ordinary two-room flat with kitchen, preserved as it looked when the working-class families moved in. The setting is so authentic that it has been used for film shoots set in the past. Citytorget square right next to it was built at the same time, between 1955 and 1957, with tower blocks, rows of shops and a street kiosk.
Klättra upp till stångmärket Valen: Climb up to the Valen pole beacon
Knarrholmen var en present till arbetare: Knarrholmen was a gift to workers. The shipowner Axel Ax:son Johnson donated the island to Götaverken's shipyard workers in 1940, and after 1945 summer cottages were built here. In 2014 the trade unions sold the island with its 33 cottages, restaurant and village shop. The neighbouring island of Sillfarsholmen was bought in 1935 by the Aeolus sailing club for a single krona.
Kolla in Flatenbanan för radiostyrda bil: Check out Flatenbanan, the track for radio-controlled cars
Kolla utställningen i biblioteket: Check out the exhibition in the library
Kollektivhuset Sockenstugan är ett gemen: The Sockenstugan cohousing building is a community living arrangement for the second half of life, one of many cohousing buildings created in Stockholm after a political decision in 1980. One report described it as a truly successful example. Right next door is Gränsberget park, an old moraine hill shared between the districts of Enskededalen and Kärrtorp.
Kommunalvägen löper genom Huddinges hjär: Kommunalvägen runs through the heart of Huddinge, with the station, centre, church and municipal offices along its 1.3 kilometres. Things have happened recently too: Sjödalsgymnasiet, an upper secondary school that started in 1994, closed in 2026. In its last year the school had 185 students, compared with 608 just three years earlier.
Kommundelen Tibble rymmer både Täby cent: The Tibble district holds both Täby Centre and the church that has been called the Cathedral of Roslagen. Täby Centre has 215 shops and, since 2022, the formal name Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library holds two Viking Age runestone fragments found in Lissby in 1930, and it later turned out that several of the pieces belonged to another stone.
Konsthallen Accelerator har sina utställ: The Accelerator art gallery has its exhibition halls in a former underground laboratory for accelerator physics, and it opened in 2019 with a work by Tino Sehgal. Its neighbour is Villa Frescati, which Louis Jean Desprez designed in 1791–1792 as Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt's summer retreat, opposite Gustav III's pavilion. And at the Swedish Museum of Natural History is Cosmonova, Sweden's only dome-shaped IMAX cinema.
Konstnären Olle Olsson Hagalund bodde he: The artist Olle Olsson Hagalund lived his whole life in the same wooden house, built in 1897 by the master carpenter Carl Jakob Brolin. Today the house is a museum, both for his art and for the old shanty town of Hagalund, which was demolished in the 1960s to make way for the high-rises of Blåkulla. There is a model of old Hagalund there. Nearby stands Hagalund water tower from 1912.
Kontorshusen vid Solna strand står på ga: The office buildings at Solna strand stand on old industrial land, and the area used to be called Vretens industriområde. Granite was once quarried nearby: from 1875 the City of Stockholm leased Huvudsta quarry by Lake Ulvsundasjön to make paving stones. By the early 1880s the rock was considered exhausted. The metro station here, by the way, lies in a rock cavern a full 28 metres underground.
Kontorsområdet hette förr Virebergs indu: The office area used to be called Virebergs industriområde, the Vireberg industrial area. It was planned in the 1950s by the Wallenberg-owned property company Valvet, which had bought the land from Huvudsta gård in 1947. Being close to the railway, with its own track, was an attraction, but it took until the 1960s before construction took off. The neighbour, Löfströms gymnasium, an upper secondary school, takes in just over 55 elite athletes every year in football, ice hockey and floorball.
Kornhall är en liten hamnby vid Nordre ä: Kornhall is a small harbour village on Nordre älv river, with a small shipyard and a marina. From here the Kornhall ferry runs, a cable ferry across the river to Brunstorpsnäs on Hisingen. The route was started in 1850 and got its first motorised ferry in 1951, when traffic had increased because the road shortened the journey to Gothenburg so much.
Korsvägen är porten till Göteborgs evene: Korsvägen is the gateway to Gothenburg's events district. Here you'll find the Liseberg amusement park, which opened in 1923, the Universeum science centre and the Museum of World Culture. The Swedish Exhibition and Congress Centre, Svenska Mässan, is right next door too.
Kortedala byggdes på 1950-talet som en m: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as a modern suburb with everything close at hand: homes, a square, schools and green spaces. Much of the architecture from that era is still here.
Kortedala byggdes som Göteborgs första f: Kortedala was built as Gothenburg's first suburb during the 1950s, on the city's north-eastern outlying land, where previously there had only been croft-like buildings. Some farms remained right into the 1960s. A little way from here, at the entrance to Bergsjön, the slab blocks on Siriusgatan stand lined up on a hill like a landmark.
Kortedala torg, en bit härifrån, hette f: Kortedala torg, a little way from here, was first called Kortedalstorget. But Göteborgs Spårvägar, the Gothenburg tramways, pointed out that people said Kortedalatorget and that the name was awkward to pronounce. The city council voted 24 to 17, and in 1959 the square got its current name. The same year, the Forum cinema opened on the square, but it closed as early as the end of 1965.
Kovikshamn ligger vid havet, strax norr: Kovikshamn lies by the sea, just north of the mouth of the Nordre älv river, and here there is not one but two marinas. The northern one, Kovikshamns Norra Småbåtshamn, is privately owned and the larger of the two. Since 2015 Kovikshamn has counted as an urban area, and at that point the neighbouring villages of Sundhammar and Tofta as well as Brunnefjäll were merged with it.
Kring Bromma kyrka ligger en liten klung: Around Bromma Church lies a small cluster of rectory buildings with a long history. The red Sockenstugan, the parish cottage, from the 17th century, was the vicar's home right up until 1850, when the new rectory was finished. On the same plot is a tithe barn, where the priest once collected the Bromma farmers' tax in kind. And up on Kråsberget hill, north of Sockenstugan, stands the church's bell tower.
Kring köpcentrumet i norra Botkyrka finn: Around the shopping centre in northern Botkyrka is an unusually close-knit group of churches. Botkyrka Folk High School, started in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, but is open to everyone regardless of religion. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen is next door to the Syriac Orthodox Church of St Peter and St Paul, and Hallundakyrkan is almost wall to wall with the centre.
Krokslätts fabriker är gamla industribyg: Krokslätts fabriker are old industrial buildings where textiles were once made. Today they house businesses, restaurants and homes, an example of how old factories get a new lease of life.
Krokängsparken, en promenadpark på cirka: Krokängsparken, a walking park of about 7.5 hectares, was laid out as early as 1902 between Bratteråsberget hill and Pölsebo. A little further away, towards the river, rises the Eriksberg crane, the gantry crane from 1969, just over 70 metres high and nearly 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the bygone shipyard era, when everything in shipbuilding was on a huge scale.
Krontorpet Hökmossen nämns första gången: The Crown croft Hökmossen is first mentioned in 1748, in a document from the Military Archives, and was then called Hökmåsen, after a bog north of the farm that has since disappeared. A little way off, in an old co-op building in the villa area of Långbro, was the restaurant Aloë, which between 2015 and 2025 served luxury tasting menus and was awarded two stars in the Michelin Guide.
Krossgatan ligger i Vinsta industriområd: Krossgatan is in the Vinsta industrial area, where Vällingby fire station went into service in December 1964, and its firefighters are specially trained in roof ventilation and high-altitude climbing. Johannelund metro station was built as a so-called industrial station with two side platforms, the only one of its kind on the Stockholm metro, and until October 1997 it was only open at peak hours. The Vinsta district is named after the village of Vinsta.
Krusboda byggdes under åren 1970–1975 oc: Krusboda was built in the years 1970 to 1975 and has its own school. A little way off, by Lake Albysjön, lies Nyfors, a well-preserved holiday cottage area from the 1940s where more and more people now live all year round. Between the branches of the Wättinge stream lies Bullerholmen, which despite its name, 'Noisy Islet', is now completely uninhabited, and north of the cottages the Alby nature reserve begins.
Kulan på kullen är Bällsta radartorn, i: The ball on the hill is the Bällsta radar tower, popularly known as the Golf Ball, between Bromma Airport and Solvalla. The Solvalla trotting track opened in 1927, has room for 35,000 guests and hosts the Elitloppet race every year. In Bällsta itself, around 200 cottages were built by their owners themselves, with materials and instructions from the city's small-cottage office.
The ball bearing giant SKF has deep roots here. A little way off was Mariedal's landeri, a country estate, in Gamlestaden, and that is where SKF had its office from 1910 to 1914. Nearby was also Torpavallen, Qviding FIF's old home ground, with two gravel pitches and a grass pitch with a stand. Where the football once rolled, there is now the Torpavallen shopping centre.
Kultur i oväntade lokaler finns en bit h: Culture in unexpected venues awaits a little way from here in Fullersta. Fullersta bio is today an art gallery and theatre, housed in former Konsum co-op shops and an old cinema. At the manor house Fullersta gård, a former manor estate whose lands covered the area, a gallery for contemporary art has been run since 2009.
Kulturhuset Bergsjön: Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house
Kungens kurva har fått sitt namn från en: Kungens kurva, 'the King's Curve', got its name from a real accident. On 28 September 1946, Gustaf V's chauffeur drove off Södertäljevägen near here and got stuck in a water-filled ditch. The name stuck. IKEA built its second store here in 1965, and the round building is inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York.
Kungliga tennishallen: Kungliga tennishallen, the Royal Tennis Hall
Kungsgatan 65 har levt många liv. Biogra: Kungsgatan 65 has lived many lives. The Palladium cinema opened in 1918, with the dance restaurant Bal Palais in the basement. Then it became the nightclub Heaven, and from 2003 to 2025 Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern from 1906, named after Oscar II and a listed building. In the same building is Fasching, Scandinavia's largest jazz venue since 1977.
Kungsholms folkskola var Sveriges störst: Kungsholms folkskola was Sweden's largest elementary school and one of the largest in the world, with room for 4,000 pupils. Today only the northern part remains, which houses Stockholm's arts school, among others. The neighbourhood is full of records: Kungsholmen's crèche was the first of its kind in Sweden, and Kvinnohuset, a fourteen-storey collective housing block for women, opened in 1947.
Kungsladugård är tidigt bostadsbyggande: Kungsladugård is early housing construction in Gothenburg. The Svärdsliljan block from 1927 was one of HSB's first blocks of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical buildings with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors. The district also has the bronze statue Ung man, Young Man, made in 1948 by Astrid Noack and put up on the corner of Ståthållaregatan and Fågelfängaregatan in 1968. Kungsladugård Church is a short walk away.
Kungsladugårdsgatan är bred av en anledn: Kungsladugårdsgatan is wide for a reason. In Albert Lilienberg's town plan from 1916, it was drawn twice as wide, to make room for a future railway between the harbour and the city. The name comes from Älvsborgs Kungsladugård, the royal farm that supplied Älvsborg Castle with horses and grain. Along the street stands the Broström Foundation's building from 1924, listed since 2017.
Kungssten is near the mouth of the Göta älv river. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966. Out in the river mouth is the 17th-century New Älvsborg Fortress, which protected the city against the Danes. By the water below is Klippan, with old seamen's houses and the remains of the older Älvsborg Fortress.
Kungsträdgården var från början kungens: Kungsträdgården, the King's Garden, was originally the king's kitchen garden. Today it is one of the city's best-loved parks, and in spring the cherry trees here blossom in pink and white.
Kvarnholmen var en gång en ö full av mjö: Kvarnholmen, ‘Mill Island’, was once an island full of flour and bread. The Tre Kronor mill started in 1897, and there was a macaroni factory, an oat mill and a crispbread bakery here. Today people live in the silos. When Silo III was converted into housing, for a while only the outer walls were left standing. The old Bakery, Bageriet, now houses Kvarnholmen's centre, and the Oat Mill, Havrekvarnen, has been a listed building since 2016.
Kvarnholmen var från början en ö, men su: Kvarnholmen was originally an island, but the strait was filled in during the 1970s to give the industries a better transport route. This is where the Tre Kronor mill ground its grain, and the Oat Mill, Havrekvarnen, from 1927 to 1928, is today a listed building. Around Tre Kronors väg a model community was built for the employees, with terraced houses and narrow apartment blocks and its own Konsum co-op shop, which was open from 1935 to 1977. The Munspelet office building, "the Harmonica", from 1966, is listed for its spectacular modernist architecture.
Kvarnholmens centrum ligger i Bageriet,: Kvarnholmen's centre is in Bageriet, the Bakery, the old crispbread factory whose oldest drawings date from 1929, and today people live where crispbread used to be baked. Right next to it stands Disponentvillan, the manager's villa, built in 1931 as a home for the head of Kvarnen Tre Kronor, the Three Crowns Mill. The Makaronifabriken, the macaroni factory, is still there too, and at the Lilla Kvarnholmen playground the theme is inspired by the island's old industrial buildings.
Kvarteren vid Åkerbyvägen hör till HSB:s: The blocks along Åkerbyvägen belong to HSB's low-rise areas in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 1960s. A little further away is Täby centrum with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, with five screens and 516 seats. In the other direction is Ensta station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where about 500 people board on an ordinary winter weekday.
Kvarteret Gamlebo, intill Svedmyra tunne: The Gamlebo block, next to Svedmyra metro station, was originally built as the City of Stockholm's old people's home Gamlebo, later called Gammelbyn's old people's home. The ten original residential buildings are now owner-occupied flats. Much closer, on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen, was the Corso cinema, which opened in 1938 as Tusse-Bio and closed in 1969.
Kvarteret Holmia bildades 1906 av det ny: The Holmia district was founded in 1906 by the new company AB Lidingö Villastad, and it still has a well-preserved early 20th-century setting, with villas in National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. This is where you'll find Lidingö museum, in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions about Lidingö in the 20th century and a turn-of-the-century salon. The museum is run by Lidingö's local heritage society, one of the largest in Sweden, which among other things organises Bellman Day.
Kvarteret Rosteriet har fått namn efter: The Rosteriet block is named after a German roastery that made coffee substitute here between 1913 and 1920. Then Pharmacia made medicines in the block, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi made fuel rods for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill is Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, home to the Nordic Music upper secondary school since 2003.
Kvastekulla griftegård, en bit härifrån,: Kvastekulla cemetery, a little way from here, was designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander after a Nordic architecture competition. Their idea was to preserve the beautiful landscape with as little intervention in nature as possible. Planning began in 1952, the cemetery opened in 1959 and the chapel four years later.
Kvibergs kaserner var militärförläggning: Kviberg barracks were a military base from 1895 to 1994 and are today listed buildings with a restaurant, museum and market. The barracks house the Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, started in 1983, which has among other things displayed two Olympic medals. Just to the north is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the largest multi-sport facility in the Nordic countries, with a 1.2-kilometre indoor ski track.
Kvibergs marknad håller till i det gamla: Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market, is held in the old artillery regiment's horse stables. Every weekend 10,000–15,000 visitors hunt for antiques, curiosities and bits and bobs in 160 stalls. A little further away is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the largest multi-sport facility in the Nordic countries, with a full-size football pitch and a 1.2-kilometre indoor ski track.
Kvibergsnäs landeri: Kvibergsnäs landeri, a historic country estate
Kynäsberget, ett par hundra meter bort,: Kynäsberget, a couple of hundred metres away, is a large area of forest and rock of national interest for outdoor recreation. Further south, in Lake Trehörningen, is Storholmen, which was originally an island. In the 1920s it was divided into summer cottage plots, mostly sold to workers from Stockholm, and the island got a footbridge to the mainland. Today most of it is forest and shoreline open to everyone.
Kyrkan i slutet av Värmlandsgatan bär ku: The church at the end of Värmlandsgatan bears King Oscar II's full name, and the king himself visited in 1898 and signed the guestbook. Around the corner runs Nordhemsgatan, with the Briggen food hall, and the area is also home to SS Manhem, Gothenburg's largest chess club, with over 400 members and one of Sweden's leading clubs.
Kyrkan med de två tornen här bredvid är: The church with the two towers right next to us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. Keep your eyes peeled, because we'll soon drive up onto Västerbron, the bridge with one of Stockholm's best views.
Kyrkbytorgets hus byggdes i mitten av 19: The buildings on Kyrkbytorget were built in the mid-1950s, and on the square the Roxy cinema showed films between 1956 and 1965. The library opened the same autumn as the cinema, in November 1956, and much of the 1950s interior was kept during the renovation for its 60th anniversary. Nearby runs the Lundby Tunnel, which at 2,060 metres is one of Sweden's longer road tunnels.
Kyrkeby och Nereby är ett gott exempel p: Kyrkeby and Nereby are a good example of how the statistical maps get redrawn. Before 2015 there was a small locality here called Nereby and Sjöhed. In a new division, a larger urban area was defined instead, which was given the name Kyrkeby and Nereby. A little further away is the church village of Kyrkeby with Harestad Church.
Källö, officiellt Stora Källö, har fått: Källö, officially Stora Källö, is named after a pothole, a giant's kettle, on the island. People here used to live off fishing and farming, and the oldest houses are from the 1700s. In 1932 the Gothenburg motorboat club bought land and built a jetty, a dance floor and a kiosk, and today there are around 30 summer cottages here.
Kälvestas radhus och villor har en helt: Kälvesta's terraced houses and villas have a completely different neighbour to the north-east: Lunda, a district dominated by a large business and industrial area just south of Hjulsta and west of Spånga. Two very different worlds, then, at a comfortable distance from each other, and a good example of how mixed Västerort, Stockholm's western suburbs, can be.
Kärleksstigen vid Isbladskärret: Kärleksstigen, the Lovers' Path, by Isbladskärret
Kärna bokskog ligger nära, ett naturrese: Kärna beech forest is close by, a nature reserve of about 18 hectares managed by the West Coast Foundation, established in 2008. Among the beeches grows the rare grass species wood fescue, and there are several red-listed lichens here. Parts of the area are adapted for accessibility, so the forest is open to more than just the most experienced hikers.
Kärra kyrka alldeles intill hette faktis: Kärra church right next to here was actually called Kärra chapel right up until 2001. North of the church is a parish hall from 1978. And Kärra has been a place of justice: between 1824 and 1887 it was the court venue for the Askim district court, which covered the Askim hundred.
Kärrdal hör till Östra Sjöberg, en kommu: Kärrdal belongs to Östra Sjöberg, a district between Edsviken bay, Lake Rösjön and the Rinkeby forest. A little further away, on the eastern shore of Edsviken, lies Bergendal Manor, Bergendals herrgård. The site has been known since the 1650s through the croft Snickartorpet, and the stately manor was built in 1913 on the initiative of the landowner Ragnar Liljenroth. Today it is a hotel and conference venue. Along the same road lies Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Kärringstan är inget officiellt namn, me: Kärringstan, roughly Old Wives' Town, is not an official name, but the villa area has earned it thanks to streets named after famous women and blocks with names like Baderskan, Barnjungfrun, Kallskänkan and Tvätterskan, the Bath Attendant, the Nursemaid, the Cold Kitchen Maid and the Washerwoman. So the block Barnmorskan, the Midwife, fits in perfectly, and its terraced houses won the Stockholm Building of the Year award in 2011. Just a stone's throw away stands Modellvillan 21, which took the same title in 2017.
Kåhög är ett litet villasamhälle vid Säv: Kåhög is a small village of houses by the Säveån river, with the Western Main Line railway to the south. At the bridge in Kåhög begins the Jonsered Rapids nature reserve, Jonsereds strömmar, which follows the Säveån valley all the way to Lake Aspen. With a bit of luck you might see kingfishers and dippers there.
Kållered ligger precis vid gränsen till: Kållered lies right on the border with the province of Halland. The town used to be farming country, but today western Kållered is dominated by hypermarkets. A short distance away is Kållered station, where a station first opened as early as 1891, and the area also has the Shopping Park Kållered retail centre.
Kållered ligger vid gränsen mot Halland: Kållered is on the border with the province of Halland and used to be farming country. Today it has superstores such as IKEA, a small hotel and a golf course next to the Torrekulla nature reserve. A little way from here is Kållered Church, the oldest building in Mölndal municipality.
Kållered var en gång lantbruksbygd, men: Kållered was once farming country, but today western Kållered is dominated by hypermarkets. Shopping Park Kållered is right next to here, and a little way off was EkenCenter, a shopping centre with about 25 shops from 1990. The competition became too fierce, the building was demolished in 2013, and yet another retail building was built on the site.
Kållereds socken hörde till Askims härad: Kållered parish belonged to Askim hundred and existed long before any motorways were built here. The parish church, Kållered Church, stands on a hill in the village and is actually the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. The same area used to have the EkenCenter shopping centre, which was demolished in 2013.
Kållereds station har haft två liv. Den: Kållered station has had two lives. The first station opened in 1891 but closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka returned, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in rush hour trains now run every fifteen minutes in each direction.
Köpcentret Allum har ett namn från forns: The Allum shopping centre has a name from Old Swedish: it's the dative form of alla, all, and means roughly for everyone. It opened in 2006 and stretches across the E20 motorway with shops and a passage. A little way off, Partille herrgård, the manor popularly called Slottet, the Castle, sits on a hill overlooking the Säveån river valley. The manor has been a listed building since 1995.
Köpcentret Allum, alldeles intill, har e: The Allum shopping centre, right next to us, has a name with a history. Allum, or allom, is the Old Swedish dative form of the word for all, and means roughly for everyone or to everyone. Construction started in September 2004, and it opened in April 2006. Above the E20 motorway, a building with shops and a passage links the northern and southern parts.
Köpcentret Stinsen invigdes 1995 av Ingv: The Stinsen shopping centre was opened in 1995 by Ingvar Oldsberg in a former car dealership, where Mercedes-Benz cars used to be sold. One trace of the old days remains: the two large car lifts are still in use, now as goods lifts. The centre was expanded in stages and reopened in 2009.
Köpcentret här hette Mörby Centrum ända: The shopping centre here was called Mörby Centrum until May 2026, when it became Danderyds Centrum, while the metro station in the northern part of the building kept the name. It opened on 29 January 1978. A little way off is Villa Markelius, which the architect Sven Markelius designed in 1945 for himself and his family, and down by the Edsviken bay stands Berzelius' Oak, Berzelii ek, today a so-called oak ruin.
Landshövdingehus i kvarteren runt omkrin: Landshövdingehus – three-storey houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors – in the surrounding blocks
Landstingshuset, där Region Stockholms p: Landstingshuset, where Region Stockholm's politicians meet today, was a military hospital, Garnisonssjukhuset, for more than 150 years, from 1811 to 1969. Next to it stands Graverska huset from 1754, built as a home for the tanner Jacob Graver. And for food lovers: at Bergsgatan 33, Mathias Dahlgren ran the restaurant Bon Lloc, Catalan for good place, which had a star in the Michelin Guide from 1997 to 2005.
Lasse and Maja have moved into Skogås. Härbreparken, a little way from here, is a themed play park inspired by Valleby, the fictional small town where the children's detective agency Lasse-Majas detektivbyrå solves its mysteries. The park won Huddinge's architecture award in 2020. In the middle of Skogås centrum, at Yttertorget, stands Mariakyrkan, the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås parish.
Lemmingvallen heter fotbollsanläggningen: Lemmingvallen, the Lemming Ground, is the name of the football facility a stone's throw away, a name that makes many think of small mountain rodents. Here in Utby in eastern Gothenburg there's a grass pitch and an artificial turf pitch for eleven-a-side, plus two gravel pitches for seven-a-side football. Utby Church is also nearby.
Lerkrogen är ett hus som har flyttat. De: Lerkrogen is a house that has moved. The old tavern building first stood near Brännkyrka church, but was taken down in 1968 in connection with road building and the construction of the Stockholmsmässan exhibition centre. In 1986 it was put up again near Älvsjö station and is now used by local heritage societies. Next to it is the Älvkvarn stone, a cup-mark stone that has also been moved twice.
