Lexby var landsbygd ända tills radhusen: Lexby was countryside right up until the terraced houses arrived in the 1950s, and in the late 1960s the Vintergäcken area followed. The actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up here and writes about it in her autobiography. Partille IF and the rugby club Spartacus have their home grounds in Lexby, and a little further away is Partille Arena.
Lidingö centrum, kommunens största centr: Lidingö Centre, the municipality's largest shopping area, opened in 1995 and holds both shops and owner-occupied flats. Next door is Lidingö Town Hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson and marked blue for its high architectural and historical value. The Grand cinema, which opened in autumn 1993, is the only cinema in the entire municipality.
Lidingö har bara tre vattentorn, och ett: Lidingö has only three water towers, and one of them stands a short walk from here, at the end of Tallbergsvägen. Käppala water tower is sometimes called Brevik water tower, even though it's actually in western Käppala. The area also has Villa Brevik from 1920, which for many years was used for HSB's internal courses.
Lilla Bommen och Göteborgsoperan: Lilla Bommen and the Gothenburg Opera
Lilla Ursvik har en oväntad industrihist: Lilla Ursvik has an unexpected industrial history. In 1906 the brothers Alexander and Patrick Graham set up the lift company Graham Brothers here, and from 1929 neon signs were made too. A new factory building went up in 1937. Lift manufacturing continued right up to the end of the 1970s, after the Finnish company Kone had taken over the business.
Lilla Varholmen är porten till Öckeröarn: Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. The island is linked to Hisingen by a bridge, and from here the car ferries run out to the islands of Öckerö municipality, on both the Björkö route and the Hönö route. The Björkö route is only about 900 metres long, and the crossing takes about five minutes. The island has lighthouses too: the range lights here today date from 1927.
Lilla Ösbysjön är bara 4,1 meter djup oc: Lilla Ösbysjön is only 4.1 metres deep and lies a couple of minutes away, a small lake in the middle of the villa area. Nearby is Vendevägen station on Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, which opened in 1912 under the name Parkvägen and only changed its name in 1956. The waiting shelter was designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt.
Lilleby vid havet på Hisingen var länge: Lilleby by the sea on Hisingen was long pure countryside and belonged to Björlanda parish, until the area became part of Gothenburg in 1967. A land reform redistributing the farm plots was carried out here as early as 1846. Today the residential areas are growing fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and also offers Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony with its preserved 1950s cabins.
Lillängen nämns första gången 1653 och v: Lillängen is first mentioned in 1653 and was then a grazing and hay meadow belonging to Järla farm. The villa area was planned in 1937, and that same autumn the first families were able to move into their new houses. The same year the area got its own stop on the Saltsjöbanan railway, and the functionalist waiting shelter from 1937, green with white corners, still stands today.
Lindevägen fick sitt namn 1917, och vill: Lindevägen got its name in 1917, and the villa area along the street was at first called Nya Enskede, New Enskede, or Palmeska förstaden, the Palme suburb. The name Linde comes from a croft, an inn and a coaching station that stood nearby from 1762. Since 2012 the metro station has had Maria Miesenberger's artwork Ögonblick i rörelse, Moments in Motion, with walls in granite ceramic and aluminium sculptures.
Lindholmen var länge ett av Göteborgs st: For a long time, Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's big shipyards. Where ships were once built, there is now Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay you can see straight across the river towards the city centre.
Lindholmspiren ligger vid den gamla varv: Lindholmspiren lies in the old shipyard area of Lindholmen, where ships were built for over a hundred years. Today Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers are here, and from the quay you can look straight across the river towards the city centre.
Lindome ligger cirka 15 kilometer söder: Lindome lies about 15 kilometres south of Gothenburg but still counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. It is the church village of Lindome parish in the province of Halland and is squeezed between the E6 motorway and the West Coast Line. A little way off is Lindome station, where the commuter trains stop and the buses have a larger stop.
Lindome socken är stor, hela 81,7 kvadra: Lindome parish is large, a whole 81.7 square kilometres, and includes both the town of Hällesåker and Lindome with its parish church. Lindome church is a short walk from here. The parish belonged to the province of Halland and the Fjäre hundred, but since 1998 it has been part of Västra Götaland County.
Lindome station har varit död och återup: Lindome station has died and risen again. It opened on 1 September 1888 when the Gothenburg to Halland railway was completed, but passenger services were withdrawn in 1970 and in 1989 the station closed completely. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started running again, it made a comeback on 17 August 1992, and in 2012 it was rebuilt for longer trains.
Lindvreten var ett torp under Vårby gård: Lindvreten was a croft under Vårby gård, and the name probably means "the plot with the lime trees". Nearby was the croft Månskär, whose odd name has nothing to do with a crescent moon, månskära. It comes from one of the first tenants, Måns, and the word kärr, meaning wetland. Here too is Södra djursjukhuset, an animal hospital that started in 1967 with two people in a villa.
Liseberg ligger alldeles i närheten. Där: Liseberg amusement park is right nearby. There you can ride the Flume Ride, opened in 1973, where log-shaped boats travel along a 610-metre water channel with drops of up to 14 metres. Next to the park, the Grand Curiosa Hotel opened in 2023, just in time for Liseberg's 100th anniversary. Eklandagatan, by the way, is named after the village of Eklanda, and the ending landa means shoreland.
Ljudet av speedway har ekat här. Arendal: The sound of speedway has echoed here. The Arendal track was the home track of Kaparna, 336 metres long. The attendance record of 5,940 spectators was set in September 2002 against Rospiggarna, and the track record was set by Tony Rickardsson for Masarna in 2004. A little further away, in Rödjan, is Rya skog, a nature reserve since 1928 and a remnant of the mixed oak forest that once covered large parts of the west coast.
Ljusets kyrka: Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light
Loviseberg, en bit härifrån, är till sto: Loviseberg, a little way from here, is largely a scenic recreation area with a ski slope, a beach and hiking trails. By Lake Albysjön is the Gömsta äng nature reserve, created in 1966 and both Huddinge's oldest and smallest reserve, with meadowland, alder shore forest and a grove with rich flora. Part of the 80-kilometre-long Huddingeleden trail runs through the reserve.
Lovö skogskyrkogård anlades på 1830-tale: Lovö Woodland Cemetery was laid out in the 1830s, after complaints that the old churchyard at Lovö Church had become too cramped and was on swampy ground. It lies on Lovö kyrkallé, within the World Heritage area of Drottningholm Palace. From here you can also reach Lovöns fornstig, an 18-kilometre trail on the island of Lovön that links ancient remains, memorials and interesting buildings.
Lovö socken rymmer både Drottningholms s: Lovö parish includes both Drottningholm Palace and the old parish church, Lovö church, a little way from here. Outside the church stand five runestones, and one of them has a real adventure story: in the 17th century it stood by the porch door, but when the porch was demolished in 1798 the stone ended up underground. Only in 1935, during a restoration of the church, was it found again, a full 2.7 metres tall and raised in memory of a woman.
Lovön is full of traces from the Viking Age. About 500 metres south of Edeby Farm there is a rune carving cut directly into the bedrock, known as U 52. It's a reminder that people have lived and travelled here for a thousand years, long before the buses started running towards Ekerö.
Lovön är ön i Mälaren där Drottningholms: Lovön is the island in Lake Mälaren where Drottningholm Palace stands, and it is reached from the mainland via the Drottningholm and Nockeby bridges. A short walk away is Lovö Church, with no fewer than five runestones set up outside, among them a small sandstone that is only just over a metre tall. From the church, the Lovö church avenue runs dead straight for about 1,800 metres towards the palace grounds.
Lullehovsbron spänner över det drygt 200: Lullehovsbron bridge spans the Lullehovssundet strait, just over 200 metres wide, between Färingsö and Lindö, and both the bridge and the strait are named after the settlement of Lullehov at the eastern end of the bridge. The present bridge opened to traffic in 1980. In the middle of the strait the water is about seven metres deep, and in the southern part lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island.
Lundbergs konditori: Lundbergs konditori, a classic café and pastry shop
Lundens vattentorn, en åttkantig putsad: Lunden water tower, an octagonal rendered building about 45 metres tall, was built in 1930 to designs by Eugen Thorburn, the same architect who designed Lundenskolan. A little further away, at the corner of Sankt Pauligatan and Femkampsgatan, is Kolerakyrkogården, the Cholera Cemetery, with a memorial stone to the victims of the cholera epidemic of 1834. The front of the stone simply says År 1834, the year 1834.
Lundenskolan invigdes den 15 maj 1914, o: Lundenskolan opened on 15 May 1914, and its architect, Eugen Thorburn, later also designed the district's water tower. Next to it is Örgryte New Cemetery from 1890, with almost 3,900 graves. A little way off is Tån cemetery, whose name comes from the word tun, the area next to the infields where livestock were let out to graze.
Luxgatan är en blinkning till AB Lux, se: Luxgatan is a nod to AB Lux, later Electrolux, which had its factories on the south-eastern part of the island. Lux means light in Latin. Here was also Nya Chartago, the stronghold of the Coldinu Order fraternal society, and the Fridberg inn welcomed guests from the 18th century until the 1850s. On the Marieberg side, Gideon Forslund built fast motorboats, so-called flat-iron racers.
Lägg märke till gatunamnen: Sedelvägen,: Notice the street names: Sedelvägen, Riksdalervägen and Sparbanksvägen, meaning Banknote Road, Riksdaler Road and Savings Bank Road, with blocks such as Valutan, the Currency, and Förskottet, the Advance. In the Förskottet block is Hägerstensåsen's old post office from 1951, designed by Lars-Erik Lallerstedt and blue-listed by the City Museum. The public can no longer post letters here, but the mail sorting is still there. The district sits on a ridge, at most 67 metres above sea level.
Läkare och sjuksköterskor har gett namn: Doctors and nurses have given their names to the streets of Guldheden. Doktor Allards gata honours the doctor behind free bathing trips to Askim for Gothenburg's children, known as ‘Doktor Allard's bathing children’. In the middle of the square, Fina fisken, the Fine Fish, spouts water – Palle Pernevi's steel sculpture from 1961. He welded it together himself, and the five jets of water are meant to recall Lyrön in Bohuslän, where it was made.
Längre västerut än så här kommer man int: You can't get further west than this on the metro: Norsborg is the westernmost station in the whole network and the terminus of the red line since 1975. A short walk away is Botkyrka poorhouse, built in 1798 and used as a poorhouse right up until 1911, then as an old people's home and nursing home. Since 1998 there have been schoolchildren in the building, where Botkyrka friskola, an independent school, now holds its lessons.
Längs Bergsunds strand låg förr varv och: Along the Bergsund shore there used to be shipyards and workshops. Opposite lies Långholmen. For a long time it was the site of Stockholm's central prison, which closed in 1975. Today the prison is a hotel and hostel, and the island has a popular swimming spot and lovely walking paths.

Along Bergsunds strand there used to be shipyards and workshops. Opposite lies Långholmen. For a long time it was home to Stockholm's central prison, which closed in 1975. Today the prison is a hotel and hostel, and the island has a popular swimming spot.
Längs Delsjövägen låg förr Synvillan, so: Along Delsjövägen used to stand Synvillan, the Optical Illusion, as Gothenburg humour nicknamed the old building of Swedish Television and Swedish Radio. SVT moved out in 2007, and the building was demolished in 2010 to make way for housing. One of the new buildings, Studio 1, in black-fired Danish brick, won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 2016, but the same year it was also nominated for the Kasper Kalkon prize for the ugliest building of the year.
Längs Ekerövägen väster om Träkvista fin: Along Ekerövägen west of Träkvista is Fantans hög, an offering cairn with a grim legend. Fantan is said to have murdered her husband and been made to run the gauntlet: if she got far enough up Asknäsmalmen to see Ekerö Church, she would be set free. Just before, she collapsed and was stoned to death. According to the legend, anyone passing the spot should leave a coin, a stone or a dry twig.
Längs Elfviksvägen finns två villor av a: Along Elfviksvägen are two villas by the architect Ralph Erskine: Villa Gadelius, designed in 1961 for the businessman Knut Saburo Gadelius, and Villa Molin from 1947, built for the garden architect and editor Ulla Molin. A little way off is the Canada block, whose terraced houses, together with those in Gamla Enskede, are considered Sweden's very first, and which has been a listed building since 1981.
Längs Farstaviken byggde porslinsfabrike: Along Farstaviken bay, the Odelberg family of the porcelain factory built their dream houses. In 1910 Ferdinand Boberg designed Villa Farsta udde for Maria Bennich, daughter of the factory director Wilhelm Odelberg, and the following year Villa Strandvik for her brother Axel. The director himself lived at Farsta Manor, whose original building from the 1620s was burned down by the Russians in 1719. On a hill by the harbour is a burial ground from the late Iron Age.
Längs Farstavägen ligger kvarteren Kampö: Along Farstavägen are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, with terraced houses from the late 1950s designed by the architect Birger Nygell and given a green heritage rating by the City Museum. A short walk away, Farsta torg opens up, laid out as an Italian piazza and inaugurated on 23 October 1960. Around the square there were once Nordiska Kompaniet, Kvickly and Tempo department stores, and the shopping centre has several times been named shopping centre of the year.
Längs Lantmäterivägen går en gammal tipp: Along Lantmäterivägen runs an old landfill that marks the northern edge of Hummelmoraberget, a hilly area in the Görväln nature reserve where, after the Ice Age, the waves of the sea left beach ridges of gravel and stone. In the other direction, in Viksjö centre, is Viksjö Church, consecrated as recently as 2005 by Bishop Caroline Krook.
Längs Långedragsvägen fanns förr bio. Ol: There used to be cinemas along Långedragsvägen. Olympia opened in 1929 and kept going until 1971, and even earlier the Oden cinema was here, just outside the city boundary of the time, from 1919 to 1925. The Kungssten area used to be called, quite simply, Stadsgränsen, the City Boundary. A little way off is the Sjöbergen allotment area, where people kept small animals as early as the 1930s.
Längs Malmvägen står tio höghus med 1 24: Along Malmvägen stand ten tower blocks with 1,247 apartments, which is why the street is called "Tian", the Ten. The service building was designed by Åke Arell and attracted international attention when it opened in 1972. Its ground floor brought together preschools, shops and club premises. By the square rises the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipality and, since 2023, also the library.
Längs Margaretavägen står Gamla Enskedes: Along Margaretavägen stand the Gamla Enskede terraced houses, also called the English terraces, which together with the Canada houses on Lidingö are Sweden's very first terraced houses. Enskede Church sits clearly visible on a rise in a park in the middle of the villa area. And on Enskedevägen is Enskedestationen, a former transformer station opened in 1911 that now houses offices.
Längs Margaretavägen står några av Sveri: Along Margaretavägen stand some of Sweden's very first terraced houses. Together with the Canada houses on Lidingö, the terraced houses of Gamla Enskede, also known as the English terraced houses, were the first in the country, and the 37 properties in six rows are marked blue by the City Museum for their high cultural value. Gamla Enskede is a garden city, and here you'll also find Enskede skola, one of Stockholm's largest primary schools, with more than 900 pupils.
Längs Sveavägen här har kulturlivet levt: Along Sveavägen here, cultural life has flourished. At the jazz club Gyllene Cirkeln, the Golden Circle, in the ABF building, jazz was played from 1962 to 1969, and in the Student Union Building, Kårhuset, where Prince Eugen gave a speech at its opening in 1935, the much-publicised student occupation took place in May 1968. The Grand cinema has been showing films since 1933. Rådmansgatan, by the way, is the only metro station named after a street.
Längs gamla Södertäljevägen, strax norr: Along the old Södertäljevägen road, just north of Långbro hospital, there used to be the inn Långpannan. It had started as a croft under Långbro gård and was demolished in 1964. The name Långbro itself is even older: it comes from a medieval log bridge, a "long bridge", that made it possible to cross the area as part of the Göta landsväg highway.
Längs länsvägen mellan Mölnlycke och Möl: Along the county road between Mölnlycke and Mölndal lies Lilla Kullbäckstorp, and a little way from here glitters Lake Vällsjön, only four and a half metres deep. On the other side of the lake begins Pixbo, a very hilly residential area built on and around a height called Björnåsen. Pixbo even has its own postal town.
Längs Ältavägen låg dagsverkstorpet Snör: Along Ältavägen was the croft Snörom, pronounced ‘snör-om’ but also called Snurrom, whose crofters paid their rent in labour to the Erstavik estate. North of Lake Sandasjön stood Tuppstugan, a former soldier-sailor's croft that has had names such as Oxberget, Svartbäcken and Solmärke. The 18th-century cottage had unique wall paintings by the artist Olle Nyman, but sadly it burned down over the Whitsun weekend of 2004.
Lärje var en gång den första stationen p: Lärje was once the first station on the Västergötland–Gothenburg Railway counting from Gothenburg, around six kilometres from the city's station. Just after the station, the track crossed the Bergslagen Railway's tracks on a viaduct and then followed the Lärjeån river valley. Nearby is also the Alelyckan sports centre.
Lärjeholms gård, alldeles i närheten, ha: Lärjeholms gård, right nearby, has an arched stone bridge over Lärjeån river east of the farm, and this is where the river flows into Göta älv. Nearby also runs the two-kilometre-long Tideräkningsgatan, which got its name, from the almanac's calendar terms, in 1953, along with 53 other streets in Kortedala.
Lärjeån har gett namn åt Lärjedalen, som: The Lärjeån river has given its name to Lärjedalen, which between 1989 and 2010 was a district of its own, including Hammarkullen, Hjällbo and Agnesberg. The river starts north of Gråbo and flows into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm, and its catchment area covers 119 square kilometres. Closer to the stop is the Bäckebol Center retail area.
Lärjeån, som slingrar förbi en bit härif: Lärjeån, the river winding past a little way from here, gave the former district of Lärjedalen its name. The river starts north of Gråbo and flows into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm, and its catchment area covers 119 square kilometres. Nearby is also the Bäckebol Center shopping area with around twenty shops.
Lärkstadens villor har haft spännande gr: The villas of Lärkstaden have had exciting neighbours. The villa on the corner of Baldersgatan and Valhallavägen was designed by the architect Erik Josephson as his own home, and it has since been the residence of Denmark's ambassador as well as the embassy of both Yugoslavia and Serbia. The neighbouring villa, designed by Torben Grut, has been Libya's embassy since 1978. A little further on, a villa was built for the theatre and film man Anders Sandrew.
Långbro gård har anor från senare delen: Långbro gård dates back to the later part of the 15th century and was already a manor estate by the end of the 16th century. The farm gave its name to the district, and the name in turn comes from a long medieval log causeway. That bridge probably lay where the northernmost part of Sjättenovembervägen runs today. The main building is blue-listed by the City Museum and now contains public housing.
Långsjön är bara tre meter djup men har: Långsjön is only three metres deep but has an important job: the lake forms the boundary between the municipalities of Stockholm and Huddinge, or more precisely between the residential areas of Herrängen and Segeltorp. On the north side of the lake is Långsjö gård, dating back to the 1600s when it was a croft under Långbro gård. The street Segeltorpsvägen got its name in 1928 from the Segeltorp farm, which was demolished in 1964.
Långsjön är en liten sjö med badplats oc: Långsjön is a small lake with a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail around it, and since 2005 the lake and the land closest to it have been a nature reserve. The lake is 5.6 metres deep and lies just over 20 metres above sea level. A little further away in Storängen stands Villa Widstrand, built in 1906 for the publisher Wilhelm Widstrand, known from the publishing house Wahlström och Widstrand.
Långsjövägen, ett par hundra meter bort,: Långsjövägen, a couple of hundred metres away, is more than an ordinary villa street. From its northern start up to Myrvägen it's part of the old Göta landsväg, the historic Göta highway, and it forms the boundary between the districts of Älvsjö and Långbro, and between Älvsjö and Långsjö. Nearby is also Långsjöhöjden, which is a nature area, a residential area and a street all at once.
Långt innan industriområdena fanns Nylös: Long before the industrial areas, there was Nylöse parish, a parish in Nya Lödöse. It ceased around 1624, but the hospital's congregation lived on and in 1627 became Gothenburg's hospital parish. It existed right up to 1883. The Marieholm industrial area, by the way, is named after the Marieholm country estate.
Långt innan tunnelbanan fanns här rullad: Long before the metro was here, trams were already rolling past: from 1930 the Örbybanan line ran by and had a stop on this spot. The metro came in 1951, first with a temporary station, and the permanent station opened in 1953, then as a terminus. The metro section between Globen and Stureby actually follows the route of the old tramway.
Lövgärdets kyrka, en kort promenad härif: Lövgärdet Church, a short walk from here, is a church that's no longer a church. It was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016. During its years in use it belonged first to Gunnared parish and from 2014 to Angered parish. Lövgärdet in turn is a neighbourhood within the Gårdsten district in northeastern Gothenburg.
Malmvägen i Tureberg kallas Tian, efter: Malmvägen in Tureberg is called Tian, the Ten, after the ten high-rise blocks designed by Åke Arell in 1970. The service complex holds 1,247 flats, and on the ground floor preschools, shops, a gym and club rooms. The project was part of the Million Programme housing drive and attracted international attention when it opened in 1972. The street name Bagarby nearby recalls Bagare by, an older name for Tureberg farm.
Manillaskolan grundades 1809 av Pär Aron: Manillaskolan was founded in 1809 by Pär Aron Borg as a school for deaf and blind children, and it was based here on Södra Djurgården, southern Djurgården, until 2013. Just east of the school stands the mighty King's Oak, Kungseken. In the villa Nedre Manilla, the Bonnier family keeps its portrait collection of more than 300 works, mostly of Swedish authors. The first painting was bought in 1905: Hanna Pauli's portrait of Verner von Heidenstam. Down on the islet of Manillaholmen stands the sculpture Frihetens port, the Gate of Freedom, from 1994.
Marabou kom hit 1916 som dotterbolag til: Marabou came here in 1916 as a subsidiary of the Norwegian company Freia, and the factory was designed by Ivar Tengbom. Production moved to Upplands Väsby in 1976. The old chocolate factory and Marabouparken by the Bällstaån stream now have very high cultural and historical value, and the park is known for its art gallery.
Marabouparken började fyllas med skulptu: Marabouparken began filling up with sculptures as soon as it was laid out, and by the 1970s the collection had grown to sixteen works of art. Underground in the eastern part of the park lies the Marabouparken art gallery, opened in 2010 next to the old cocoa laboratory designed by Artur von Schmalensee. The park is now also home to Långholmen Folk High School, which used to be housed in a former pavilion at Långholmen Central Prison.
Mariakyrkan i Hammarkullen: Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church, in Hammarkullen
Mariakyrkan vid Skogås Yttertorg ligger: Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church by Skogås Yttertorg, is just a few steps away and is the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås parish. Up on the cliff a little way from here hides Lännafortet, a fort built in 1908–1909 as part of the Southern Front. Together with the Northern Front, known as Korvlinjen, the Sausage Line, it was an important part of Stockholm's fixed defences until 1952, and Lännafortet is one of the well-preserved forts.
Mariebergs kyrkogård intill anlades 1787: Marieberg cemetery next door was laid out in 1787 on Majberget hill, and the name is a so-called prettification, from Maj to Marie. Among those resting here are Wilhelm Stenhammar and Johan Fredrik Carpelan. Nearby stands Captain Hansson's house from 1850, which was threatened with demolition and moved to Chapmansgatan in 1953. At Chapmans torg square, the Gothenburg English Studio Theatre performs, the only English-language theatre in western Sweden.
Mariehällskyrkan har bytt psalmer mot ba: Mariehällskyrkan has swapped hymns for children's songs. Until 2015 it was the church and parish hall of Bromma parish, but then the building was sold to the municipality, which opened a preschool here in 2016. The congregation moved to Kvarterskyrkan on the other side of the street. A little further away is Annedal, named after Anna Augusta Wickman-Olsson, who owned a plot by the Bällstaån stream in the 1880s.
The ground here has a dramatic past. On 29 September 1950 Surte was struck by the Surte landslide, which counts among the largest natural disasters in Swedish history. Several houses were carried away by the slide, but miraculously only one person died. A little way from here is Surte station, which opened in 1879 and, after a break of more than 40 years, got passenger trains again in 2012.
Marken här tillhörde Klara kloster, till: This land belonged to Klara convent until the Reformation parliament in Västerås in 1527 decided that the convent should be demolished. In the 1560s it was granted to Torbjörn Klockare, who has had a street named after him. The Röda bergen area around here is Stockholm's largest unified inner-city environment built to the town planning ideals of the 1920s. At Torsplan the Norra tornen, the Northern Towers, stick up, two skyscrapers of 104 and 120 metres.
Mars 1566 small det rejält i trakten. Un: In March 1566 there was a huge bang in this area. During the Swedish siege of Bohus Fortress, the Danish-Norwegian defenders blew up their own keep, Röde Torn, the Red Tower, an event that has gone down in history as Bohusiska smällen, 'the Bohus Bang'. All around, Rödbo spreads out across the very northern tip of Hisingen, between the Göta älv and Nordre älv rivers, with mostly forest, open land towards the rivers and the odd cottage. Rödbo Church is just a couple of hundred metres away.
Masthugget hör till Göteborgs allra älds: Masthugget is among Gothenburg's very oldest land, from 1621, and was declared a suburb as early as 1646. An unplanned settlement grew up here around the ship harbours along the river. Right nearby stands the Sjömannasällskapet building, the Seamen's Society house, from 1901 and 1903, and Oscar Fredriksskolan from 1897 is said to have been named after Oscar II, who was supposed to speak at the opening but never turned up.
Masthuggskyrkan, stadens bästa utsikt: Masthuggskyrkan church, the city's best view
Masthuggstorget ligger nedanför Masthugg: Masthuggstorget square lies below Masthuggsberget hill. Up on the hill is Masthugget Church from 1914, and around the square are some of the city's oldest landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical buildings with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors.
Med 1 390 elever år 2024 hör gymnasiet h: With 1,390 students in 2024, the upper secondary school here, opened in 1982, is one of the largest in Stockholm County. Nearby is also the Good to Great tennis academy, founded in 2011 by the former tennis pros Magnus Norman, Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillström. Among the players who have trained there are the brothers Mikael and Elias Ymer.
Med sina 199 kvadratkilometer utgör Hisi: At 199 square kilometres, Hisingen makes up roughly half of Gothenburg municipality's area. The island belongs to Västra Götaland County and is Sweden's fifth largest. It is surrounded by water on all sides: Göta älv, Nordre älv and the Kattegat. Roughly a quarter of the island counts as part of Västergötland, the rest as Bohuslän.
Medborgarplatsen är Södermalms stora tor: Medborgarplatsen is Södermalm's big square, with outdoor cafés in summer and an ice rink in winter. From here you can reach Götgatan, Söder's lively main street.
Mellan Hjulsta och Lunda ligger Hjulsta: Between Hjulsta and Lunda lies Hjulsta allotment garden, an association formed in 1973 that is today an example of multicultural growing areas. Lunda itself is dominated by business and industrial areas. The old windmill Kälvesta kvarn, by the way, is also called Lunda kvarn, and actually stood in Lunda for a time after 1884.
Mellan nybyggda hus och köpcentrum står: Between new buildings and shopping centres stand four stones from prehistoric times. The Sannegården monument is the remains of a burial ground from the transition between the Bronze Age and the Iron Age. The largest, triangular standing stone remains in its original place, while the others have been moved because of gravel extraction. The harbour below, Sannegårdshamnen, opened in 1914.
Metalfans, spetsa öronen. En bit härifrå: Metal fans, prick up your ears. A short distance from here is Studio Fredman, which the producer Fredrik Nordström started in 1990 and still runs. Bands such as In Flames, At The Gates, Hammerfall, Opeth and Arch Enemy have recorded albums here, as well as foreign guests like Dimmu Borgir and Panic! at the Disco. Closer to the stop is the Motor Industry Technical upper secondary school, where it's the engines doing the noise.
Midsommarkransens tunnelbanestation ligg: Midsommarkransen metro station lies in a rock cavern 17 metres underground and opened when the red line was inaugurated in 1964. Along Främlingsvägen stand narrow apartment buildings from the 1940s, and in 2013 they were joined by six new buildings that were nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year the following year. A little further on, the Hägerstensviadukten viaduct carries the Essingeleden motorway.
Millesgården var skulptören Carl Milles: Millesgården was the home, studio and garden of the sculptor Carl Milles and his wife Olga, and today it is an art museum and sculpture park. Milles created the sculpture Skridskoprinsessan, the Skating Princess, in 1949 after seeing a girl ice skating at Rockefeller Plaza in New York; he was so taken with her movements that he tried to capture them in bronze. The entrance is through the art gallery, designed by Johan Celsing.
