Mitt bland forskningshusen står ett lite: Among the research buildings stands a small, Falu red timber house with a royal history. The Falconers' Lodge, Falkenerarbostället, was built in 1726 as official housing for the royal falconers and originally belonged to Karlberg Palace. The house is very well preserved and classed as exceptionally valuable in cultural and historical terms, but today it is a private home.
Mitt bland lagerhallar och verkstäder st: In the middle of warehouses and workshops stands an old windmill. Ulvsunda kvarn, also called Bällsta kvarn, stands at the foot of Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, next to Ulvsundavägen, just south of Bromma Airport. Even closer is the Fructus building, the white functionalist factory where the soft drink Pommac was made.
Mitt bland villorna i Smedslätten, på en: In the middle of the villas in Smedslätten, on an undeveloped plot on Aladdinsvägen, lies Kämpakumlet, a Bronze Age burial ground with round stone settings resembling cairns. It was partly excavated in 1922, when the garden suburb was being built. The district is named after Smedslätten farm, of which only the main building from the early 19th century remains, now in the middle of a terraced-house area.
Mitt emot Solna centrum ligger Eric Grat: Opposite Solna centrum is Eric Grate's park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. Three of his bronze sculptures stand here: Oberon, Nike de Sant Andria and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God. The shopping centre itself is one of the region's largest, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants.
Mitt hjärta i världen: Mitt hjärta i världen, My Heart in the World
Mitt i Eklanda, en stadsdel där cirka 3: In the middle of Eklanda, a district where about 3,100 people live in around 700 houses, the forest never feels far away. The area borders the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve and Högsbo. Most of it was built after 1993, and according to the plans Eklanda will eventually grow together with the village of Fässberg.
Mitt i Lövgärdet, ett primärområde i sta: In the middle of Lövgärdet, an area within the Gårdsten district, stands a church that has bid farewell to its role. Lövgärdet church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016, having belonged to Gunnared parish from 1973 and, in its last years, to Angered parish. The building is still right nearby, but the services have moved.
Mitt i Rävekärr står de gråa, kvadratisk: In the middle of Rävekärr stand the grey, square terraced houses nicknamed ‘lådhus’, box houses – a housing area with a geometry all its own. Right next door is Fågelberg Church, which belongs to Stensjön parish. South-east of the area are the two lakes Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten, perfect if you want to swap boxes for water.
Mitt i Solberga ligger Solbergaskogen, m: In the middle of Solberga lies Solbergaskogen, a forest with bare rock and pine trees, which the Swedish Forest Agency classified as a key habitat in 2009. There are ancient remains there, including the Solberga burial ground, and the name comes from Solberga farm, mentioned as early as 1636. A little further away is Apelsinlunden, the Orange Grove, a Million Programme housing area from 1967 that got its popular name from its orange-red colour scheme.
Mitt i Volvos värld står Volvohallen, en: In the middle of Volvo's world stands Volvohallen, a dome-shaped exhibition hall on a square floor plan, built in 1975 next to what was then the head office, to designs by Lund & Valentin. Right next to it is Torslandaverken, the Volvo Cars factory. When it opened, it was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic region.
Mitt i centrum ligger Viksjö kyrka, som: In the middle of the centre is Viksjö church, consecrated by Bishop Caroline Krook on 19 June 2005, the fourth Sunday after Trinity. The name Viksjö itself is much older than that: it is a corruption of an original Vikhusa, a name that already appears on a runestone from the 11th century.
Mitt i ett industriområde gömmer sig en: In the middle of an industrial area hides a real survivor: Rya skog, Rya Forest, a remnant of the Central European mixed oak forest that once covered large parts of the west coast. Most of it became a nature reserve as early as 1928, and a survey in 2007 found 22 threatened and rare species here. Botanists and birdwatchers love the place, especially in spring.
Mitt i ett svenskt villaområde vid kuste: In the middle of a Swedish villa area on the coast there's a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion pleasure palace. Skintebo in Billdal was farmland for a long time, but in the 1970s Skintebodalen was built up with car-free walkways, terraced houses, two-storey wooden houses and so-called boatswain's houses, a funny mix of terraced house and villa.
Mitt i handelsområdet Kungens kurva finn: In the middle of the Kungens kurva retail area there's an Oasis, at least in name. The sculpture Oas, meaning Oasis, was created in 2009 to designs by the artist and designer Thomas Nordström, in collaboration with the landscape architect Torsten Wallin. A little further away is Kolartorp, a croft with many names: it has also been called Kålartorp, Crone and Cavalryman's Croft number two.
Mitt i kvarteret står Coldinuorden 3, et: In the middle of the block stands Coldinuorden 3, one of Bredäng's many slab blocks from the mid-1960s, but the only one the City Museum has given a blue rating for its exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Slättgårdsskolan school nearby burned down in June 2020, and the owner decided to rebuild it with a new look. A new gymnasium opened as early as 2021.
Mitt i rondellen står en 4,5 meter hög k: In the middle of the roundabout stands a 4.5-metre-tall pin, stuck through a cross in the ground. The sculpture is called Här, Here, and is by Ebba Matz. The name itself was disputed. The city's property office would rather have had Reutersplatsen, partly because Wavrinsky was so hard to pronounce. On the hill next to it, students now live in Guldheden's old northern water tower.
Mitt i skogen mellan sjöarna Flaten och: In the middle of the forest between the lakes Flaten and Drevviken lies Torpet i Orhem, a culture café that has been here since the 1940s. On its small stage, now in a converted container, artists such as Frida Hyvönen and Joel Alme have performed. Right next to it is Orhems gård, a farm dating back to the 15th century, and by Lake Drevviken is Gebers, a former convalescent home that in 1997 became one of Sweden's first ecological co-housing communities.
Mitt på torget, som hette Adolf Fredriks: In the middle of the square, which was called Adolf Fredriks torg until 1959, stands the fountain Tors fiske, Thor's Fishing, by Anders Wissler, put up in 1903. On the square is Hotel Rival, owned by the composer Benny Andersson and named after the old Rival cinema in the same building. This was also the site of Sutherska huset, a private palace from 1774 where the Philipsen school taught poor children from 1811, until the building was demolished in 1909.
Mittemot Segeltorpsskolan, vid nuvarande: Opposite Segeltorp school, at what is now Kapellvägen 1, there used to be a croft called Holmtorp. The first crofter family was Jonas Olsson and his wife Kjärstin Eriksdotter, both born in 1710, and in the 1760s the place was called Holmtorp or Cronan. The croft was demolished in 1859. Another croft, Segeltorp, survived right up until 1964, when the Jakobslundsvägen terraced-housing area was built on the site.
Morgonen den 23 september 2009 använde r: On the morning of 23 September 2009, robbers used a stolen helicopter to collect their loot from a cash depot in the Västberga industrial area. It was the first time a helicopter had been used in a robbery in Sweden. The police helicopters never took off, because someone had placed a fake bomb on their landing pad. The building, Vreten 17, was originally built for Volvo, among others.
Motionsanläggningen Fysiken vid Mossen h: The Fysiken sports facility by Mossen has a stormy prehistory. Its predecessor Plastiken opened in 1969, a tent of coated fabric held up by internal air pressure, and during the autumn storm that same year it nearly ended badly. Its replacement Fysiken opened in 1983, and for a few years students paid ten kronor extra in their term fee to contribute.
Mulle Meckparken, ett par minuter härifr: Mulle Meckparken, a couple of minutes from here, was created under the direction of the artist Tor Svae and opened in the autumn of 2008. Two years later it won Solna's urban environment prize. Nearby there is also a little detective story: a runestone found by a spring in 1900 was seen for the last time in 1908, and only a small fragment of it has been found since.
Munkebäckstorget fick sitt namn 1947 eft: Munkebäckstorget got its name in 1947 from Munkebäcken, an old name for the Härlandabäcken stream. The monks, munkar, in the name probably refer to monks in Nya Lödöse. Right next to it are the remains of the old Härlanda Church as a church ruin, a reminder of a parish that merged into Nylöse parish as early as 1528. Next to the ruin stands Härlanda New Church.
Museerna här lockar upp till en miljon b: The museums here draw up to a million visitors a year. Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology, was named Museum of the Year in 2025 and once had Sweden's only 4D cinema, where the seats moved and the auditorium offered gusts of wind, splashes of water and scents. In the park of the Ethnographic Museum stands the teahouse Zui-Ki-Tei, whose name means the Dwelling of the Promising Light. Zui stands both for promising and for Sweden.
Mycket av marken runt Hammarby sjö fanns: Much of the land around Hammarby sjö lake didn't exist a hundred years ago. In 1925 a new canal was blasted at the Danvik cliffs, and the level of Hammarby sjö dropped by about five metres. The new shoreline was filled in with blasted rock. There, Lugnet grew up, an area of car workshops and small industry. Today Hammarby sjöstad stands here, built between 1994 and 2020.
Mysterna har ett namn med mystik, men fö: Mysterna has a mysterious-sounding name, but the explanation is down to earth: myst means a small bog. The village is a kilometre west of Göta älv, the Göta River, and on its outskirts is Svankälla wetland park. It was created in 2003 and 2004 and is rich in birds such as marsh harrier, little grebe, lesser spotted woodpecker, coot and mallard.
Mälarhöjdens skola är stadsdelens störst: Mälarhöjden school is the largest in the district, with more than 1,100 pupils in 2016, from preschool class to year nine. A little way off was Mälarbio, also called Mälarhöjdsbio, Kvistoperan and later Färglådan, where regular film screenings began in the spring of 1924 and continued until January 1959. Today a school is housed in the old cinema building.
Mälarskogens naturreservat, ett par hund: The Mälarskogen nature reserve, a couple of hundred metres away, has been protected since 2022 and is crossed by the Mälarpromenaden hiking trail. The trail passes Hallundaröset, Södermanland's second-largest known Bronze Age burial cairn. The cairn survived when the homes were built in the 1970s, thanks to its position at the edge of the forest up on a hill.
Mälarstranden här var förr full av sjökr: The shore of Lake Mälaren here used to be full of lakeside inns. Arboga kök, near Sätra shipyard, was probably built in 1829 and burned down in 1967, and in what is now Sätraskogen nature reserve stood Råstock, where an inn was run from 1665 to 1813 – well into the time of the poet Bellman. On the shore, sailing ships and barges were repaired at Sätra varv, Sätra shipyard, between 1878 and 1935, and several of the workers' houses still stand on the hill.
Möbelsnickare på riktigt utbildas en bit: Real cabinetmakers are trained a little way from here. At Malmstens, formerly the Carl Malmsten school, about 65 students study furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery in purpose-built workshops. The area was also home to Bodal church, now demolished, and Bodals gård, the old main farmhouse of an agricultural property.
Mölndal betyder kvarndalen, och forsen s: Mölndal means mill valley, and the rapids that gave it the name are right nearby. In Kvarnbyn, the Mill Village, there have been mills by the rapids since the 1300s, and until the 1600s the Crown owned most of them. The falls are about 800 metres long with a drop of around 45–48 metres. The water power later drove industries, and today Kvarnbyn is a cultural environment of national interest, with Mölndal City Museum by the rapids.
Mölndal hade förr två järnvägsstationer,: Mölndal once had two railway stations, a lower and an upper one. The lower one opened in 1888 on the West Coast Line and its station building was demolished in 1977, while the upper one, on the Borås Line, opened in 1894 in red brick and was demolished in 1983. A little way from here is also the steep hill of Kvarnbygatan, known as Mölndals kråka, Mölndal's Crow, or just Kråkan.
Mölndal har fått sitt namn efter kvarnar: Mölndal is named after the mills that stood by the rapids of the Mölndalsån river ever since the Middle Ages. A little way from here was the Grand cinema at Göteborgsvägen 1, which opened on Boxing Day 1938 and closed in 1966. A little further away is Mölndal travel centre, on a 500-metre-long bridge over the motorway, with about 3.5 million passengers a year.
Mölndal är ett ställe för både simtag oc: Mölndal is a place for both swimming strokes and hoofbeats. A few hundred metres from here is Åbybadet, opened in the summer of 2023 at a cost of 500 million kronor, and in the same area is Åbytravet, Sweden's second largest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. So here you can choose between swimming yourself or watching the horses run.
Mölndals sjukhus invigdes 1924 och ersat: Mölndal hospital opened in 1924, replacing a municipal infirmary. Today it is part of Sahlgrenska University Hospital. The Möllan cinema in Mölndal's Folkets hus, the community hall, has been showing films since 1959. It has 289 seats and was modernised and digitised with support from the municipality.
Mölndals stadsmuseum ligger sedan 2002 h: Since 2002, Mölndal City Museum has been at the top of the steep slope called Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow, with a café for anyone who needs a rest. Just below, Mölndalsfallen, the Mölndal rapids, roar; in the 1800s their power drove cotton mills, paper mills and a weaving mill. Royens gata nearby is named after three Roy brothers who emigrated from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölndalsfallen strax intill har gett sta: Mölndalsfallen, the Mölndal rapids right nearby, have given the town both food and its name, because there was salmon fishing and mills here, and Mölndal roughly means Mill Valley. The steep slope east of the square is called Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow. The streets here have their secrets too: Götaforsliden has been called both Glada gatan, the Happy Street, and Tysta gatan, the Quiet Street, and nobody knows why, while Royens gata is named after three Roy brothers from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölnlycke station en bit härifrån har fl: Mölnlycke station, a little way from here, has moved. It opened in 1894, about 350 metres east of where it is today, and was moved to its current site in 2003. The old station building was demolished in 2013. Today the Västtågen regional trains stop here on their way between Gothenburg and Borås along the Coast-to-Coast line.
Mölnlycke är kyrkbyn i Råda socken, och: Mölnlycke is the church village of Råda parish, and the local administration for the Råda rural municipality used to be here. Although it's mostly villas, terraced houses and linked houses, the town has plenty of greenery, including the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area. A small number of properties are actually in Mölndal municipality.
Mölnlycke, centralort i Härryda kommun,: Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda Municipality, lies about ten kilometres south-east of Gothenburg and consists mostly of detached, terraced and linked houses. Despite the dense development there is plenty of greenery, such as the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area. Through the centre flows the Mölndalsån river on its way from Landvettersjön lake to Rådasjön, and in the middle of the town lies the little lake Massetjärnen.
Mörby centrum byggdes 1961 och glasades: Mörby centrum was built in 1961 and glazed over in 1977. In 2026 it got a new name: after ten years of rebuilding, the centre is now called Danderyds Centrum. The metro ends here, because Mörby centrum is the terminus of route 14 on the red line. The new look was designed by Gatun Arkitekter.
Mörby station har legat på Roslagsbanan: Mörby station has been on the Roslagsbanan railway since 1906, and just south of it the line's workshops have been since 1907, designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt. A few hundred metres away is Danderyd hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, where around 6,300 births take place every year. So many people have taken their first breaths here.
Mörbyleden slingrar sig mellan E18 och V: Mörbyleden winds between the E18 and Vendevägen and passes right by the Mörbyskogen housing area. A little way from here is Danderyd Hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, which receives about 90,000 emergency patients every year. And the nearby shopping centre changed its name in May 2026 from Mörby Centrum to Danderyds Centrum.
Nacka Forum öppnade den 1 mars 1989 och: Nacka Forum opened on 1 March 1989, replacing a temporary centre in prefab huts that had had to do for many years. Right next to it begins the villa idyll of Storängen, where Villa Wållgren from 1907 has been judged irreplaceable. A stone's throw away also stands Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner and his wife Elin, née Bonnier.
Nacka kyrka byggdes 1891 i nygotisk stil: Nacka Church was built in 1891 in neo-Gothic style and is surrounded by Nacka North Cemetery. Around the church is Birka, one of Nacka's oldest villa areas, where the first houses came in the 1880s for employees of the area's growing industries, such as Atlas Copco in Sickla and de Lavals Ångturbin in Järla. The area has changed name several times and has been called Järla, Järlaby and Birka-Järla.
Nacka strand hette länge Augustendal. 18: Nacka strand was long called Augustendal. In 1899 the industrial pioneer J.V. Svenson bought the area, and by 1916 his engine factory had 500 employees, one of Sweden's largest workplaces. After a bankruptcy in 1922, the company was taken over by Handelsbanken. In the 1980s offices and homes were built, and in 1988 the area was given the name Nacka strand. In the marina, since 1995, Carl Milles' sculpture God the Father on the Rainbow has been spraying water in an arc over the Saltsjön bay.
Namnet Beckomberga är gammalt. Det äldst: The name Beckomberga is old. The earliest record, Bäknaberga, is from 1319, and the name means those who live by the stream. In the Middle Ages the village consisted of three farms: Södergården, Mellangården and Norrgården – the south, middle and north farms. At the corner of Bällstavägen and Spångavägen, the so-called Round Houses were built in the 1950s, homes for the nurses at Beckomberga hospital.
Namnet Blåsut kommer från en krog vid et: The name Blåsut, roughly Blow Out, comes from a tavern at a forester's residence, and in the 19th century Blåsut was a common name for blustery, windswept places. The metro station opened in 1950 and in 2008 got art by Ann Edholm, with speed stripes in black and white tiles. A little further away is Framtiden 1, the Future, from 1915, and in the building next door, fittingly called Nutiden, the Present, was the cinema Enskede Kvarn.
Namnet Bräcke kommer av fornsvenskans br: The name Bräcke comes from the Old Swedish brækko, a broad slope or hill. A stone's throw away is Bräcke diakoni, the foundation set up in 1923 under the name Göteborgs diakonissanstalt to train deaconesses. A short walk away is Bräcke cemetery, laid out during the cholera epidemic of 1834, when the disease entered Sweden through Gothenburg.
Namnet Gårda dyker upp redan 1550 och är: The name Gårda appears as early as 1550 and is simply an inflected form of the word "gård", meaning farm. A stone's throw away stands Hästskosömsfabriken, the horseshoe-nail factory, with factory buildings from around 1890 and 1900 that are today a state-listed building. And Drakegatan is named after the Drake brickworks, which Anders Drake founded in the mid-18th century.
Namnet Högsätra betyder högre belägen än: The name Högsätra means 'the higher meadow' and comes from an area with three 19th-century villas. The complex was built to provide public services for all ages, with a school, sports, healthcare and a pharmacy. Högsätrahuset, which once housed Lidingö hospital, is to be demolished to make way for the new Kärnan area.
Namnet Jättesten kommer från de stora st: The name Jättesten, "giant stone", comes from the large boulders on the hill behind the houses. The neighbouring street has a fun naming story: A C Lindblads gata, named in 1954 after the editor-in-chief and labour movement pioneer Anders Christensen Lindblad. The naming committee wanted to call it Lindbladsgatan, but in the city council Hugo Höglund objected that Lindblad was usually called simply A C – and so it was.
Namnet Kallebäck betyder bäcken med kitt: The name Kallebäck means "the stream with the kettle" and is first mentioned in 1496. The district lies on the south-eastern edge of Gothenburg between the big main roads. There you'll also find Ostkupan, the Cheese Dome, a 14-storey student building from 1964 with a nickname that's appetising, to say the least. A little further away is a cholera cemetery from the 1866 epidemic, today protected as an ancient monument.
Namnet Kungens kurva kommer från en alld: The name Kungens kurva, "the King's Bend", comes from a genuinely royal trip into a ditch. On a Saturday afternoon, 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur drove off Södertäljevägen road and ended up stuck in a water-filled ditch, and the newspapers were quickly on the scene. Today the area is one of Scandinavia's largest shopping centres, and together with Skärholmen centrum it draws 30 million visitors every year.
Namnet Kvarnskogen passar bra: en bit bo: The name Kvarnskogen, the Mill Forest, fits well: a little way off, on the north-eastern shore of Edsviken bay, there has been a mill for more than 400 years. The first was abandoned some time in the late 16th century – nobody knows why – but a new one was soon built on the same spot. The mill and the sawmill next to it were used into the 1950s and are now a museum.
Namnet Käppala klingar bekant för många: The name Käppala rings a bell for many people for another reason: Käppalaverket, the sewage treatment plant opened in 1969 and considered one of the most efficient in the world. A little way from here is also Käppalaställningen, an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War that was rededicated in 1994 as a monument to Stockholm's air defence.
Namnet Marievik har använts sedan 1930-t: The name Marievik has been used since the 1930s and is a Swedish version of Maryvik, one of four estates that stood here. Right next to it was Liljeholmen station, which opened for passenger traffic on 1 December 1860 and remained a goods station until 1998. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill stands the old parish hall from the 1920s, where since 2003 Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music school, has filled the halls with music.
Namnet Masmo bär på en gammal rädsla: fö: The name Masmo carries an old fear: the first part, "mas", is thought to be a so-called taboo word for wolf, and the whole name is said to mean roughly "the forest where the wolf has been seen". A stone's throw away, Myrstuguberget clings to the hillside by Albysjön lake – architect Ralph Erskine's first residential area in the Stockholm region, completed in 1986. The name comes from the boatswain's croft Myrstugan, which was moved when the houses were built.
Namnet Mysterna kommer av ordet myst, en: The name Mysterna comes from the word myst, a small bog. The village, with mostly newly built villas and terraced houses, lies a kilometre or so north of Hisings Kärra and since 2015 has counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area. On its outskirts is the Svankälla wetland park, a place rich in birds where coots and mallards, among others, feel at home.
Namnet Rud är gammalt, belagt redan 1495: The name Rud is old, recorded as early as 1495 with spellings such as Rudh and Rwdh, and it means a clearing or cleared place. A little way from here is Ruddalens IP, a football ground for 3,000 spectators that has had artificial turf since 2003. The first match was played on 27 April 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF met IFK Malmö.
Namnet Skra Bro sägs komma av det skrapa: The name Skra Bro is said to come from the scraping sound of sledge runners scraping against the ground in thawing weather. The old bridge over the Osbäcken stream is still right next to us, but today it's just a footbridge between the park-and-ride and a grocery store. Car traffic now crosses a larger road bridge north of the roundabout.
Namnet Skvaltan minner om en sjö vars ut: The name Skvaltan recalls a lake whose outflow through Vikdalen once drove several small "skvaltkvarnar", simple horizontal water mills. A little further away in Storängen stands Villa Waern, built in 1905 for the wholesaler Charles Waern to designs by Torben Grut and judged irreplaceable. Nearby is also Villa Kallstenius, designed for the artist couple Gottfrid Kallstenius and Gerda Roosval-Kallstenius.
Namnet Spånga finns i skrift redan år 13: The name Spånga appears in writing as early as the year 1300, as 'apud Ecclesiam spangar'. It comes from the old church village and simply means footbridges, several narrow plank walkways. The station is on the Mälarbanan line, just over eleven kilometres from Stockholm Central. A little further away is Svandammen, the Swan Pond, a park with a bathing spot where both young people and families with children like to gather.
Namnet Tegeludden är belagt sedan 1649 o: The name Tegeludden is recorded from 1649 and refers to a master forester's residence on Royal Djurgården, but nobody knows why it was called that. On the street stands Philipshuset, the Philips Building, built in the early 1960s as headquarters and warehouse for Svenska Philips. Today the Administrative Court sits in the old offices, and TV4 makes television in the warehouse.
Namnet Trolldalen har använts sedan 1700: The name Trolldalen, the Troll Valley, has been used since the 18th century and then referred to the ravine in the middle of the forest on the Henriksdal hill, a rift valley that easily fires the imagination. Up on the hill is Henriksdalsringen, built from 1964 to 1969 to designs by the brothers Erik and Tore Ahlsén, who afterwards chose to move there themselves. A little way off, in Finnboda, the Finnboda shipyard operated between 1884 and 1991.
Namnet Tulebo kan lura en. Den gamla tät: The name Tulebo can fool you. The old village of Tulebo is northeast of Lake Tulebosjön, but recently new residential areas on the lake's southwest side have been given Tulebo names, such as Tulebo Villastad and Tulebo Park, even though they're in the villages of Hultet and Stretered. Nearby is also the recording studio Nilento Studio.
Namnet Vantör är riktigt gammalt. Den me: The name Vantör is really old. The medieval parish was called that, but since a fire in the 1400s its church has been called Brännkyrka, the Burnt Church. Today Vantör church is in Högdalen, a short walk away. Högdalen centre also used to have the Rondo cinema, which showed films from January 1961 right up to May 1983.
Namnet Viksjö har en lång historia: det: The name Viksjö has a long history: it is a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which appears as early as on an 11th-century runestone. In 1963 a building consortium began developing the land, and today Viksjö is dominated by small houses from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s. A little way off is Hummelmoraberget, a hill where old beach ridges show that the sea once reached all the way here.
Namnet Viksjö är äldre än gården. Det dy: The name Viksjö is older than the farm. It appears as early as on an 11th-century runestone, which is the oldest place name recorded in writing in Järfälla. It says that 'Knut in Vikhusum had the stone raised and the bridge made' in memory of his parents and siblings. The farm itself is recorded from 1734, and the district around it was built in the 1970s.
Namnet har sin förklaring: här låg Hande: The name has an explanation: Handen's old folkpark, a people's park, was here. What remains today is Haninge kulturpark, where local associations have taken care of the last old buildings, among them RoJteatern in the old Folkets hus, the community hall. Every June the area fills with music, theatre and dance during the Kulturparksfestivalen. A stone's throw away is Handens museum och smedja, a museum and smithy with goats, hens and time-travel trips for schoolchildren.
Namnet kommer från Stuvsta gårds väderkv: The name comes from the windmill of Stuvsta gård, which once stood on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill. The mill is gone, but several millstones remain. The municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen. North of Huddinge station, a train derailed on the bend one Saturday evening in 1908. Nobody died, and the event was immortalised on two postcards.
Namnet kommer från en våg. Här vägdes jä: The name comes from a weighing scale. This is where the iron shipped out through Gothenburg's harbour was weighed, including iron from ironworks in Värmland. In the 1780s the city's iron weigh-house was moved to a plot just north of today's Järntorget, the Iron Square, and the square was named after it. The iron carriers, who handled the iron bars, settled in the surrounding blocks. The weigh-house itself was demolished long ago.
Nationalmuseum står på det som en gång v: Nationalmuseum, Sweden's national museum of art and design, stands on what was once its own little islet, Kyrkholmen. When the city granted the land for the museum in 1846, the head of construction, Johan af Kleen, filled in the canal towards Blasieholmen, entirely without permission. The museum was completed in 1866 and is Sweden's largest art museum. Just outside stands The Foster Brothers by Theodor Lundberg, and its twin sculpture is in Copenhagen.
Naturhistoriska museet och blåvalen: The Natural History Museum and the blue whale
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet och Cosmonova: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History, and Cosmonova
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, Sveriges stö: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History and Sweden's largest museum complex, was established in 1819, and its current building by Axel Anderberg opened in 1916. Next door is Bergianska trädgården, the Bergius Botanic Garden, whose largest building is the Edvard Anderson greenhouse from 1995, named after the wholesaler who left money in his will for a winter garden of Mediterranean plants. The residential area Ekhagen is one of the few areas built entirely in the functionalist style.
Naturreservatet Välen ligger några minut: The Välen nature reserve is a few minutes' walk away, at the far end of Askimsviken bay. Here there's a wetland museum, a bird-watching platform, a nature trail and a time trail. The reserve was created in 2014 and covers around 68 hectares, and within it are a cairn and a stone setting from the Bronze Age.
Nedanför Baggeby, ner mot Lilla Värtan,: Below Baggeby, down towards Lilla Värtan, lies Lidingsberg. It is one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer residences on Lidingö. The estate is owned by the Wedberg family and has the island's largest private plot, about six hectares. It is reached by Lidingsbergsvägen, which is Lidingö's shortest named road. The buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nedanför Sankt Pauli kyrka står fontängr: Below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, stands the fountain group Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements, by Anders Jönsson, unveiled on Swedish Flag Day in 1930. It first stood on Olskrokstorget, but was moved when the square disappeared during construction of the approach roads to the Tingstad tunnel. A little way off on Redbergsvägen is Flamman, a cinema with 684 seats that showed films from 1935 to 1982 and is now a listed building.
Nedanför Tahultsdrumlinen ligger lilla A: Below the Tahult drumlin, a glacial ridge, lies little Agntjärnen, a pond only 6.5 metres deep. The slope down to the pond is protected as the Gallhålan nature reserve, a large continuous oak woodland in hilly terrain where wood vetch, wood violet, wood anemone and liverleaf grow. On the pond you may spot mallard, goldeneye, goosander and tufted duck.
Nedanför Torsvik vid Lilla Värtan står T: Below Torsvik, by the Lilla Värtan strait, stands Torsvik lighthouse, which was built in 1950 and put out of service in 1980. Today it serves as the finish-line reference for the Lidingö Runt sailing race. At the landing of the old Lidingö bridge is a small waiting shelter designed by Ivar Tengbom, which, because of its windy location, earned the nickname the Temple of the Winds. The Torsvikshöjden housing area from the 1940s is seen as an early example of the post-war neighbourhood units.
Ner mot Lilla Värtan ligger Kappsta natu: Down towards Lilla Värtan lies Kappsta nature reserve, full of unusual house foundations. One of them belonged to Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. Today the memorial Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W., marks the spot. Close by stood Villa Nidaros, Trondheim's pavilion at the 1897 Stockholm Exhibition. It was shipped here as a summer house and burned after a lightning strike in 1960.
Nere i Klippans kulturreservat ligger An: Down in the Klippan cultural reserve is Ankarsmedjan, the anchor forge. Anchors and chains were forged there for the ships of the Swedish East India Company, which used Klippan as an outer harbour. The building is said to date from the 1770s. The walls were one ell and nine inches thick, around 80 centimetres, built of grey stone, and there was also a cooper's workshop here.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Ekhagens st: Down by Lilla Värtan is Ekhagen beach, also called Lappis Beach. The student area of Lappkärrsberget, popularly known as Lappis, is a little way off and is Stockholm's largest, with more than 3,000 student flats built in 1968–1970. The streets have fitting names such as Professorsslingan, Amanuensvägen and Forskarbacken – the Professor's Loop, the Assistant's Road and the Researcher's Hill.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Lidingsberg: Down by Lilla Värtan lies Lidingsberg, one of Lidingö's best-preserved 19th-century summer residences. The estate is owned by the Wedberg family and has the island's largest privately owned plot, about six hectares, and it is reached by Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen. The area is also crossed by Södra Lidingöstråket, a walking trail about 18 kilometres long that runs all the way from Gåshaga jetty to Stortorget, the main square in Gamla stan, the Old Town.

Down by the Lilla Värtan strait is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer residences on Lidingö. The estate is owned by the Wedberg family and has Lidingö's largest private plot, around six hectares. Leading to it is Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen. The buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nere vid Magelungen står en stor röd trä: Down by Lake Magelungen stands a large red wooden villa from 1916 to 1917, built as a children's home. The name Rödkinda, Red Cheek, came from the idea that fresh air would give the children rosy cheeks. The villa stands on a hill with a south-facing slope down towards the lake. The old premises of Farsta gymnasium are now used by Farsta grundskola, a primary school, and the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Nils Ericsonsplatsen är uppkallad efter: Nils Ericsonsplatsen is named after Nils Ericson, who built Sweden's first main railway lines. He was the brother of the inventor John Ericsson. Beneath us, Västlänken, the West Link, a railway tunnel under central Gothenburg, is being built.
Nockeby torg, en kort promenad härifrån,: Nockeby torg, a short walk from here, was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza, a typical garden-suburb square. Tram 12 had already been extended here in the autumn of 1929. Less romantic but impressive is the nearby Bromma sewage treatment plant: since 1989 the purified water has been carried through a tunnel about twelve kilometres long under Solna and Stockholm all the way out to the Saltsjön waters at Kastellholmen.
Norr om Humlegården skapades på 1870-tal: North of Humlegården park, a villa town was created in the 1870s on English and German lines. Most of the villas were later replaced by splendid apartment buildings, and Floragatan is today one of Sweden's most expensive addresses. The Curman Villa from 1880 to 1881 is one of the few still standing, a free interpretation of a Roman country house with a tall, glass-roofed atrium in the middle. Next door is Villa Sandrew.
Norr om Hågelby gård skulle det en gång: North of Hågelby manor, northern Europe's biggest amusement attraction was once supposed to be built. The Lindgren family, who have run Gröna Lund amusement park for generations, were going to lease the land for the Hågelby Family Park, but in 2014 the plans were dropped. What remains is the Älvestaån stream, which flows from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön with a drop of 17 metres and partly hides in a culvert under Hågelby manor.
Norr om Tumlehed, en bit härifrån, finns: North of Tumlehed, a little way from here, is a natural area with walking paths and trails, hiding several ancient monuments. Among them are rock paintings showing four ships, a deer and four fish. Think about that the next time you take a walk in the woods here on western Hisingen.
Norr om sjön Flaten, inne i Flatens natu: North of Lake Flaten, inside the Flaten nature reserve, hides Skarpnäcksgrottan, a cave protected as an ancient monument. The Flaten district borders both Lake Drevviken and Lake Ältasjön, a lake only about four and a half metres deep. Test fishing there has caught perch, bream and ruffe, among others.
Norra Biskopsgårdens kyrka byggdes 1970: Norra Biskopsgården church was built in 1970 as a parish hall, when Lundby parish was at its largest and needed more space. It has a free-standing bell tower. The Church of Sweden deconsecrated it in 2004, and today it is used by the City Mission and the Finnish parish. A little way off is Jättesten, named after the boulders on the hill behind the houses.
Nu har staden blivit kust. Långedrag är: Now the city has become coast. Långedrag is Gothenburg's sailing harbour, and in summer the jetties are packed with boats. From here you can look out towards the archipelago and, on a clear day, Vinga lighthouse far out at the edge of the open sea.
Nu kör vi ner mot Göta älv och Stenpiren: Now we're heading down towards the Göta älv river and Stenpiren. During the 19th and early 20th centuries, more than a million Swedes left the country to seek a new life in America, and most of them travelled via Gothenburg. Many of them boarded right here. Today the Älvsnabben ferry leaves from here across the river, and it's included in the same ticket as the tram. On the other side you can see Lindholmen and Eriksberg, where the city's great shipyards once stood.
Nu kör vi över den lilla bron ut till Re: Now we're crossing the little bridge out to Reimersholme. The island is named after Anders Reimers, who owned it in the 18th century. For a long time there was a distillery here, and the Reimersholms name lived on on the bottles. Today the island is a quiet residential area with a waterfront walk all the way round it. We'll soon reach the final stop. Thank you for riding with us!
Nu passerar vi Lisebergs södra sida. Här: We're now passing the south side of Liseberg amusement park. Here you'll often catch a glimpse of the roller coasters. Lisebergshöjden, the hill behind the park, was once part of the Liseberg estate, a country house that gave the park its name.
Nu är vi i SoFo, området söder om Folkun: Now we're in SoFo, the area south of Folkungagatan. There are small shops, cafés and bars here, and in the middle is Nytorget, one of Södermalm's best-loved parks. Many of the buildings in the surrounding blocks date from the late 1800s.
Nu är vi på Södermalm. Västerbron, som v: Now we're on Södermalm. Västerbron, the Western Bridge we just crossed, opened in 1935 and is over six hundred metres long. The church with the two towers right here is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923.

We're now on Södermalm. Västerbron, the bridge we just crossed, opened in 1935 and is more than six hundred metres long. The church with the two towers right next to us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. It can be seen from far away and is a landmark for the whole of western Söder.
Nya Ullevi byggdes till fotbolls-VM 1958: Nya Ullevi was built for the 1958 football World Cup and is still one of Sweden's largest arenas. It is also famous for its concerts. When Bruce Springsteen played here in 1985, the stands swayed so much that the arena later had to be reinforced.
Nya Varvet blev örlogshamn kring år 1700: Nya Varvet became a naval base around the year 1700, and in 1717 and 1719 it was attacked by Danish warships under Vice Admiral Peter Tordenskjold. Right next to it is Nya Varvet cemetery from 1701, with a memorial to those who died on the submarine HMS Ulven, which was blown up by a mine in 1943. The officers' mess Nobis, a little way up the hill, is a listed building.
Nytorget och kaféerna runt torget: Nytorget square and the cafés around it
Nälsta är en av nio stadsdelar i Hässelb: Nälsta is one of nine districts in Hässelby-Vällingby and has a mix of villas, terraced houses and blocks of flats. A little way from here is Spånga torg, the square near Spånga station, where both commuter trains and buses run. The square has a fairly large range of shops, businesses and restaurants, so there's most of what you need if you're hungry or have errands to run.
När LM Ericsson flyttade till Telefonpla: When LM Ericsson moved to Telefonplan in the late 1930s, the master builder Olle Engkvist built about 1,000 flats in LM-staden, at a fast pace and with narrow buildings of 8 to 10 metres. A little way off in Aspudden stands the fountain sculpture Fontändamm from 1912, in the middle of a small park on Manhemsgatan. It was paid for by the building firm Manhem, which also had the street named after it.
När Trädgårn öppnade som kafé 1858 fanns: When Trädgårn opened as a café in 1858, all the staff were men, and punsch, a Swedish arrack liqueur, was the only spirit on offer. The building next to the stop, Exercishuset, was completed in 1867 as a gift from the wholesaler Julius Lindström. There, schoolchildren were to do gymnastics and riflemen were to drill. Heden itself was the military's training ground, and until 2019 there was a bandy rink here.
När Tuletorget invigdes 1964 var det Sun: When Tuletorget opened in 1964 it was Sundbyberg's most modern shopping centre, with an underground garage, a BP petrol station, a Systembolaget state liquor store, a Tempo department store, a post office and a shoe shop. But the customers never came, and by the 1970s the square was growing ever more deserted. Since 2016 it has been renovated and gained two new high-rises, Tuletornen. The name Tulegatan comes from the mythical Thule, because the street was once Sundbyberg's northernmost boundary.
När området började bebyggas 1921 hette: When building began here in 1921, the area was called Ersta Villastad. The name provoked protests, and in 1926 it was swapped for the invented name Stureby. A couple of hundred metres away is the Vivstavarvsvägen terraced-house area from the early 1950s, designed by Erik F. Dahl. Its 36 terraced houses are the only ones in Stureby marked blue by the City Museum for their high cultural value.
När tunnelbanan nådde Farsta den 19 nove: When the metro reached Farsta on 19 November 1958, a temporary station opened first, and it was right here at Farstavägen 78 and Pepparvägen 81. Two years later the station moved into Farsta centrum, where Farsta torg was laid out like an Italian piazza, perhaps inspired by Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. Fruit and flowers are still sold on the square most days of the week.
När tunnelbanan till Hässelby strand inv: When the metro to Hässelby strand opened on 18 November 1958, it was a celebration. The first train, decorated with a bundle of six flags at the front and back, left Bagarmossen at 13.28. The 320 invited guests were served coffee during the journey, and at the controls sat the tramway's oldest driver, Karl Johan Gustavsson. Today the station is the green line's north-western terminus.
När Örby slott hade sålts 1897 och ägorn: When Örby Palace was sold in 1897 and its land divided up into plots, Valdorshem was probably built, the very first villa in the area. The villa was demolished in the autumn of 2020. Going back even further is Örby kvarn, a windmill whose first version was built in 1672 and replaced by a new one in 1885. What remains from the mill era is the miller's cottage, which has now been converted into a villa.
Nära Villa Källhagen, en anrik krog med: Near Villa Källhagen, a long-established restaurant with roots in the 18th century, lies a large stone bearing a thank-you. It was presented in 1983 by Norway's King Olav V to Carl XVI Gustaf, as an official thanks for Sweden's help to Norway during the Second World War. Among other things, a Norwegian army of 15,000 soldiers was trained on Swedish soil, under the cover name of the police troops. Nearby there were also film studios, used from 1940 to 1960.
Nära stationen finns Leksaks- och samlar: Near the station is the Toy and Collectors' Museum, a museum about toys and play, which since May 2018 has been in the same building as the Historiearvsmuseet, the History Heritage Museum. The latter, also called HAMN, was Sweden's first and only battlefield museum. Fisksätra itself, by the way, is Sweden's most densely populated urban area, with 7,724 inhabitants per square kilometre.
Närlunda är ett av bostadsområdena i tät: Närlunda is one of the residential areas in the town of Ekerö. A little further away is Tappström, which counted as a separate town right up until 1975. That's also where you'll find Ekerö centrum, designed by the architect Ralph Erskine and completed in 1991, with a dot on top more than twenty metres high as its trademark. The area has received international attention thanks to Erskine's idea of a Mälaren town.
Näsby slott ligger vid Näsbyviken av Sto: Näsby Palace lies on Näsbyviken, a bay of Stora Värtan, and is today a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant. The station next door has a little naming story: it opened in 1937 as Alléparken, but after only four months it changed its name to Näsby allé. Sometimes the name has even been written as one word, Näsbyallé.
Näsbydal är format som ett ägg, med 900: Näsbydal is shaped like an egg, with 900 flats ranging from studios with a sleeping alcove to seven-room flats on two floors. The housing cooperative even has its own football pitch, tennis court and several playgrounds. Right next to it is Kvarntorpshällen, a runic rock slab that the author Jan Fridegård discovered in 1943, with the word "stepsons" carved into it.
Näsbypark räknas som ett av Täbys mer ex: Näsbypark is considered one of Täby's more exclusive residential areas, with villas, flats and terraced houses by the water at Stora Värtan. A little further away is Näsby allé station, which opened in 1937 under the name Alléparken but switched to its current name after just four months. By Näsbyviken bay lies Näsby slott, a palace that is today a conference hotel with a restaurant.
Näsets kyrka ligger bara ett par hundra: Näset Church is only a couple of hundred metres away. The Näset peninsula has many bathing spots along its rocky coast, including a nudist beach, and at the highest point, 50 metres above sea level, stands an old pilot lookout hut. In 1964 to 1966 Åkered was built, with around 600 homes.
Nästan granne med hållplatsen ligger Blå: Almost next door to the stop is Blå Stjärnan animal hospital, Sweden's largest, which treats dogs, cats and small pets around the clock, all year round. Many recognise it from the SVT television series Djursjukhuset. A little way off, Hotel The Weaver towers 22 storeys high. The name, Vävaren in Swedish, refers to the Krokslätt factories, which were a complete weaving business until the 1970s.
Nästan granne med hållplatsen står Kasta: Almost next door to the stop stands Kastala church, the church of the Komarken district. Kungälv lies where the Göta älv river forks and the Nordre älv takes over, a couple of Swedish miles, about 20 kilometres, north of central Gothenburg. The town is also home to the Nordic Folk High School, and to the west the municipality stretches out into a rocky coastal area with an archipelago.
Någonstans här i närheten gömmer sig kan: Somewhere around here a runestone may be hiding. It is said to have stood by the avenue from Ulriksdal Palace, where there is now a road interchange, and it was probably walled into a road culvert in the second half of the 1800s. It has been searched for several times, without result. Right next to it is Villa Jacobsdal, which shares its name with an older name for Ulriksdal Palace.
Någonstans i Veddesta stod en gång en vi: Somewhere in Veddesta there once stood a Viking Age runestone, U 93. Olof Celsius the Elder wrote about it in 1728, and since then no one has seen hide nor hair of it. The area is named after Veddesta gård, a farm that survived until 1983, and the industrial area is set to be transformed into a mixed-use district with several thousand new homes.
Några hundra meter bort ligger lilla Sto: A few hundred metres away is little Stockbysjön lake, only about two metres at its deepest, where yellow water lilies grow. The lake drains into Kottlasjön via the Stockbyån stream, which is surrounded by flood forest and swamp where beavers, among others, thrive. The area also has the Skärsätra water tower, a drinking-water reservoir opened in 1912 and closed in 1959.
Några hundra meter bort står en runsten: A few hundred metres away stands a runestone from the late 11th century, the Kummelby stone, next to Kummelby church. The church has a little history of its own: the first one was built on the site of the old Kummelby farm, but held only 50 people and got the nickname Kummelby's little church. In 1999 it was taken out of use, and just before Christmas 2000 a new one was consecrated.
Några hundra meter härifrån glittrar Söd: A few hundred metres from here glitters Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow clear-water lake that is popular for swimming. The water flows north to Stensjön, which is close to Gunnebo House and has given its name to both Stensjön parish and Stensjökyrkan church. At the ridge Kikås next door there's also Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Safjä: A few hundred metres from here is the Safjället nature reserve, on a rocky plateau near the border with Gothenburg. To the south-west, the hill slopes steeply down towards the Toltorp valley. The reserve was set up in 1991 and covers 88 hectares. Closer to the stop is the Bifrost area, where the street names are connected to farming.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Studi: A few hundred metres from here is Studio Fredman, the recording studio Fredrik Nordström started in 1990. A long line of Swedish metal bands have recorded here, such as In Flames, Hammerfall, Opeth, Dark Tranquillity and Soilwork, and even Britain's Bring me the Horizon. Just beyond is Radiotorget, Sweden's first satellite town square, opened in 1954.
Några hundra meter härifrån ligger Åbyba: A few hundred metres from here is Åbybadet, Mölndal's swimming baths, which opened on 16 June 2023 and cost 500 million kronor to build. In the same area is Åbytravet, Sweden's second largest trotting track. In the other direction lies Eklanda, a district built largely from 1993 onwards.
Några minuter bort ligger Bandyhallen i: A few minutes away is Bandyhallen in Gubbängen, Stockholm's first indoor bandy hall. It is 25 metres high and came into use in the summer of 2020, after first being planned for Tallkrogen. The area also has the Majroskogen nature reserve, created in 2026, the largest continuous forest area in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Några minuters promenad bort tar Fagersj: A few minutes' walk away begins Fagersjöskogen, at 100 hectares one of the largest forests in Stockholm's southern suburbs. Stockholm's biggest spruce grows there too! Nearby stands Villa Lindhov, a wooden villa from 1910 that Harald Lind had built and then named after himself, one of the few well-preserved villas left from Södertörns villastad, a planned villa town.
Oasen sim- och ishall: Oasen swimming pool and ice rink
Oljeraffinaderiet Preemraff Göteborg en: The Preemraff Göteborg oil refinery, a little way off, buys most of its crude oil from the North Sea. Giant tankers dock at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen, and the oil is stored in rock caverns next to it. Tankers also unload inside Skarvikshamnen harbour, but there the water is too shallow for the very largest.
Oljeraffinaderiet Preemraff Göteborg kan: The Preemraff Göteborg oil refinery can process about six million tonnes of crude oil a year, mostly from the North Sea. Even ULCC-class tankers, the world's largest, 333 metres long, have called at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen. The oil is then stored in large rock caverns next to the harbour.
Olof Skötkonungsgatan fick 1925 sitt nam: Olof Skötkonungsgatan was given its name in 1925 after King Olof Skötkonung and his alleged connection to Örgryte old church, which is a short walk from here. The church is one of Gothenburg's most popular for weddings, and in the old churchyard from the 13th century lie, among others, three bishops. At the entrance stands the statue Genomkämpat, roughly 'Fought Through', whose original is in Berlin.
Olshammarsgatan, en av Hagsätras två huv: Olshammarsgatan, one of Hagsätra's two main streets, runs about 600 metres from Hagsätra centrum out to Ormkärr, and on the way it crosses both Huddingevägen and the green metro line. The centre itself was built in a single year and opened in 1960. There the copper sculpture “The Child with the Hobby Horse” still stands guard.
Om man bortser från en liten flik av Mäl: Apart from a small corner of Lake Mälaren, Lötsjön is Sundbyberg's only lake, and since 2018 it has been protected as a nature reserve together with the neighbouring Golfängarna meadows. By the lake is Lötsjökapellet, a chapel on the edge of Sundbyberg cemetery. The nearby sports ground is popularly called Sumpan IP, and its all-weather track is not full-size but only 366 metres.
Området Sandbäck i närheten har långa rö: The nearby area of Sandbäck has deep roots. As early as the 1550s it consisted of two homesteads, that is, two farms, long before any buses rolled through here. A little further away is Rävekärr, with its grey, square terraced houses popularly known as box houses, and to the south-east of them glitters Lake Horsikan.
Ormkärr kallas den del av Hagsätra som l: Ormkärr is the name for the part of Hagsätra that lies south-west of Huddingevägen. From here it's not far to Hagsätra torg, a square that got its name in 1962 and surrounds the centre, where the copper sculpture “The Child with the Hobby Horse” by Marie Stenqvist has become something of a trademark. And in the neighbourhood spreads Hagsätraskogen, a forest of 31 hectares of protected nature.
Ormo naturreservat ligger nära, 25 hekta: Ormo nature reserve is close by: 25 hectares of broadleaf forest and pasture along the valley of the Ormbäcken stream, between wooded hills and open grazing land. The area has been protected since 2018. A little way off, in Nordre älv, is the Ormo barrier, an adjustable dam that can move water from Nordre älv over to the Gothenburg branch of Göta älv, the Göta River.
Orten Kil i Boo har fått sitt namn efter: The village of Kil in Boo is named after Kils gård, a well-preserved manor on Graningevägen. The main building and wings got their Empire-style look in the 1820s under Major General Louis Marie de Camps. A little way off is Lake Insjön, almost twelve metres deep, with the old Velamsund estate and a swimming spot at its northern end.
Ortnamnen här har bytt skepnad flera gån: The place names here have changed shape several times. Before 2010, Statistics Sweden called the settlement of Röset and Pusta, on the north side of Lake Landvettersjön, Bårhult. And Landvetters-Kärret got its prefix only so as not to be confused with another Kärret in the same municipality. Nowadays both areas count as part of the town of Landvetter.
Ovanför Vårberg reser sig Vårbergstoppen: Above Vårberg rises Vårbergstoppen, known locally as Tippen, the Tip, an artificial hill built between 1965 and 1982 that reaches 90 metres above sea level. Don't confuse it with its neighbour Vikingaberget, which at just over 77 metres is Stockholm's highest natural point! Right nearby is the Kummelholmen art gallery, named after the building's property designation.
Ovanför gatan reser sig Stadshagsberget,: Above the street rises Stadshagsberget, Kungsholmen's highest natural point at 52 metres above sea level. From the top you can look out over Karlberg Palace, where the Karlberg Military Academy is the world's oldest military academy still in the same place and the same building. By Lake Karlbergssjön on the other side, Rörstrand porcelain was once made – a brand dating from 1726 and Europe's second-oldest porcelain brand after Meissen.
Ovanför oss reser sig Ramberget med Keil: Above us rises Ramberget hill with Keillers park. From the top you have one of the best views over Gothenburg and the river. It's a steep but short walk up.
Ovanpå Guldhedens vattentorn, med sina v: On top of the Guldheden water tower, with its arches and yellow brick, there was once a café for 40 guests, which opened in 1953. Since 2020 the tower has been a protected site and is closed to the public. A little further away stands Hästen, 'the Horse', a two-metre-tall teak horse by Ivar Lindekrantz from 1956, built using boatbuilding techniques, rather like a barrel.
Paddan, båttur på kanalerna: Paddan, boat tour on the canals
Park-Bio i Örby Folkets hus invigdes 192: Park-Bio in Örby Folkets hus, the community hall, opened in 1928 and showed films until 1968, and since 2021 film screenings have been held in the building again. Nearby is Park Studios, where Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander, among others, recorded during the 1990s, and which the band Kent owned between 2004 and 2016. And Örby Castle? Since the 1970s it has been let to the Embassy of Vietnam.
Parken här är kärnan i det som en gång v: The park here is the heart of what was once Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built from 1905 to 1910 to designs by Gustaf Wickman and closed in 1997. The distinctive buildings Stora Mans and Stora Kvinns, the large men's and women's wards, still stand in the park. And the old chief physician's residence? It has become Långbro värdshus, an inn.
Partille kan verka som en ren förort, me: Partille may seem like a pure suburb, but no less than 60 per cent of the municipality is protected nature. It is small in area but mid-sized in population, and its main town has long since grown together with Gothenburg. The municipality is made up of four parts: Partille, Sävedalen, Öjersjö and Jonsered.
Patent- och registreringsverkets hus: The Swedish Patent and Registration Office building
Pendeltågen stannar vid Huddinge centrum: The commuter trains stop at Huddinge centrum, the heart and shopping centre of the municipality. Along Kommunalvägen, which runs almost parallel to the tracks of the Western Main Line for about 1.3 kilometres, you'll find both Huddinge church and the municipal hall. Nearby are also traces of the Svartlösa judicial district, whose courthouse was designed in 1959 by the architect Karl Karlström – the district lasted only twelve years and was dissolved in the court reform of 1971.
Per Anders Fogelström skildrade det gaml: Per Anders Fogelström portrayed the old factory area of Barnängen by Hammarby sjö in his novel Vävarnas barn, 'Children of the Weavers', and this is where the Hammarby IF sports club has its roots. Barnängsparken runs down to the quay, with lawns and a ferry jetty facing Hammarby sjöstad. A little further away is the Toy Museum, where the collections range from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars.
Peter Celsing ritade Filmhuset åt Svensk: Peter Celsing designed Filmhuset, the Film House, for the Swedish Film Institute, and it opened in 1971. The Film Institute, which among other things presents the Guldbagge awards, Sweden's film prizes, is run from here. A stone's throw away, on Hakberget hill, stands the sculpture Protest from 1986: three blocks of red granite, the middle one shaped like a clenched fist. The spot was the destination of the labour movement's May Day marches from 1890 to 1965. And right next to it is a military heliport without any special infrastructure.
Pilgrimskapellet är ett träkapell helt u: Pilgrimskapellet, the Pilgrim Chapel, is a wooden chapel with no religious symbols at all, consecrated in 1977 by Bishop Ingmar Ström. Both the chapel and the cemetery around it were designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg, and together they make up Järfälla's entire burial ground. The graves lie both in open fields and in the forest, and a 300-metre waterway with eleven waterfalls leads down to a large reflecting pond.
Pixbo ligger vid Rådasjön, en sjö som är: Pixbo lies on Rådasjön, a lake that is 23 metres deep and also a drinking water source for Mölndal municipality. The Mölndalsån river flows through the lake and further downstream changes its name to Gullbergsån. Pixbo itself is built on and around the Björnåsen hill, so there are plenty of slopes.
Pixbo är ett bostadsområde där man får g: Pixbo is a residential area where you get fit for free, because it is built on and around the Björnåsen height and is very hilly. The area lies on the south side of Lake Rådasjön and has its own postal town. To the south-east, little Lake Vällsjön forms a border, and to the east flows the Vällbäcken stream.
Platsen bär namnet Wieselgren, och enlig: The square bears the name Wieselgren, and according to Gothenburg City Museum it refers to Peter Wieselgren and his son Sigfrid. Peter became dean of Gothenburg and is regarded as a pioneer of the Swedish temperance movement. His followers promised to give up brännvin, Swedish schnapps, but beer and wine were allowed. The square is in Rambergsstaden, below the hill Ramberget.
Platsen har fått namn efter Frantz Zinck: The place is named after Frantz Zinck, who lived on the farm for only five years in the 17th century and never formally owned it. Yet the name lives on. The neighbourhood also has food memories: at Brännkyrkagatan 93 was the restaurant Gässlingen, which got a Michelin star in 1999. The children's hospital Samariten was expanded thanks to money that the singer Jenny Lind left in her will.
Polhemsplatsen fick 1883 sitt namn efter: Polhemsplatsen got its name in 1883, after the inventor Christopher Polhem. Here stands the GP building, which the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten moved into in 1935 and which is still the main building of the Stampen media group. A stone's throw away is the statue of footballer Gunnar Gren, one of the Gre-No-Li trio and one of Gothenburg's most successful footballers of the 20th century.
Precis här intill, vid Stensjön, låg Mus: Right here, by Lake Stensjön, Mustad's margarine factory operated between 1897 and 1960. A little way from here is Kristinedal, a small-house area completed in 1964 with about a hundred villas, terraced houses and linked houses. It was built by Skånska Cementgjuteriet to designs from Malmö, in the ideal of the time with single-storey houses and brick facades.
Precis intill doftar det jul året om. Gö: Right next door it smells of Christmas all year round. Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, was established in 1924 and nowadays bakes just one thing: gingerbread biscuits with a hint of citrus, to a secret recipe. The shop on Sankt Sigfridsgatan has its original interior from 1940, and the bakery has received a diploma from the Gastronomic Academy for its unrivalled gingerbread.
Precis intill ligger Skändla sörgård, en: Right next door is Skändla sörgård, a typical Hisingen farm from the early 1800s and one of the best-preserved farm complexes in the Gothenburg area. The City of Gothenburg bought the farm in 1966 to save it, and today it is a listed building rented by the Tuve local heritage and antiquities society. A little further away rises the Bronze Age cairn Skändla rös.
Precis intill står Villa Brevik, byggd 1: Right next door stands Villa Brevik, built in 1920 for the district judge Franz Stolt and designed by Jacob Gate. For many years the housing cooperative HSB held its internal courses here, and the facade is protected so that it may not be altered. A short way off is Abeniuska villan from 1910, designed by Ferdinand Boberg and Bror Almquist and classed as culturally and historically irreplaceable.
Precis vid korsningen mellan Vårby allé: Right at the crossing of Vårby allé and Mogårdsvägen stood Vårby grindstuga, the gate cottage, a croft belonging to the Vårby gård manor estate since 1689. At first craftsmen lived here, and the last crofter was Johannes Larsson with his wife Eva Charlotta. The cottage was demolished around 1970. A little further away, a milestone marks the spot where Vårby School stood between 1901 and 1942.
Prins Bertil invigde Skärholmens centrum: Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen Centre on 8 September 1968. It was planned as a regional shopping centre for 250,000 people in southern Greater Stockholm and is still counted among Sweden's largest shopping centres. The centre was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, and is included in the SOS Brutalism database of brutalist concrete architecture.

Promenera till parken och badplatsen Sva: Walk to Svandammen, the park and bathing spot
Promenera till runstenarna i folkhögskol: Walk to the runestones in the folk high school's park
