Prova curling i Göteborgs Curlinghall: Try curling at Göteborgs Curlinghall, the Gothenburg curling hall
Pucken är i centrum här: på Björkängens: The puck is at the centre of things here: Björkängen sports ground has a football pitch and two ice rinks, and Björkängshallen is the home rink of the ice hockey team Huddinge IK. The B rink used to be known as Nickehallen, after one of the club's key figures, Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. A little further away is Kvarnberget, where Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood.
På 1880-talet skulle här byggas en roman: In the 1880s a romantic villa town, Hornsbergs villastad, was to be built here, but the project was a total fiasco: the company failed to sell a single plot. What remains of the dream are a few block names and Nelly Sachs park, formerly called Hornsbergsparken. Today Lindhagsskrapan rises here instead, by Lake Ulvsundasjön, 78 metres tall with 24 floors. Nearby Hornsbergs hage was once a gathering place for the workers of Kungsholmen.
På 1930-talet var Långbrodalsvägen centr: In the 1930s, Långbrodalsvägen was the main street of what was then the district of Långbrodal, with bustling commercial life. When the shopping area at Kungens kurva was established, the bustle moved there. Right next door is Linboda, one of the earliest owner-built housing areas in Långbro, where a hundred properties were once numbered from one to a hundred. Today fewer than twenty or so of the original houses remain.
På Björkängens idrottsplats, en kort pro: At Björkängen sports ground, a short walk away, the ice hockey team Huddinge IK plays in Björkängshallen. One of the rinks used to be known as Nickehallen, named after the club's strongman Bengt "Nicke" Nilsson. In the other direction, Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, and that's what gave the Kvarnbergsplan area its name.
På Byfogdegatan 3 ligger Nostalgicum, et: At Byfogdegatan 3 is Nostalgicum, a museum about the 1950s and 1960s that opened in 2009. The exhibition shows both everyday life and major events: modern homes were built, industry was running at full speed and needed labour immigration. Out in the world, the civil rights movement grew in the USA, the Berlin Wall was built and there was an uprising in Hungary.
På Hallunda tunnelbanestation, några min: At Hallunda metro station, a few minutes from here, a neon loop and rods of Plexiglas glow – the artist Kazuko Tamura's work from 1993. In the other direction, on Sankt Botvids väg, stands Botkyrka's oldest school building, the church school from 1849, still used as an annex to Botkyrka Free School. It belongs to the old church setting that was once the centre of Botkyrka parish.
På Kaggeledstorget en bit härifrån står: On Kaggeledstorget, a little way from here, stands Våren, Spring, a bronze sculpture by Eric Grate from 1944 depicting a naked woman on a granite plinth. It was put in place in 1950 and was bought together with its sister statue Sommaren, Summer. Another copy is in Museiparken in Alingsås. The square got its name in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg.
På Kikås, den höga åsen vid Stensjöns sö: On Kikås, the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, is Sweden's largest freestanding insect hotel. A little way from here is Lake Södra Långevattnet, a full 13.5 metres deep and surrounded by wooded ridges. The fish in the lake have been stocked, and the water flows on northwards towards Stensjön and the Mölndalsån river.
På Krällingegränd 3 ligger Järvabadet, e: At Krällingegränd 3 is Järvabadet, an outdoor pool that opened on 12 June 2020 and the following year was one of the finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year. Right next door is Eggeby gård, a farm where people have lived and worked the land ever since the Viking Age. The runestone U 69, the Eggeby Stone, also stands at the farm, and today Järva Folkets Park runs cultural activities here.
På Måndalshöjden en bit härifrån ligger: On Måndalshöjden, a little way from here, lies Måndalsfortet, a fort whose construction began in 1903. It was part of the Southern Front, which together with the Northern Front, also called the Sausage Line, was an important part of Stockholm's fixed defences until 1952. The fort is counted among the best preserved. Closer to the stop is Trollbäckens IP, a sports ground with an ice rink, an athletics track and three football pitches.
På Narvavägen 7, runt hörnet, låg först: At Narvavägen 7, round the corner, there was first the Narva cinema and then a theatre with an unusual pair of owners: the actor Sture Lagerwall and the businessman Oscar Lindgren, who was also consul general for Haiti. They renamed the venue Alléteatern and staged light comedies there between 1951 and 1957. In the building at Strandvägen 45 lived several generations of the von Platen family.
På Nyängsvägen 155 bodde makarna Alva oc: At Nyängsvägen 155 lived the couple Alva and Gunnar Myrdal, in a villa that Sven Markelius designed in 1937 in his typical functionalist style. The neighbourhood also has a down-to-earth history: the Stora Mossen allotment gardens began to be laid out during the First World War, so that the allotment holders could grow their own root vegetables during the hard war years.
På Ringön en bit härifrån ligger Vagnhal: On Ringön, a little way from here, is Vagnhallen Ringön, where Gothenburg's trams sleep. The first stage opened at the turn of May and June 2020, with covered parking. Today there's room for about 30 trams, and when the depot is extended there'll be room for about 70 more. Nearby is Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen, the public transport hub of southeastern Hisingen.
På Råsundavägen 45 låg en gång biografen: At Råsundavägen 45 there was once a cinema called the Savoy. In 1974 the auditorium became the Marcus Music recording studio, according to Studio Sound magazine the first in Sweden with a 24-track tape recorder. Abba recorded most of The Album here in 1977. Today the studio is called Soundtrade Studios, and over the years artists such as Robyn and Joey Tempest have recorded here.
På Sandhamnsgatan står ett kontorshus fr: On Sandhamnsgatan stands an office building from 1961 that was once Preem's headquarters. Between 2009 and 2011 it was converted into homes, and it also got a row of terraced houses placed on its roof. A little further away is 79&Park, designed by the Danish firm Bjarke Ingels Group, and Kampementsbadet, a municipal outdoor pool. The pool opened in 1962, and the low entrance building was designed by the city's head gardener, Holger Blom.
På Sundby gård en bit härifrån finns Lit: At Sundby gård, a farm a little way from here, is the Lithographic Museum, the only museum of its kind in Sweden, entirely devoted to the art of printing from stone. Just south of the farm is Sundbyfortet, also called the Eagle's Nest, by the southern bay of Lake Orlången. The fort was part of the Southern Front, built around the First World War to protect Stockholm from attacks from the south.
På Surbrunnsgatan ligger Norra Brunn, so: On Surbrunnsgatan is Norra Brunn, which opened as an inn in 1903 and today is a stand-up comedy venue. During the 1900s the place was called, among other things, Zum Alten Brunnen and Old Bowler. On the corner of Birger Jarlsgatan and Odengatan stands Sankt Georgios katedral, St George's Cathedral, built for the Catholic Apostolic Church and now Greek Orthodox. The inn Clas på Hörnet dates back to the 1700s.
På Teknologgatan en bit härifrån låg Thö: On Teknologgatan, a little way from here, was Thörnströms Kök, which Anne and Håkan Thörnström ran from 1997. From 2011 until it closed in 2021, the restaurant had a star in the Michelin Guide. Underground, the trams climb through the Chalmers tunnel, 1,050 metres long with a gradient of 24 per mille.
På Torshamnsgatan 21–23 ligger Isafjord: At Torshamnsgatan 21 to 23 is Isafjord 1, the block where Ericsson has its headquarters. The office complex was designed by Wingårdh Architects and was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2013. A stone's throw away is Kistamässan, the Kista exhibition centre, which opened in September 2008 and is built together with the hotel skyscraper Victoria Tower.
På Tunberget en bit bort står Tunbergsre: On Tunberget hill, a little way off, stands the Tunberg reservoir, a water tower completed in 1973 that holds 25,000 cubic metres of drinking water. Closer by is the Häggvik tunnel, the shortest of the Norrortsleden road's three tunnels, opened in 1998. It's only 289 metres long, and a park has been laid out on its roof.
På Vasagatan 7 låg krogen Tre Remmare, m: At Vasagatan 7 was the restaurant Tre Remmare, with a casino and nightclub in the same premises. It was one of the few in Stockholm allowed to stay open until five in the morning, and it became notorious for drunkenness and drug abuse. In 2007 it lost its licence and closed. Today the Bishops Arms pub is in the premises. Opposite stands the World Trade Center, designed by Ralph Erskine.
På en 45 meter hög bergknalle, en kort p: On a 45-metre-high rocky knoll, a short walk from here, stood Skärholmen's hillfort, from the Migration Period and the Viking Age. The location was strategic, close to the ancient shipping lane to Helgö and Birka. The rock drops steeply towards Lake Mälaren, and on the flatter inland side there are still remains of a wall of large boulders piled on top of each other.
På en av Äppelvikens högsta punkter, ett: On one of Äppelviken's highest points, a stone's throw from here, Västerled Church presides over villas from the 1920s and 1930s. Stora mossen is part of the Old Bromma garden city, and almost two thirds of the houses are villas. Nearby Bromma Upper Secondary School is a so-called World Heritage school, working with its nearest World Heritage Site, Drottningholm Palace.
På en berghäll i Skylsta, en bit härifrå: On a rock slab at Skylsta, a little way from here, is a Viking Age rune carving, 1.7 metres long and 0.85 metres wide, with runes six centimetres high. According to Richard Dybeck there was also a runestone fragment on the same hill, but it has never been found again. A little rune mystery at the edge of the forest.
På en berghäll vid Drottningholmsvägen f: On a rock slab by Drottningholmsvägen there are two rune carvings from the 11th century. They were discovered by chance in 1904, when someone was out picking berries. For centuries they had lain under soil and moss, which is why they are still well preserved. One of them says that Sigvid and Sigrev had the stone carved in memory of their father Sinar.
På en höjd med utsikt över Säveåns dalgå: On a hill overlooking the Säveån river valley stands Partille Manor, Partille herrgård, popularly known as the Castle. It is a little way from here, about 200 metres west of Partille Church, and you reach it via Carl Wilhelm Carlbergs Allé. Since December 1995 the manor has been a listed building.
På en kulle alldeles intill står Burås k: On a hill right next to here stands Burås kvarn, a three-storey windmill built in 1892 to 1893 by the master builder Emanuel Andréasson. The wind has been put to work here for a long time, because there have been windmills on the same spot ever since the 18th century. Since 2004 the mill has been a listed building, a landmark in south-western Kungälv municipality.
På en liten kulle i kvarteret Grimhild s: On a small hill in the Grimhild block stands the Ekeby water tower, designed by Axel Bergman and built in 1908. The tank was drained in 1965, and since 1995 the tower has been a private home – a rather unusual address. Below it lies Lake Ekebysjön, only three metres deep, in the middle of a nature reserve with wooded meadows and swamp forest of black alder.
På en numera skogbeväxt kulle, kallad Kv: On a now wooded hill called Kvarnbacken, Mill Hill, there once stood two windmills with lovely names: Stora Stampan and Holländskan, the Big Stamp and the Dutch Lady. Together they were called the Rinkeby mills, after the village of Rinkeby in Spånga parish, on whose land they stood. Today only the western one, Stora Stampan, remains, just a couple of minutes' walk from here.
På en trädbevuxen kulle söder om Ekerövä: On a wooded hill south of Ekerövägen rests the Wallenberg family. The mausoleum has become a landmark for the whole area. Lindö, by the way, was once an island of its own, but land uplift has made it bigger and joined it to Lovön. At Tappström, bricks were fired at the Tappsund brickworks right up until 1959.
På ett hustak i Råcksta centrum lyser en: On a rooftop in Råcksta centre glows a neon sign from the 1950s, with RÅCKSTA in green and a jaunty Centrum in yellow. It was restored in 2011 and now shines in its former glory. The nearby metro depot was originally called Spångahallen, because Vällingby lay in Spånga municipality, which had become part of Stockholm just a few years earlier. And Råcksta cemetery holds around 30,000 urn graves.
På höjden alldeles i närheten fanns unde: On the hill right nearby, during the emergency years of 1939 to 1945, stood the Skanskvarn anti-aircraft position, with trenches, gun emplacements and tank obstacles. Its task was to protect the Skansbron and Skanstullsbron bridges and the important railway bridge Årstabron, and had the defence collapsed, the plan was to blow up Årstabron before the enemy could use it. Below lies an allotment garden established as early as 1917 under the name Koloniföreningen Stugan.
På nordöstra Lidingö, norr om Hustegafjä: On north-eastern Lidingö, north of Hustegafjärden bay, lies the small village of Furutorp. Nearby is Långnäs gård, a privately owned farm that originated as a larger farmstead from the mid-14th century, and the Sjövik housing area, on a strip of shore along Kyrkviken bay that was excluded from the Långängen-Elfvik nature reserve.
På slottsområdet står en stuga som har v: In the palace grounds stands a cottage that has been to a World's Fair! The Ornäs cottage is a slightly smaller copy of the Ornäs cottage in Ornäs in Dalarna; it was shown at the 1867 World's Fair in Paris and has stood here since 1869. The neighbourhood also has villas with funny names, like Villa Snörin, pronounced 'snör-in'.
På torget står Vesslan, en fontänskulptu: On the square stands Vesslan, the Weasel, a fountain sculpture from 1912 by Otto Strandman. A naked bronze youth has just caught sight of a weasel hiding in a grotto at the very bottom of the sculpture, and on each side is a drinking fountain. Around the corner, at Scheelegatan 8, was the restaurant L'Escargot, which in 1984 became one of the first four in Sweden to be awarded a Michelin star.
På tunnelbanestationen står ett exemplar: In the metro station stands a copy of Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's sculpture The Knotted Gun. The most famous copy stands outside the UN headquarters in New York. A couple of hundred metres away is Fittja farm, whose inn in the 17th and 18th centuries was one of the largest coaching inns in Sweden, and where one of the buildings served as a courthouse right up until 1916. Today the Multicultural Centre runs its activities at the farm.
Radhus och villor präglar Kälvesta, en s: Terraced houses and villas characterise Kälvesta, a district in the north-western corner of Hässelby-Vällingby that acts a bit like a border guard. To the north lies Skälby in Järfälla Municipality, to the west Hässelby Villastad and to the south-west Vinsta. The neighbour Vinsta, by the way, is named after an old village of the same name, and only became a district in 1953.
Radhusbyn Atlantisområdet byggdes 1952–1: The terraced housing village of Atlantisområdet was built in 1952–1955 to designs by Bertil Karlén, Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist and drew international attention. Lisbeth and Olof Palme lived in one of the terraced houses with their three sons between 1968 and 1983. Today the houses have the City Museum's blue rating, the highest class, for their exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Radhusen i kvarteret Tegen: The terraced houses in the Tegen block
Radhusområdet Hersby Åker byggdes 1949–1: The terraced-house area Hersby Åker was built in 1949–1955 to designs by Holger Blom: thirteen rows of terraced houses with 115 homes in total, a fine example of Swedish folkhem, 'people's home', welfare-state architecture after the Second World War. A little way off, Hersby farm storehouse stands on a small hill, a listed building that belonged to Hersby gård, one of Lidingö's so-called main farms.
Radiotorget i närheten var något helt ny: Radiotorget nearby was something completely new when it opened in 1954. It was a so-called satellite square, a square outside the city centre on an American model, the first of its kind in Sweden and one of the first in Europe. The square was renovated from 2019 to 2020 and still has several small shops.
Radiotorget, några hundra meter bort, in: Radiotorget, a few hundred metres away, opened in 1954 as Sweden's first satellite square, a shopping centre on the American model. A little further off is Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined between 1945 and the late 1950s. Rare minerals such as monazite and bismuthinite have also been found there.
Rakt fram ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges äl: Straight ahead is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
Rakt fram ligger Skansen Lejonet, en för: Straight ahead is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Fort, a 17th-century defensive fort with a gilded lion on top.
Rakt fram ser du den röd-vita skyskrapan: Straight ahead you can see the red and white skyscraper that the people of Gothenburg call the Lipstick.
Rakt under Östasiatiska museet finns ett: Right under the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities is a rock cavern blasted out in the early 1940s for the naval commander and his staff in wartime. Today it houses Stockholm Toy Museum, with toys and comics. Next to it is Högvakten, the Main Guard building, built in 1777, and the former Skeppsholmen Church, now the concert venue Eric Ericsonhallen, with a seven-metre-high tapestry called Havets sång, Song of the Sea.
Rannebergen Centrum byggdes 1974 och har: Rannebergen Centrum was built in 1974 and has a swimming pool, and on the other side of the street the Bohusleden trail and the Vättlefjäll hills await, with fine waters for swimming and fishing. Nearby also begins the Lärjeån valley nature reserve, which was protected in 2026 and covers more than 1,100 hectares.
Rannebergen ligger högt och nära naturen: Rannebergen sits high up and close to nature. Just a few minutes away is the forest lake Idtjärnet, 109 metres above sea level, and a little further off Lake Stora Mölnesjön, with a swimming spot and jetty. The centre itself, with a swimming pool and a pizzeria, was built in 1974 and has the Bohusleden trail and Vättlefjäll hills right on its doorstep.
Redan innan Stadion fanns idrottade stoc: Even before Stadion, the Olympic stadium, Stockholmers did sport here. Stockholms idrottspark opened in 1896 and was the city's first civilian sports arena. It had a 400-metre cement track for cycling and running and was demolished in 1910. Along Valhallavägen stand blue-marked 1880s houses in Villastaden.
Redaren Jacob Gustaf Setterwall gjorde s: The shipowner Jacob Gustaf Setterwall was highly successful, and in 1896 he had a magnificent patrician villa built in Finntorp, today one of the oldest buildings in Nacka. A little further away, by the bay of Svindersviken, is Svindersvik, a summer retreat from the mid-18th century designed by Carl Hårleman for the merchant Claes Grill. It is considered one of Sweden's best-preserved Rococo estates, partly because no one has ever lived there all year round.
Redaren Jacob Gustaf Setterwall köpte 18: In 1871 the shipowner Jacob Gustaf Setterwall bought the land between Kyrkviken and Svindersviken bays and first built a small Swiss-style wooden villa as a summer home. After great success for the shipping company, things got grander: in 1896 the lavish Setterwall villa was finished, designed by Johan Laurentz. On the Nysätra headland a little further away was the Nackanäs inn, which welcomed guests right up until it burned down in 1960.
Redbergsplatsen hette förr Korsvägen och: Redbergsplatsen square used to be called Korsvägen and got its current name in 1883. In 1873 a public water pump was set up here, where people could enjoy water from Lake Delsjön. Just north of the square, in Redbergslids Folkpark, a people's park, a pavilion with a stage for performers went up in 1886. Below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, stands the bronze fountain group Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements, moved here from Olskrokstorget in 1968.
Reenstiernska palatset, även kallat Momm: The Reenstierna Palace, also called Momma's House, was built in the 1660s and retains much of its original appearance, a fine example of how Dutch immigrants influenced Stockholm's architecture. Right next to it stood Södra barnbördshuset, the city's maternity hospital, and Maria Hospital, which opened in 1876. The hospital started with 125 beds in an old 18th-century factory building, which has today been converted into flats and a preschool.
Riddarfjärden är Mälarens östligaste fjä: Riddarfjärden is the easternmost bay of Lake Mälaren, and the border between the provinces of Uppland and Södermanland actually runs through the middle span of the Västerbron bridge. On the Kungsholmen shore, Mälarbadet opened in 1906, at the time Scandinavia's largest and most exclusive indoor baths, with pools under large skylights. The street names in the area recall the tanners who worked here, such as Garvar Lundins gränd, named after the tannery owner Anders Wilhelm Lundin.
Riddarholmen och utsikten över Riddarfjä: Riddarholmen and the view over Riddarfjärden bay
Rinkeby i Danderyd ska inte förväxlas me: Rinkeby in Danderyd should not be confused with the district of Rinkeby in northern Stockholm; this one is an old farm and a housing area. There was once a Viking Age runestone fragment here, U 132, but it vanished without trace in the second half of the 1800s. Nobody knows where it went.
Rinkeby är äldre än många tror. Byn omta: Rinkeby is older than many people think. The village is mentioned as early as 1347 and then consisted of several farms. Modern Rinkeby was built from 1968 onwards, during the so-called Million Programme, Sweden's large-scale housing drive. At Rinkebytorget square there's now a small shopping centre and Folkets hus, the community hall, and you can buy things like fruit and vegetables there.
Rissne är den enda tunnelbanestationen i: Rissne is the only metro station in Stockholm that has its name carved in runes. The name also appears on a runestone in Sigtuna, raised in memory of "Gunnar's son in Risnö". In 1640 Rissne gård was bought by Reinhold Goevert Leuhusen, secretary of the Admiralty board. Today Rissne gård is a restaurant and conference venue.
Ritorp anlades redan på 1600-talet som e: Ritorp was established as early as the 1600s as a croft under the village of Nederjärva, just south of the country road to Enköping, and today's farmhouse dates from the 1770s. The house is a private home, but Stockholm County Museum calls it irreplaceable. Two thousand years ago the site was under water: the bay of Fröfjärden then linked the Baltic waters of Saltsjön with Lake Mälaren, and the shoreline of Brunnsviken was about ten metres higher than today.
Ritorp började som ett torp på 1600-tale: Ritorp began as a croft in the 17th century, and the current farmhouse from the 1770s is described by the Stockholm County Museum as indispensable. All around are buildings with charming nicknames: the Tower Villa from 1903, the Majhill house from 1911 and the Horseshoe Stable from 1929, which was moved in 1993. In the northern part you'll notice the so-called Rödingarna, the Red Ones.
Roslags Näsby är Roslagsbanans stora väg: Roslags Näsby is the big junction of the Roslagsbanan railway: here the lines split towards Kårsta, formerly Rimbo, and towards Österskär. The station has two island platforms reached by a footbridge over the tracks. A little way off is Kvarntorpshällen, a rune-inscribed rock that the writer Jan Fridegård discovered in 1943 while living in Täby. It contains the unusual word styvsöner, stepsons.
Roslagsbanan nådde Lahäll 1928, när linj: Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, reached Lahäll in 1928, when the line from Altorp opened, and in 1937 it was extended to Näsbypark. A little further away, by Näsbyviken bay, is Näsby Castle, today a conference hotel with a restaurant. And to the south, in Djursholm, is the Svalnäs burial ground, with graves from around the year 500 to 1000, one of Danderyd's largest and most impressive burial grounds.
Roslagsbanan nådde hit 1937, när Stockho: The Roslagsbanan railway reached here in 1937, when Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where that branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive residential areas, with villas and terraced houses near the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right next to the station is Näsbypark Church, which belongs to Täby parish.
Rudboda har fått sitt namn efter Rudboda: Rudboda is named after Rudboda gård, a farm mentioned in writing as early as 1381. The area includes the Lojo block, built during the Million Programme housing drive in 1970–1973 but described by the municipality as a higher-quality, smaller-scale version. Out on Bosön there is a student campus from 1998–1999 that was meant to show what the Olympic Village could have looked like for the 2004 Summer Games, which Stockholm bid for but did not get.

Rudboda is named after Rudboda farm, which is mentioned in writing as early as 1381. The Lojo block was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, between 1970 and 1973, and the municipality calls it an excellent example of a more small-scale application of the Million Programme's ideology. On Bosön, student flats were built to show what an Olympic village could look like, ahead of the 2004 Summer Games that Stockholm never got.

Runhällarna vid Sundby: The runic rock slabs at Sundby
Runstenen U 88 i Skälby, en bit härifrån: The runestone U 88 in Skälby, a little way from here, has had a colourful life. For at least part of the 19th century it was used as a doorstep in Lindal, so people stepped over the Vikings' text every day. Then it was gone for a while, until it was found in 1938 at Skälby Farm, lying on a burial mound. Now it stands next to its companion, U 89.
Runstenen vid slottets infart: The runestone at the palace entrance
Runt 14 000 studenter läser vid Södertör: Around 14,000 students study at Södertörn University, which offers, among other things, police training and teacher training with an intercultural profile. Much of the research is about the Baltic Sea and Eastern Europe, supported by the Foundation for Baltic and East European Studies, Östersjöstiftelsen, which the government set up in 1994. The library is open to everyone, and right next to it is Flemingsberg Park, which won Huddinge's building award in 2021.
Runt Järfälla kyrka har runstenar kommit: Around Järfälla Church, runestones have come and gone. In 1728 Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone inside the church, probably used as a step, which then disappeared until seven fragments turned up in 1939. Another stone lay outside the porch door and was already described back then as lost and worn, and it's still missing today. Next door is Kyrkbyn, the church village, which used to be called Järfälla gård.
Runt Rådasjön breder ett naturreservat u: Around Lake Rådasjön stretches a nature reserve with pastures, broadleaf woodland and biologically rich alder swamp forest. The area around Mölnlycke is known for its huge numbers of wood anemones, so in spring the ground turns white. By the lake is also Råda säteri, a manor with wings and farm buildings, listed since 1969.
Runt hörnet ligger kvarteren Kampö och H: Around the corner are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, terraced houses from the late 1950s that the City Museum has marked green as especially valuable. A little way off rise the administrative buildings of Televerket, the old national telecoms agency, which until 2016 were the headquarters of Telia Company. They were designed by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan were awarded the Kasper Salin Prize.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970 och är hjärtat i: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe, like Tellusgatan. On the square is the Bergsjön Culture House, Kulturhuset Bergsjön, with a library, café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. It offers everything from music and art to crafts and children's events.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970, och gatunamnen: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970, and the street names around it follow the space theme, like Tellusgatan and Merkuriusgatan. By the square is the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, music studio, studios and exhibition hall. It offers a mix of concerts, crafts and children's programmes.
Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Uni: Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan and Meteorgatan: Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön the street names come from outer space. A little way from here is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, with Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, and offers everything from music and art to children's events.
Rådsparken, alldeles i närheten, har båd: Rådsparken park, right nearby, has both an animal park and a sports ground, next to Huddinge Church, which has been the parish church ever since the Middle Ages. A runestone fragment is walled into the church's outer wall, and just east of the church was the assembly site Tomtabergh, mentioned as early as 1433. The church school nearby, opened in 1914, was threatened with demolition in the 1950s but is still standing – today the parish choirs rehearse there.
Rågsved är en stadsdel med två ansikten,: Rågsved is a district with two faces, split down the middle by the metro. On one side is the iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre, and on the other the buildings rise up on a hill. The station opened in 1959 and is about 8.5 kilometres from Slussen.
Rågsved är känt för sin ikoniska hästsko: Rågsved is known for its iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre, and the metro station was a terminus when it opened in 1959. On the platform stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Green Bird, by the artist Björn Selder. A little further away in Högdalen is Cyklopen, a self-managed cultural centre run entirely by volunteers. The first building burned down in 2008 in an arson attack by suspected Nazis, but the association built a new one.
Råsunda vattentorn, ritat av Sigge Crons: The Råsunda water tower, designed by Sigge Cronstedt, opened in 1910 and went out of use in the early 1950s. Since 1994 people have lived in the tower, which has been converted into flats. On a hilltop by Näckrosparken, the Water Lily Park, stands Råsunda Church, and on the southern side of Lake Råstasjön is Råstahällen, Solna's only natural monument, where you can see three crossing sets of glacial striations from the last Ice Age.

Rösjön är en avlång sjö, 7,3 meter djup,: Rösjön is an elongated lake, 7.3 metres deep, most of which belongs to Sollentuna while a smaller part belongs to Danderyd. Täby, right next door on the eastern side, has no shoreline on it at all. A little further away, Landsnoravägen, about three kilometres long, runs past Edsberg Palace and Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Salems centrala bebyggelse hette förr Sa: Salem's central built-up area used to be called Salemstaden. For a long time the area was crofting land under the Fågelsta farm. One of the crofts, Bergfana, was built in the late 1840s, and the first to move in was the estate labourer and former soldier Eric Ode and his family. When the railway arrived in 1860, Bergfana became one of four track keepers' cottages in Salem.
Salems kyrka står på en udde söder om Bo: Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, surrounded by large oaks, limes and birches. Gamla Södertäljevägen, the old Södertälje road, runs past the church, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. If you follow the road east, you come to Sankt Botvid's spring, a cold-water spring at the south-eastern tip of Bornsjön. About fifty metres from the spring stands the old Söderby runestone.
Saltsjö-Järla station invigdes 1894 unde: Saltsjö-Järla station opened in 1894 under the old-fashioned name Jerla, and branch lines once ran from the station to both a yeast factory and De Laval's steam turbine factory. Today the old industrial buildings by Lake Järlasjön have become Järla sjö, with around 700 homes, shops, restaurants and about 1,200 workplaces. In 2004 the area received the Urban Environment Council's award for having improved the townscape.
The Saltsjöbanan railway's station here opened in 1894. During the construction of the new Slussen, Henriksdal was the line's inner terminus from 2016 until the end of 2022. Since 2023, large parts of the line have been closed, and the section to Slussen is expected to reopen in 2028 at the earliest. At Danvikstull there was once the Klippan summer theatre, where audiences laughed at John Elfström and Arthur Fischer.
Saltsjöbanans station invigdes 1894, då: The Saltsjöbanan railway station opened in 1894, then spelled Jerla. From here, sidings ran to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine factory. Fun detail: Anna Book was a pupil at Nacka music school when she sang "ABC" in Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection, in 1986. From 2030 you'll be able to change to the metro's blue line at a new station here.
Sandbäck är ingen ny plats. Redan på 155: Sandbäck is no new place. As early as the 1550s, more than four hundred years ago, the area consisted of two homesteads. Today it lies in the south-western part of Östra Mölndal, and a little way off is the Pepparred nature reserve, with old pastureland and broadleaf trees, protected since 1925.
Sandås ligger i Askim, och namnet Askim: Sandås is in Askim, and the name Askim is actually pronounced "Ashim". The parish has medieval origins. To the south, Sandås borders Skintebo, a coastal residential area that was farmland until the 1970s, with car-free footpaths, boatman's cottages and, more unexpectedly, a copy of the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm.
Sankt Olofs kyrka, en kort bit bort, hör: St Olof's Church, a short way off, belongs to Täby parish. Through the neighbouring district of Hägernäs runs the E18 motorway, completed in 1957 on the Danderyd–Ullna stretch, which cuts right through the area. A bit further north is Rönninge, with no built-up areas at all, with the Rönninge by-Skavlöten nature reserve and the Skavlöten outdoor recreation area.
Sankt Pauli kyrka: St Paul's Church, Sankt Pauli kyrka
Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka alldeles i: The Church of Saint Paul of the Cross, right next door, is the Catholic parish church in Angered. A short walk away stands Alexander Calder's steel sculpture The Three Wings, which spent twelve years on Götaplatsen before it was finally allowed to come to Angered in 1979. Since 2013 it has stood on an open lawn in the town park.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka: St Sigfrid's Church, Sankt Sigfrids kyrka
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en riktig flyttf: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka is a real bird of passage: the red wooden church first stood in Vasastaden and was moved here in 1904, then under the name Sankt Stefans kapell. As a movable small church it resembles the prefabricated timber villas of the time, and since 1993 it has been a listed building. A little further along Hägerstensvägen is the Aspen cinema, which when it opened in 1952 was the first private cinema in Stockholm since 1943.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes 1960–1962: Saint Birgitta's Church was built in 1960–1962 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, the bell tower and the parish hall next to it. In Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius also built his own villa in 1930, one of the first to be built according to the new ideals of functionalism.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka i Nockeby står på: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church, in Nockeby stands on land where the trams used to turn. This was the old terminus of the number 12, with its turning loop, before construction of the church began in November 1960. It was consecrated on 9 December 1962. All around in Nockebyhov are rows of terraced houses from the late 1940s that the City Museum has marked blue for their exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Sanna betyder ungefär sandmark. Här i nä: Sanna means roughly "sandy ground". Nearby is Plaskis, or Älvsborgsdammen, as it's really called. In summer, families paddle in 20–45 centimetres of water, and when the pond is dry, skateboarders take over. At the edge is the sculpture Boll, Ball, a two-metre blue steel sphere that looks like a giant beach ball.
Sannegårdshamnen invigdes i januari 1914: Sannegårdshamnen, the Sannegården harbour, opened in January 1914, but today the name usually refers to the residential area around the harbour. Culture has moved into old industrial buildings: Backa teater, one of Sweden's leading theatres for children and young people, performs in a converted sheet-metal workshop on Lindholmen. And a stone's throw away is Aftonstjärnan, a cinema and theatre and a listed building since 1995.
Scheelegatan hette förr Trädgårdsgatan,: Scheelegatan used to be called Trädgårdsgatan, but in 1885 it got its current name after the chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele. On the corner of Fleminggatan and Pipersgatan stands Separatorhuset, built around 1900 as the head office of AB Separator, later Alfa Laval, whose factory once filled the whole large site by Barnhusviken bay. The building now has the City Museum's blue heritage rating.

Sedan 1946 har Lundbergs konditori legat: Since 1946, Lundbergs konditori has been in the same corner of Gröndalsvägen, under the same name and in the same premises, which makes it a true fika classic – fika being the Swedish coffee-and-cake break. Up on the Sannadal plateau rise the point blocks of the Ljuskronan, Ljussaxen and Lyktan blocks, built between 1958 and 1972, which have become a familiar feature of Gröndal's townscape. The light-themed block names – the Chandelier, the Candle Snuffer and the Lantern – suit the hill nicely.
Shopping i gamla flyghangarer! Köpcentre: Shopping in old aircraft hangars! The Bromma Blocks shopping centre is housed in Bromma Airport's hangars, which in their day were the largest in northern Europe. The architect Paul Hedqvist designed them in a block-like functionalist style, hence the name. And out in Bällstaviken bay there is an islet that is really a shipwreck: an old cargo ship that sank and has slowly become overgrown with greenery.
Shoppingen här sker i Bromma flygplats g: The shopping here happens in Bromma Airport's old hangars, which were once the largest in northern Europe. In 1972 the first hypermarket moved into one of them. In September 2010 the converted Hangar 3 opened, with around 80 shops under one roof. The name Bromma Blocks alludes to the block-like functionalist architecture.
Shoppingsugen? Bäckebol Center rymmer et: In the mood for shopping? Bäckebol Center has around twenty shops on 95,000 square metres. The area has changed owners several times, and in 2008 Media Markt, later Power, opened its second store in Gothenburg in Coop Bygg's old premises. A short walk away flows Lärjeån river, which has given its name to the whole Lärjedalen valley.
Sickla har länge varit en plats där bruk: Sickla has long been a place where industrial workers lived close to their jobs. As early as the late 1890s, homes were built in Tallbacken for workers and foremen at AB Diesels Motorer, and the residential area of Sickla strand was built in 1947 to 1948 for the employees of Atlas Diesel, later Atlas Copco, to designs by the architects Erik and Tore Ahlsén. The name Sickla itself roughly means a low-lying place where water emerges.
Sickla kanal skiljer Södra Hammarbyhamne: Sickla canal separates Södra Hammarbyhamnen from Nacka. The industrial history is clear here: in the 1920s Atlas Diesel, later Atlas Copco, moved all its operations to Sickla, and the head office is still here today. The factories were running until the late 1980s. In 1994 the area was turned into the Sickla shopping quarter.
Sieverts Kabelverk grundades av Max Siev: Sieverts Kabelverk, the cable works, was founded by Max Sievert in 1888 and was originally called Trådfabriken, the Wire Factory. For a long time it was Sundbyberg's largest employer. Today the Signalfabriken block, with homes, restaurants and hotels, has grown up among the old industrial buildings. A little way off, Bällsta bro, the Bällsta bridge, spans the Bällstaån stream, which here forms the boundary between Sundbyberg and Stockholm.
Sikreno låter italienskt, men namnet har: Sikreno sounds Italian, but the name has nothing to do with its neighbours Frescati and Albano. According to an unconfirmed theory, it is instead an anagram based on the name Erikson! Here you'll also find the Stocksund Inn, built between 1814 and 1816 at the old abutment of the Stocksund Bridge. The business closed in 1938, and today the building contains homes.
Silverdals griftegård anlades 1914 som g: Silverdal cemetery was laid out in 1914 as a garrison cemetery for the Stockholm garrison and was taken over by Sollentuna parish in 1960. Later both a crematorium and a funeral chapel were added. In the area now called Silverdal there used to be the crofts Rådan and Silverdal, which over time grew into farms.
Sim- och sporthallen invigdes 1973 och a: The swimming and sports hall opened in 1973, and in 1975 the architects Gustaf Rosenberg and Olle Stål were awarded the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, for it. Just a couple of hundred metres away is Edsberg Palace from 1760, where the Rudbeck family lived for almost 200 years. On the stable hill, until 2019, was Edsvik konsthall, an art gallery that showed twelve exhibitions a year.
Sisjöns industriområde ligger runt hörne: Sisjön's industrial area is just around the corner, directly south of the Söderleden road. The area grew up in the 1960s as an industrial area, but has step by step turned into a shopping area. Frölunda torg is just over two kilometres away and Mölndal's centre four.
Sju rader med skivhus på en höjd, det är: Seven rows of slab blocks on a hill, that's Siriusgatan, a real landmark at the entrance to Bergsjön. From some flats you can see all the way out to the island of Vinga! The street is Gothenburg's most populous. Originally the facades were grey and yellow, but during a renovation in 1992 in an ecological spirit, the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs gave the buildings a colour scheme in various light shades.
Själva Byälvsvägen byggdes runt 1970 och: Byälvsvägen itself was built around 1970 and is the exception in a Bagarmossen that is otherwise a well-preserved 1950s suburb. The district won international recognition for its consistent separation of pedestrians and cars and for buildings that follow the natural landscape. A little further on, the Nacka nature reserve begins, with forests along the southern shore of Lake Sicklasjön and historic settings around Lilla Sickla.
Sjättenovembervägen hette tidigare Torsv: Sjättenovembervägen, Sixth of November Road, used to be called Torsvägen and is mostly part of the old Göta landsväg, the historic main road. The long log causeway that gave Långbro – ‘long bridge’ – its name in the 15th century probably lay where the northernmost part of the street runs today. The district of Älvsjö was formed in 1932 and at that time also included today's Rågsved, Solberga and Hagsätra.
Sjöberg ligger inklämt mellan tre naturo: Sjöberg is squeezed in between three nature areas: Edsviken, Rösjön and Rinkebyskogen. A little further away is Rösjön, an elongated lake that is 7.3 metres deep and lies 6.3 metres above sea level. Most of the lake belongs to Sollentuna, but a smaller part belongs to Danderyd, and Täby, right next door, has no shoreline on it at all.
Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet: Sjöfartsmuseet Akvariet, the Maritime Museum and Aquarium
Sjön Bergsjön, som gett stadsdelen sitt: Lake Bergsjön, which gave the district its name, is very close by, but it is compact, to say the least. Its area is only 0.0257 square kilometres, roughly two and a half hectares. It does sit high, though, 101.7 metres above sea level, and its water belongs to the catchment area of the Göta älv river.
Sjön Grötfatet ligger bara några hundra: Lake Grötfatet, "the porridge bowl", is only a few hundred metres away – a name that makes most people smile. Fisksätra Church next to the square is somewhat unusual: it belongs to Nacka parish but is also regularly used by the Catholic parish of Saint Konrad, as part of the project Guds hus, God's House.
Sjön Trekanten hette Trehörningen fram t: Lake Trekanten was called Trehörningen until the mid-19th century. On its north side lay Nynäs, a ramshackle working-class suburb with a tannery, a coffee roastery and workshops, and a bakery that baked the locally famous Nynäs loaf. When the houses fell into disrepair, they became the backdrop for Bo Widerberg's 1970 film Joe Hill, where they played the 'Lumberyard' and the 'Saloon'. The last remains were demolished in 1980.
Sjöräddningens station vid Hammarbysluss: The Sea Rescue Society station by Hammarbyslussen lock
Sjötorp var ett torp under Balingsta går: Sjötorp was a croft belonging to Balingsta Farm by the Flemingsbergsviken bay. The main building was put up in 1904 by the Ersta Diaconal Society as a home for, in the words of the time, "wayward girls". Since 1998 it has been a private residence, in the middle of the Orlången nature reserve. A couple of hundred metres away is Stensättra gård, an old noble estate in an area that was probably settled as early as the Viking Age.
Skalden Carl Michael Bellman tillbringad: The poet Carl Michael Bellman spent the summer of 1773 at Fållan by Lake Magelungen, where the Zetterman family, who were his relatives, had their summer retreat. Four lime trees by the old house foundations are therefore called the Bellman Limes, Bellmanslindarna. The houses themselves were torn down around 1840. Closer to the stop is Magelungsfortet, a fort squeezed between Nynäsvägen and Gamla Nynäsvägen, a remnant of the Southern Front that was meant to protect Stockholm around the time of the First World War.
Skandiahamnen intill är Sveriges största: Skandiahamnen next door is Sweden's largest container port, with 2,200 metres of quayside. Large container ships and car carriers sail from here. A little further away is Arendalsbanan, the old speedway track of the team Kaparna. The attendance record of 5,940 spectators was set in 2002, and the track record was set by none other than Tony Rickardsson in 2004.
Skansen Kronan, utsikt över staden: Skansen Kronan fortification, with a view over the city
Skansen öppnade 1891 och är världens äld: Skansen opened in 1891 and is the world's oldest open-air museum. It has old farmsteads from all over Sweden, Nordic animals and a sweeping view over Stockholm.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter Söder: Skanstull takes its name from Söder skans, a fortification between Årstaviken bay and Hammarby sjö lake that was built in 1645 and expanded to plans by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder. The last remains weren't demolished until the 1920s. Today it's the Folksamhuset building that watches over the spot, 27 storeys high since 1960 and called an indispensable part of Stockholm's skyline. At Hammarbyslussen lock lies the Swedish Sea Rescue Society's floating station house, opened in 2019 by Prince Carl Philip.
Skanstull har fått sitt namn efter en sk: Skanstull is named after a "skans", a small fortification, and the toll gate at the city's southern entrance. Here Skanstullsbron bridge runs south towards Johanneshov, and across the water you can see the big white dome at the Globen area. Götgatan, Södermalm's main street, starts just north of here.

Skanstull is named after a 'skans', a small fortification, and the toll gate, 'tull', at the city's southern entrance. From here the Skanstull bridge heads south, and on the other side of the water you can see the big white dome in the Globen area.
Skarpa by nämns för första gången redan: Skarpa village is first mentioned as early as 1318. The Skarpnäck manor estate was formed in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace, but its heyday came with the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, who had the main building put up between 1865 and 1867. In 1922 his descendants sold the farm and land to the City of Stockholm.
Skarpa by nämns första gången redan 1318: The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as early as 1318, and the Skarpnäck manor estate was created in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace. The current main building was put up in the 1860s by the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, and under him the estate enjoyed its heyday. The district was formed in 1963 from Pungpinan and Skarpnäck, and the metro station, opened in 1994, sits in a rock cavern 25 metres underground.
Skarpnäcks tunnelbanestation, en kort pr: Skarpnäck metro station, a short walk away, became the hundredth station in the network when it opened on 15 August 1994. It lies in a rock cavern 25 metres underground, and the artist Richard Nonas has decorated it with 17 bench-like sculptures. Even closer is Skarpnäck Folk High School, Stockholm's largest folk high school.
Skarpnäcksfältet var förr ett flygfält,: Skarpnäcksfältet was once an airfield, and for many years the Skarpnäcksloppet motor race was held here. The last air show took place in August 1980, and in the 1980s a new residential area grew up on the field. Today Australian football is played at The Jordo Cricket Ground, where the first match was played between the Södermalm Blues and the Norrtälje Dockers on 6 August 2012.
Skarpäng har fått sitt namn av ett dagsv: Skarpäng got its name from a day-labourer's croft under the Ella farm, built in 1715. In the 1920s plots began to be divided off for holiday homes, and by 1940 about 550 plots had been sold. The neighbour, Ella park, got its name in the early 1930s, when what was then called northern Ella was divided up, and today it's a purely residential area of large villas.
Skeppsholmen var länge flottans ö. I dag: Skeppsholmen was long the navy's island. Today it is home to Moderna museet, the Museum of Modern Art, and the old sailing ship af Chapman, which is a youth hostel. From the shore you have one of the finest views towards Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Skidbacken Ekebyhovsbacken är hemmabacke: The ski slope Ekebyhovsbacken is the home slope of Mälaröarnas Alpina Skidklubb, the local alpine ski club, and from the slope you get a wide view over Ekerö and Lake Mälaren. A little further away, on Gällstaö, grows the Gällstaö oak, which may be between 400 and 500 years old. It is Sweden's second-largest deciduous tree by volume, beaten only by the Ekebyhov oak.
Skinnarviksberget, utsikt över Riddarfjä: Skinnarviksberget, a view over Riddarfjärden bay
Skivhusen på Siriusgatan står i sju rade: The slab blocks on Siriusgatan stand in seven rows on a hill, a landmark at the entrance to Bergsjön. From some flats you can see all the way out to Vinga! The street is Gothenburg's most populous, with 3,199 residents in 2021. Originally the facades were grey and yellow, but during a renovation in 1992 the anthroposophist Fritz Fuchs was given the job of painting them in various light shades.
Skog och berg dominerar i den här delen: Forest and rock dominate this part of Huddinge. A little way from here, Kynäsberget spreads out south-west of Lake Magelungen, a forest and rock area of national interest for outdoor recreation, where there are plans to protect the northern part as a nature reserve. In the other direction is Björkängen sports ground, home ground of the ice hockey team Huddinge IK.
Skog och berg tar över en bit härifrån:: Forest and rock take over a little way from here: Kynäsberget, south-west of lake Magelungen, is of national interest for outdoor recreation, and its northern part may become a nature reserve. Further away, on the border with Stockholm, is Rågsveds friområde, also called Kräppladalen – just over 100 hectares of rift valley landscape with ridges, steep slopes and clay-filled valleys.
Skogarna här hör till Nackareservatet, e: The forests here belong to Nackareservatet, a large nature reserve and outdoor area shared between the municipalities of Stockholm and Nacka. A little further away is Lake Källtorpssjön, 7.6 metres deep, with the outdoor sports centre Hellasgården on its shore. Test fishing in the lake has caught perch, white bream, common bream, ruffe and roach.
Skogen här är full av små sjöar. Örtjärn: The forest here is full of small lakes. Örtjärnen, a few hundred metres away, is all of ten metres deep despite its small size, and its water flows out through Finnebäcken stream. A little further away is Västra Kroppedammen, which is only 0.006 square kilometres in size, a real dwarf among lakes.
Skogskapellet var det allra första kapel: The Woodland Chapel, Skogskapellet, was the very first chapel at Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, designed by Gunnar Asplund and built in 1919 to 1920. A little way off stands the Resurrection Monument, a bronze sculpture group with six figures that John Lundqvist worked on from 1928 to 1941. The new crematorium, designed by Johan Celsing, has also won praise, receiving the 2013 Kasper Salin Prize.
Skogskyrkogården skapades av Gunnar Aspl: Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, was created by Gunnar Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz on a pine-covered gravel ridge and has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1994. On the roof above the entrance to the Woodland Chapel stands Carl Milles' small gilded Angel of Death, the only collaboration between Milles and Asplund. The angel caused a debate in the city council, because some priests found it offensive and indecent!
Skogås sträcker sig från Mörtvik i norr: Skogås stretches from Mörtvik in the north to Gräsvreten in the south and borders Lake Drevviken to the east. At Mörtviken, a bay of the lake, is Mörtviks gård, a group of buildings that has kept the character of a farm even though several of the houses have been thoroughly rebuilt. Closer to the stop is Östra gymnasiet, an upper secondary school named one of the buildings of the year in 2005.
Skolan är uppkallad efter Johan Skytte,: The school is named after Johan Skytte, and the main building, begun in 1946, was designed by the architect Paul Hedqvist. A little way off is Långbrodal School, which got a much-noticed extension in 2017. And further away was Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built from 1905 to 1910 and closed in 1997.
Skulpturen Arbetarhustru: The sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife
Skulpturen Fosterbröderna: The sculpture Fosterbröderna, the Foster Brothers
Skulpturen Husmorssemester: The sculpture Husmorssemester, the Housewives' Holiday
Skuru var från början namnet på en gård,: Skuru was originally the name of a farm, and that farm lives on as Solsunda. Gustav Vasa donated it in the 1500s to Danvik's hospital, and in the early 1900s it was owned by Stockholms sjukhem, a care home. The area also has Bastusjön, a lake you can swim in, and a little further away is Glasbrukssjön, which is all of 13 metres deep despite its small size.

Skuru was originally the name of a farm, and today the area is mostly villas and semi-detached houses framed by nature. A little way from here, on the shore of the Saltsjön, is the manor Stora Nyckelviken from the mid-1700s, and as early as the 1600s there was a sailors' inn on the site. Around the manor stretches the Nyckelviken nature conservation area, 171 hectares of hilly cultural landscape.
Skvalta var ursprungligen en sjö, och va: Skvalta was originally a lake, and the water that flowed out through Vikdalen drove several "skvaltkvarnar", small horizontal water mills – hence the name. A little further away in the villa community of Storängen are two genuine artists' homes: Villa Bergh, where the painter Richard Bergh lived between 1904 and 1919, and its neighbour Villa Pauli, the artists' home of Georg and Hanna Pauli. Both were designed in 1904 by the architect Albin Brag.
SkyView, gondolen upp på kupolen: SkyView, the gondola up the dome
Skälby är ett villaområde i södra delen: Skälby is a residential area of villas in the southern part of Järfälla, within the Stockholm urban area, and in 2005 it had a population of 6,336. The name comes from the manor Skälby gård, which has existed since the 16th century. To the south, on the other side of the municipal border, Stockholm's terraced-house and villa area of Kälvesta begins.
Skälby, villaområdet runt omkring, har f: Skälby, the villa area all around, is named after the manor Skälby gård a little way from here. The manor is a former noble estate in Järfälla parish and has existed since the 1500s, although the current main building was put up in 1802. It also has an unusual location, right in the middle of four burial grounds.
Skälltorp, området här intill, omfattar: Skälltorp, the area next to here, includes northern Backa with Selma Lagerlöfs torg square, Backadalen, Blå staden, Åketorp and Backatorp. A little further away is Sophie Elkans gata, named in 1992 after the Gothenburg-born author Sophie Elkan, better known as Selma Lagerlöf's close friend. So here in the area the two friends meet in the street names.
Skärholmen har en egen liten bergbana. S: Skärholmen has its own little funicular. The inclined lift between Skärholmen and Ekholmshöjden is 63 metres long, has room for about 30 people and takes about a minute, with no driver on board. Nearby is also Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is part of Kulturhuset Stadsteatern.
Skärholmen hörde till Huddinge ända fram: Skärholmen belonged to Huddinge right up until 1963, when the district, together with Vårberg, was transferred to Stockholm. On the metro station platform you can take a little trip to the USA: in 1990 the artist Ulf Wahlberg depicted a place in New Mexico in 23 pictures, from sunrise to sunset. The funicular, right nearby, lifts passengers up to Ekholmshöjden.
Skärholmens gård, vid Mälaren en bit här: Skärholmens gård, by Lake Mälaren a little way from here, began as a simple croft under Vårby gård. In the mid-18th century it was rebuilt as a summer retreat for well-to-do Stockholmers. Since 1945 the farm has been owned by the City of Stockholm, and it is blue-listed by the City Museum, which means its buildings are judged to have exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Skärsätra gård, alldeles intill, har get: Skärsätra farm, right next to us, has given its name to the whole district, and the old main house is still there, though rebuilt. The villas round about offer a little architecture walk: Villa Bergtomta in Art Nouveau style from 1910, the Orange Villa by Lake Kottlasjön, a listed building since 1982, and Villa Smith, which the architect Nils Tesch designed for himself in 1959 but never moved into.
Skårsgatan har fått namn efter gården Sk: Skårsgatan is named after the farm Skår, and the word 'skår' means a notch or ledge in the rock. The name is spelled Shor in a court letter as early as 1496. Sankt Sigfridsgatan next to it is named after the patron saint of Västergötland. And along that street is Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, which since 1924 has baked citrus-scented gingerbread biscuits to a secret recipe.
Sköndal blev en egen stadsdel 1932 och h: Sköndal became a district of its own in 1932 and has plenty of architecture to discover. The architect Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl in 1955 as his own home, and Sköndalsskolan, opened in 1953, was designed by none other than Cyrillus Johansson. A little way off, Stora Sköndal Church sits on a cliff near Lake Drevviken.
Sköndalsbro var en gång ett torp, och hu: Sköndalsbro was once a croft, and the main building was probably built sometime between 1700 and 1750, or later. The surrounding blocks are a small museum of architecture: Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the architect couple Hanna and Roy Victorson built Villa Victorson. Both houses, from 1955 and 1958 respectively, are marked blue by the City Museum for their exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Slussen är platsen där Mälaren möter Sal: Slussen is where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic waters of Saltsjön, and where Södermalm meets Gamla stan, the Old Town. There have been locks here since the 17th century, and right now the whole area is being rebuilt in one of Stockholm's largest construction projects. From the quays you can look out towards Gamla stan, Skeppsholmen and Djurgården.
Släktforskare, spetsa öronen! Alldeles i: Genealogists, listen up! Right next door is the home of the Genealogical Society, Genealogiska Föreningen, a national association founded in 1933 and one of Sweden's oldest in family history research. A stone's throw away is Jungfrudansen, today a housing area with culturally and historically valuable Million Programme buildings, but once a festival ground. The Huvudsta quarry was also there.
Slättens gård är ett före detta torp som: Slättens gård is a former croft that originally came under Sätra manor, and one of the few remaining buildings from before the Mälarhöjden villa suburb was built. Today the farm's three houses are managed by AB Stadsholmen. A little further away is Mälarhöjden sports ground, popularly known as Myren, which despite the name is in Fruängen.
Smycketorget i närheten anlades på 1960-: Smycketorget nearby was laid out in the 1960s and has two levels: upstairs there are shops and a hairdresser, downstairs an Asian restaurant and a pizzeria. A little further away is Frölunda torg, which was opened on 8 September 1966 by Olof Palme. It was then the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries, built over seven years.
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ab: We'll soon reach the final stop, Abrahamsberg. A little naming joke: Abrahamsberg metro station isn't actually in Abrahamsberg, but in Riksby. Before the metro arrived, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals of glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are inspired by the tiled stations of the tram era. Nearby is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ak: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Akalla. The main walkway through Akalla is called Sibeliusgången, after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius, and it's 900 metres long. Along the way, Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubble away. But the name Akalla has been known since the Middle Ages: in Akalla village stands Storgården from the 17th century, in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area, with a 4-H farm and a café. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Al: We'll soon reach the final stop, Alvik. Alvik is a hub where the Tvärbanan and Nockebybanan light rail lines meet the metro. From here you can reach Bromma, with its villa neighbourhoods and the shores of Lake Mälaren. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Alviks strand. Where Alvik's old industrial area once stood by Lake Mälaren, there are now mostly offices and a few restaurants. In Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, an event venue nearby, the competition show Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail disappears into the rock through the roughly 250-metre-long Alvik tunnel, and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the Alvik bridge, which is 400 metres long and was completed in 2000. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Am: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Amhult Resecentrum. Here in Amhult, a few hundred metres away, was Torslanda airfield, Gothenburg's airport from 1923 right up to 1977, when Landvetter took over. It was originally called Göteborgs Flyghamn and also had a seaplane harbour. When it closed, it was one of Europe's oldest airfields with scheduled flights. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen An: We'll soon reach the final stop, Angered Centrum. Angered was built in the 1970s and is today one of Gothenburg's most international districts. Here is the Blå Stället cultural centre, and all around there are large nature areas with lakes and forest. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Angereds Storåsväg. A little way from here is Hammarkulletorget, built in 1971. During a renovation in 1997 the square got both new colours and a new shape. You get there by tram and get off at what is called Gothenburg's only underground station. Closer to the stop lies Eriksbo, part of the Hjällbo district. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ap: We'll soon reach the final stop, Aprilgatan. Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, is known to many simply as Norra, or Norra centrum, and it is the small meeting point of northern Kortedala. Here you'll find a health centre, a pizzeria, tobacconists and a pastry shop for anyone in need of a fika break – a Swedish coffee-and-cake pause – and there's a pub nearby. Local associations have their premises on the square too. The square is on tram line six, by its terminus. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ar: We'll soon reach the final stop, Arendal Portal. Right next door is the Arken combi terminal in Skandia Harbour, Skandiahamnen, where semi-trailers are transferred between ships and trains. It replaced the terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to move when the Västlänken rail tunnel was built. Work began in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen As: We'll soon reach the final stop, Askims Svartmosse. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ax: We'll soon reach the final stop, Axel Dahlströms Torg. The square stands out with a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and on the community centre there is a mural in the form of a marble inlay by the artist Endre Nemes. The same year, Högsboskolan, the Högsbo school, opened right next door, built for about 1,000 pupils. The school is no longer here, though – it was demolished in 2013. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ba: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Backlura. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bagarmossen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Bagartorp södra. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Balingsnäs. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby handelsplats. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Barkarby station övre. Barkarby is a place in full transformation. The commuter train station got its current form on 10 October 2016, with four tracks and a ticket hall on the Barkarby bridge. At the same time, a new metro station is being built underground, and a new entrance at the north end of the station will become the main entrance when everything is finished. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barkarby station. From here it's about 14.5 kilometres into Stockholm Central, and the commuter train station has four tracks so that freight trains and long-distance trains can whizz past. In Järfälla church, Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone in 1728 that had probably been used as a step. It later disappeared, but in 1939 seven fragments turned up, and today they are kept at the Swedish History Museum. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Barnängen. Per Anders Fogelström portrayed the old factory area of Barnängen by Hammarby sjö, Lake Hammarby, in the novel Vävarnas barn, "The Weavers' Children", and this is where the football club Hammarby IF has its roots. Barnängsparken park slopes down to the quay with lawns and a ferry pier towards Hammarby sjöstad. A little further away is Leksaksmuseet, the toy museum, where the collections range from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Be: We'll soon reach the final stop, Beatrice Lesslies Gata. A few hundred metres from here is Studio Fredman, the recording studio Fredrik Nordström started in 1990. A long line of Swedish metal bands have recorded here, such as In Flames, Hammerfall, Opeth, Dark Tranquillity and Soilwork, as well as the British band Bring Me the Horizon. Just beyond lies Radiotorget, Sweden's first satellite town square, opened in 1954. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Björknäs centrum. Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436 and takes its name from the Stora Björknäs farm. The area lies at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where the Skurusundet strait divides two historic provinces: west of the water is Södermanland, east of it Uppland. The bridges have been built in three rounds, in 1915, 1957 and 2023, and when the newest one opened it took over the name Skurubron, while the older ones became known as Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnbo. Along Elfviksvägen there are two villas by the architect Ralph Erskine: Villa Gadelius, designed in 1961 for the businessman Knut Saburo Gadelius, and Villa Molin from 1947, built for the garden architect and editor Ulla Molin. A little further away is the Canada block, whose terraced houses, together with those in Gamla Enskede, are considered Sweden's very first, and which has been a listed building since 1981. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Björnkulla. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bl: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Blackebergs gård. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Blockhusudden. The headland takes its name from a blockhouse of timber and stone, built in Gustav Vasa's time to protect the approach to Stockholm. Later the spot became a customs station for boats coming in, and the customs houses at Stora Sjötullen are now homes. Out here you'll also find the Thiel Gallery, Thielska galleriet, the art museum on Djurgården. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bo: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Bockkranen. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Borås resecentrum. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Bosön. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Br: We'll soon reach the final stop, Bredäng. Bredäng is properly hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, is 62 metres above sea level and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken next to the centre is one of the district's largest parks, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because it used to be rowdy. Bredäng Church isn't a building of its own but is housed in a parish hall at one end of the centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Bromma flygplats. The building on Ulvsundavägen was built in 1946 as the head office of the airline ABA and was later used by SAS. The architect Paul Hedqvist designed it, and he also designed several of the airport's hangars. In their day they were the largest in northern Europe. Today the hangars house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Brommaplan. By the metro viaduct stands the sculpture "Bird Rock with Three Eggs" by Berndt Helleberg from 1969. The viaduct is older than the metro. It came into use in 1944 and was served by trams back then. The station's art, in sheet metal, glass and photographs, is about the history of Bromma and of aviation. The 16-storey Brommahöjden tower block didn't arrive until 2008. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Brunnsparken. Brunnsparken is the heart of the city's public transport. Almost all the tram lines run from here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, with the statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that is why Gothenburg has canals. The Dutch knew how to build on clay. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Brännö Rödsten. Brännö is a car-free island in Gothenburg's southern archipelago. In summer, the jetty dances on Brännö are famous throughout Gothenburg, and the island has lovely rocks to swim from. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Bu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Burö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ce: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Centralen. At Vasagatan 7 was the bar Tre Remmare, with a casino and nightclub in the same premises. It was one of the few places in Stockholm allowed to stay open until five in the morning, and it became notorious for drunkenness and drug abuse. In 2007 it lost its licence and closed. Today the Bishops Arms pub occupies the premises. Opposite stands the World Trade Center, designed by Ralph Erskine. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ci: We'll soon reach the final stop, Cityterminalen. Kungsgatan 65 has lived many lives. The Palladium cinema opened in 1918, with the dance restaurant Bal Palais in the basement. Then it became the nightclub Heaven, and from 2003 to 2025 Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern from 1906, named after Oscar II and a listed building. In the same building is Fasching, Scandinavia's largest jazz venue since 1977. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Da: We'll soon reach the final stop, Dalens sjukhus. Dalen hospital, from 1977, is a well-preserved example of the late modernist architecture typical of its time, with value for the history of urban planning. A little further away, on Nytorps gärde, the field of Nytorp, stood the croft Nytorp under Hammarby gård, which disappeared in the early 1960s when the Nytorpsbadet pool was built in its place. The residential area of Dalen consists of 14 blocks and is green-listed in its entirety by the Stockholm City Museum. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Danderyds sjukhus. In Inverness, the brewery Inverness brunn operated between 1929 and 1945. Among other things, Sweden's first club soda was made here. The spring is still there on the shore of Stocksundet, but the water is unfit to drink and tastes salty. Closer to the stop was the 18th-century farm Mörby gård, which gave the area its name. It became a listed building in 1944 but burned down in 1976. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dj: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Djurgårdsbrunn. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Djursholms torg. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Djurstensvägen. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Do: We'll soon reach the final stop, Doktor Sydows Gata. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Dr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Drottningtorget. Drottningtorget lies right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Large parts of the biggest tram network in the Nordic countries start from here. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and the city chose to keep its trams when many other Swedish cities got rid of theirs. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Du: We'll soon reach the final stop, Duvbo. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ek: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensberg. Ekensberg is named after the Ekensberg inn, which was built in the early 18th century and still stands at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, Ekensberg was the name of most of what is now called Gröndal. The headland lies between Mörtviken and Essingesundet. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekensbergsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ekerö centrum. From Tappström, commuter boat line 89 runs all the way to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay in Stockholm, with boats including M/S Lux. In the Tappström strait, where the boundary between the islands of Lovön and Ekerön runs, there's also a guest harbour for leisure boats. A little further away was Tappsund brickworks, founded in the late 19th century and closed in 1959. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Eketrägatan. The street commemorates the noble family Eketrä, who from the 18th century owned the Västra Pilegården estate right up until 1875 – just where the asphalt lies today. The Bräcke tram line also turned south from here. The tramway was closed in 1968 and dismantled in the 1980s, but the old trackbed remains almost untouched, like a trace from another time. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Ekstubben. Ältavägen is 8.1 kilometres long and got its route in 1934. It runs mostly through undeveloped countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. In the Flaten nature reserve there is an unusual attraction: a racing track for radio-controlled model cars. It is at Ältavägen 301 in the Flaten district. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Ektorps centrum. Much of the neighbouring area of Ekängen was built in the 1940s with small single-family houses, and it is still a quiet residential area north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further away is Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005, with a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round. Perfect if you want to swap town-centre life for a lap around the lake. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen El: We'll soon reach the final stop, Elfvik. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen En: We'll soon reach the final stop, Enbacksskolan. The Bussenhus croft next to Spånga Church was a soldier's croft with an unusual side income: in the 1740s, the cavalryman here had the right to run a tavern. The tavern sometimes turns up in the records of the Sollentuna district court, after various brawls. Inside the church there are fragments of Viking Age runestones, and one of them is built into the church's outer wall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Eq: We'll soon reach the final stop, Equmeniakyrkan. Every spring Björkö turns blue. At Bovik is the area called Pjonken, known for the huge number of hepaticas, or blue anemones, that bloom there.
