The island is in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, and the village has around 1,400 residents. A short way from here stands Björkö Church, which belongs to Öckerö parish. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Er: We'll soon reach the final stop, Eriksbo Östergärde. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Es: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Essingetorget.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Farsta centrum. Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was big for its time, escalators and all. The car park was one of Europe's largest, with space for 4,000 cars. To shorten the walk to the shops, moving walkways were installed to carry customers from their cars. Farsta was called the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Farsta strand. The square by the station is named after the crime writer Stieg Trenter, who was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery shop by the railway station, then called Södertörns villastad, where young Stieg sometimes helped out – and his crime novel Träff i helfigur is set in the surrounding area. The garden suburb itself never happened: the plots sold slowly, mainly because of poor transport links. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fi: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Finnberget. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fiskebäcks Småbåtshamn. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Fittja. At the metro station stands a copy of Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's sculpture The Knotted Gun, also known as Non-Violence – the most famous one stands outside the UN headquarters in New York. A couple of hundred metres away is Fittja gård, a farm whose inn was one of Sweden's largest coaching inns in the 17th and 18th centuries, and where one of the buildings served as a district courthouse right up until 1916. Today the Multicultural Centre runs its activities at the farm. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Fjällsyran. Rannebergen Centrum was built in 1974 and has a swimming pool, and across the street the Bohusleden trail and Vättlefjäll hills await, with fine waters for swimming and fishing. Nearby also begins the Lärjeån Valley nature reserve, which became protected in 2026 and covers more than 1,100 hectares. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fr: We'll soon reach the final stop, Framnäs. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fredriksdal. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Fridhemsplan. Fridhemsplan is one of Kungsholmen's major hubs, with the metro, buses and shops. In the 16th century, Kungsholmen was called Munklägret, 'the Monks' Camp', after the monks who owned land here. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Frihamnen. Stockholm's free port, Frihamnen, opened as a temporary arrangement in 1919 and kept expanding right up to the 1970s. During the same period, between 1921 and 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the free port now lies. Fordhuset, the Ford Building, designed by Uno Åhrén, was built from 1929 to 1931 as an assembly plant for Ford cars, and today the stock exchange company Nasdaq is based there. The enormous Magasin 6 warehouse, on the other hand, quickly became outdated when container traffic took over. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Fritidsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Fruängen. Fruängen station is the highest-lying in the entire metro network, 46.8 metres above sea level. Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady, has an unusual history: the church centre opened in 1963, but the actual church hall shown on the plans wasn't started until 2004, and it was consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent 2005. A block away stands the Triangle House, Triangelhuset, from 1955, named after its unique triangular floor plan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Frölunda Torg. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 and was one of Sweden's first large suburban shopping centres. All around lies Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Frösundavik.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Furulund. Furulund Church is a little unusual: it is a joint church shared by EFS, the Evangelical Homeland Foundation, and the Furulund-Öjersjö parish. A little way from here hides Prästtjärnen, a small lake that, despite its modest size, is a full 14 metres deep. It lies just over 108 metres above sea level and is part of the main Göta älv river basin. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Furulunds centrum. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Fy: We'll soon reach the final stop, Fyrktorget. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ga: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Gamlestads Torg. Gamlestaden is exactly that, the old town. Nya Lödöse was founded here in 1473, long before today's Gothenburg was laid out in 1621. Later the area became industrial, and this is where the ball-bearing company SKF grew up. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gl: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Gladö kvarn. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Glasbruksgatan. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Go: We'll soon reach the final stop, Godsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Godsterminalen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gr: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Grimbo. In the area lies Gunnestorps mosse, a mix of lake, fen and bog in Hisingsparken park. Here reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow side by side with cranberries, sundews and cotton grass. North of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården adventure playground. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Grötö färjeläge. Grötö is small: 84 permanent residents and just under two thirds of a square kilometre. Yet the island has something unusual for Bohuslän, namely a sandy beach. It's in the Grötö Knöten nature reserve at the island's northern tip, and a glacial ridge of rounded stones runs along the west coast. In summer the kiosk in the main harbour is open, and near the harbour there's both sand and rocks with a swimming ladder. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gubbängens centrum. On Gubbängstorget square there was once the City cinema, which opened in April 1953 and closed twenty years later. In the 1950s, the new suburbs were meant to be self-sufficient in every kind of service, even having their own cinemas. Today the auditorium has a new life as Moment teater, a theatre that started here in 2000 and whose work with theatre classics won Svenska Dagbladet's Thalia Prize in 2008. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Gullmarsplan. Gullmarsplan is named after Gullmarn, the fjord near Lysekil in the province of Bohuslän. The square was built in the 1940s at the same time as the surrounding district, and the metro station opened on 1 October 1950. Before that, trams stopped here. Today it is one of Stockholm's biggest transport hubs, where the metro, the Tvärbana light rail and buses meet. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Gustavsbergs centrum. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gärdsås Torg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Gåshaga brygga. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Gåshaga. Behind the houses, the Käppala plant has been treating wastewater since 1969, and it is considered one of the most efficient treatment plants in the world. A little further away is Käppalaställningen, an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War, which was reopened in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defence, unique in Sweden. Also nearby is M/S Soya III, a tanker from 1936 built to carry soya oil, now a conference ship. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Gö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Görvälns griftegård. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ha: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Hagsätra. A stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local centre, opened in 1960, the same year the metro reached here. Keep an eye out for "Barnet med käpphästen", the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further away there's also an outdoor pool with a funny name: Älvsjöbadet, which despite its name isn't in Älvsjö at all but here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hallonbergen. Go down into the metro and it feels like stepping into a child's drawing. The artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark decorated the station with motifs that look like children's drawings, inspired by their own childhoods. The station opened on 31 August 1975, with the blue line's first stretch between T-Centralen and Hjulsta. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hallunda centrum. Around the shopping centre in northern Botkyrka there is an unusually close-knit church neighbourhood. Botkyrka folkhögskola, a folk high school founded in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, but it is open to everyone regardless of religion. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen, is next door to the Syriac Orthodox Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul, and Hallundakyrkan, Hallunda Church, stands almost wall to wall with the centre. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen He: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Heden. When Trädgårn opened as a café in 1858, all the staff were men, and punsch, a sweet Swedish liqueur, was the only spirit served. The building next to the stop, Exercishuset, the Drill House, was completed in 1867 as a gift from the wholesaler Julius Lindström. It was where elementary schoolchildren were to do gymnastics and sharpshooters were to drill. Heden itself was the military's training ground, and until 2019 there was a bandy rink here. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Helenelunds station. From here it is 10.9 kilometres by commuter train to Stockholm Central, and on an ordinary winter weekday about 5,400 people board here. The neighbour is Eriksberg, a narrow strip between the E4 motorway and the railway, named after the Eriksberg croft from 1819. A little further away is Silverdal cemetery, laid out in 1914 as the garrison cemetery for the Stockholm garrison. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Henriksdalsberget. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Henriksdalsviadukten. Through the Henriksdalsberget hill runs the 337-metre tunnel of Saltsjöbanan, the Saltsjö railway, where trains have been rolling since 1893. The area around Henriksborg used to be industrial land, and from 1882 until the end of the 1950s the Rylander and Rudolph factory made, among other things, batteries for crank telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps. The office building Danvikcenter won a European prize for its steel structures in 1987. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Himlabacken. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Hinnebäcksgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hj: We'll soon reach the final stop, Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen. Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen is Hisingen's big transport hub. Hisingen is Sweden's fourth-largest island, and both ships and cars were once built here. Volvo was founded in Gothenburg in 1927, and its headquarters are still on Hisingen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hjulsta. Beneath Hjulstaskolan, a cavern was blasted out for the metro, and on 31 August 1975 the blue line's trains could start running here, about 14 kilometres from Kungsträdgården. Close by is the green Hjulsta allotment garden, whose association was formed in 1973 and which today is held up as an example of multicultural gardening. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Hjuvik.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ho: We'll soon reach the final stop, Hornkamsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hovås Nedre. Askim Church stands just a couple of hundred metres away, the parish church of a parish stretching along the coast south of Gothenburg, which became part of Gothenburg municipality in 1974. At the marina in Hovås there's also a sea rescue station, whose first boat in 1983 was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Huddinge sjukhus. Right next door is the Swedish Red Cross University, Röda Korsets Högskola, Sweden's oldest secular nursing school. It was founded in 1867 by Emmy Rappe, who had herself been trained by none other than Florence Nightingale in London. The school started in Uppsala and spent a long time at Sabbatsberg Hospital before ending up here. A short distance away is Flemingsberg Church, consecrated in 1976. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Huddinge station. Commuter trains stop at Huddinge centrum, the municipality's heart and shopping centre. Along Kommunalvägen, which runs almost parallel to the tracks of the Western Main Line for about 1.3 kilometres, you'll find both Huddinge Church and the municipal hall. Nearby are also the traces of Svartlösa domsaga, a former court district, whose courthouse was designed in 1959 by the architect Karl Karlström – the court district lasted only twelve years and was dissolved in the district court reform of 1971. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Hultåsen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Häggvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Härlanda. Behind the walls in Härlanda, prisoners were held from 1907 to 1997. The old central prison is a listed building and is now called Härlanda park. The Saga cinema on Sofiagatan closed in 1964. The following year it became a grocery shop – Saga Hemköp, the first in the Sagabutikerna chain. Among the buildings there's also an old church ruin. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hässelby gård. In the assembly hall of Hässelbygårdsskolan, the local school, there was once the Prisma cinema, which opened in November 1960 and showed films to the public until December 1984. The school also got both a doctor's surgery and a swimming pool. A little further away is Hässelby familjehotell, which at its opening in 1955 was master builder Olle Engkvist's largest collective housing block. The professional services were closed down in 1976, but the residents still run some activities on a voluntary basis. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Hö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Höga hallar. A little way from here is Benareby, between the lakes Nordsjön, Yxsjön, Finnsjön and Gravsjön. Benareby was once known for its wooden barrels, which mainly went to the fish-processing industry, and the cooper's tradition lives on to this day. There are also many old holiday homes here that are now permanent residences. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Högdalen. Not far from here rise three artificial hills made of demolition rubble and bulky waste. The first, Högdalstoppen, was finished in 1964, and the rock there used to be the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the peaks are an outdoor recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still being topped up with excavated soil from road building. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Högnäsvägen. A short distance from here, in the schoolyard of Klockargården school, Carl Milles' elephants are at play: the sculpture group Playing Elephants has stood there since 1947. The school itself is the oldest one still in use in the municipality, dating back to 1843. Along Stockholmsvägen in Näset you'll also find Näsets krog, a preserved 18th-century roadside inn, and Villa Nynäs, where Lidingö's first general store opened in the late 19th century. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Högsätra. The ice rink a little way from here became famous throughout the country through the TV series HCZ. It has changed its name several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club plays here, and figure skaters train here. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Högsätrahuset. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hökarängen. Hökarängen was one of the first suburbs to grow up along the new metro after the Second World War, and David Helldén's car-free town centre became a model for suburbs all over Sweden. Right next to it is Farsta fire station, which was originally called Enskede fire station. And the light, arched roof of Gubbängshallen can be seen from far across the Gubbängsfältet field. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Hökmossen. Hökmossen once included the cottage Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. A little way off is Hägerstensbadet, popularly called Personnebadet after Personnevägen, an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Hönö färjeläge. Hönöleden is Sweden's busiest ferry route counted in motor vehicles, with just over 2.3 million vehicles in 2009. The ferries run between Lilla Varholmen on Hisingen and Hönö, a distance of 2,500 metres that takes twelve minutes. It counts as part of county road 155 and is therefore free. Among the ferries are M/S Ada, M/S Beda, M/S Göta and M/S Marie. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen IA: We'll soon reach the final stop, IAC Group. Sörred has a name that isn't flattering. It is recorded from 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a negligent man, a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The second part comes from the Old Swedish "ryd", cleared land. The slacker's clearing turned out to be hard-working all the same: this is where Volvo's Torslandaverken factory began to be built in 1960 to 1961. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen In: We'll soon reach the final stop, Inseros. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ja: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Jakobsbergs sjukhus. Aspnässkolan, a couple of minutes away, was the very first school of Järfälla parish and opened in 1846 in a purchased manor house that had previously been a roadside tavern. The oldest school building was torn down in 1959, but it lives on in an unexpected way: today it serves as a wind shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor recreation centre. The hospital itself is owned by Region Stockholm and houses, among other things, a health centre and a pharmacy. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Jakobsbergs station. Jakobsberg is named after a dead man. Jakob Lilliehöök inherited the farms in the village of Vibble, and after his death in 1657 his widow Brita Cruus built a manor house that was given his name. Today it houses Jakobsberg folk high school. By the station stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, the station building from 1876. The windmill from the 1840s burned three times and was not rebuilt after the fire in 2005. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Jarlaberg. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Jo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Jons väg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ju: We'll soon reach the final stop, Julitavägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Jungfrusund. Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden bay, on the eastern side of Ekerön island. Out in the water are Jungfruholmarna, two islands that are the club islands of Göta segelsällskap, a sailing club. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse in 1955. The Ekeröleden ferry also crosses the bay. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Jupitervägen. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Jä: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Järntorget. Järntorget, Iron Square, is named after the iron that was weighed and shipped from here. The fountain in the middle is from 1927 and depicts the earth's five continents. This is where the working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga with its cafés and landshövdingehus, the typical Gothenburg houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors, and to the west run the Långgatorna streets with vintage shops and bars. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Järnvågen. The name comes from a scale. Here the iron shipped out through Gothenburg's harbour was weighed, including iron from the ironworks in Värmland. In the 1780s the city's iron weighing station was moved to a plot just north of today's Järntorget, the Iron Square, and the square was named after it. The iron carriers, who handled the iron bars, settled in the blocks around it. The scale itself was demolished long ago. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Järva närsjukhus. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ka: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kallebäcks Källa. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kanehall. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Karolinska institutet västra. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Karolinska sjukhuset norra. Sweden's first clinic for cancer treatment, Radiumhemmet, was founded in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. A little further away stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's well-known roadside inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. A lookout tower was also meant to be built in Hagaparken, but work on it never even started. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Kastellholmsbron.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ki: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kippholmen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Kista centrum. Kista metro station is the only one on the blue line that's above ground. It rests on a viaduct 1,120 metres long, the longest in the whole metro network. When the station was to be named, the naming committee first wanted to add "Gård", meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a likkista, a coffin. Above the shopping mall rises Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Klara Mälarstrand. From the quay next to the City Hall, Strömma's boats head out onto Lake Mälaren, towards Drottningholm and the Viking town of Birka, but also on lunch and dinner cruises. The boats run from May to the end of October. Right nearby is the mouth of Klara sjö, the canal that separates Kungsholmen from Norrmalm and links Barnhusviken bay with Riddarfjärden. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Klareberg. Klareberg in Kärra is a place where the buses take a breather. Bus drivers like to take a break here, and the big bus stop is used for journeys to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also known among riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and train their dogs. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Klippans Färjeläge. Klippan is named after Skinnareklippan, the rock where St Birgitta's Chapel stands. The chapel was consecrated in 1857 and designed by A W Edelsvärd from drawings that the brewer David Carnegie had brought from a church in Scotland. Carnegie's brewery is now a hotel. The area also has the remains of the fortress Gamla Älvsborg, which was ransomed from the Danes in 1619. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Klubbacken. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kn: We'll soon reach the final stop, Knalleborg. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ko: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Komettorget. Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan and Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street: here in Bergsjön the street names have been taken from outer space. A short distance from here is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, with the Bergsjön Culture House. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, and offers everything from music and art to children's programmes. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kongahällagatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Kornhalls Färja. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Korseberget. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Kottla station.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ku: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungsbacka station. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungssten. Kungssten is near the mouth of Göta älv, the Göta River. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966. Out in the river mouth lies Nya Älvsborg fortress from the 1600s, which protected the city against the Danes. By the water below is Klippan, with old seamen's houses and the remains of the older Älvsborg fortress. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungälv resecentrum. The buses to Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsund and Tjörn pull in at the travel centre, and right next door is Kongahälla Center, with around a hundred shops and restaurants, opened in 2019. The E6 motorway rushes past right alongside. A little further away is Oasen, a swimming pool and ice rink built after the old swimming baths burned down. It has both a 25-metre pool and a rehab pool with warmer water. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kungälvs sjukhus södra. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kv: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Kvarnhagen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Kvarter 13.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Källbrinks idrottsplats. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kärna bussterminal. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Kärrtorp. From Kärrtorp you can reach all the way to the Nacka Reserve, Nackareservatet, in Nacka municipality, so the forest is never far away. Closer at hand is the Reflexen cinema, which has been showing films since 1961, and the Kärrtorp sports hall, Kärrtorpshallen, from the early 1960s, designed by Kjell Ödeen and given a green listing by the City Museum. Kärrtorp Park only got its current name in 2009, but in its southern part stands the old crofter's cottage that gave the district its name. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Kållered station. Kållered station has had two lives. The first station opened in 1891 but closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka returned, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in rush hour trains now run every fifteen minutes in each direction. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Kålleredgården. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Kålsered. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Kö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Körkarlens gata. On 3 April 1973, OBS opened in Bäckebol, 30,000 square metres in size and at the time the country's largest hypermarket. Long before that, there was Bäckebol Farm. Construction of the stone manor house began in 1764 under the weighmaster Johan Oliveholm, and it has been a listed building since 1969. The owners of the estate even have their own burial ground, in use since the mid-18th century. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen La: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Landvetter resecentrum. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Larsberg. Up on the hill stand the Larsberg buildings with brick-red facades, green metal roofs and white balcony fronts, typical of the 1960s. Just over 1,200 flats were completed in 1969, designed by the architect Bengt Gate. Below lies Malmstens, where students study furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery. The old hospital building in Högsätra was to be demolished during 2025 to make way for the new district of Kärnan. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Le: We'll soon reach the final stop, Lektorsstigen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Li: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Liljeholmen. The Rosteriet block is named after a German roastery that made coffee substitute here between 1913 and 1920. Later Pharmacia made medicines in the block, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi made fuel rods for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill stands Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, home since 2003 to Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music high school. Thanks for travelling with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Lilla Dalens begravningsplats. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lilla Varholmen. Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. The island is connected to Hisingen by a bridge, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality, on both the Björkö route and the Hönö route. The Björkö route is only about 900 metres long, and the crossing takes about five minutes. The island has lighthouses too: the leading lights here today date from 1927. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lillebyvägen. Lilleby by the sea on Hisingen was long pure countryside and belonged to Björlanda parish, until the area became part of Gothenburg in 1967. A land reform redistributing the farm plots was carried out here as early as 1846. Today the residential areas are growing fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and also offers Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony with its preserved 1950s cabins. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Lillövägen. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Lindholmen. For a long time, Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's big shipyards. Where ships used to be built, there's now Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay you look straight across the river towards the city centre. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Lindholmspiren. Lindholmspiren is by the old shipyard area on Lindholmen, where ships were built for over a hundred years. Today Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology are here, and from the quay you can look straight across the river towards the city centre. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindome station. Lindome station has died and risen again. It opened on 1 September 1888, when the Gothenburg–Halland Railway was completed, but passenger services were withdrawn in 1970 and the station closed completely in 1989. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started running again, it made a comeback on 17 August 1992, and in 2012 it was rebuilt for longer trains. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Lindvreten. Lindvreten was a croft belonging to Vårby manor, and the name probably means 'the patch of land with the lime trees'. Nearby was the croft Månskär, whose curious name has nothing to do with the crescent moon, or 'månskära'. It comes from one of the first tenants, Måns, and the word 'kärr', meaning marsh. Here you'll also find Södra djursjukhuset, the Southern Animal Hospital, which started in 1967 with two people in a villa. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Linnéplatsen. At Linnéplatsen begins Slottsskogen, the city's big park from 1874. There you'll find animals, ponds and the Natural History Museum, which has a stuffed blue whale from 1865. In the other direction runs Linnégatan, one of the city's best-loved restaurant streets. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Lise Meitners gata. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Liseberg Station. We're on the north side of Liseberg. The amusement park opened in 1923 as part of the city's anniversary exhibition and is today one of the most visited in the Nordic region. At Christmas it turns into a Christmas market with millions of lights. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lj: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Ljungkullen. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Ljusterögatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Lunda industri. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Lundbystrand. Götaverken built ships here, and the shipyard halls live on in unexpected ways. Curling has been played in an old workshop since 2001, and the former sheet-metal workshop houses Lundbystrandshallen, with five handball courts. The glass building by the water, Kanalhuset, was built for the camera company Hasselblad, which soon moved out. Today SVT and Sveriges Radio, Swedish public television and radio, broadcast from there. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Luxgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Lå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Långsjö torg. The businessman Robert Ditzinger was a thoughtful father. In 1882 he had two identical main buildings built on Långsjö farm, one for each of his two sons. The farm later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö, which is bounded by the lake Långsjön towards Huddinge. Not far from here runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg, the historic highway to the south. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ma: We'll soon reach the final stop, Marklandsgatan. The street is named after markland, an old unit for valuing land. Right next to it is the Frölundaborg ice stadium. It opened in 1967 with a friendly match in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. By Slottsskogsvallen, where high jumpers such as Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, winds Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Masthugget. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Me: We'll soon reach the final stop, Merkuriusgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Mo: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Moa Martinsons torg. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Mossvägen. Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. A little way from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the windmill Stora Stampan. Its companion Holländskan burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was renovated over the winter of 2019 to 2020 and now has new sails. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Motalavägen. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Mö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Mölndals Innerstad. Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Mölndal's mill village, Mölndals kvarnby, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today the mill village is a heritage area with a museum and cafés. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Mölndals bro. Mölndal means 'the mill valley', and the rapids that gave the name are right nearby. In Kvarnbyn, the Mill Village, there have been mills by the rapids since the 14th century, and until the 17th century the Crown owned most of them. The falls are around 800 metres long, with a drop of about 45 to 48 metres. The water power later drove industries, and today Kvarnbyn is a cultural environment of national interest, with the Mölndal City Museum by the rapids. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Mölnlycke resecentrum. Trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop at Mölnlycke station, but the station hasn't always been here. It opened in 1894 about 350 metres further east and was only moved to its current location in 2003. The old station building was demolished in 2013. A little way off is Wallenstam Arena, where Pixbo Wallenstam IBK play their home floorball matches in front of up to 1,600 spectators. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Mörby station. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Na: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka Forum. Nacka Forum opened on 1 March 1989, replacing a temporary centre in prefab huts that had had to do for many years. Right next to it begins the villa idyll of Storängen, where Villa Wållgren from 1907 has been judged irreplaceable. A stone's throw away also stands Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner and his wife Elin, née Bonnier. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Nacka gymnasium. There are plenty of school desks around here: Nacka gymnasium is one of Sweden's largest upper secondary schools, and its neighbour, Eklidens skola, is one of the country's largest lower secondary schools, with an ice rink and a swimming pool right next door. The name Järla comes from the title jarl, an old Norse word for earl. In nearby Vikdalen, Stockholm families built summer villas in the late 1800s and came out by steamboat, but when the car engine factory in Augustendal arrived, workers moved in and the villas became workers' housing. Thanks for travelling with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Nacka sjukhus. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Nacka strand. Nacka strand was long called Augustendal. In 1899 the industrial pioneer J.V. Svenson bought the area, and by 1916 his engine factory had 500 employees, one of Sweden's largest workplaces. After a bankruptcy in 1922, the company was taken over by Handelsbanken. In the 1980s offices and homes were built, and in 1988 the area was given the name Nacka strand. In the marina, since 1995, Carl Milles' sculpture God the Father on the Rainbow has been spraying water in an arc over the Saltsjön bay. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ni: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Nils Ericson Terminalen. Gothenburg will soon get a new station beneath your feet. The glass terminal itself was designed by the Norwegian Niels Torp and won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 1996. In Nordstan, the shopping centre, is Emotrappan, the Emo Stairs, where punks and hard rockers gathered as far back as the 1980s. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Nils Ericsonsplatsen. Nils Ericsonsplatsen is named after Nils Ericson, who built Sweden's first main railway lines. He was the brother of the inventor John Ericsson. Beneath us, Västlänken, the West Link, a railway tunnel under central Gothenburg, is being built. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen No: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nockeby. St Birgitta's Church was built in 1960–1962 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, the bell tower and the parish hall next to it. In Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius also built his own villa in 1930, one of the first built according to the new ideals of functionalism. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Nockebyhov. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Norsborg. You can't get further west than this on the metro: Norsborg is the westernmost station in the whole network and has been the terminus of the red line since 1975. A short walk away is the Botkyrka poorhouse, built in 1798 and used as a poorhouse until 1911, and then as an old people's home and nursing home. Since 1998 schoolchildren have sat in the building, where Botkyrka friskola, an independent school, now holds its lessons. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ny: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Nybroplan. At Nybroplan stands Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, inaugurated in 1908. This is where Strandvägen begins, with its grand turn-of-the-century buildings along the water, and from Nybrokajen quay boats head out into the archipelago. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Nyfors. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Nä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Nämdöstigen. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Näsbovägen.  Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Näsbypark. Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, reached here in 1937, when Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where the branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive residential areas, with villas and terraced houses close to the water by Stora Värtan bay. Right next to the station is Näsbypark Church, which belongs to Täby parish. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Näset. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Od: We'll soon reach the final stop, Odenplan. At Odenplan stands Gustav Vasa church. A short distance away, on Sveavägen, is the Stockholm Public Library, designed by Gunnar Asplund and famous for its round lending hall. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Op: We'll soon reach the final stop, Opaltorget. We're in Tynnered, where the streets are named after gemstones: Opaltorget, Smaragdgatan and Briljantgatan – Opal Square, Emerald Street and Diamond Street. From here it's not far to nature reserves and sea bathing in Västra Frölunda. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Or: We'll soon reach the final stop, Orhem. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pa: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Paradistorget. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Parksidan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Partille centrum. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pe: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pelikanvägen. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Peppareds torg. A little way from here stands an old barn that has become a theatre. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is the stage for six amateur theatre societies. Since 1998 it has offered revues and comedies, mainly by young people, and there's even an English theatre group in the house. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Peppargatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Persiljegatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pi: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pilotvägen. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Po: We'll soon reach the final stop, Polhemsplatsen. Polhemsplatsen got its name in 1883, after the inventor Christopher Polhem. Here stands the GP building, which the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten moved into in 1935 and which is still the main building of the Stampen media group. A stone's throw away is the statue of footballer Gunnar Gren, one of the Gre-No-Li trio and one of Gothenburg's most successful footballers of the 20th century. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Pu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Pumpgatan. The shipbuilding giant Götaverken was based here right up until 1991, and the shipyard halls live on as sports halls. Kanalhuset, by the water, was designed for the camera company Hasselblad, which moved out after a short time. Today SVT and Swedish Radio broadcast from there. And Lundbybadet, the public baths from 1915, became a karate club when the last bath attendant, Ante Melander, went home in 1973. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ra: We'll soon reach the final stop, Radiohuset. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Rannebergen Centrum. Rannebergen sits high up and close to nature. Just a few minutes away is the forest lake Idtjärnet, 109 metres above sea level, and a bit further away Stora Mölnesjön, a lake with a swimming spot and a jetty. The centre itself, with a swimming pool and a pizzeria, was built in 1974 and has the Bohusleden hiking trail and the Vättlefjäll hills right on its doorstep. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Re: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Redbergsplatsen. Redbergsplatsen square used to be called Korsvägen and got its current name in 1883. In 1873 a public water pump was set up here, where people could enjoy water from Lake Delsjön. Just north of the square, in Redbergslids Folkpark, a people's park, a pavilion with a stage for performers went up in 1886. Below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, stands the bronze fountain group Elementens kamp, the Struggle of the Elements, moved here from Olskrokstorget in 1968. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Reimersholme. Reimersholme is a small island named after Anders Reimers, who owned it in the 1700s. For a long time there was a schnapps distillery here, and the name Reimersholms lived on on the bottles. Today the island is a quiet residential area with a waterfront promenade all the way around. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ri: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rinkeby centrum. Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg enlarged small Viking Age finds, dug up in the area, into big wall mosaics on brick-red walls with gold inlays and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was inaugurated. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Rissne. Rissne is the only metro station in Stockholm with its name carved in runes. The name also appears on a runestone in Sigtuna, raised in memory of ‘Gunnar's son in Risnö’. In 1640 Rissne gård was bought by Reinhold Goevert Leuhusen, secretary at the Admiralty Board. Today the Rissne estate is a restaurant and conference venue. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ro: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Rondovägen. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Ropsten. From Ropsten, the Lidingöbanan line runs over Lidingöbron bridge out to Lidingö. The bridge opened in 1925 and was for a long time the only land connection to the island. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ru: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ruddammen. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Rudsjöterrassen. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ry: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rymdtorget Buss. Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe, such as Tellusgatan. By the square is Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house, with a library, café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. It offers everything from music and art to crafts and children's events. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Rö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Rörby FRA. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Rörby gård. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen S:: We'll soon reach the final stop, S:t Eriksplan. Behind the triangular park lies one of Stockholm's most talked-about unsolved crimes. On 4 May 1932, Lilly Lindeström was found murdered in her flat at Sankt Eriksplan 11, in what is known as the Vampire Murder. Brighter memories are found round the corner: the Capitol cinema from 1926 closed in 1985 but reopened in 2018 as Bio & Bistro Capitol. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Saltholmen, porten till Göteborgs södra skärgård. From here, ferries run to car-free islands such as Brännö, Styrsö and Vrångö, and the boats are included in the same ticket as the tram. Take a dip at the open-air bathhouse or hop on the next boat. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Saltholmen. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Saltängen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sankt Sigfrids Plan. Örgryte Old Cemetery dates back to the 13th century, and many well-known Gothenburg figures are buried here, among them three bishops. The old church is one of the city's most popular churches for ceremonies, with around sixty weddings a year. By the main entrance stands the bronze statue Genomkämpat, 'The Struggle Is Over', whose original is in a cemetery in Berlin. And where the old ossuary once stood, the wholesale merchant Julius Lindström was granted a family grave in 1870, in return for paying for a new ossuary. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Se: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Sergels torg. Sergels torg is Stockholm's modern centre, with the black-and-white pattern known as Plattan and the glass obelisk in the middle of the fountain. Kulturhuset, the House of Culture, with a library and exhibitions, is on the square. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Servicehuset Tor. The Holmia district was founded in 1906 by the new company AB Lidingö Villastad, and it still has a well-preserved early 20th-century setting, with villas in National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. This is where you'll find Lidingö museum, in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions about Lidingö in the 20th century and a turn-of-the-century salon. The museum is run by Lidingö's local heritage society, one of the largest in Sweden, which among other things organises Bellman Day. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Si: We'll soon reach the final stop, Sickla udde. Much of the land around Hammarby sjö lake didn't exist a hundred years ago. In 1925 a new canal was blasted at the Danvik cliffs, and the level of Hammarby sjö dropped by about five metres. The new shoreline was filled in with blasted rock. There, Lugnet grew up, an area of car workshops and small industry. Today Hammarby sjöstad stands here, built between 1994 and 2020. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sickla. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Sillvik. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sk: We'll soon reach the final stop, Skarpnäck. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Skarpnäcks gård. The village of Skarpa is first mentioned as early as 1318, and the Skarpnäck manor estate was created in 1660 by Maria Sofia De la Gardie of Tyresö Palace. The current main building was put up in the 1860s by the German brewer Friedrich Rudolph Neumüller, and under him the estate enjoyed its heyday. The district was formed in 1963 from Pungpinan and Skarpnäck, and the metro station, opened in 1994, sits in a rock cavern 25 metres underground. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Skintebo. In the middle of a Swedish villa area on the coast there's a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion pleasure palace. Skintebo in Billdal was farmland for a long time, but in the 1970s Skintebodalen was built up with car-free walkways, terraced houses, two-storey wooden houses and so-called boatswain's houses, a funny mix of terraced house and villa. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Skoga äldrecentrum. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Skogome.  Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. The farm and inn of Sandsborg gave its name to both a cemetery and a metro station here in Gamla Enskede. A little way off is the Museum of the Visually Impaired, in premises that once belonged to the Technical Factory for the Blind, with collections on the history of visually impaired people in Sweden going all the way back to the late 18th century. And inside Skogskyrkogården awaits Almhöjden, the Elm Hill, a mound of umbrella elms reminiscent of a painting by Caspar David Friedrich. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skra Bro. The name Skra Bro is said to come from the scraping sound of sledge runners scraping against the ground in a thaw. The old bridge over Osbäcken stream is still there right next to it, but today it's just a footbridge between the park-and-ride car park and a grocery shop. Car traffic now goes over a bigger road bridge north of the roundabout. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Skälltorpsvägen. A short distance from here is Lillhagsparken hospital, originally Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. No care is provided there any longer; the forensic psychiatric unit moved out in 2013. Closer to the stop stood Hökälla manor, an old estate in Skogome. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skärholmen. Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen Centre on 8 September 1968. It was planned as a regional shopping centre for 250,000 people in southern Greater Stockholm and is still counted among Sweden's largest shopping centres. The centre was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, and is included in the SOS Brutalism database of brutalist concrete architecture. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Skärvik. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Skårs Kyrka. Right next door it smells of Christmas all year round. Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, was established in 1924 and nowadays bakes just one thing: gingerbread biscuits with a hint of citrus, to a secret recipe. The shop on Sankt Sigfridsgatan has its original interior from 1940, and the bakery has received a diploma from the Gastronomic Academy for its unrivalled gingerbread. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Sköndalsbro. Sköndalsbro was once a croft, a small tenant farm, and its main building was probably put up sometime between 1700 and 1750, or later. The surrounding streets are a little architecture museum: Eskil Sundahl designed Villa Sundahl as his own home, and the architect couple Hanna and Roy Victorson built Villa Victorson. Both houses, from 1955 and 1958 respectively, are marked blue by the City Museum for their exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sl: We'll soon reach the final stop, Slussen. Slussen is where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic waters of Saltsjön, and where Södermalm meets Gamla stan, the Old Town. There have been locks here since the 17th century, and right now the whole area is being rebuilt in one of Stockholm's largest construction projects. From the quays you can look out towards Gamla stan, Skeppsholmen and Djurgården. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Slåttervägen. Right next door is Viksjö gård, a manor and former noble estate that in the 1600s was held by, among others, the Skytte family. The manor sits on a hill, and modern Viksjö has spread out around it across the former fields. A little further away, in Jakobsberg, Järfällabadet swimming centre opened in 2018, replacing the old pool from 1971, which had a 48-metre-long water slide. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sn: We'll soon reach the final stop, Snipen. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen So: We'll soon reach the final stop, Solbacka. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Solgård. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sollentuna station. Along Malmvägen stand ten high-rises with 1,247 flats, which is why the street is called 'Tian', 'the Ten'. The service building was designed by Åke Arell and attracted international attention when it opened in 1972. Preschools, shops and club premises were gathered on the ground floor. By the square rises the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipality and, since 2023, also the library. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Solna centrum. Deep beneath your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, lies the metro station, which opened in 1975. Above it awaits one of the Stockholm region's largest shopping centres, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen is Eric Grates park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. That is where his bronze sculptures Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God, stand. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Solna station. At Råsundavägen 45 there was once a cinema called the Savoy. In 1974 the auditorium became the Marcus Music recording studio, according to Studio Sound magazine the first in Sweden with a 24-track tape recorder. Abba recorded most of The Album here in 1977. Today the studio is called Soundtrade Studios, and over the years artists such as Robyn and Joey Tempest have recorded here. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Solna strand.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sp: We'll soon reach the final stop, Spånga station. The name Spånga appears in writing as early as the year 1300, as "apud Ecclesiam spangar". It comes from the old church village and simply means "spångar", several narrow footbridges. The station is on the Mälarbanan railway, just over eleven kilometres from the Central Station. A little further away is Svandammen, the Swan Pond, a park with a bathing spot where both young people and families with children like to gather. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen St: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Stenhuggarevägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Stenpiren. Now we're heading down towards Göta älv, the Göta River, and Stenpiren pier. During the 1800s and early 1900s, more than a million Swedes left the country to seek a new life in America, and most of them travelled via Gothenburg. Many of them boarded their ships right here. Today the Älvsnabben ferry crosses the river from here, and it's included in the same ticket as the tram. On the other side you can see Lindholmen and Eriksberg, where the city's big shipyards once stood. Thanks for travelling with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sticklinge. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Stockholms östra. Next to the station is Nymble, the engineering students' union building from 1930, designed by Sven Markelius and Uno Åhrén. In Gasqueparken, with its fountain, the students have celebrated their gasques, formal student dinners, ever since. On the other side of Valhallavägen is Lärkstaden, where the architects Per Olof Hallman and Erik Josephson designed villas for themselves around 1910. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Storkällan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Strandbergsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Strömdal. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Stuvsta station. Häradsvägen, which ends a little way from here at the Stuvsta tunnel, was laid out in the mid-1920s as a relief work project by the road association of Svartlösa härad, the old district, and that's where the name comes from. Forest had to be cleared to get through, and villas sprang up along the road. The tunnel itself is unusual: its northern entrance is built into an apartment building that straddles the approach. Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Styrsö Bratten. Styrsö is one of the largest islands in the southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has bathing coves, meadows and old fishing villages. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Styrsö Tången. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Stärtered. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Su: We'll soon reach the final stop, Sundbybergs station. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Sundhammar. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sv: We'll soon reach the final stop, Svalnäs Gästhem. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Svarte Mosse. Thank Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Svedmyra T-stn. Svedmyra metro station, despite its name, isn't in Svedmyra but in Stureby. A stone's throw away is the Svedmyra baths from 1969, where the pool water is kept at a full 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted jumping competitions right up until 1990. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Svingeln. Up on the hill nearby is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Redoubt, a 17th-century fortification with a gilded lion on top. It was built to protect the city from attacks from the east. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sä: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Säteriet. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Sätra äng.  Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Säve Depå. Inside the rock a little way from here hides Aeroseum, an aviation experience centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing air base, one of only five built within the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000, visitors have been able to go down into the bunker and experience aviation history up close. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Säve Flygplats. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Säve Station. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Sö: We'll soon reach the final stop, Södergarnsvägen. The Östra Rudboda terraced-house area was built in the mid-1970s, with just over 450 terraced and linked houses grouped around shared courtyards known as "tun", and today it counts as part of the municipality's culturally and historically valuable buildings. The neighbouring district of Yttringe got its name from the large meadows that have been there for a very long time. A little further away is Gråviken, an important site for seabirds with natural values of national interest. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Södersjukhuset. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Sörgårdsskolan.  Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Sörredsmotet. Western Hisingen is the realm of industry and ports. A little way from here is the Preemraff oil refinery, which buys its crude oil mostly from the North Sea. In the neighbouring district of Arendal, the Arendal shipyard operated between 1963 and 1989, and today it is home to, among other things, the headquarters of Volvo Buses. Arendal is such a purely industrial area that only 90 people lived there in 2012. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Sörskogen. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen T-: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, T-Centralen. Beneath the streets, blue vines and leaves climb over the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and among the tendrils you can see silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was otherwise best known for his mechanical sculptures and helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, 'She – a Cathedral', in 1966. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ta: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Tanto.  Thanks for travelling with us!

We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Tappström. Tappström is a narrow strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön, about 1.5 kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore Ralph Erskine designed Ekerö centrum, completed in 1991, with a "dot" over twenty metres high as its landmark. Erskine himself lived on Lovön and said he liked coming here to shop. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way in to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay. Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Te: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Tekniska högskolan. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Telefonplan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Tengdahlsgatan. Tengdahlsgatan is in Sofia, the easternmost part of Södermalm. From here you can stroll through Vita bergen and SoFo, or down towards the water at Hammarby sjö, Lake Hammarby. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Tensta centrum. If you want to step straight into 1969, there is Kämpingebacken 13, a museum flat rented by the City Museum. The interior is preserved from when it was built and shows what things looked like when Tensta was built during the Million Programme housing drive, between 1966 and 1972. Tensta konsthall, an art centre for contemporary art, is also just a couple of minutes away. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen To: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tomteboda postterminal. The gigantic postal terminal was counted as one of Sweden's largest single buildings, and mail was sorted here from 1983. After the operation closed, others moved in, and in 2021 SL, Stockholm's public transport authority, opened the largest bus depot in the Nordic countries in parts of the building. On the grounds of Tomtebodaskolan, two fragments of a Viking Age runestone were found. One was found in 1903 but probably disappeared before 1911. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Torslandakrysset. It's also called the old airfield: Torslanda Airport, which was built in 1923 a little way from here on the western side of Hisingen island, around 15 kilometres from central Gothenburg. For more than fifty years it was the city's airport, until Landvetter replaced it in 1977. Today Torslanda is best known for Volvo's car factory, Torslandaverken. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Torvmossegränd. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tr: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Trekanten. Lake Trekanten was called Trehörningen until the mid-19th century. On its north side lay Nynäs, a ramshackle working-class suburb with a tannery, a coffee roastery and workshops, and a bakery that baked the locally famous Nynäs loaf. When the houses fell into disrepair, they became the backdrop for Bo Widerberg's 1970 film Joe Hill, where they played the 'Lumberyard' and the 'Saloon'. The last remains were demolished in 1980. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Trollbäckens centrum. Trollbäcken is a borrowed name. The area used to be called Kumla, after the manor by Lake Drevviken, which dates back to the Middle Ages, but in 1947 the villa neighbourhoods changed their name to Trollbäcken so as not to be confused with Kumla in the province of Närke. A couple of hundred metres away is Trollbäcken Church, by county road 260. The manor itself is still called Kumla herrgård, Kumla Manor, and since 2013 it has housed a restaurant and conference centre. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tu: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tulebohöjd. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Tullinge station södra. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Tumba station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ty: We'll soon reach the final stop, Tyresö centrum. The tall building you can see from far away is called Tyresö View. It is 82 metres high with 23 storeys, and in 2016 it was the fourth-tallest residential building in Stockholm County. Under the roof of the glazed shopping centre are around 70 shops, the town hall and a library with its own exhibition hall. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Tyresö kyrka. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Tä: We'll soon reach the final stop, Täby centrum. Täby centrum has 215 shops, 34 restaurants and cafés, and since 2022 the formal name Westfield Täby Centrum. The Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, has five screens with a total of 516 seats. And the library keeps something much older: Viking Age runestone fragments found in Lissby in 1930. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ul: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Ulriksdals begravningsplats. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Un: We'll soon reach the final stop, Universitetet. Deep beneath the campus, research was once done in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the laboratory has been the art space Accelerator, opened by the artist Tino Sehgal. The laboratory is named after Manne Siegbahn, who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1924. Ralph Erskine designed Juristernas hus, the House of Law, as a semicircle around an old oak, and the same idea of saving the oaks can be found at Aula Magna. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ur: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ursviks holme. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Va: We'll soon reach the final stop, Varmfrontsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Varvsvägen. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Vasaplatsen. We are in Vasastaden, with grand stone buildings from the late 1800s. Several of the University of Gothenburg's buildings are also here. Vasaparken, with the university's main building, is right next door. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vi: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Vikdalsvägen. Jarlaberg water tower is 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-eastern Stockholm since it was completed in 1987. A little further away, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899 to build a car factory. But car development moved too fast, so instead the factory made paraffin engines under the name Avance, and they soon became a success. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Virginsgatan. We're approaching Kålltorp, a quiet area of villas and homes in eastern Gothenburg. From here it isn't far to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes and forest. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vo: We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda PVH. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Torslanda RA. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Volvo Torslanda TA. The Torslanda Works, originally the Volvo Torslanda factory, was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Construction began in 1960–1961 in the district of Sörred, whose name has a funny background: the first part, Sör-, is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a negligent man, a sloven or a good-for-nothing. The ending -red comes from the Old Swedish ryd, cleared land. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Volvo Torslanda TK. The stop is by Volvo's car factory, the Torslanda plant. Ground was broken on 4 November 1957, and on 24 April 1964 the factory was opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf. The first car to roll off the line was a Volvo Amazon, and the sporty P1800 was also built here from the start. Today the XC90, among others, is made in Torslanda. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Volvo Tuve L B. At 199 square kilometres, Hisingen makes up roughly half of Gothenburg municipality's area. The island belongs to Västra Götaland County and is Sweden's fifth largest. It is surrounded by water on all sides: Göta älv, Nordre älv and the Kattegat. Roughly a quarter of the island counts as part of Västergötland, the rest as Bohuslän. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Volvohallen. The dome-shaped building is Volvohallen, an exhibition hall that Volvo Cars built in 1975 to designs by Lund & Valentin architects. Volvo's Torslanda plant, Torslandaverken, began to be built in the district of Sörred, a village name recorded as early as 1388 in the form Surfua rudi. Sörred belonged to Björlanda parish until it was incorporated into Gothenburg in 1967. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vr: We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Vrångö. Vrångö is the southernmost inhabited island in the Gothenburg archipelago. There's a nature reserve here with sandy beaches and rocks facing the open sea. Thanks for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vä: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Väderilsgatan. Thanks for riding with us!

We'll soon arrive at the final stop, Vällingby. Vällingby was planned as the ABC town, with work, home and centre – arbete, bostad, centrum – all in one place. It even included its own cinema. The Fontänen cinema opened in 1956 and was named after the fountains in the square. The same year saw the opening of the Trappan civic centre, built in terraces between a lower and an upper square. Both were designed by Backström & Reinius. Thanks for riding with us!
We'll soon reach the final stop, Västra Röd. Thank Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Vå: We'll soon reach the final stop, Vårbergs sjukhem. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Wa: We'll soon reach the final stop, Waldemarsudde. Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen. He was the son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his time. Today his villa and garden are an art museum by the water. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Yn: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Ynglingagatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Yt: We'll soon reach the final stop, Ytterby station. Just a couple of minutes' walk from here are the ruins of Ytterby Old Church. It was built in the 12th century, when this area was Norwegian land, and according to legend it was Saint Olaf who built it. It was the parish church until 1870. The railway station itself, on the Bohusbanan line, is much younger; it opened in 1907. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Äl: We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Älvnäs. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Älvsjö station. Älvsjö gård has very old roots, with known owners since the mid-15th century. One and the same family held the estate for almost two centuries, right up until 1968. For a long time the area was sparsely built up. Around the turn of the 20th century, the population consisted mostly of people who worked on the estate and at the station. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Åk: We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Åkareplatsen.  Thanks for travelling with us!
We'll soon be arriving at the final stop, Åkerby industriområde.  Thanks for travelling with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen År: We'll soon reach the final stop, Årsringsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Årstaberg. Årstalänken offers an unusual sight: the eastern part of this stretch of motorway has been closed since 2004 and is a so-called ruin motorway, where housing is now being planned. Årstaberg commuter train station has around 8,300 people boarding on an ordinary winter weekday, and the Tvärbanan light rail has stopped here since 2000. On Årstaskogs väg rise the Årstahusen, three residential high-rises built between 2017 and 2020. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Öc: We'll soon reach the final stop, Öckerö färjeläge. Thank you for riding with us!
Snart är vi framme vid ändhållplatsen Ös: We'll soon reach the final stop, Österlyckan. Thank you for riding with us!

We'll soon reach the final stop, Östervägen. Artillerigården, the Artillery Yard, has served the artillery's needs since the 1640s, and today it is home to the Army Museum. Beneath the yard hide two air-raid shelters from the Second World War, which are sometimes opened for tours. Round the corner, at Artillerigatan 14, was the Michelin-starred restaurant Gastrologik, where guests got no menu – the chefs decided. Since 2024 the restaurant ergo has occupied the same premises. Thank you for riding with us!
We'll soon arrive at the last stop, Östhammarsgatan. Thank you for riding with us!
Sockenstugan och Bromma kyrka: Sockenstugan, the old parish hall, and Bromma Church
