Sofielundsskolan har ett eget litet kapi: Sofielundsskolan school has its own little chapter in school history: from 1994 the newly founded Sollentuna Fria Gymnasium, an upper secondary school, had temporary premises here for its academic subjects. Right next to it runs Sollentunavägen, which was the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala until Uppsalavägen was built out in the 1950s. A little further away is Sollentuna Hospital, opened in 1978 and completely renovated between 2015 and 2020.
Solgård är ett villaområde söder om Hudd: Solgård is a villa area south of Huddinge centrum, and the view here is something out of the ordinary. From the highest hills, about 60 metres above sea level, you can see all the way to the Globe arena in Stockholm. By car, there are only two ways in. In the forest by Solgårdsvägen there is also a hillfort, Solgårds fornborg.
Sollentuna station, en kort promenad bor: Sollentuna station, a short walk away, is the busiest commuter train station on the Märsta branch, 13.2 kilometres north of Stockholm Central. Here in Tureberg the municipality's centre has been located since the administration moved here from Norrviken in the 1940s. Today you'll find Tureberg Church, the shopping mall and the fifteen-storey Turebergshuset, home to the municipality and, since 2023, also the library.
Sollentunas centrum har flyttat. Från bö: Sollentuna's centre has moved. Originally it was by the church village at Sollentuna Church, then the administration grew up in Norrviken, and in the 1940s it moved to Tureberg. Right next door are Turebergskyrkan church and the remand prison, which opened in 2011 and is part of Rättscentrum Sollentuna, the justice centre. And a couple of hundred metres away was once Sollentunamässan, in its day Sweden's third-largest exhibition centre.
Sollentunas förvaltning låg förr i Norrv: Sollentuna's administration used to be in Norrviken, but in the 1940s it moved here to Tureberg, which has been the municipality's natural centre ever since. A little further away is Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, with sports halls, a music studio, a café and a fully equipped theatre stage. And on Malmvägen stands Tian, 'the Ten', ten high-rises from the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive.
Sollentunavallen ligger i ett gammalt gr: Sollentunavallen lies in an old gravel pit in the Stockholm esker and was opened in connection with the Swedish Athletics Championships in August 1969. The stands hold about 4,500 people, and in winter the artificial turf pitch next to it becomes a bandy rink for Helenelunds IK. A little further away is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to get two Michelin stars.
Sollentunavägen var en gång huvudvägen m: Sollentunavägen was once the main road between Stockholm and Uppsala, before Uppsalavägen was expanded in the 1950s. Nearby rises the fifteen-storey Tureberg Building, Turebergshuset, with the municipal administration and, since 2023, the library too. Arena Satelliten, opened in 2009, has sports halls, a media studio and a theatre stage seating 200.
Solnahallen stod klar 1983, och fasadern: Solnahallen was completed in 1983, and the façades facing east and north are decorated by the artist Per Olov Ultvedt. AIK plays floorball, handball and basketball here, and in the late 1980s the hall hosted national teams such as Cuba, Bulgaria and Germany during the Euro Volley volleyball tournament. The hall is also used for concerts.
Solsunda hette fram till 1922 Skuru gård: Until 1922 Solsunda was called Skuru gård, and in the 16th century King Gustav Vasa gave the farm to Danvik hospital, so that the rent would help pay the hospital's expenses. Since the early 20th century, the manor house has served as a rest and treatment home. Little Bastusjön lake nearby has perch, roach and two kinds of freshwater mussel.
Som en skärgård på land: begravningsplat: Like an archipelago on land: the cemetery here opened in October 2024 and is shaped like small islands, each island its own burial section, with a reflecting pool in the middle of the landscape. Its neighbour is Granholmstoppen, an old rubbish tip that has grown into a hill 49 metres above sea level, built up from earth excavated during the construction of the blue metro line and the surrounding districts. According to the drivers who built it, though, a bit of everything got dumped there.
Spana in Tomtehuset vid Vasagatan: Check out Tomtehuset, the Gnome House, on Vasagatan
Spana in soffan på möbelhusets tak: Spot the sofa on the furniture store's roof
Sporthallen en kort promenad bort, Botky: The sports hall a short walk away, Botkyrkahallen, has both royal glamour and everyday use: it was opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf in the summer of 2000 and also serves as the sports hall for Brunnaskolan school. Balrog IK's men's team plays here in front of up to 1,500 spectators. A little way in the other direction is Slagsta gård, a historic manor and former noble estate.
Spånga IP är en riktig allt-i-ett-anlägg: Spånga IP is a real all-in-one sports centre: an ice rink, an indoor football hall, a bandy rink, street basketball and athletics tracks. In snowy winters, cross-country ski tracks are even laid on the running track. A little way off was once Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large graffiti painting, until the wall was demolished in December 2021.
Spånga är ett riktigt gammalt namn. Det: Spånga is a really old name. It appears in writing as early as the year 1300, in Latin as apud Ecclesiam spangar, and refers to the old church village. The name is simply the plural of the word "spång", a footbridge. Today Spånga is an informal area that roughly corresponds to the districts of Bromsten, Flysta, Solhem, Lunda and Sundby.
Spårvagnarna under Frölunda torg en bit: The trams under Frölunda torg, a little way from here, originally ran into a completely underground stop when it was built in 1966, but in 2008 it was partly opened up to the outside world. Next to the square was also Frölunda specialist hospital, opened in 1968, which was replaced in early 2024 by the new Högsbo local hospital. Closest by are Tynnered Church and Smycketorget square.
Spårvagnen kom hit redan hösten 1929, in: The tram arrived here as early as autumn 1929, before the square existed. The square itself was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza, a typical garden-city square. The town plan was approved in 1932 and is signed by Albert Lilienberg. All around spreads Nockeby, part of the Bromma garden city.
Spårvägsmuseet i Norra Djurgårdsstaden v: The Tramway Museum in Norra Djurgårdsstaden shows how public transport in the Stockholm area has developed all the way from the 1650s to the present day, at sea as well. Right next to it is Husarviken bay, whose name has nothing to do with hussars: it comes from the village of Husarnæ, mentioned in 1288, and should therefore be stressed on the first syllable. Since 2018 the Husarviken bridge, a bascule bridge for pedestrians and cyclists, has crossed the bay.
Stadsarkivet Liljeholmskajen: Stadsarkivet, the City Archives, at Liljeholmskajen
Stadsdelen Backa, ofta kallad Hisings Ba: The district of Backa, often called Hisings Backa, is no small place: 1,473 hectares, from Brunnsbo in the south, via Backa in the middle, to Skälltorp in the north. Backa was once a rural municipality of its own in what was then Gothenburg and Bohus County. A little way from here is Selma Lagerlöfs torg, the local centre of northern Backa.
Stadsdelen Gubbängen har fått sitt namn: The Gubbängen district takes its name from Gubbängens gård, a croft that later became an independent farm and was demolished in 1965. Nearby stretches Gubbängsparken, a landscaped park of almost twelve hectares with a supervised playground. A little further away, south of Skogskyrkogården, is the Southern Jewish Cemetery, which came into use in 1952.
Stadsdelen Larsboda ligger klämd mellan: The Larsboda district is squeezed between Nynäsvägen and Magelungsvägen, and just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, 73 metres high. A little further away, by Lake Drevviken, is Hökarängsbadet, with a sandy beach about 60 metres long, a bathing jetty, a large meadow and rocks for sunbathing. There's also a barbecue area and a café for anyone who wants to stay a while.
Stadsdelen Rud har ett namn som berättar: The Rud district has a name that speaks of hard work: it comes from the Old Swedish rýdh and means a cleared place. The village is recorded as early as 1495 as Rudh. A little way from here is Ruddalens IP, a sports ground with room for 3,000 spectators. The first match was played in 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF met IFK Malmö, and the arena has seen several seasons in Allsvenskan, Sweden's top football league.
The district of Syrhåla has an honest name. It is recorded from 1550 and means 'swampy place' or 'sour ground', after the low, damp land between the hills. Syrhåla became a district of its own in 1957, when Arendal was split in two. Arendal itself is today a purely industrial and logistics area, where Volvo Buses, among others, has its headquarters.
Stadsdelen Torp har fått sitt namn efter: The district of Torp is named after two old farms. Lilla Torp was built in 1748 by Bengt Wilhelm Carlberg, and a little way from here is the manor Stora Torp, dating back to the 1550s. Back then the estate was called Torpit, and the tenant farmers there were under Sten Eriksson Leijonhufvud's estate Kärra. After his bloody end in 1568, the farm passed to his widow, Gref Ebba.
Stadsdelen Vinsta är en ganska ung skape: The district of Vinsta is a fairly young creation. The City of Stockholm bought the land from Spånga in 1949, and four years later the district was established and named after the old village of Vinsta. On its 1.67 square kilometres it today includes, among other things, an industrial area with Vällingby fire station, designed by the architect Mårten J. Larsson and opened in 1965.
Stadsdelen bildades 1954 och gränsar öve: The district was formed in 1954 and borders Ekerö municipality across the waters of Lake Mälaren. On the street Strandliden stand 16 slab blocks from the second half of the 1950s, which the City Museum has green-listed for their cultural, historical and artistic value. In the middle of the centre, on Maltesholmstorget, is Hässelby Strand Church.
Stadsdelen har fått sitt namn efter ett: The district is named after a small croft under Hammarby gård, and the croft cottage is actually still there in the southern part of Kärrtorpsparken. Near the square is the Reflexen cinema, opened in 1961 and today run by volunteers from a cultural association, which shares the premises with Teater Reflex. In the metro station glows Björn Olsén's artwork Ljuslådor med hemliga tecken, Light Boxes with Secret Signs, unveiled in 1994.
Stadshuset invigdes 1923 och är en av St: Stockholm City Hall was inaugurated in 1923 and is one of Stockholm's symbols. The Nobel Banquet is held here every December in the Blue Hall, and from the tower you have a wide view over Riddarfjärden bay and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Stallbacken är ett passande namn, för hä: Stallbacken, "Stable Hill", is a fitting name, because this is where Åby Travgymnasium is, a trotting upper secondary school that started in autumn 2005 and takes students from all over Sweden and the Nordic countries who want to work with harness racing or riding. The school is at Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track. A little further away you can swap hoofbeats for film music at Fässbergs Bio, a cinema with 400 seats in a converted school assembly hall.
Statarmuseet, Överjärva gård: Statarmuseet, the farm workers' museum, at Överjärva gård
Stationen öppnade 1890 och fick el redan: The station opened in 1890 and got electricity as early as 1895. In the early 1950s it was Sweden's busiest station for trains, with about 340 trains a day, freight trains included. Back then, trains ran in four directions. The villas round about began to be built in 1896, when Djursholms AB sold plots near the station. In the 1970s and 80s, the whole Roslagsbanan railway was threatened with closure.
Stationen öppnade 1890 och hette först D: The station opened in 1890 and was first called Djursholm, then Ösby, and from 1920 Djursholms Ösby. As early as 1895 the line was electrified. With trains in four directions and about 340 trains a day, freight included, it was once counted as Sweden's busiest station for trains. The villas around it began to be built in 1896, when plots were sold near the station.
Stationen öppnade 1937, när Roslagsbanan: The station opened in 1937, when the Roslagsbanan railway was extended to Näsbypark. At first it was called Alléparken, but the name was changed after just four months. Here the trains run on single track with a single platform. By the Näsbyviken bay is Näsby Castle, today a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant.
Stationen öppnade 1944 som spårvagnshåll: The station opened in 1944 as a tram stop on the Ängby line and was then called Färjestadsvägen. It became a metro station in 1952 and wasn't named Ängbyplan until 1962. A little way from here, as early as the 16th century, lay Karsvik farm, on the shore of the now vanished Lake Ängbysjön. Today the Mälaren Scouts are based in Karsvik's meadow. And nearby Ängby torg square got its official name as late as 2005.
Stationsnamnet är en ledtråd. En kort bi: The station name is a clue. A short distance away was Täby Galopp, Scandinavia's largest gallop racecourse, which King Gustaf VI Adolf opened in 1960 as a replacement for the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, and the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track used to be, the new district of Täby Park is now taking shape, planned for around 20,000 residents.
Statyn Avskedet på polarisen: The statue Avskedet, The Farewell, on the polar ice
Statyn mitt på platsen föreställer Karl: The statue in the middle of the square shows Karl IX, King Charles IX, on horseback, but Gothenburgers call it Kopparmärra, the Copper Mare. It was put up in 1904. This is where Kungsportsavenyn, the city's grand avenue, begins, and on the canal next to it run the flat Paddan sightseeing boats, which have to duck under the city's low bridges. A short distance away is Stora Saluhallen, the big market hall, from 1889.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö m: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö island in the middle of Lake Mälaren, is best known for its disused 19th-century quarry and the industrial village that grew up around it. The neighbouring village of Törnby is much older than that: it is first mentioned as early as 1342, in connection with a land exchange with Vårfruberga convent, and has now grown together with Stenhamra.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö,: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö, is best known for its disused 19th-century stone quarry and the company town that went with it. If you want to go even further back in time, you can seek out the runestone U 32, which stands in a patch of forest just under a kilometre from the centre. Ekerö municipality, by the way, consists of a group of islands in Lake Mälaren that have long been called Mälaröarna, the Mälaren Islands.
Stensö har fått sitt namn efter en halvö: Stensö is named after a peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip is the Stensö bathing spot. Through the area runs Ältavägen, laid out in 1934, which winds just over eight kilometres through the undeveloped landscape between Älta and Nackanäs. A little way off, inside the Flaten nature reserve, people race radio-controlled model cars.
Sticklinge på nordvästra Lidingö är beka: Sticklinge in north-western Lidingö is familiar to everyone who has run the Lidingöloppet cross-country race, because the course goes straight through the area. South of the houses stretches the Sticklinge nature reserve, 108 hectares of forest, coast and grassland, protected since 2021. By Rödstuguviken bay stands Rödstugan, a house with roots in the 17th century where crofters, ferrymen and farm labourers' families have lived.
Stjärnbildsgatan, en bit härifrån, fick: Stjärnbildsgatan, a little way from here, got an unusual makeover: the four-storey blocks were rebuilt so radically that the upper floors were removed, leaving terraced houses around spacious courtyards. Nearby, the Intercultural Folk High School, Interkulturella folkhögskolan, started in 2007, the first folk high school in the Nordic countries for Roma students, opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
Stjärnhusen i Gröndal byggdes av Olle En: The Star Houses in Gröndal were built by Olle Engkvist to designs by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the architectural historian Fredric Bedoire counts them among Stockholm's finest groups of buildings. The area is of national interest and a textbook example of folkhem architecture, from the era of the Swedish welfare state. And after the architecture comes fika, the Swedish coffee break: Lundbergs konditori has been in the same corner under the same name since 1946.
Stockholms frihamn öppnade som ett provi: Stockholm's free port, Frihamnen, opened as a temporary arrangement in 1919 and kept expanding right up to the 1970s. During the same period, between 1921 and 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the free port now lies. The Ford Building, designed by Uno Åhrén, was built from 1929 to 1931 as an assembly plant for Ford cars, and today the listed company Nasdaq has its home there. The enormous Magasin 6 warehouse, on the other hand, quickly became outdated when container traffic took over.
Stockholms stad köpte egendomen Gubbänge: The City of Stockholm bought the Gubbängen estate in 1908 from the farmer Albin Arvidsson, but it wasn't until the 1940s that building got under way. The district's original core consisted of two farms, Herrängen Farm and Gubbängen Farm, and neither of them remains. The metro arrived here on 1 October 1950, when the Slussen–Hökarängen metro line opened.
Stockholms största koloniområde ligger a: Stockholm's largest allotment area is right nearby, with no fewer than 554 allotment plots with cottages. It was laid out in three stages, in 1936, 1939 and 1941, to replace several allotment areas in the southern suburbs that were demolished during the 1920s and 1930s. In the neighbourhood is also the small-cottage area Pungpinan, where the houses on Lugna Gatan began to be built as early as 1927.
Stockholms ånglokssällskap: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the steam locomotive society
Stockholms ånglokssällskap bevarar och r: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm Steam Locomotive Society, preserves and restores old railway vehicles and began in 1974 with an emergency reserve locomotive bought from SJ, the Swedish state railways. The society was first based at Tomteboda and then at the slaughterhouse area, but when the Globe arena was to be built it had to move in 1988 to an industrial siding here in Västberga. Midsommarkransens skola nearby was an elementary school between 1915 and 1962.
Stockholmsmässan hette Älvsjömässan fram: Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, was called Älvsjömässan until 1976 and is today Sweden's largest exhibition and congress venue, with around seventy fairs a year and just over a million visitors. In spring 2020 the halls were given a completely different purpose, when the field hospital Älvsjö sjukhus was set up in the exhibition centre.
Stockholmsvägen är en av Lidingös äldsta: Stockholmsvägen is one of Lidingö's oldest roads, and the municipality calls it Lidingö's historic lifeline. Along it are Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, three tower blocks from the 1950s and 1960s, the oldest of which is marked by the city museum for its very high cultural and historical value. A little further away rises Lidingö Arena, an office and retail building from the 1970s by the architect Bo Möller, with such a striking design that it has become a landmark.
Stocksund är rikt på arkitektvillor. Vil: Stocksund is rich in architect-designed villas. Villa Gärdsgården was built in 1904 to 1905 to designs by Ragnar Östberg, commissioned by the artist Alf Wallander. Villa Tallom was built in 1904 to 1906 by the architect Lars Israel Wahlman as a home for himself and his family, and has been a listed building since 1979.
Stocksundet förbinder Lilla Värtan med E: Stocksundet links Lilla Värtan with Edsviken bay and forms the border between Danderyd and Solna. Stocksund station used to be closer to the harbour, with tracks down there for transferring goods to ships. The harbour also had the power station that supplied the Djursholm railway with electricity, and the Långängsbanan tramway started from the station.
Stora Essingen är en 73 hektar stor ö i: Stora Essingen is a 73-hectare island in Lake Mälaren, and its highest point, Kungsklippan, reaches 41 metres above sea level. On the island's second-highest point stands Essinge church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. The neighbourhood cinema Orkanen opened close by in 1938, and the two apartment buildings on Badstrandsvägen were named Byggindustrihuset after the construction company AB Byggindustri that built them.
Stora Essingens sommarvillor från 1700-t: The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 20th century. Things really took off when the Essinge bridge opened in 1929. In 1966 came Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing huge traffic jams.
Stora Förö är genom landhöjningen numera: Because of land uplift, Stora Förö has now grown together with Lilla Förö via a narrow isthmus. The island has a burial cairn and finds from the Stone Age. When the master carpenter Axel Hellqvist came here on a boat trip in 1927, there wasn't a single tree, because the island had long been used for sheep grazing and timber cutting.
Stora Kåsjön är Partille kommuns största: Stora Kåsjön is the largest lake in Partille municipality, just over a square kilometre in size and a full 32 metres deep. It lies high up, about 109 metres above sea level, and is also the municipality's drinking water source. All around are more small lakes, such as Haketjärnen in the Natura 2000 area Maderna-Haketjärn.
Stora Saluhallen vid Kungstorget: Stora Saluhallen, the market hall, on Kungstorget
Stora Sjötullen: Stora Sjötullen, the old customs house
Stora Ursvik gränsar mot Kymlinge, Lilla: Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. A little way from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the windmill Stora Stampan. Its companion Holländskan burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was renovated over the winter of 2019 to 2020 and now has new sails.
Stora delar av grannområdet Ekängen bygg: Large parts of the neighbouring area of Ekängen were built in the 1940s with small single-family villas, and it is still a quiet residential area north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further away is Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005, with a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round. Perfect if you want to swap town-centre life for a lap around the lake.
Storholmen i sjön Trehörningen var en gå: Storholmen in Lake Trehörningen was once a real island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots that were mostly sold to workers from Stockholm, and a footbridge was built to the mainland. Around twenty small summer cottages sprang up. Today most of it is forest and shores open to everyone, and the lake is rich in fish, birds such as the lesser spotted woodpecker, and even bats.
Storskogstorget invigdes 1958 och formga: Storskogstorget opened in 1958 and was designed in the spirit of the time by the landscape architect N.H. Orénto, with seating areas, greenery and two ponds. From here you can also reach Näckrosen metro station, the only one in the metro with exits in two municipalities. A little further away is Filmstaden in Råsunda, the film studios where nearly 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973, and which are especially associated with Ingmar Bergman.
Storängens industriområde, alldeles i nä: Construction of the Storängen industrial area, right nearby, began in the early 1950s, just under a kilometre south-east of Huddinge centrum. Now the area faces a transformation. According to a plan from 2009, it is eventually to become a mixed-use district, mostly with housing and businesses that fit well alongside residents. The area is also home to Storängshallen, a hall for athletics and gymnastics.
Storängshallen alldeles intill, invigd 2: Storängshallen right next door, opened in 2007, is a hall mainly for athletics and gymnastics. The area has a funny history. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård launched Huddinge villastad, a project for a whole new garden suburb of villas. Only a few of the old villas remain, and right where the villa town was meant to be, Huddinge centrum stands today.
Strandvägen, promenad längs vattnet: Strandvägen, a walk along the water
Strawberry Arena, som invigdes under nam: Strawberry Arena, which opened under the name Friends Arena, is Sweden's national stadium for the men's football team and since 2013 has hosted the finals of Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection. For concerts it holds up to 65,000 people. Next door is a 25-storey hotel whose round windows are meant to remind you of footballs, and Mall of Scandinavia has an IMAX cinema with Sweden's largest screen, almost 22 metres wide.
Strax härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget,: Just from here is Hammarkulletorget, designed by White Architects and built in 1971. Beneath the square is Sweden's only completely underground tram stop. It was built with the Stockholm metro as its model, because in the 1970s there actually were plans for a metro all the way out to Angered. That's why it's sometimes called Gothenburg's only metro station.
Strax intill inträffade Tuveraset, en av: Right nearby, the Tuve landslide happened, one of the worst natural disasters in Sweden in modern times. At 4.09 pm on 30 November 1977, the ground in Tuve collapsed in a massive landslide. The landslide claimed nine lives. It's also called Raset i Tuve or Tuveskredet.
Strax intill ligger Arken kombiterminal: Right next to us is the Arken combi terminal in Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are transferred between ships and trains. It replaced the terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to move when the Västlänken rail tunnel was built. Work began in January 2018 and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019.
Strax intill ligger Fässbergs kyrkogård,: Right next to it is Fässberg cemetery, with 4,800 graves and a chapel from 1936. A little further away is Fässbergs Bio, a cinema with 400 seats in the converted assembly hall Fässbergssalen, which opened in January 2013 and is run by the municipality. The upper secondary school where the hall is located was once one of Sweden's 20 schools with specialist elite programmes.
Strax intill ligger Hult Åsens naturvård: Right next to it is the Hult Åsen nature conservation area, a stretch of high ground with pine, birch and bare rock. It was set aside in 1994, covers ten hectares and is managed by the City of Gothenburg. A little further away is Askims torg square in the heart of the district of Askim, which faces Askimsfjorden bay.
Strax intill ligger Kvibergsnäs landeri,: Right next door is Kvibergsnäs landeri, a country estate between Kviberg and Gamlestaden. The present buildings were put up in the first half of the 19th century. Kvibergsnäs is something of a survivor: it is the only country estate in Gothenburg where both the house and the barns remain.
Strax intill ligger Lillhagsparkens sjuk: Right next to us is Lillhagsparken hospital, which was originally called Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just said Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. No care is provided here any longer; the forensic psychiatric unit moved to Rågården in 2013.
Strax intill ligger Mariakyrkan i Hammar: Right next to here is Mariakyrkan in Hammarkullen, a church shared between the Uniting Church in Sweden and the Angered parish, previously called Tomaskyrkan. Nearby there was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a cinema with 200 seats. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget, where you go for Gothenburg's only underground tram station.
Strax intill ligger Motorbranschens tekn: Right next door is the Motor Industry Technical Upper Secondary School, where the vehicle and transport programme is at the centre. A little way from here is Västra Frölunda Cemetery, with medieval roots, where the old Västra Frölunda Church stood until it was demolished in the 1860s. Iron rings meant for horses are still set into the cemetery wall – a kind of parking from days gone by.
Strax intill ligger Nylöse kyrka, som ti: Right next to it is Nylöse Church, which used to be called Gamlestadens kapell. A little further away on Gamlestadsvägen is Göteborgs Hospitalskyrkogård, the hospital cemetery, which has existed since the late 1500s. Today only the odd gravestone remains, but the site is protected under the Cultural Environment Act, and a Franciscan friary also once stood here.
Strax intill ligger Rudboda gård, ett ti: Right nearby is Rudboda gård, a former croft that has given its name to the whole district. Along Elfviksvägen stands Villa Molin, which Ralph Erskine designed in 1947 for the garden architect Ulla Molin. A little way off is Kyrkviken, with the older name Koltorpsviken, the narrow sea inlet that divides Lidingö into a northern and a southern part.
Strax intill ligger Råda säteri, en herr: Right next door is Råda säteri, a manor by Lake Rådasjön with a main building, wings and old farm buildings, listed since 1969. The lake itself is up to 23 metres deep and serves as Mölndal's source of drinking water. The Mölndalsån river flows straight through it and further downstream changes its name to Gullbergsån, so the water here carries on all the way into Gothenburg.
Strax intill ligger Solvalla, Sveriges n: Right next to us is Solvalla, Sweden's national arena for harness racing and the largest trotting track in the Nordic countries. Every year Elitloppet is run here, one of the world's biggest trotting races, and the stands hold 35,000 visitors. The track opened on 31 July 1927, and twelve races were run in its first year.
Strax intill ligger Tuve kyrka, en av Gö: Right next to us is Tuve Church, one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Since 2010 it has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish. The old Tuve parish was counted as part of Västergötland and the Östra Hising hundred, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000, just over 10,000 people lived in the parish.
Strax intill låg Karlsrofältet, en idrot: Right next to here was Karlsrofältet, a sports ground for nearly sixty years. The name goes back to the iron carrier Carl Jonsson and appears as Carlsro as early as 1834. A little further on begins the Botanical Garden, which opened in 1923 in connection with the Jubilee Exhibition but was only considered finished in 1948. Its symbol is a wood anemone, and it has two stars in the Michelin tourist guide.
Strax intill reser sig Fässbergs kyrka p: Right nearby, Fässberg Church rises on its hill. Between 1922 and 1976 it was called Mölndal Church, because that year the old Fässberg parish became the town of Mölndal. The parish had medieval origins, and Gunnebo House also lies within it. A stone's throw away is Fässbergs Bio, a cinema with 400 seats in a converted assembly hall.
Strax intill rinner Tappström, sundet me: Right nearby flows Tappström, the strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön. It's about 1.5 kilometres long but only 3.2 metres deep. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for leisure boats, and the bridge here carries Ekerövägen, county road 261, all the way in towards Brommaplan. So this is where the border between two islands runs.
Strax intill studsar basketbollarna i Go: Right next door, basketballs bounce in Gothia Arena, Högsbo Basket's home ground and the only club-owned hall in Gothenburg. For matches it can hold a thousand people. The whole area once belonged to the parish of Västra Frölunda, which had around 13,500 residents in 1944 and was merged into the City of Gothenburg the following year.
Strax intill står Akalla värmeverk, ett: Right next to us stands Akalla värmeverk, a district heating plant from the mid-1970s. That may sound dry, but the Stockholm City Museum has singled out two of the buildings as particularly valuable in terms of cultural history. A little further away, in Akalla centrum, there is a church with an unusual journey behind it: consecrated in 1976, first a shared church for EFS, a Lutheran revival movement, and the Church of Sweden, and since 2020 sold to the Catholic diocese as the home church for Syriac Catholics.
Strax intill står Gibraltar herrgård, fa: Right next to here stands Gibraltar herrgård, the Chalmers family's old manor, which gave its name to Gibraltargatan. The wooden main building in Empire style was built in 1847, and since 2024 it has had a new location on Orrspelsgatan, south of the Chalmers campus. A former steward's house was used as the student union building for Chalmers students between 1948 and 1952.
Strax intill står Nacka kyrka, byggd 189: Right next door stands Nacka Church, built in 1891 in Gothic Revival style, which got a new burial chapel in 1908 to 1909. The church belongs to the old parish of Nacka, which had just 1,708 residents in 1887 and became the town of Nacka in 1949. On the other side of Kyrkviken bay, the Nysätra headland juts out, where the Nackanäs Inn once welcomed guests before it burned down in 1960.
Strax söder om Barkarby ligger Vålberga,: Just south of Barkarby lies Vålberga, a residential area built around 1963 that consists mostly of long rows of terraced houses around a sports field. A little further away is Barkarby Villastad, with the residential areas Tingsbyn and Kyrkbyn, which are regarded as a culturally and historically valuable environment in Järfälla.
Strax utanför kusten ligger ön Trälen, o: Just off the coast lies the island of Trälen, and it has been a TV star. In autumn 2006, TV4 broadcast the reality show Trälen every weekday, in which well-off inner-city Stockholmers and some less well-off suburbanites lived together on the island for 40 days. The first episode was watched by half a million viewers, but the figures dropped quickly. The winner was Serhan Sören Erdal.
Strax väster om Danderyds kyrka, en bit: Just west of Danderyd Church, a little way from here, the runestone U 131 stands between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall. The Danderyd district borders the Edsviken bay to both the south and the west, and just over 11,000 people live here, most of them west of the E18.
Strax öster om Filipstadsbacken reser si: Just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, 73 metres high and named after Burmanstorp. Around the turn of the 20th century, the area towards Lake Magelungen was meant to become Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb with nearly 600 villa plots for well-off Stockholmers. But the plots sold slowly, mainly because of poor transport links, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought the whole company.
Strosa förbi Engelska radhusen i kvarter: Stroll past the Engelska radhusen, the English terraced houses, in the Drivbänken block
Strosa genom Gasqueparken vid Nymble: Stroll through Gasqueparken park by Nymble
Strosa i Ekerö centrum och leta upp den: Stroll around Ekerö centrum and look for the tall dot
Strosa i Järla sjö bland gamla industrih: Stroll around Järla sjö among old industrial buildings
Studenthuset Fyrtalet heter så för att m: The student residence Fyrtalet, the Foursome, got its name because four identical buildings were planned, but only one was built. It was designed by the architect Léonie Geisendorf. On Furusundsgatan stands YK-huset, built in 1939 as a collective housing block for the Professional Women's Club, with a nursery, restaurant and gymnasium. Värtan's station building from 1882 has a blue rating, the strongest protection the City Museum gives.
Studentområdet Kungshamra har ett kungli: The Kungshamra student area has a royal name for good reason: the land was donated by King Gustaf VI Adolf. The buildings went up between 1965 and 1967, and today there are 1,383 student homes here. A short walk away, in a patch of woodland, is Invalidkyrkogården, the Invalids' Cemetery, a burial ground established in 1824, where the last burial took place in 1905.
Stureby började byggas 1921 och hette då: Stureby started being built in 1921 and was then called Ersta Villastad, but after protests the name was changed in 1926 to the invented Stureby. Nearby is the Vivstavarvsvägen terraced housing area, with 36 terraced houses from the early 1950s designed by Erik F. Dahl, the only one in Stureby blue-listed by the City Museum. And Sockenvägen, which ties together the northern part of Brännkyrka parish, is a full 5,450 metres long.
Stureplan är Östermalms livliga mötespla: Stureplan is Östermalm's lively meeting place. In the middle of the square stands Svampen, the Mushroom, a concrete weather shelter from the 1930s that has become a classic place to arrange to meet.
Stuvsta och Snättringe var fram till 201: Until 2018, Stuvsta and Snättringe were a single municipal district with just over 16,000 inhabitants, before being split in two. A little way from here, Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, and several millstones have been preserved. The municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen, where Huddingegymnasiet, the upper secondary school, is housed in a building counted among the municipality's particularly valuable buildings.
Stuvsta sträcker sig hela vägen från Hag: Stuvsta stretches all the way from Hagsätra in the north down to Tomtberga and Hörningsnäs farm in the south, and east to Lake Trehörningen. A little way from here, the Stuvstaleden road runs through the Kungsklippan rock in the Stuvsta tunnel, opened in 1994, whose northern entrance is built into a residential building that straddles the approach.
Styrsö är en av de största öarna i södra: Styrsö is one of the largest islands in the southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has bathing coves, meadows and old fishing villages.
Subtopia, en kort promenad bort, hette t: Subtopia, a short walk away, used to be called Kulturhuset Rotemannen and is today a production venue for culture, with studios, workshops and rehearsal spaces, and it has supported the circus world for many years. A little further away is Fittja farm, whose inn in the 17th and 18th centuries was one of the largest coaching inns in Sweden. Since 1987 the Multicultural Centre has run its activities at the farm.
Sundbyberg är Sveriges till ytan minsta: Sundbyberg is Sweden's smallest municipality by area, just 8.79 square kilometres. On Esplanaden you'll find the library, Det Nya Museet and a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström. Right next to it is the Bristol cinema, which opened on New Year's Eve 1939 and is today also a cultural venue.
Sundbyberg är en av Stockholms äldsta fö: Sundbyberg is one of Stockholm's oldest suburbs. Sundbyberg's market town was formed here in 1888, and in 1927 it became the town of Sundbyberg. The railway station is even older: it opened in 1876 as part of the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen railway. Beneath your feet, 26 metres down in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with sculptures of building façades and the human senses.
Sundbybergs stadsmuseum berättar histori: Sundbyberg City Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb, from the 1860s onwards. Among the objects are burnt bones from a Viking Age grave that was excavated where the Sieverts cable works was later established. There are also parts of the runestone U 78, which disappeared in the 18th century: two pieces were found in Ursvik, lay for a long time in the porch of Solna Church and came to the museum in 1976.
Sundbybergs viktigaste landmärke, det nu: Sundbyberg's most important landmark, the now disused water tower, was designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912 as a symbol of the growth of modern Sundbyberg. Around the tower is Tornparken, the Tower Park, whose dance floor was a popular meeting place in the 1940s and 1950s, and in the 1970s the community sing-along evenings drew crowds. The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened as early as New Year's Eve 1939.
Svandammen i Solhem är både park och bad: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, in Solhem is both a park and a bathing spot, and it has become a central meeting place for teenagers and families with children alike. Perhaps not so strange, because buses leave from there in almost every direction: towards Brommaplan, Backlura, Vällingby, Hallonbergen, Solna centrum and Spånga station. A dip and a bus ride, in short.
Svandammen är både park och badplats, oc: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, is both a park and a bathing spot, and a meeting point for young people and families with children in Solhem. The name Spånga is really old: it appears in writing as early as the year 1300 and means roughly "spångar", simple bridges over wet ground. Spånga parish once included both Hässelby Castle and Akalla.
Svartedalen byggdes mest under 1950- och: Svartedalen was built mostly in the 1950s and 1960s, and between 1965 and 1967 the City of Gothenburg's housing company put up 358 flats here. A little way off is Jättesten, named after the boulders on the hill, and A C Lindblads gata, named after the newspaperman who became the first Gothenburg resident elected to parliament as a Social Democrat.
Svedmyra låter oskyldigt, men namnet kom: Svedmyra sounds innocent, but the name comes from a croft called Svinmyran, 'the pig bog'. The croft has been known since the 14th century and belonged to Östberga farm. The district is surrounded by forest and green spaces, and the City of Stockholm classes the Svedmyra woods as an ecologically important core area. At the metro station, the artist Torgny Larsson has made a 40-metre-long glass screen with leaves of deciduous trees.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger, trots: Svedmyra metro station, despite its name, isn't in Svedmyra but in Stureby. A stone's throw away is Svedmyrabadet from 1969, where the pool water is kept at a full 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further away was Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted jumping competitions right up until 1990.
Sveriges första klinik för cancerbehandl: Sweden's first clinic for cancer treatment, Radiumhemmet, was founded in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. A little further away stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's well-known roadside inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. A lookout tower was also meant to be built in Hagaparken, but work on it never even started.
Sveriges volymmässigt största levande lö: Sweden's largest living deciduous tree by volume grows a short walk from here: the Ekebyhov Oak, which may be around 500 years old and was declared a natural monument in 1956. Next to it is Ekebyhov Palace, a manor house in Caroline style built in the late 17th century for Carl Gustav Wrangel. It is said possibly to be Sweden's largest surviving wooden palace.
Synskadades museum: Synskadades museum, the museum of the visually impaired
Syrhåla, stadsdelen en bit härifrån, har: Syrhåla, the district a little way from here, has a name that hardly sounds like an advertising slogan. The name is recorded from 1550 in the form Siöralla and means a swampy place or sour ground, after the low, damp land between the hills east and south-east of the older village. The district was formed in 1957, when Arendal was split in two.
Säby kyrka, församlingskyrkan för hela S: Säby Church, the parish church for the whole of Salem municipality, is just a few steps away. A couple of hundred metres from here stood the little farm labourer's cottage Charlottenlund, also called Lottalund. In the autumn of 1853 the labourer Lars Björkman moved in with his wife Christina Charlotta, and he did his days of work at Fågelsta farm. The family stayed until Björkman died in 1887.
Sätra gård hör till Stockholms äldsta gå: Sätra gård is one of Stockholm's oldest farms and has been known ever since the 1300s. It gave its name to the whole district, and the two surviving buildings are probably from the 1700s. On the district's highest point, Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, the water tower has stood since 1969, a landmark visible all the way to Ekerö.
Sätra radiolänktorn, även kallat Sätra t: Sätra radio link tower, also called Sätra telelänktorn, stands on Backvindeln near the border between Mälarhöjden and Bredäng. With its Stockholm white colour scheme it has become a well-known landmark, but the facility is not open to the public. A little further on is Bredängshallen, a swimming and sports hall from the mid-1960s with a green rating from the City Museum.
Sätras högsta punkt är Sätra berg, 71 me: Sätra's highest point is Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, where the water tower has stood since 1969. The district is named after Sätra gård, one of Stockholm's oldest farms, known as early as the 1300s. A little further away is the Church of Saint Maroun, formerly called Sätra church, and the Smistabron footbridge and cycle bridge, which has spanned the motorway since 2008.
Säve har vuxit rejält. År 1913 bodde 1 5: Säve has grown a lot. In 1913, 1,598 people lived in Säve parish, and by 2000 there were almost 12,000. The parish belonged to the Västra Hising hundred in Bohuslän and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. The parish church, Säve Church, is a short walk away and since 2010 has belonged to Tuve-Säve parish.
Sävedalen betyder helt enkelt Säveåns da: Sävedalen simply means the Säveån river valley, and it is an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. Right here was Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop, between 1985 and 2013. It stocked mostly Swedish titles, but also books in French – a little piece of Paris in the middle of Sävedalen.
Så sent som på 1940-talet bestod området: As recently as the 1940s, the area around Blackeberg was mostly forest and rock. Then the district was built in the early 1950s, following a town plan led by Sven Markelius. Bio Kaskad, the cinema at Blackebergsplan, opened in 1957, closed at the end of the 1990s and was brought back to life in 2018. And little Råcksta träsk, the pond nearby, was dredged in the early 1970s, when it was becoming overgrown.
Sågen är själva mittpunkten i Vendelsö,: Sågen is the very centre of Vendelsö, a residential area consisting mostly of blocks of flats from the 1950s to the 1970s, with a grocery shop and a restaurant in the centre. Vendelsö lies on both sides of the Gudöbroleden road, between Lake Drevviken and Tyresta National Park to the east. Winding through the area is the Vendelsån stream, which collects water from three lakes on its way to Drevviken.
Söder om Lundby nya kyrka står Sannegård: South of Lundby nya kyrka, Lundby New Church, stands Sannegårdsmonumentet, the remains of a burial ground from the period between the Bronze and Iron Ages. Four standing stones are lined up in a row. The largest, triangular stone remains in its original place, while the other three have been moved because of gravel extraction. The church itself bears a name that has actually been used for two different church buildings.
Söder om Rågsved tar Rågsveds friområde: South of Rågsved begins the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of nature with at times dramatic topography, heights, cliffs and valleys in an old fissure-valley landscape. Part of the area became a nature reserve in 2018. In the other direction is Högdalen skatepark, Stockholm's largest, created on the initiative of the association Stockholm Sub Surfers.
Söderhöjden, en bit härifrån, byggdes 19: Söderhöjden, a little way from here, was built in 1967 as part of the Million Programme, and this is where Jakobsberg's bowling alley is. The square was renovated and reopened on 31 August 2013. In the middle of the square stands a spherical artwork that glows in different colours depending on the season.
To the south, Årstaviken bay glitters.
Sörred har ett namn som inte smickrar. D: Sörred has a rather unflattering name. It is recorded from 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a careless man, a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The second part comes from the Old Swedish 'ryd', cleared land. The slacker's clearing turned out to be hard work after all: this is where Volvo's Torslanda plant began to be built in 1960 and 1961.
Ta en fika eller middag på Trädgårn: Have a fika, a coffee break, or dinner at Trädgårn
Ta en paus i Trekantsparken vid sjön Tre: Take a break in Trekantsparken park by the lake Trekanten
Ta en paus vid dammen: Take a break by the pond
Ta med kikaren! En bit bort ligger Svank: Bring your binoculars! A little way off is Svankälla wetland park, with marsh harriers, little grebes and lesser spotted woodpeckers. A little further west is Ligårds mosse, a bog so surrounded by marshland that it is hard to reach. In the reeds and among the water lilies, crucian carp and grass carp weighing several kilos are said to swim.
Tallkrogen har fått sitt namn efter ett: Tallkrogen is named after an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. The district is counted among Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of the streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. The area also had the croft Svedmyra, which in older times was called Svinmyra, Pig Bog. It was torn down in the 1930s but gave its name to the neighbouring district.
Talludden kallas också Neptuns udde. I o: Talludden is also called Neptune's Point. In the area is Käppalaställningen, an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War with gun pits and weapon emplacements, which was restored and reinaugurated in 1994 as a heritage-listed monument to Stockholm's air defence, unique in Sweden. A little further away is Käppalaverket, a sewage treatment plant from 1969 that is considered one of the most efficient in the world.
Tallumpaviljongen, med sina pyramidforma: The Tallum Pavilion, with its pyramid-shaped roofs, was designed by Gunnar Asplund in 1922. The name comes from the motto Tallum, which Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz used in the architectural competition for Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, in 1915. The building was probably meant to be temporary, but it remained and served as a utility building until 1981. Since 1994 Skogskyrkogården has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Tappström är ett smalt sund mellan Ekerö: Tappström is a narrow strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön, about 1.5 kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore Ralph Erskine designed Ekerö centrum, completed in 1991, with a "dot" over twenty metres high as its landmark. Erskine himself lived on Lovön and said he liked coming here to shop. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way in to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay.
Teaterälskare, spetsa öronen! Angereds t: Theatre lovers, prick up your ears! Angereds teater, in the Blå Stället cultural centre, performs newly written drama for children, young people and adults, and also runs an acting school. The cultural centre is on Angereds torg square, which until 1977 was called Triörtorget. Closer to the stop is Gunnared cemetery.
Tekniska museet: Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology
Telefonpionjären Lars Magnus Ericsson äg: The telephone pioneer Lars Magnus Ericsson owned Alby gård by Albysjön lake, a little way from here, from 1895 to 1913, and it was during his time that the manor got its distinctive appearance. A later owner, Alfred Ekström, started AB Fittja Familietvätt and used ground-breaking methods for industrial laundry. In the neighbourhood is also Fittja gård, which was the assembly site of the Svartlösa district court.
Telefonplan domineras av LM Ericssons ga: Telefonplan is dominated by LM Ericsson's old factory and head office, built from 1938 to 1940 to designs by Ture Wennerholm. The architectural historian Fredric Bedoire has called it perhaps the most beautiful of Stockholm's functionalist industrial complexes. Today the area is home to, among other things, Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design, and at Telefonplan the interactive light installation Colour by Numbers glows.
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader: Televerket's administrative buildings, the old telecoms agency
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader, en ko: Televerket's administrative buildings, a short walk away, were the headquarters of Telia Company until 2016. Televerket was the old Swedish telecoms authority. The complex grew in stages between 1962 and 1972 to designs by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan were awarded the prestigious Kasper Salin Prize. If you want to know more about the area, you can turn to Farsta hembygdsförening, the local history society, which spreads knowledge about Farsta's history from prehistoric times to the present day.
Tensta byggdes mellan 1966 och 1972 som: Tensta was built between 1966 and 1972 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's large-scale housing drive, but today it's the culture that draws people. Tensta konsthall shows contemporary art just a few minutes away, and in Tenstakyrkan church the music scene is rich, with strong roots in gospel, where many different Christian traditions share the same community.
Tensta gymnasium och Tekniska i Tensta: Tensta gymnasium and Tekniska i Tensta, upper secondary schools
Tensta konsthall: Tensta konsthall, the Tensta art gallery
Tensta vattentorn tronar på Tenstas högs: Tensta water tower stands on Tensta's highest point and can be seen far across the Järvafältet fields. It was built in 1969 and is marked green by the Stockholm City Museum as particularly valuable. Below the tower runs the Tensta tunnel, where the E18 motorway runs in two separate concrete tunnels, 300 metres long and built between 2010 and 2014.
Tenstakyrkan, alldeles intill, är en fri: Tenstakyrkan, right next door, is a free church known for its rich musical life with strong roots in gospel. A stone's throw away is Tensta konsthall, an art centre for contemporary art. And down in the metro, the artist Helga Henschen created the decoration on the theme A Rose for the Immigrants, with texts and poems among other things.
Till Hökmossen hörde förr backstugan Mic: Hökmossen once included the cottage Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. A little further away is Hägerstensbadet, popularly called Personnebadet after Personnevägen, an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free.
Till en annan värld: The sculpture Till en annan värld, To Another World
Till höger ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges ä: On the right is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your right is Kungliga slottet, Stockholm Palace.
Till höger ligger Skansen Lejonet, en fö: On your right is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Fort, a 17th-century defensive fort with a gilded lion on top.
On the right is the Liseberg amusement park.
Till höger reser sig Avicii Arena, den s: On the right rises Avicii Arena, the big white dome that used to be called Globen, the Globe.
Till höger reser sig Nya Ullevi, arenan: On your right rises Nya Ullevi, the arena built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till höger ser du Vasamuseets tak, med m: On your right you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show how tall the ship Vasa is.
Till höger ser du den röd-vita skyskrapa: On your right you can see the red-and-white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet, the Lipstick.
Till höger syns Kaknästornet, ett av Sto: On the right you can see Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of Stockholm's tallest towers.
Till höger syns Riddarholmskyrkan med si: On the right you can see Riddarholmen Church with its pointed cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till höger syns Stadshuset med sitt torn: On the right you can see Stockholm City Hall, Stadshuset, with its tower and the three crowns at the top.
Till höger syns Älvsborgsbron, invigd 19: On the right you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, opened in 1966.
Till höger, på andra sidan vattnet, ligg: On the right, across the water, lies the island of Långholmen.
Till höger, uppe på berget, ser du Masth: On your right, up on the hill, you can see Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget Church, from 1914.
Till höger, uppe på berget, syns Skansen: On your right, up on the hill, you can see Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, a 17th-century defensive fort.
Till höger, vid kanalen, ligger Feskekôr: On your right, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks like a church, and Gothenburgers call it the fish church.
Till vänster ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges: On the left is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your left is the Royal Palace.
Till vänster ligger Skansen Lejonet, en: On your left is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century defensive fort with a gilded lion on top.
Till vänster ligger nöjesparken Liseberg: On your left is the Liseberg amusement park.
Till vänster på berget ser du Masthuggsk: On the hill to your left you can see Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church. To your right you can glimpse the harbour and the Göta älv river.
Till vänster reser sig Avicii Arena, den: On your left rises Avicii Arena, the big white dome formerly known as the Globe, Globen.
Till vänster reser sig Nya Ullevi, arena: On the left rises Nya Ullevi, the arena built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till vänster ser du Vasamuseets tak, med: On your left you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show how tall the ship Vasa is.
Till vänster ser du den röd-vita skyskra: On your left you can see the red and white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet, the Lipstick.
Till vänster syns Kaknästornet, ett av S: On your left you can see Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of Stockholm's tallest towers.
Till vänster syns Riddarholmskyrkan med: On the left you can see Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, with its pointed cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till vänster syns Stadshuset med sitt to: On your left is Stockholm City Hall, with its tower and the three crowns at the top.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, ser du Mas: On your left, up on the hill, you can see Masthugget Church, Masthuggskyrkan, from 1914.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, syns Skans: On the left, up on the hill, you can see Skansen Kronan, a 17th-century defensive fortress.
Till vänster, vid kanalen, ligger Feskek: On your left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks like a church, and the people of Gothenburg have called it the fish church ever since.
On the left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks like a church, and Gothenburgers call it the fish church.
Tingstadsvassen bär ett riktigt gammalt: Tingstadsvassen bears a really old name: Tingstad is recorded as early as 1388 and comes from a village that was a ting, an assembly site. At first the city was stingy, and in 1874 it declined to buy the reed beds for ten öre per square foot. Two years later it changed its mind and paid 300,000 kronor. Today Ringön makes up most of the district.
Titta in i Childhoodhallen, känd från HC: Look into the Childhoodhallen rink, known from HCZ
Titta på Trisshusen, tidiga radhus från: See the Trisshusen, early terraced houses from 1909
Titta på gamla Lundbybadet på Herkulesga: See the old Lundbybadet bathhouse on Herkulesgatan
Titta på perrongen. Där sitter en kvinna: Look at the platform. A bronze woman in a pointed hat sits there waiting, and she has been doing so since 2001. The sculpture is called Väntan, Waiting, and is by Britt Ignell. Perhaps she's waiting for someone to get off the tram. Meanwhile, she has watched the multi-storey car park opposite get homes built on top of it.
Titta upp mot en fyra meter hög granitpe: Look up at a four-metre-tall granite pillar outside Karolinska Institutet. Up there runs the bronze sculpture The Entomological Abduction of a Woman by Eric Grate: a woman and a man carrying off a third figure without arms or legs. The lady wears a hat or a crown, and the man carrying her has insect-like antennae in his jaw.
Titta upp på ÅF-huset, 65 meter högt: Look up at ÅF-huset, 65 metres tall
Titteridamm, en bit härifrån, har fått s: Titteridamm, a little way from here, got its name from a legend. On Saturday evenings, the girls went down to the pond to look at their reflections in the shiny water and make themselves pretty for the dance. They looked, 'tittade', into the pond, hence the name! Nearby is Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka, the Church of St Paul of the Cross, a Catholic parish church.
Tolered hette ursprungligen Toleröd och: Tolered was originally called Toleröd and consists mostly of detached and terraced houses. A little way from here is Torpet Klara, a day-labour croft with five buildings. It was so tucked away at the end of a road through a modern villa area that for a long time the post office had no address for it. Since 2006 it has been a listed building.
Torget Hagaplan ligger delvis ovanpå mot: The square Hagaplan sits partly on top of the motorway tunnels of Norra länken, the Northern Link, and opened in 2023. The round office building Forskaren, the Researcher, stands in the middle of the southern part, and some sixty trees are planned here, including sequoias and tulip trees. Since September 2023 the square has also been home to the artwork Inflyttarna, The Newcomers, by Johanna Karlin.
Torget byggdes 1971 och är uppkallat eft: The square was built in 1971 and is named after the author and Nobel laureate Selma Lagerlöf. It lies about four kilometres north of central Gothenburg and is a local centre for northern Backa. Here you'll find the schools Svenska Balettskolan, the Swedish Ballet School, and Skälltorpsskolan, and the square was also home to Bäckebol's church hall, which belonged to Backa parish.
Torget en kort promenad härifrån hette t: The square a short walk from here used to be called Dragonplan and has an octagonal building that has become Rissne's landmark. Under the square lies the metro station, in a rock cavern 25 to 40 metres down. There runs a lettered timeline of historical events from 3000 BC up to 1985, an artwork by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
Torget fick sitt namn 1886 efter Landala: The square got its name in 1886 from Landala chapel, and fish was already being sold here in the 1880s. Landala was one of Gothenburg's first three working-class suburbs outside the Vallgraven moat. It is honoured by the sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife, on Landala torg, with the text: With a firm hand, strong from work, soft with love, you held the home together. The school next door opened in 1892 as Landalaskolan.
Torget fick sitt namn 1924 efter den hög: The square got its name in 1924 from the high-lying terrain, and it was the square that then gave the whole Höglandet district its name, meaning the Highlands. From 1926 to 1929 Höglandstorget was the terminus of tram line 12. On the square is the cinema Höglandsbiografen, opened in 1936, and a small park a little further away is named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa in the neighbourhood from 1925 to 1981.
Torget fick sitt namn 1946, troligen eft: The square got its name in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg. Here stands Eric Grate's bronze statue Spring, a naked woman on a granite plinth, put in place in 1950. An identical one is in Alingsås. The old Torpavallen ground, where Qviding FIF played on gravel, is now a retail area.
Torget har fått namn efter en by i Ostpr: The square is named after a village in East Prussia, known for a battle during the Seven Years' War. Down at Klippan there are old inns associated with the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg and his book Min son på galejan, My Son on the Galley. At Kustens hus next door, emigrants liked to have a last beer before the boat left for America.
Torget hette Torsnästorget fram till sep: The square was called Torsnästorget until September 2010, when it was renamed after Jan Stenbeck to honour his importance to the telecoms industry in Sweden. Its neighbour is Kista Science Tower, which at 123.9 metres is the second tallest office building in the Nordic countries. And the Filmstaden Kista cinema was opened on 27 November 2002 by Josephine Bornebusch and Fares Fares.
Torget sticker ut med ett 16 våningar hö: The square stands out with a 16-storey tower block completed in 1956, and on the community centre there's a mural in the form of a marble inlay by the artist Endre Nemes. The same year, Högsboskolan school opened right next door, built for about 1,000 pupils. The school is no longer there, though; it was demolished in 2013.
Torget vid stationen är uppkallat efter: The square by the station is named after the crime writer Stieg Trenter, who was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery shop by the railway station, which was then called Södertörns villastad, where young Stieg sometimes helped out – and his crime novel Träff i helfigur is set in the surrounding area. The villa town itself never happened: the plots sold slowly, mainly because of poor transport links.
Torget är uppkallat efter polarforskaren: The square is named after the polar explorer and meteorologist Finn Malmgren, and here stands the statue Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice, dedicated to him. The oaks and pines around the square were spared when it was built in the 1930s. And an unexpected neighbour: the future West German Chancellor Willy Brandt lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23 during his exile from Nazi Germany in the 1940s, and a park a little way off bears his name today.
Torpet Bussenhus intill Spånga kyrka var: The croft Bussenhus next to Spånga Church was a soldier's croft with an unusual side income: in the 1740s the cavalryman here had the right to run a tavern. The tavern sometimes turns up in the records of the Sollentuna district court, after various brawls. Inside the church are runestone fragments from the Viking Age, and one of them is built into the church's outer wall.
Torpet Månskär hade ett egendomligt namn: The croft Månskär had a peculiar name that has nothing to do with the crescent moon, "månskära" in Swedish. The first part comes from one of the first tenants, Måns, and the second from "kärr", meaning marsh. The croft grew up along the new route of Södertäljevägen road, completed in 1673. Right next to it is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's largest cinema, with eighteen screens and more than four thousand seats.
Torpet Spikborn hade ett märkligt namn,: The croft Spikborn had a curious name, which probably comes from the tool spikborr, a gimlet. It was probably built in the 1650s under Vårby gård, and the last remains were demolished in February 1977. Segeltorpsskolan, the Segeltorp school, has a dramatic history too: the first school building from 1917 burned down in 1971, and an entirely new main building opened in 2010.
Torrekullagården, en kort promenad bort,: Torrekullagården, a short walk away, has had many lives. The City of Mölndal has owned the farm since 1973 and has run it as a labour-market project and a camp centre. There have been ideas for a hotel, the adult education association Studiefrämjandet wanted to run it, and between 2015 and 2019 unaccompanied young refugees lived in the house.
Torsby finns inte bara i Värmland. Det h: Torsby isn't only in Värmland. This is Torsby parish in Bohuslän, which since 1971 has belonged to Kungälv municipality, and whose parish church, Torsby Church, is a short walk from here. The parish stretches out towards the North Sea coast just north of the mouth of the Nordre älv river and includes both the town of Kärna and several small villages, such as Kovikshamn and Brunnefjäll.
Torslanda hörde länge till Bohuslän och: Torslanda long belonged to the province of Bohuslän and the Västra Hising district. Only in 1967 did the parish become part of the City of Gothenburg. Today Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, with a series of smaller villages such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Lilleby, Nolered and Tumlehed. A little way from here stands Torslanda Church, one of the diocese's most popular wedding churches.
Torslanda på västra Hisingen är känt för: Torslanda on western Hisingen is known for its many beaches and its nature, but above all for Volvo Cars' Torslandaverken factory. Before Landvetter Airport was built in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was also here in Torslanda. The housing is mostly villas and terraced houses, and the shopping areas are called Torslanda Torg and Amhult.
Torslanda är en stor stadsdel på västra: Torslanda is a large district on western Hisingen, 4,425 hectares, with smaller places such as Amhult, Hjuvik, Hällsvik and Tumlehed. A short walk away stands Torslanda church, one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. And before Landvetter was built in 1977, Gothenburg's main airport was right here in Torslanda.
Torslanda är kyrkbyn i den gamla Torslan: Torslanda is the church village of the old Torslanda parish, which became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. The place is known for its many beaches and its nature, but above all for Volvo's car factory, Torslandaverken. Sport has deep roots here: Torslanda IK was founded on 18 January 1944, and together with Torslanda HK it is one of the local sports clubs.
Torslandaverken, ursprungligen Volvo Tor: Torslandaverken, originally the Volvo Torslanda factory, was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Construction started in 1960–1961 in the district of Sörred, whose name has a funny background: the first part, Sör-, is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a negligent fellow, a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The ending -red comes from the Old Swedish ‘ryd’, cleared land.
Torsviks skola har vuxit fram i etapper,: Torsviks skola has grown in stages, with buildings from 1906 all the way to 2021, and today has around 850 pupils from preschool to year 9. On Stockholmsvägen you can see Lidingö Arena, an office and retail building from 1974–1978 designed by Bo Möller, which has become a local landmark. Just west of Lidingö centrum is Ansgarskyrkan, the Ansgar Church, built and opened in 1996 by Lidingö Missionsförsamling, a free church congregation.
Trakten här var kanske Stockholms mest k: This area was perhaps the place in Stockholm with the most mills. Two windmills were called Lilla and Stora Tissan, and nearby Stora Adam and Lilla Eva, among others, were turning. One of the Tissans was moved in 1887 to Rolsta gård in Märsta. Next door was also Åhlinska skolan, a girls' school that Karin Åhlin opened in 1847 when she was only 17 years old, with 14 pupils and her sisters as teachers.
Tre villor vid Gasverksvägen, Ingenjörsv: Three villas on Gasverksvägen, Ingenjörsvillorna, were built as homes for the engineers at Värtagasverket gasworks. The gasworks buildings were designed by Ferdinand Boberg, and it supplied town gas to Stockholm right up to January 2011. Gasklockan was also planned here, a residential tower of about 170 metres and around 50 floors, designed by Herzog & de Meuron. It was never built, however.
Trollbäcken är ett lånat namn. Trakten h: Trollbäcken is a borrowed name. The area used to be called Kumla, after the manor by Drevviken lake that dates back to the Middle Ages, but in 1947 the residential areas changed their name to Trollbäcken so as not to be confused with Kumla in the province of Närke. A couple of hundred metres away is Trollbäcken church, by county road 260. The manor itself is still called Kumla herrgård, and since 2013 it has housed a restaurant and conference centre.
Trollbäckens IP: Trollbäckens IP, the Trollbäcken sports ground
Trots att Göteborg känns nära är marken: Although Gothenburg feels close, the land here is actually part of Halland. Lindome parish belonged to Fjäre hundred in Halland, and only in 1971 did it become part of Mölndal municipality. Lindome church, the parish's old church, is a short walk away, and the church village of Lindome has now grown together with the Gothenburg urban area.
Trots namnet ligger Älvsjöbadet inte all: Despite its name, Älvsjöbadet isn't in Älvsjö at all but in Hagsätra. The outdoor pool was built in 1937 to 1938 to designs by the architects Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom. A little way off is Teknik och Servicegymnasiet, founded in 1963 as a workshop school to supply Stockholm's tramways with trained workshop staff.
Trähästen Havre och betong: The wooden horse Havre, and concrete
Träkvista är en idrottsglad del av Ekerö: Träkvista is a sporty part of Ekerö, with Ekerövallen, Träkvistavallen and Vikingahallen. The buildings are mostly villas, linked houses and terraced houses, and there are several schools here. The town centre moved in 1990, when Ekerö centrum, designed by Ralph Erskine, opened, but before then Träkvista was the heart of the town.
Tulegatan har fått sitt namn efter det m: Tulegatan is named after the mythological Thule, because the street used to mark the northern edge of built-up Sundbyberg. Between 1928 and 1959, tram line 15 ran here, and north of the street lies Tulemarken with its functionalist villas from the 1930s. A short distance away rises the town's most important landmark, the water tower designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912.
Tullinge gymnasium startade i oktober år: Tullinge upper secondary school opened in October 2000 and is built like a small campus with six buildings side by side, attended by about 730 students. One of its former students is the athlete Michel Tornéus. The school also has an unusual tradition: every year it is visited by a Nobel laureate.
Tumba gymnasium: Tumba upper secondary school, Tumba gymnasium
Tumba gymnasium öppnade 1974, och de röd: Tumba gymnasium opened in 1974, and its red sheet-metal facades were seen at the time as really bold and modern. It was Botkyrka's first upper secondary school and one of the first in the country built for both academic and vocational programmes under one roof. In 1978 the school became one of the first in Sweden to get its own computer, connected to no fewer than 16 users.
Tumba kyrka ligger alldeles intill. Den: Tumba Church is right next to us. It was consecrated in 1973 and reconsecrated on Palm Sunday 2023 after a rebuild. A little further away is Lill-Tumba farm, which the paper mill bought in 1900 just so that nobody else would use the land. The mill has, to say the least, a money-filled history: Tumba bruksmuseum, the mill museum, is about paper and banknote making and was nominated for the European Museum of the Year Award in 2008.
Tunnelbanan svävar fram här: Bredängs st: The metro floats along here: Bredäng station sits on a 180-metre viaduct over Bredängs allé and opened in 1965. In the ticket hall you'll find Pusselbitar, 'Puzzle Pieces', sculptures with wooden reliefs that the artist Lena Kriström made together with residents of Bredäng in 1982. The district is hilly and has a shoreline of one and a half kilometres on Lake Mälaren.
Tunnelbanestationen strax intill är smyc: The metro station right next to us is decorated with Plexiglas rods and a neon loop, an artwork by Kazuko Tamura from 1993. Just a couple of hundred metres away stands Botkyrka's oldest school building, the church school from 1849, which is still used by Botkyrka friskola. And in Hallunda Folkets hus, the community hall, the residents themselves run a cultural meeting place for northern Botkyrka.
Tureberg är Sollentunas administrativa o: Tureberg is Sollentuna's administrative and commercial heart, and the centre is a short walk away. By the square rises Turebergshuset, the municipal hall, together with Arena Satelliten and the Sollentuna centrum shopping mall. Closer by, in the Töjnan area, is Töjnaskolan, a school where children go all the way from the preschool class to year nine.
Tuve kyrka en bit härifrån är en av Göte: Tuve church, a little way from here, is one of the most popular wedding churches in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Past it winds Tuve kyrkväg, which was once the official highway from Säve into central Gothenburg. The southern part of the road, between Tången and the church, disappeared completely in the Tuve landslide of 1977, because it ran straight through the slide area.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, precis på: Tuve is in the middle of Hisingen, right on the border between the built-up city and the countryside. A little way from here is Gunnestorps mosse, a mix of lake, fen and bog where reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow side by side with cranberries, sundew and cotton grass. Around the bog are wet meadows that used to be pasture.
Tuve ligger mitt på Hisingen, på gränsen: Tuve is in the middle of Hisingen, on the border between the built-up city to the south and the countryside to the north. The district covers 1,720 hectares. Right next to it is the residential area of Tångedal, with terraced houses and L-shaped houses that were ready to move into in 1968–1969, and a little further away is Tuve torg square.
Tuve torg, alldeles intill, stod klart 1: Tuve torg, right next door, was completed in 1971 and was originally called Norums torg. Only in 1998 did it change its name to Tuve torg, and in 2007 it got a proper facelift. On the square there's a café and pâtisserie, a library and a pharmacy, among other things, and right next to it is Glöstorp Church, which today belongs to Tuve-Säve parish.
Tuvevägen, som passerar en bit härifrån,: Tuvevägen, which passes a little way from here, is a long through road that starts at Björlandavägen, passes Tuve and Skändla and ends in Säve. It gathers the traffic from Tuve and Säve towards central Hisingen. The area was also home to Hökälla säteri, a manor farm in the Skogome district.
Tvärbanan tar sig här över en vik av Ulv: Here the Tvärbanan light rail crosses an inlet of Lake Ulvsundasjön on the Ulvsunda bridge, 374 metres long, and right next to it is the Ulvsunda depot from 2014, where the trams have their workshop. On the other side of the inlet stands Margretelund farm, built in 1830. The city bought it in 1904, and it has been used among other things as a summer camp for the YMCA. Today boats from a number of boat clubs are stored here over the winter.
Två höga hus, Loket 1 och Porslinsbruket: Two tall buildings, Loket 1 and Porslinsbruket 29, mark the northern end of the Sankt Erik Bridge, and the porcelain in the second name – ‘porslin’ – is no coincidence. Next door is Rörstrand Castle, since 2020 home to Kaggeholm Folk High School. The Atlas area is named after the engineering company AB Atlas, which in turn was named after the giant Atlas from Greek mythology. And Rörstrandsgatan, incidentally, is pronounced with the stress on ‘rör’.
Två kyrkor ligger nästan vägg i vägg. Su: Two churches stand almost wall to wall. Sundbyberg church on Rosengatan is protected as an ecclesiastical heritage site.
