Centrumkyrkan was built in 1906 as a Baptist church and was taken over in 1986 by an independent congregation, founded the same year by the former Pentecostal pastor Stanley Sjöberg. Today the congregation has more than 700 members.
Tyresö kyrka, en bit härifrån nära Tyres: Tyresö church, a little way from here near Tyresö Palace, was consecrated on 9 March 1641 – and the very first service was the funeral of its builder, Gabriel Oxenstierna. By the church stands the Tyresö stone, the municipality's only known runestone, whose two fragments were found in 1969 and bear a Christian prayer. Near the palace, the Follbrinkströmmen stream also flows out; its water power drove various businesses from the Middle Ages right up to the 1940s.
Tyresö är sprickdalslandskap med låga ku: Tyresö is a rift-valley landscape of low hills and valleys, and a little way from here hides Barnsjön, a small forest lake by Farmarstigen. It's just under nine metres deep and has a swimming spot looked after by the municipality. Closer at hand is Trollbäcken sports ground, with an ice rink for ice hockey, an athletics facility and three football pitches, so here you can choose between skates and football boots.
Tyresö är typiskt sprickdalslandskap, me: Tyresö is typical fissure valley landscape, with low hills and valleys but also steep rocks and swirling rapids. In the south of the municipality, Storskogen begins, with patches of real old-growth forest in Tyresta National Park. Most people who work commute to other municipalities, and the municipal administration is in Tyresö Centre in Bollmora.
Täby Enskilda Gymnasium startade 1999 un: Täby Enskilda Gymnasium, a private upper secondary school, started in 1999 under the name Täby Mediagymnasium and is located by Galoppfältet station on the Roslagsbanan railway. The station has an unusual way of reaching the platform: via pedestrian level crossings with barriers at both ends. A little further on is Täby swimming hall, opened in November 2022 and the only one in the whole of Täby.
Täby Enskilda gymnasium: Täby Enskilda gymnasium, an upper secondary school
Täby Park är en hel stadsdel under uppby: Täby Park is a whole district under construction, where Täby Galopp, the horse racing track, was located between 1960 and 2016. The name was decided on 24 March 2015, people started moving in in 2020, and it is expected to take 20 to 30 years before everything is finished. A couple of hundred metres away is Täby swimming hall, designed by Norconsult and opened in 2022, the municipality's only swimming hall.
Täby centrum har 215 butiker, 34 restaur: Täby centrum has 215 shops, 34 restaurants and cafés, and since 2022 the formal name Westfield Täby Centrum. The Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, has five screens with a total of 516 seats. And the library keeps something much older: Viking Age runestone fragments found in Lissby in 1930.
Täby kommun bildades 1971, och 2017 flyt: Täby municipality was formed in 1971, and in 2017 the municipal administration moved from Roslags-Näsby to a new town hall by Täby Centre. Grindtorp, a short distance away, is one of Tibble's residential areas from the 1950s and 1960s, along the E18 between Näsbydal and Täby's former horse racing track. The name comes from a gate, 'grind', on the road between Näsby and Tibble, which marked the boundary between manor and farm.
Täby var fram till 2010 namnet på en tät: Until 2010, Täby was the name of an urban area that stretched across municipal borders, including Enebyberg in Danderyd and a small piece of Sollentuna. At the time it was Sweden's eighteenth largest urban area. A little way off is Grindtorp, a housing area along the E18 between Näsbydal, Täby's former horse racing track and Täby centrum.
Tändstickor för hela världen tillverkade: Matches for the whole world were once made in the block next door. In 1904 Södertelje Tändsticksfabrik began building a branch factory in Elisedal, and in 1913 it became part of Ivar Kreuger's match empire. The factory was demolished in the early 2000s. On the site, still called the Tändstickan block, the Match, now stands the ÅF building: 16 storeys and 65 metres tall, opened in 2014.
Tänk att gå på förskola i ett slott! Huv: Imagine going to preschool in a palace! Huvudsta Old Palace, a wooden building from 1750 by Lake Ulvsundasjön, was the main house of Huvudsta gård until it was moved in 1834. Until the summer of 2018 it housed Förskolan Slottet, the Palace Preschool, run by the Church of Sweden. Right next to it is Huvudstabadet, a heated outdoor pool by the waterfront promenade.
Tänk dig en hel församling för de boende: Imagine a whole parish for the residents of a single foundation. The parish of the Stiftelsen Konung Oscar I:s minne foundation was exactly that, for the residents of the foundation in Bagarmossen, and it initially belonged to Maria Magdalena parish. Nearby is also Skarpnäck school from 1952, designed by Ture Ryberg, and the park Gränsberget on an old moraine hill.
Tågen har stannat här sedan 1856, och fr: Trains have stopped here since 1856, and until 1912 the station was called Partilled. The first station building was designed by Adolf W. Edelsvärd, chief architect of the Swedish State Railways, and became the model for several other stations, a type known as the Partilled model. In 1901 it was replaced by a new station building in Art Nouveau style, and since the 1960s the commuter trains between Gothenburg and Alingsås have stopped here.
Tågen mellan Göteborg och Borås stannar: Trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop at Mölnlycke station, but the station hasn't always been here. It opened in 1894 about 350 metres to the east and was only moved to its current location in 2003. The old station building was demolished in 2013. A little further away is Wallenstam Arena, where Pixbo Wallenstam IBK play their home floorball matches in front of up to 1,600 spectators.
Tågen stannade här från 1890 till 1976,: Trains stopped here from 1890 to 1976, when the railway line between Djursholms Ösby and Eddavägen was closed. A couple of minutes away is the Mittag-Leffler Institute, an international research institute for mathematics, in the castle-like Villa Mittag-Leffler, which has been rebuilt several times, with Ferdinand Boberg among its architects.
Törstig? I Fructushuset på Ulvsundavägen: Thirsty? The Fructus building on Ulvsundavägen once made the soft drink Pommac. The factory was built in 1939 to 1940 to designs by Ture Wennerholm and is considered an elegant example of functionalist industrial architecture. Close by was also Flygtekniska försöksanstalten, the Aeronautical Research Institute, a government agency that researched and experimented in aeronautics until the turn of the millennium.
Udden Hustegaholm vid Kyrkvikens norra s: The Hustegaholm headland on the north shore of Kyrkviken bay has been owned by the City of Lidingö since 1964 and is open to the public. Three of the houses can be rented for parties and meetings, and in Sjövillan the Lidingö Pensioners' Association runs a café during the summer months. Here Kyrkviken, which divides Lidingö into a northern and a southern part, narrows to a strait of about 25 metres before opening into Hustegafjärden bay.
Udden har fått sitt namn efter ett block: The headland is named after a blockhouse of timber and stone that was built in the time of Gustav Vasa to protect the entrance to Stockholm. Later the place became a customs station for boats on their way in, and the customs houses at Stora Sjötullen are now homes. Out here is also Thielska galleriet, the art museum on Djurgården.
Ulvesund är en liten ort med åkrar som s: Ulvesund is a small place with fields sloping down to the Nordre älv river, and there is also a summer cottage area here. The village has had a somewhat fickle relationship with the statistics: in 2000 it became an official small locality with 51 inhabitants, in 2005 the population was too small and the status disappeared, but by 2010 the inhabitants numbered 70 and Ulvesund was a small locality again.
Ulvsunda slott byggdes på 1640-talet av: Ulvsunda Castle was built in the 1640s by Field Marshal Lennart Torstenson, and several streets in the district have names linked to him. The castle's current appearance dates from the 1830s, and today it's a hotel and conference centre. Next to it is the almost round Lillsjön lake, with allotments since 1917, and on Ulvsundavägen stands one of the few preserved emergency housing buildings from 1917 to 1918.
Ulvsunda trädgårdsstad började planeras: Planning for Ulvsunda garden city began as early as 1912, and it was originally called Kungsholms villastad. The area also has two unusual reminders from the same time. Lillsjöstationen is a substation for Stockholm's electricity works from 1913, designed by Gustaf de Frumerie, and on Ulvsundavägen there's a large building put up as emergency housing in 1917 to 1918, one of the few of its kind preserved in Stockholm.
Under Göta älv i närheten löper Tingstad: Under the Göta älv river nearby runs the Tingstad tunnel, a so-called immersed tunnel that links Hisingen with the rest of Gothenburg via the E6. It is actually two tubes with three lanes in each, and 455 metres long. The tunnel is also a link in the important motorway between Oslo and Copenhagen, so under the riverbed here traffic whizzes between two capitals.
Under Hagalund går tåget i berget. Hagal: Under Hagalund, the trains run through the rock. The Hagalund tunnels are four railway tunnels, about 500 metres long, and the first was built in 1911, when Solna station moved to its current location at the northern entrance. More tunnels were added later in the 1900s. The tram stop is below the residential area known as Blåkulla.
Under Hammarkullen ligger en hemlis: Sve: Underneath Hammarkullen there's a secret: Sweden's only completely underground tram stop, 25 metres below ground. The platforms were built so that they could be 120 metres long, but because of ramps and unbuilt sections in the tunnels, only 70 metres are used. Above is Hammarkulletorget, built in 1971 and rebuilt in 1997 with new colours and a new shape.
Under Hjulstaskolan sprängdes ett bergru: Beneath Hjulsta School, a rock cavern was blasted out for the metro, and on 31 August 1975 the blue line's trains could start running here, around 14 kilometres from Kungsträdgården. Close by is the green Hjulsta allotment garden, whose association was formed in 1973 and which is now held up as an example of multicultural gardening.
Under Huvudsta centrum gömmer sig en trä: Beneath Huvudsta centrum hides a garden, although it's in the rock. The metro station lies in a rock cavern 25 metres underground and is decorated with the artwork Hanging Gardens by Per Holmberg from 1985, the same year the station opened. The entrance was designed by the architect Yorgo Turac.
Under fötterna här i trakten går Gnistän: Under your feet around here runs the Gnistäng tunnel, built in 1978 as part of the Västerleden road. At 712 metres, it is one of Sweden's longer road tunnels. At first it was one single shared tube, but as traffic queues grew, the air became stagnant and exhaust fumes built up, despite an extensive fan system. So in the summer of 1996 the tunnel was given a concrete wall separating the two directions of traffic.
Under fötterna ligger Husby tunnelbanest: Beneath your feet is Husby metro station, blasted into the bedrock and opened in 1977. The artist Birgit Broms has painted its yellow walls with birch trunks and Vaxholm archipelago boats – an unexpected archipelago feel in the middle of Järva. Above ground stands Husby Church from 1976, green-listed by the City Museum for its high cultural and historical value.
Under gatorna klättrar blå rankor och bl: Beneath the streets, blue vines and leaves climb over the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and among the tendrils you can see silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was otherwise best known for his mechanical sculptures and helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, 'She – a Cathedral', in 1966.
Under jord pågår ett stort bygge: Södra: Underground, a major construction project is under way: Södra Hagalund will be a new station on the green line's branch towards Arenastaden, a full 45 metres below ground. It is expected to open in 2029. Above ground, in Eric Grate's park, you can meet the sculptor Eric Grate's bronzes, including Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.
Under korsningen Sveavägen–Odengatan lig: Under the intersection of Sveavägen and Odengatan lies a buried bridge. Sveabron was built in 1897, but when Sveavägen was raised in the 1910s, the bridge was simply left in the fill. The blocks here were also a cinema strip. Rialto opened in 1921 on the corner of Odengatan, and since 1993 Teater Pero has staged children's theatre in its premises. Röda Lyktan, the Red Lantern, showed films from 1917 to 1982.
Under marken här i närheten gömmer sig E: Underground, somewhere near here, hides Elefanten, the Elephant, a nuclear-bomb-proof command centre of 3,300 square metres, blasted into the rock in the 1970s. It stood unused for 19 years before the Swedish Armed Forces bought it in 2017 and brought it back into use. Much older is the Edsängen burial ground a short walk away, with about 125 Viking Age graves, one of the largest in Sollentuna.
Under shoppingstråken i Sickla Köpkvarte: Beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter lies something unexpected: a test mine where rock drills and mining machines are tested, today owned by Epiroc, which was spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018. The name Sickla roughly means a low-lying place where water emerges, a small marsh, and comes from the Stora Sickla estate. The area was also home to Nobelberget, an old warehouse that became a concert and event venue.
Under sin exil från Nazityskland på 1940: During his exile from Nazi Germany in the 1940s, Willy Brandt, later Chancellor of West Germany, lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23. Since 1997 the park by the metro's eastern entrance has borne his name. The street is named after the polar explorer Finn Malmgren, and at Finn Malmgrens plan stands the statue Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice. The station, by the way, has the metro's smallest artwork, a decoration in the brickwork.
Under torget byggs tunnelbanestationen B: Under the square, the Barkarbystaden metro station is being built, and all around a whole new district is growing up on what was once the grounds of the Svea air wing at the closed-down airfield. A little further away is Kyrkbyn, the church village, which used to be called Järfälla gård and played a central role in Järfälla's early history.
Under Älvsborgsbron, en bit härifrån, li: Under Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, a little way from here, lies one of the city's least glamorous but most important facilities: Ryaverket. This plant treats the wastewater of nearly 800,000 people in the Gothenburg region, and it has been extended again and again since construction began in 1968. Further off rises the Rya accumulator tank, a cylinder about 60 metres tall that evens out peaks in demand for district heating and can be seen from the harbour entrance.
Under älven en bit härifrån ligger Marie: Under the river a little way from here lies the Marieholm tunnel, opened to traffic on 16 December 2020. It was built as an immersed tunnel and, just like the Tingstad tunnel, it is not anchored to solid bedrock but floats in the clay. The cost was estimated at 3.5 billion kronor. The Säveån river also flows through the area, 130 kilometres long including its headwaters.
Uppe på Albyberget börjar en lång rulltr: Up on Albyberget hill begins a long escalator that goes down to Alby metro station, about 24 metres underground. Down there, the artist Olle Ängkvist has painted flowers in bright colours on moss-green concrete walls. Alby is also home to Cirkus Cirkör, based in the Subtopia cultural centre a little way from here.
Uppe på Hökeberget står Guldhedens norra: Up on Hökeberget stands Guldheden's northern water tower, which since 2008 has been converted into 74 student flats. The roof is about 140 metres above sea level, and on the eleventh floor there is a shared roof terrace. The flats on each floor are arranged in a fan shape. The KV art school, founded in 1969, was also around here before it moved to Lindholmen in 2023.
Uppe på Kvarnberget snurrade en gång Stu: Up on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill, the windmill of Stuvsta gård once turned, and it's what gave the whole Kvarnbergsplan area its name. Several millstones have been preserved, and the municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen. That's also where you'll find Huddingegymnasiet, an upper secondary school whose building counts as one of the municipality's especially valuable buildings.
Uppe på Kyrkåsberget, i villastaden Para: Up on Kyrkåsberget, in the villa suburb of Paradiset, stands Villa Porthälla, which the locals have always called Borgen, the Castle. The company director Ernst Harbeck had it built between 1914 and 1918 and wanted it to look like a medieval German castle in stone and brick: five floors, 17 rooms. In the autumn of 1972 a big police raid was carried out on the villa; today it is divided into flats.
Uppe på Störtfjällsberget invigdes Kvarn: Up on Störtfjällsberget hill, Kvarnbyvallen opened one Sunday in high summer 1934, Mölndal's first proper sports ground and home of FK Herkules, Sweden's oldest 'frisksport' club, part of a healthy-living sports movement. The ground was closed in 2007 and is now housing. A little way from here, Biografen Möllan has been showing films since 1959, with 289 seats in the Folkets hus community hall.
Uppe på Vattentornsberget reser sig Jarl: Up on Vattentornsberget, the Water Tower Hill, rises the Jarlaberg water tower, 47.5 metres high and with two reservoirs that supply Sicklaön with water. The Nacka Forum shopping centre opened in 1989, replacing a makeshift set of huts that had been there for many years. A little further away, in Storängen, stands Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner Yngve Larsson and his wife Elin, née Bonnier.
Uppe på berget i närheten ligger Skansen: Up on the hill nearby is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century defensive tower with a gilded lion on top. It was built to protect the city from attacks from the east.
Uppe på berget står Larsbergs hus med te: Up on the hill stand the Larsberg buildings, with brick-red facades, green metal roofs and white balcony fronts – typical of the 1960s. Just over 1,200 apartments were completed in 1969, designed by the architect Bengt Gate. Below is Malmstens, where students study furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery. The old hospital building in Högsätra was due to be demolished during 2025 to make way for the new Kärnan district.
Uppe på berget står ett långt hus som lä: Up on the hill stands a long building that was for a long time the only one in the area. It was built in 1914 as workers' housing for AGA employees and is today a state listed building. In 2001 the building was renovated and the flats were sold as tenant-owned apartments. A little way from there stands AGA's yellow optics tower.
Up on the hill you can see Sofia Church.
Uppe på ett hustak i Råcksta lyser en bi: Up on a rooftop in Råcksta, a piece of the 1950s shines. The neon sign with the word RÅCKSTA in green and a swooping "Centrum" in yellow was put up in the 1950s, when the suburbs' shops drew customers with small neon signs such as BLOMMOR, FRISÖR and KONDITORI – flowers, hairdresser and patisserie. Most of that glowing heritage is gone, but this sign was renovated in 2011 and shines in its former glory.
Uppe på höjden i området ligger Furulund: Up on the heights in this area is Furulund, and there the snow shovel gets more work than down in the valley. Furulund is more than 100 metres higher than Gothenburg, and since the temperature hovers around zero on many days, the area gets more snow, which also stays longer. Below lies Kåhög, a small villa community by the Säveån river.
Uppe på Åsöberget finns, tillsammans med: Up on Åsöberget hill you'll find, together with Djurgårdsstaden, Stockholm's largest continuous area of wooden houses. The area has been a cultural reserve since 1956. On Kvastmakarbacken stand Hedberg's malmgård, a traditional town estate, and wooden houses from the early 18th century. Below lay the bay of Tegelviken, which was filled in in 1910. Today Viking Line's Finland ferries dock there.
Uppe till vänster ligger Skinnarviksberg: Up on the left is Skinnarviksberget, the highest natural point in Stockholm's inner city. Climb up and you get a wide view over Riddarfjärden bay, the City Hall and Kungsholmen. The name comes from the ‘skinnare’, the craftsmen who prepared hides and leather by the cove here in days gone by.
Uppför backen ligger Kungliga slottet, s: Up the hill is the Royal Palace, completed in 1754 after the old Tre Kronor castle burned down in 1697. The palace has more than six hundred rooms, and the changing of the guard in the outer courtyard draws visitors every day.
Uppståndelsekapellet: The Chapel of the Resurrection, Uppståndelsekapellet
Ursvik är egentligen två stadsdelar, Lil: Ursvik is really two districts, Lilla Ursvik and Stora Ursvik. A short way from here stretches Rissne äng, Rissne Meadow, a city park that links Rissne, Hallonbergen and central Sundbyberg. Several red-listed beetles thrive there, and since 2024 the area has been prepared to become a nature reserve.
Utanför Hässelby trädgårds- och hembygds: Outside the Hässelby garden and local history museum stands a runestone of grey granite, Uppland runic inscription 85, which was found at Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved here in October 1988. Next to the museum is Hässelby villastad church. A little way off is the Åkermyntan shopping centre from 1977, which is mentioned in one of the comedy group Killinggänget's sketches: it's where the character Fred Asp lives, known for partying with his ferret Göran.
Utanför Lovö kyrka står inte en eller tv: Outside Lovö Church stand not one or two, but a full five runestones, so here the Viking Age and the parish church meet on the same churchyard hill. Lovö parish also includes Drottningholm Palace, and in the church there are around thirty gravestones, most of them for people who worked at the palace. Along Lovö kyrkallé, about 800 metres east of the church, is the woodland cemetery laid out in the 1830s.
Utanför Nya Ullevi står Ingo – the Champ: Outside Nya Ullevi stadium stands Ingo – the Champ, Peter Linde's bronze statue of Ingemar Johansson, world heavyweight boxing champion in 1959–1960. The statue is 2.4 metres tall and weighs 400 kilos. In the arena, Ingo beat the American Eddie Machen in front of more than 53,000 spectators. Along Stampgatan flows Fattighusån, a dug canal opened as early as 1641 by Count Per Brahe.
Utanför Västertorpshallen står Efter bad: Outside Västertorpshallen stands Efter badet, After the Bath, a limestone sculpture group by Pye Engström, shaped like a sofa where you can sit on the laps of seven people. All seven were politically engaged and in the public eye in the early 1970s. In the same block, Isprinsessan, was Västertorp upper secondary school, whose premises were converted into homes in 2007.
Utanför Önnered ligger Lilla Rösö, i fol: Off Önnered lies Lilla Rösö, known locally simply as 'Lilla öa', the Little Island. There are boathouses, ancient remains, swimming spots and even a dance floor. Along the north side of the island runs Eskil's canal, and north-west of the island lies its big sister, Stora Rösö. Önnered itself is a district of 516 hectares in the South-West city area.
Utby kyrka ligger alldeles i närheten oc: Utby Church is close by and today belongs to Nylöse parish. But Utby has an older and more dramatic church history: the old Utby parish lost its church, which was destroyed in 1566, and in 1571 the parish was merged into Partille parish. A little further away was Fjällbohemmet, a care home in Utby between 1939 and 1983.
Ute i Göteborgs södra skärgård, cirka 16: Out in Gothenburg's southern archipelago, about 16 kilometres southwest of the city centre, lies Donsö. The island is just under two square kilometres in size but still has over 1,500 permanent residents. Since 2020 the settlement has counted as part of the town of Styrsö, and the island has Donsö Church, which belongs to Styrsö parish.
Ute i Mälaren ligger Björnholmen, en ö s: Out in Lake Mälaren lies Björnholmen, an island belonging to the Drottningholm royal estate. According to legend, it got its name, 'Bear Islet', when King Karl IX once shot a bear there. In the 18th century there was a lakeside tavern on the island, and in the first half of the 19th century it was a popular day-trip destination for well-off Stockholmers. Around 1859, Stora Villan, the Great Villa, was built in Italian style by the newspaper publisher and agitator Franz Sjöberg.
Ute i Rivö fjord ligger ön Hjärtholmen,: Out in Rivö fjord lies the island of Hjärtholmen, where two families employed by Shell lived in the 1950s. There was no bridge, so the workers had to be taken to and from work by boat. Later the island got a bridge, and in the late 1960s the Torshamnen oil port was built next to it. Today crude oil is stored in rock caverns on the island, and between 1993 and 2018 five wind turbines turned here.
Ute på plattformen vid Rågsveds station: Out on the platform at Rågsved station stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Bird Green, by Björn Selder. A little way from here, in Högdalen, is the Cyklopen culture house, run entirely by volunteers from the association Kulturkampanjen. The first Cyklopen was completed in 2007 but burned down in November 2008 in an arson attack by suspected Nazis. The association didn't give up – it built a new one.
Utsikt från Katarinahissen: The view from Katarinahissen, the Katarina Lift
Uttalet är viktigt här: Ramberget sägs m: Pronunciation matters here: Ramberget is said with a short a, and the first part comes from ramn, an old word for raven. BK Häcken played at the old Rambergsvallen ground, and on the same spot today stands Nordic Wellness Arena, formerly Bravida Arena, opened in 2015. Next to it is Lundbybadet swimming baths from 1973. The arena, by the way, is turnkey, assembled from prefabricated parts, and has twins in Paderborn and Offenbach in Germany.
Valla torg har fått namn efter Valla går: Valla torg is named after Valla gård, a farm mentioned as early as 1330. The last farm buildings were demolished in 1960. In the square bubbles the Valla fountain by Bertil Johnson. Along the footpath towards Årsta centrum lies a Late Iron Age burial ground with ten burial mounds and 35 stone settings, two of them ship-shaped. Next to it stands Årsta church, designed by Johan Celsing and consecrated in 2011.
Van der Nootska palatset: Van der Nootska palatset, the Van der Noot Palace
Van der Nootska palatset byggdes 1671 ti: The Van der Noot Palace was built in 1671 to 1672 for Baron Thomas van der Noot, when Sweden was one of Europe's great powers, and the house has survived several threats of demolition. A block away is Monteliushuset, where the National Antiquarian Oscar Montelius was both born and died. Nearby, Spegelteatern, the Mirror Theatre, was based for 35 years with the motto: we shall mirror the world, without breaking the mirror.
Vanadisbadet i Vanadislunden var Stockho: Vanadisbadet in Vanadislunden park was Stockholm's first electrically heated outdoor pool. At the southern end of the park stands Stefan's church from 1904. On Surbrunnsgatan was Konditori Valand, a café that the couple Stellan and Magdalena Åström ran for 60 years from 1954. Magdalena had come to Stockholm as a refugee from Nazi Germany.
Varje vår blir det blått på Björkö. Vid: Every spring Björkö turns blue. At Bovik is the area called Pjonken, known for the huge number of hepaticas, or blue anemones, that bloom there. The island is in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, and the village has around 1,400 residents. A short way from here stands Björkö Church, which belongs to Öckerö parish.
Varvsgatan hette fram till 1885 Pipbruks: Until 1885 Varvsgatan was called Pipbruksgränd, Pipe Works Lane. The name came from a pipe works by Långholmssundet strait, where clay pipes were made from white Dutch clay in the 18th century. The memory lives on in the Pipmakartrappan, the Pipe Maker's Steps. The large buildings in the Plankan and Drakenberg blocks show that the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, reached the inner city too.
Varvsjätten Götaverken höll till här änd: The shipbuilding giant Götaverken was based here right up until 1991, and the shipyard halls live on as sports halls. Kanalhuset by the water was designed for the camera company Hasselblad, which moved out after a short time. Today SVT and Swedish Radio broadcast from there. And Lundbybadet, the bathhouse from 1915, became a karate club when the last bath attendant, Ante Melander, went home in 1973.
Vi befinner oss på Hisingen, till ytan S: We are on Hisingen, by area Sweden's fifth largest island, after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust, and the second most populous. The island is surrounded by the Göta älv river, the Nordre älv river and the Kattegat sea. Around three quarters of it belong to the province of Bohuslän, while the rest, with the parishes of Lundby and Tuve, belongs to Västergötland. Close by is the small village of Holm in Tuve parish.
Vi har just korsat Göta älv på Hisingsbr: We've just crossed the Göta älv river on Hisingsbron, a lift bridge that opened in 2021 and replaced the old Götaälvbron. Frihamnen used to be a free port, where goods could be stored without customs duty. Now a new district is growing up here.
Vi kör över Västerbron, med en av Stockh: We're driving over Västerbron, with one of Stockholm's best views over Riddarfjärden bay, the City Hall and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Vi kör över Västerbron. Titta åt vänster: We're crossing Västerbron, the Western Bridge. Look to your left: there's City Hall, Riddarholmen and Gamla stan, the Old Town. Below us, on the right, is the island of Långholmen.
Vi närmar oss Kålltorp, ett lugnt villa-: We're approaching Kålltorp, a quiet villa and residential area in eastern Gothenburg. From here it's not far to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes and forest.
Vi närmar oss Södra station. Den stora h: We're approaching Södra station. The large semicircular building around Fatbursparken park is called Bofill's Arch, Bofills båge, after the Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill. It was completed in 1992. Where the park is today there was once Fatburssjön, a lake that was filled in during the 19th century when the railway arrived.
Vi närmar oss ändhållplatsen här i Sofia: We are approaching the last stop here in Sofia, the easternmost part of Södermalm. From here you can take a walk down towards the water, or wander back through Vita bergen and SoFo at a relaxed pace. Thanks for riding with us, and welcome back for the next tour!
Vi är i Biskopsgården. Lägg märke till g: We're in Biskopsgården. Notice the street names: Vårväderstorget, Mildvädersgatan, Önskevädersgatan and Friskväderstorget, meaning Spring Weather Square, Mild Weather Street, Wished-for Weather Street and Fresh Weather Square. Here the streets are named after different kinds of weather.
Vi är i Hammarby sjöstad, en stadsdel so: We're in Hammarby sjöstad, a district built from the 1990s on old industrial land. The large functionalist building is the Luma factory, where light bulbs used to be made.
Vi är i Marieberg på Kungsholmen. Det hö: We're in Marieberg on Kungsholmen. The tall tower nearby is the DN Tower, DN-skrapan, where the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved in during the 1960s. Right next to it is Rålambshov Park, one of the city's most popular summer parks.
Vi är i Marieberg. Det höga tornet i när: We're in Marieberg. The tall tower nearby is DN-skrapan, the DN skyscraper, where the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved in during the 1960s. Right next to it is Rålambshovsparken, one of the city's most popular summer parks. Keep a lookout now, because in a little while we'll drive up onto Västerbron, the Western Bridge.

We're in Marieberg. The tall tower nearby is DN-skrapan, the DN skyscraper, where the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved in during the 1960s. Right next to it is Rålambshovsparken park. Now keep a lookout, because in a little while we'll drive up onto Västerbron, the Western Bridge.
Vi är i SoFo, området söder om Folkungag: We're in SoFo, the area south of Folkungagatan. There are small shops, cafés and bars here, and in the middle is Nytorget, one of Södermalm's best-loved parks.
Vi är i Vasastaden, med pampiga stenhus: We are in Vasastaden, with grand stone buildings from the late 1800s. Several of the University of Gothenburg's buildings are also here. Vasaparken, with the university's main building, is right next door.
Vi är på Kungsportsavenyn, som göteborga: We're on Kungsportsavenyn, which Gothenburgers simply call Avenyn, "the Avenue". It is the city's grand boulevard and runs up to Götaplatsen, where Carl Milles' statue of Poseidon has stood since 1931. Along the way are restaurants, outdoor terraces and theatres.
Vi är vid Eriksdal, på Södermalms södra: We're at Eriksdal, on the southern edge of Södermalm. Below lies Årstaviken bay, where rowers and kayakers train for much of the year. This is also where you'll find Eriksdalsbadet, one of Stockholm's largest swimming baths, with an outdoor pool in summer.

We're at Eriksdal, on the southern edge of Södermalm. Below lies Årstaviken bay, where rowers and kayakers train for much of the year. This is also where you'll find Eriksdalsbadet, one of Stockholm's largest swimming baths.
Vi är vid Lisebergs norra sida. Nöjespar: We're on the north side of Liseberg. The amusement park opened in 1923 as part of the city's anniversary exhibition and is today one of the most visited in the Nordic region. At Christmas it turns into a Christmas market with millions of lights.
Vi är vid Vita bergen. På toppen står So: We're at Vita bergen, the White Hills. At the top stands Sofia church, consecrated in 1906 and named after Queen Sofia. Around the hill are small red wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries, a reminder of what Södermalm looked like before the stone city was built.

We're at Vita bergen, the White Mountains. At the top stands Sofia Church, consecrated in 1906 and named after Queen Sofia. Around the hill are small red wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries, a reminder of what Söder, Södermalm, looked like before the stone city was built. In summer, theatre is performed in the park.
Victoria Tower, ett par minuter bort, är: Victoria Tower, a couple of minutes away, has since 2011 been the tallest hotel in Northern Europe at 117.6 metres, a narrow win over Oslo Plaza at 117 metres. The building is named after Crown Princess Victoria. A little further on, across the border into Sollentuna, is Helenelund commuter train station, 10.9 kilometres from Stockholm Central.
Vid Albysjön ligger Fittja moské, som sk: By Albysjön lake is the Fittja mosque, which made history on 26 April 2013, when it became the first mosque in Sweden where a call to prayer could be heard. Right next to it is Hagaviken, where the Ekerö ferries cross the water and where the Spendrups brewery has its plant. Over it all runs Vårbybron, a bridge opened in 1996 and nominated for the Beautiful Roads award.
Vid Albysjön, ett par hundra meter bort,: By Albysjön lake, a couple of hundred metres away, is the Fittja mosque, which made history on 26 April 2013 as the first mosque in Sweden where a call to prayer could be heard. Right next to it stretches Fittjaviken, a bay of Lake Mälaren up to 16 metres deep, where the municipal border between Huddinge and Botkyrka runs through the middle of the water. Across the water, the 1996 Vårbybron bridge carries the motorway; it was nominated for the Beautiful Roads award.
Vid Albysjöns strand, ett par hundra met: On the shore of Albysjön lake, a couple of hundred metres away, is Hagalunds tvätterimuseum, the laundry museum – when it opened in 1994 it was Sweden's first museum with laundry as its theme. It was started on the initiative of the Huddinge artist Olle Magnusson and is housed in a laundry family's drying barn from 1906. A bridge carries the metro's red line across Albysjön, and above the area rises Masmoberget hill, 94 metres above sea level.
Vid Alviksplan låg Bromma-Teatern, en bi: At Alviksplan stood Bromma-Teatern, a cinema where the first performance was given on 27 September 1921. The idea was not only to show films but also to stage theatre. The cinema closed in 1971, and the building now houses a paint shop. Just south of the square is Alviks rättarbostad, the old farm foreman's house, a double cottage from the early 19th century and all that remains of Alvik farm.
Vid Brunnbyvägen står en skålgropssten m: On Brunnbyvägen stands a cup-mark stone with over 250 cup marks, found during excavations on Årstafältet in 1958 or 1959. Its neighbour is Årsta partihallar, the wholesale market, where Trädgårdshallen with its distinctive folded roof became the area's first completed building in 1962. Today the hall is Sweden's largest marketplace for the wholesale trade in ornamental plants.
Vid Brunnsvikens nordvästra strand ligge: On the north-west shore of Brunnsviken bay lies Bergshamra village, a villa area of cultural and historical value and a cultural reserve. In the house Övre Karlsro, from around 1865, the furniture designer Carl Malmsten lived with his family, so it's also called Carl Malmsten's House. Bergshamra gård itself was called Bergshammar before 1865, and its main building was demolished in 1929.
Vid Danderyds kyrka, en bit bort, står r: At Danderyd Church, a little way off, stands the runestone U 127, one of the so-called Jarlabanke stones from his well-known runestone causeway in Täby kyrkby. In the 17th century it lay in the church doorway as a threshold, was then walled into a wall, and broke into four pieces when it was taken out. Inside the church are more fragments, including one by the rune master Öpir that was found under the central aisle in 1915.
Vid Drevvikens nordvästra kant ligger Hö: On the north-western edge of Lake Drevviken is Hökarängens gård, a farm named after ‘hökare’, grocers, which then gave its name to the whole district of Hökarängen. Curiously enough, the farm is actually in Farsta! Right next to it are the Hökarängen baths, with a sandy beach around 60 metres long, a bathing jetty, rocks for sunbathing and a large meadow.
Vid Edsvikens strand en bit härifrån lig: On the shore of Edsviken bay, a little way from here, lies the Rådan estate, known since 1599. It has had a varied life, to say the least: first a croft, then a foreman's residence, a manor, a boarding school, military quarters and a police academy, and now it is a school once again. Nearby, the Igelbäcken stream also winds through a nature reserve with pine forest, broadleaf woodland and open land.
Vid Eneby torg står Enebykyrkan, en kyrk: At Eneby torg stands Enebykyrkan, a church with two congregations under one roof. It is run as a shared church by Danderyd parish of the Church of Sweden and Enebykyrkan's congregation in the Uniting Church in Sweden, which formerly belonged to the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden. All around spreads Enebyberg, a villa community with many buildings from the first half of the 20th century.
Vid Frölunda torg står Ställbart univers: At Frölunda torg stands Ställbart universum, Adjustable Universe, an abstract copper sculpture by Arne Jones from 1967. While it was dismantled during the rebuilding of the tram stop, someone stole the innermost rings, but it has been restored and is now back in place, if slightly moved. The Gothenburg comedy duo Kal and Ada would surely have had a joke or two to make about that.
Vid Gamlestads torg ligger Världslittera: At Gamlestads torg is Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature, a public library focusing on many languages, opened on 1 December 2018. The idea came from the librarian Ingrid Atlestam in an opinion piece in the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten, and the politicians took it up. Across three floors there is literature in many languages, and an auditorium at the top. Just south of the square are the Gamlestaden factories.
Vid Gubbängstorget låg en gång biografen: On Gubbängstorget square there was once the City cinema, which opened in April 1953 and closed twenty years later. In the 1950s, the new suburbs were meant to be self-sufficient in every kind of service, even having their own cinemas. Today the auditorium has a new life as Moment teater, a theatre that started here in 2000 and whose work with theatre classics won Svenska Dagbladet's Thalia Prize in 2008.
Vid Hagsätramotet korsar Olshammarsgatan: At the Hagsätra interchange, Olshammarsgatan crosses Huddingevägen on a bridge. The street is one of the district's two main routes and connects Hagsätra centre with Ormkärr, the name of the part of Hagsätra south-west of Huddingevägen. ‘Orm’ means snake – a snaky name, but nothing to worry about! The Hagsätra forest became a nature reserve in 2021.
Vid Herkulesgatan står Renströmska badan: On Herkulesgatan stands Renströmska badanstalten, a bathhouse completed in 1915 to designs by Eugen Thorburn. The baths closed in 1973 and were converted for the karate club Banzai Karate Kai. The last bath master was called Ante Melander. A short walk away rises Karlatornet, which at 246 metres is the tallest building in the Nordic countries.
Vid Hustegafjärden ligger Rönneberga, en: By the Hustegafjärden bay lies Rönneberga, a conference centre that opened in 1969 for trade union courses, where a lot was invested in artistic decoration right from the start. At Elfvik jetty stands Villa Söderås from 1912, a large villa that was on the market in 2021–2022 for 350 to 380 million kronor. The islet of Svanholmen at the mouth of the bay has in all likelihood been named after the swans that nested there early on.
Vid Hägerstens brandstation dolde sig Nä: At Hägersten fire station hid Nässlan, the Nettle, a secret command centre. It was built into the rock in 1943 as a bombproof district centre and vehicle shelter for the Stockholm fire brigade, rebuilt in 1977 as a so-called forward unit and closed down in the 1990s. Bäckvägen, next to it, got its name in 1924 after a stream that flows out into Årstaviken bay.
Vid Hötorget ligger Konserthuset, där No: At Hötorget is the Stockholm Concert Hall, where the Nobel Prize is awarded every year. A market is held on the square, and inside Hötorgshallen there are food stalls from all over the world.
Vid Jakobsbergs station står Gula villan: By Jakobsberg station stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, Jakobsberg's old station building, put up in 1876. In contrast to the modern life of Jakobsbergs Centrum, with its shops, cafés and restaurants, it is a reminder of when the railway came here. Today Jakobsberg is Järfälla's commercial and administrative centre.
Vid Jungfrusunds hamn på Ekeröns östra s: From Jungfrusund harbour on the eastern side of Ekerön, you look out over Vårbyfjärden bay and the Jungfruholmarna islands, where the Göta Sailing Club has had its club islands since 1915. A little way from here is Ekebyhovsbacken, the home slope of the Mälaröarna Alpine Ski Club, with sweeping views over Ekerön and Lake Mälaren.
Vid Kottlasjöns västra strand ligger Ape: On the western shore of Lake Kottlasjön stands the Orange Villa, which was actually called Skogsbacken. The master carpenter Per Johan Asker built it in 1890 as a summer residence with two flats, on speculation. It was one of several summer retreats that sprang up around the lake in the late 19th century. The villa and two small outbuildings have been listed since 1982.
Vid Lilla Bommen möter staden älven. Den: At Lilla Bommen the city meets the river. The red-and-white skyscraper is known as Läppstiftet, the Lipstick. It was completed in 1989 and has an observation floor at the very top. Next to it is the Gothenburg Opera, opened in 1994, and moored at the quay is the sailing ship Barken Viking from 1906.
Vid Linnéplatsen börjar Slottsskogen, st: At Linnéplatsen begins Slottsskogen, the city's great park from 1874. There are animals, ponds and the Natural History Museum, which has a stuffed blue whale from 1865. In the other direction runs Linnégatan, one of the city's best-loved restaurant streets.
Vid Maltesholmstorget, mitt i Hässelby S: At Maltesholmstorget, in the middle of Hässelby Strand's centre, stands Hässelby Strand Church. A stone's throw away the metro comes to an end: this is the green line's north-western terminus, a full 18.6 kilometres from Slussen. The station opened in November 1958, and the guests on the first train were served coffee during the journey.
Vid Mörbyfjärden, en kort bit härifrån,: By Mörbyfjärden bay, a short way from here, lies Lovö waterworks, opened in 1933. It is no small kitchen: in 2002 the works supplied drinking water to 40 per cent of the northern region of Greater Stockholm, and on an ordinary day it produces around 133,000 cubic metres. So when someone in northern Stockholm fills a glass from the tap, the water may well have passed through right here on western Lovön.
Vid Nacka ström föddes själva namnet Nac: The very name Nacka was born at Nacka ström, the rapids here: it was here, at Nacka gård, that the place was first called that. Around the rapids grew Nacka's first industries, with roots in the Middle Ages, including mills and a works making iron and brass goods. The large yellow wooden building now called Nacka gård is the tenant farmer's house from 1874, and Lake Järlasjön next to it is named after Järla gård, a farm mentioned as early as 1426.
Vid Nordre älvs mynning, en bit härifrån: At the mouth of the Nordre älv river, a little way from here, lies the small village of Korseberget. It may be the same place as Horsaberg, where King Magnus Ladulås and his brother Valdemar negotiated peace one summer's day in 1274. Nearby are Kyrkeby and Nereby, whose settlements have been redrawn and renamed in the statistics several times.
Vid Norrtull fick resenärerna från Uppsa: At Norrtull, travellers coming from the Uppsala direction had to pay a city toll, from the 1670s until the early 19th century. The street Norra Stationsgatan, by the way, was called Solnavägen right up until 1940. Today it's home to the restaurant Etoile, French for star, with only 26 seats and tasting menus of up to 20 courses. Fittingly, it was awarded a star in the Michelin Guide in 2020.
Vid Nybroplan ligger Dramaten, Kungliga: At Nybroplan stands Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, opened in 1908. From here Strandvägen begins, with its grand turn-of-the-century buildings along the water, and from Nybrokajen quay, boats head out into the archipelago.
Vid Odenplan ligger Gustav Vasa kyrka. E: At Odenplan stands Gustav Vasa church. A short distance away, on Sveavägen, is the Stockholm Public Library, designed by Gunnar Asplund and famous for its round lending hall.
Vid Råckstavägen står två bostadshus med: On Råckstavägen stand two residential buildings with 247 flats, built using the ‘Snabba hus’, or ‘Fast Houses’, concept. Tenants moved in at the end of 2019, and the project was one of ten finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year 2020. Nearby is Råcksta gård, neighbouring the buildings where Vattenfall used to have its head office. And Anundsvägen, a residential street of villas, has been visited by none other than Queen Elizabeth II.
Vid Spånga kyrkväg en bit härifrån ligge: By Spånga kyrkväg, a little way from here, is the Sörgården block, with 76 L-shaped small houses from the early 1970s, designed by Höjer and Ljungqvist. The City Museum has given them a green rating as particularly valuable. Down in Rinkeby metro station, opened in 1975, three artists created the decoration, including Nisse Zetterberg's brick-red walls.
Vid Stadsgården hade Saltsjöbanan en gån: Saltsjöbanan, the Saltsjö railway, once had its station at Stadsgården, in use from 1893 to 1936, and the station building later became the Seamen's Institute. Beside it, the Lokatten stairs climb up towards Katarinavägen; they were built in 1914, closed in the 1970s and reopened to the public in 2023. Since 2022 the old cruise terminal has been the Stadsgårdsterminalen cultural centre, with a bar, a roof terrace and a live stage.
Vid Stocksundets strand låg bryggeriet I: On the shore of Stocksundet stood the Inverness brunn brewery, which made Sweden's first club soda. The spring is still there, but the water tastes salty. A stone's throw away is Calles klimp, Calle's Lump, a slab of rock with gilded lettering. Legends say Calle was Karl IX, Karl XII or Karl XV. Most likely it was a spice merchant, Carl Eneroth, who was given it as a birthday present.
Vid Sundby, en bit härifrån, finns spår: At Sundby, a little way from here, there are traces from the Viking Age: a large and lavish rune-carved rock, and right next to it another rune rock that was never finished. History does not tell us who left it half done. The name Sundby itself has been known since 1312, and today the district counts as part of Gamla Spånga, Old Spånga, with its many villas.
Vid Sätra prästgård, i nordvästra hörnet: At Sätra rectory, in the north-western corner of Danderyd parish, stands Sätraäng Church, a district church. The area round about is full of water and forest: a little further away, on the Sollentuna side, the district of Sjöberg is squeezed in between Edsviken bay, Lake Rösjön and the Rinkeby woods, divided into Östra Sjöberg, Västra Sjöberg and Falkberget.
Vid Södertäljevägen låg en gång Gyllene: On Södertäljevägen there was once Gyllene ratten, the Golden Steering Wheel, one of Sweden's first motels on the American model. It opened in 1957 and became a landmark for motorists thanks to its mast with a steering wheel on top, but was demolished 50 years later. A little way off is Fruängen metro station, which at 46.8 metres above sea level is the highest in the entire metro network.
Vid Södertäljevägen, i höjd med trafikpl: On Södertäljevägen road, level with the Bredäng interchange, stood the motel Gyllene ratten, the Golden Steering Wheel, one of Sweden's first on the American model. It opened in 1957, and its mast with a steering wheel on top was a landmark for motorists, until the motel was demolished 50 years later. Even older history can be found in Segeltorp, where the croft Istorp, also called Komöte, was established around 1650 under the Vårby manor.
Vid Torpagatan sitter skulpturen Ensam a: On Torpagatan sits the sculpture Ensam, Alone, by Margareta Ryndel: a small child crouching with its arms pressed tight to its chest. It was put up in 1988 in memory of the Vidkärr children's home, which stood in the neighbourhood. For a long time there was a plaque speaking of love and care at the children's home, but many of those who had lived there felt the text was a gross mockery, and the plaque has since been removed.
Vid Träkvista torg finns det mesta en vi: At Träkvista torg you'll find most things a villa suburb needs: a grocery store, a pizzeria, a paint shop, a toy shop and a restaurant. Träkvista village was actually the centre of Ekerö municipality until 1990, when Ekerö centrum opened. Nearby, on Ekerövägen, is also Fantans hög, a legendary offering cairn. The houses here are mostly villas, linked houses and terraced houses.
Vid Ulvsundasjön flyttade man en gång en: By Lake Ulvsundasjön, an entire manor house was once moved. The old main building of Huvudsta gård was moved about 300 metres to the north-west, and in 1836 the new manor was completed. Right next to it, by the waterfront promenade, is Huvudstabadet, a heated outdoor pool. A little further away is Sweden's longest escalator, 66 metres long, down in Västra skogen metro station.
Vid den stora cirkulationsplatsen Bergsl: At the large Bergslagsplan roundabout, roads including Lövstavägen and Bergslagsvägen meet, and nearby is Hässelby Palace from the 1650s, one of Stockholm's oldest surviving secular buildings. At the palace entrance stands a runestone on a Viking Age burial mound. In Vällingby centre, a little way from here, is the brick church of St Thomas, S:t Tomas kyrka, designed by Peter Celsing and consecrated in 1960, with a wooden crucifix by Bror Hjorth.
Vid kommunalhusets entré står Bror Hjort: At the entrance to the municipal building stands Bror Hjorth's bronze Flicka med fruktkorg, Girl with a Fruit Basket, from 1951. The apple basket is a tribute to Huddinge's thousands of villa gardens and the housewives who harvested the fruit and pressed juice. Behind the churchyard lies the Bishop's Stone, Biskopsstenen, a giant boulder from the Ice Age. It measures 7 by 4 metres, and its tip resembles a bishop's mitre.
Vid kyrkan står en runsten som ser ut so: By the church stands a runestone that looks like a small stone ship: the Botkyrka Monument, a grave memorial to Saint Botvid's brother Björn, who in 1129 had the predecessor of today's church built. The one here is a copy – the original is in the Swedish History Museum, and another copy, in plaster, has ended up at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London. There are more runestones around the church, one of them built into the wall beneath the church tower and only partly visible.
Vid pendeltågsstationen står Gula villan: At the commuter train station stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, Jakobsberg's old station building from 1876. Today about 10,200 people a day board the train here, 17.4 kilometres from Stockholm Central. The bus terminal next door is a so-called docking terminal, where you wait indoors and go out through a separate door to each bus bay.
Vid plaskdammen på Älvsborgsplan ligger: By the paddling pool at Älvsborgsplan lies a beach ball that nobody can throw. The sculpture Boll, Ball, by Berit Lindfeldt is a stainless steel sphere about two metres across, light blue with shiny dots. Nearby stands the bronze statue Young Man by Astrid Noack, and the Slottsskogen allotment colony, founded in 1916, today has 154 plots.
Vid sjön Drevviken ligger Strandkyrkogår: By Lake Drevviken lies Strandkyrkogården, a cemetery in the Skrubba district. Skrubba farm was once home to Skrubba skyddshem, a reform institution meant to take in and bring up boys from Stockholm who were considered “wayward” to a lesser degree. Nearby is also Skrubbatriangeln, an industrial area named quite simply because it is shaped like a triangle.
Vid sjön Flatens norra strand, en bit hä: On the northern shore of Lake Flaten, a little way from here, is Listudden, whose main building dates from the mid-18th century and which the City Museum has blue-listed for its exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Further along the same shore was Ekudden, first a tenant croft and then a summer retreat, until the main building burned down in the late 1960s. The remains are today an ancient monument.
Vid sjön Magelungen alldeles intill driv: By lake Magelungen right next door, the Salvation Army runs Ågesta folkhögskola, a folk high school, and an officers' school. The little crofter's cottage Nynäs is still there too and today belongs to the recreation area. A little further away, on a headland, is Ågestabadet, the City of Stockholm's only official naturist beach, even though it's in Huddinge. So here you're free to swim just as nature made you.
Vid tunnelbanans viadukt står skulpturen: By the metro viaduct stands the sculpture "Bird Rock with Three Eggs" by Berndt Helleberg from 1969. The viaduct is older than the metro. It came into use in 1944 and was served by trams back then. The station's art, in sheet metal, glass and photographs, is about the history of Bromma and of aviation. The 16-storey Brommahöjden tower block didn't arrive until 2008.
Vid Årstadalshamnen sträcker Kajen 4 på: At Årstadalshamnen, Kajen 4 stretches upwards, a 75-metre, 24-storey residential tower designed by Gert Wingårdh, which was named Stockholm Building of the Year in 2015. A little way off is the City Archives at Liljeholmskajen, housed in two of Vin och Sprit's old rock caverns, where the city's building history has been kept since 2019. On Sjövikstorget stands the artwork En tidsmaskin, A Time Machine, by Jan Svenungsson.
Viggbyholm delas av E18 och järnvägen, o: Viggbyholm is divided by the E18 and the railway, so people usually talk about the Lake Side, the Station Side and the Rönningesjö Side. By Stora Värtan bay is Viggbyholm Boat Club, with about 1,900 members. A little way off, Täby Park is taking shape, a new district where the Täby Galopp racecourse stood from 1960 to 2016, planned for about 20,000 residents.
Viksjö kyrka i Viksjö centrum är ovanlig: Viksjö Church in Viksjö centre is unusually young: it was consecrated by Bishop Caroline Krook on 19 June 2005. Much older is Viksjö gård, a manor and former noble estate on a hill surrounded by modern Viksjö, built on the old farmland. In the 17th century the estate was held by, among others, the Skytte family.
Viksjöleden, som byggdes ut i etapper på: Viksjöleden, built in stages in the 1970s and 80s, winds through Jakobsberg, Viksjö and Veddesta down to the E18. A little way from here is Järfälla Church, where in 1728 Olof Celsius the Elder found a runestone that was probably lying as a step. It then disappeared, but in 1939 seven fragments of it were found.
Viktoriagatan 12 är en adress för matäls: Viktoriagatan 12 is an address for food lovers. That's where Kock & Vin got a star in the Michelin Guide in 2008, and when the restaurant closed in 2014, the chef Björn Persson opened Koka in the same premises. It got its own Michelin star as early as 2015. Also take a look at Tomtehuset, the Gnome House, from 1890, on the corner of Vasagatan. Its murals show gnomes working as an architect, a printer and a photographer.
Vill man kliva rakt in i 1969 finns Kämp: If you want to step straight into 1969, there is Kämpingebacken 13, a museum flat rented by the City Museum. The interior is preserved from when it was built and shows what things looked like when Tensta was built during the Million Programme housing drive, between 1966 and 1972. Tensta konsthall, an art centre for contemporary art, is also just a couple of minutes away.
Villa Emmalund från 1885 låg när den byg: When it was built, Villa Emmalund from 1885 stood by a country road leading to Hägersten's manor. A farm slaughterhouse operated here, mainly for horses, until compulsory slaughter at the public abattoirs was introduced in 1912. After that it became a butcher's shop and other businesses, and the outbuilding served as a stable, slaughterhouse and carriage shed.
Villa Gröndal, ett stenkast härifrån, bl: Villa Gröndal, a stone's throw from here, became the last home of the poet Gustaf Fröding. A little further away winds the Love Path, which WWF gave as a wedding present to Crown Princess Victoria and Prince Daniel in 2010. Thanks to it, you can now walk all the way around Isbladskärret marsh, a 1.6-kilometre stroll. Nearby was also the Manilla school, which Pär Aron Borg founded for deaf and blind children.
Villa Lyran byggdes 1867 för Carl och Fr: Villa Lyran was built in 1867 for Carl and Fredrika Limnell with a view over Lake Mälaren, and it is one of the finest examples of the summer houses that well-off Stockholmers had built by the lake. Pettersberg, a little further away, was once a lakeside tavern and croft. Out in the strait between Fågelön and Bredäng lies the islet of Fläsket, with a lighthouse of the same name.
Villa Marieborg alldeles intill började: Villa Marieborg, right next to us, started out as the croft Aspviken in 1712. In the 1770s the commerce councillor Paul Prinzell turned it into a villa and named it after his wife Maria. Today's villa, however, was built in 1902 by the industrialist Ernst Gäbel. A little further away is Rödkinda children's home, whose name, 'red cheeks', refers to the idea that the fresh air would give the children rosy cheeks. The square by the metro is named after Stieg Trenter, who was born nearby and set his novel Träff i helfigur in this area.
Villa Strandvik i jugendstil, alldeles i: Villa Strandvik, the Art Nouveau villa right next to us, was built between 1911 and 1912 for the engineer Axel Odelberg from the porcelain factory's management. Since then the house has served as an officers' mess, hotel, offices and treatment centre, and the municipality has designated it as culturally and historically indispensable. A short walk away, in the factory's old Torkhus, or drying house, is the Gustavsberg Porcelain Museum, which has been open to the public since 1956.
Villaområdet Edsviken i Helenelund har f: The villa area Edsviken in Helenelund is named after Edsviken, the Baltic inlet it borders to the north-east. A little way off, by Kummelby church, stands a runestone from the late 11th century, the Kummelby stone. The church stands where the old Kummelby farm once lay.
Villaområdet Flysta gömmer en försvunnen: The villa area of Flysta hides a lost Viking Age runestone, Uppland runic inscription 70. It has been searched for several times without success and has probably disappeared. In the neighbouring district of Beckomberga, the so-called Round Houses were built in 1953–1954 on the corner of Bällstavägen and Spångavägen, as staff housing mainly for the nurses at Beckomberga hospital.
Villaområdet Nysätra ligger på en udde m: The villa area of Nysätra lies on a headland between Kyrkviken, Järlasjön and Sicklasjön. At the very tip, on Nackanäs, stood Nackanäs värdshus, an out-of-town inn that welcomed guests from 1859 until it burned down in 1960, and its predecessor, Nacka värdshus, stood on the other side of the water for a full 300 years. A little way off stands Setterwallska villan, a magnificent patrician villa from 1896 built by a successful shipowner.
Villaområdet Råstahem kallades ursprungl: The villa area of Råstahem was originally called Ulriksdals järnvägshem, the Ulriksdal railway homes, by SJ, the state railways, and the plots were sold only to people employed by Statens Järnvägar. Most of the houses were built in the second half of the 1920s and the first half of the 1930s. The railway is still close by: Hagalund yard is Sweden's largest marshalling yard for passenger trains.
Villaområdet Sjövalla i östra Mölndal bö: Building began in the villa area of Sjövalla in eastern Mölndal as early as the 1920s and 1930s. A little further away is Kristinedal, completed in 1964, which lies by Lake Stensjön, near Gunnebo House and Lake Rådasjön. The houses there were designed by an architect at Småhusbyrån, the small-house office in Malmö, and built by Skånska Cementgjuteriet, in the ideal of the day with brick façades and long, stretched-out floor plans.
Villaområdet Skälby i södra Järfälla har: The villa area Skälby in southern Järfälla is named after the nearby manor Skälby gård, a former noble estate. In the Barkarby-Skälby district there are neighbourhoods with almost space-age names, like the Neptuni, Orgona and Aniara areas in Skälby. Here you'll also find Kyrkbyn, with the Gästgivargården coaching inn, which in recent years has gone by the name Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja.
Villaområdet heter Edsviken efter viken: The villa area is called Edsviken after the inlet of the Baltic Sea that it borders. Edsviken itself is about 7.7 kilometres long but narrow, about 20 metres at its deepest, and stretches from Stocksund to Edsberg. Along its shores are several grand buildings: Ulriksdal Palace, Edsberg Palace, Rådan and Bergendal Manor.
Villasamhället Storängen grundades 1904: The villa community of Storängen was founded in 1904 by a home-ownership association for white-collar workers, and the same year Villa Lodén, the very first villa, was built for one of the founders. There's a health centre, a pizzeria, tobacconists and a pastry shop for anyone in need of a fika, a coffee break, and there's a restaurant nearby. Local clubs also have their premises by the square. The square is on tram line six, by its terminus.
