From here it's not far to nature reserves and sea bathing in Västra Frölunda.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Opalt: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Opaltorget! The journey takes about 66 minutes. Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan and Meteorgatan: Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön the street names come from outer space. A little way from here is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, with Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön culture house. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, and offers everything from music and art to children's events.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot T-Cen: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards T-Centralen! The journey takes about 13 minutes. Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen. He was the son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his time. Today his villa and garden are an art museum by the water.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Walde: Welcome aboard tram 7 to Waldemarsudde! The journey takes about 12 minutes. Beneath the streets, blue vines and leaves climb over the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and among the tendrils you can see silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was otherwise best known for his mechanical sculptures and helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, 'She – a Cathedral', in 1966.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 8 to Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 64 minutes. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 and was one of Sweden's first large suburban shopping centres. All around lies Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Frölu: Welcome aboard tram 8 towards Frölunda Torg! The journey takes about 63 minutes. Angered was built in the 1970s and is today one of Gothenburg's most international districts. This is where the Blå Stället culture house is, and all around are large natural areas with lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 57 minutes. Kungssten is near the mouth of Göta älv, the Göta River. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966. Out in the river mouth lies Nya Älvsborg fortress from the 1600s, which protected the city against the Danes. By the water below is Klippan, with old seamen's houses and the remains of the older Älvsborg fortress.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Kungs: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Kungssten! The journey takes about 56 minutes. Angered was built in the 1970s and is today one of Gothenburg's most international districts. Here is the Blå Stället cultural centre, and all around there are large nature areas with lakes and forest.
Välkommen ombord! Du kliver på vid Drott: Welcome aboard! You're getting on at Drottningtorget, right in front of the Central Station. You're sitting on one of the trams in the largest tram network in the Nordic countries. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and the city chose to keep its trams when many other Swedish cities scrapped theirs. The Central Station opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Sit back and relax. We'll travel along the river, through the old working-class districts and out to the sea.
Välkommen till Majorna. Titta på husen:: Welcome to Majorna. Look at the houses: a stone ground floor with two wooden storeys on top. That's a landshövdingehus, a type of house found almost only in Gothenburg. It got round an old rule that wooden houses couldn't be more than two storeys high. The stone floor didn't count.
Välkommen till Mölndal. Längs forsen i M: Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Mölndal's mill village, Kvarnbyn, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today Kvarnbyn is a cultural heritage area with a museum and cafés.
Vällingby Centrum blev en internationell: Vällingby Centrum became an international model for modern town centres when it was completed in 1954. The metro depot next door was originally called Spångahallen, a slightly odd name that came about because Vällingby was part of Spånga municipality before it merged with the City of Stockholm. Right next door is also Jan-Pers stuga, Jan-Per's cottage.
Vällingby planerades som ABC-staden, med: Vällingby was planned as an "ABC town", with work, housing and a town centre in the same place. It even included its own cinema. The Fontänen cinema opened in 1956 and was named after the fountains in the square. The same year saw the opening of the Trappan community centre, built in terraces between a lower and an upper square. Both were designed by Backström & Reinius.
Vällsjön ligger några hundra meter bort,: Lake Vällsjön is a few hundred metres away, a small lake only four and a half metres deep. It forms Pixbo's southeastern boundary, and the Vällbäcken stream runs between Vällsjön and Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo itself is built on and around the height of Björnåsen, so it's hilly here.
Världens första kurdiska bibliotek finns: The world's first Kurdish library is a stone's throw from here. The Kurdish Library opened in 1997 and was first on Skeppsholmen for ten years, before moving, after a stopover in Duvbo, into Alvik's community centre in 2011. The shelves hold around 13,000 books in almost 30 different languages, above all Kurdish. Next door is Sankt Ansgar's church.
Världskulturmuseet: Världskulturmuseet, the Museum of World Culture
Världslitteraturhuset: Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature
Värtahamnen anlades 1879 till 1886 som h: Värtahamnen harbour was built between 1879 and 1886 as a port for coal and other bulky goods; today the ferries leave from here for Finland, Åland, Estonia and Latvia. The old Kommunalhuset building housed Värtan fire station between 1905 and 1934. A little further away, outside the entrance to the Värtaverket power plant, stands Kungseken, the King's Oak, around 600 years old. It was probably named after Oscar II, who made spring outings to the oak.
Västberga begravningsplats, mellan Solbe: Västberga cemetery, between Solberga, Västberga and Liseberg, has the City Museum's blue rating for its exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Its neighbour is Liseberg, which at 38 hectares is the smallest district in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. A little further on is Årsta partihallar, where around 200 companies trade in fruit, vegetables, fish and flowers.
Västberga gård, med anor från 1300-talet: Västberga gård, dating back to the 14th century, became a noble estate in the 17th century and has given its name to the whole district. Since 1935 the manor has been owned by the City of Stockholm. A little way from here runs the Älvsjö Arch, Älvsjöbågen, a 1,396-metre railway bridge that is part of the Citybanan rail link and Sweden's fourth-longest railway bridge, built using a technique unusual in Sweden.
Västerortskyrkan i Vällingby centrum rit: Västerortskyrkan in Vällingby centre was designed by Carl Nyrén and Bertil Engstrand and built in 1956. From the outside it is closed and rendered, but inside you meet New Brutalism, with dramatically leaning walls of untreated concrete and light filtering in from the roof. The church is also built together with an eleven-storey residential block.
Västertorps tunnelbanestation är den näs: Västertorp metro station is the second-highest in the whole network, 42.8 metres above sea level. The district is also home to Stockholm's largest sculpture park, with 21 outdoor sculptures. And at Västertorpsplan was the neighbourhood cinema Västan, which showed films between 1954 and 1971.
Västra Balltorp ligger alldeles intill e: Västra Balltorp is right next to a golf course, and the golf club has even been a party to the development of the area. Its neighbour, Östra Balltorp, has had trouble making up its mind: sometimes it counts as a town of its own, sometimes as part of Gothenburg, depending on which year Statistics Sweden did its count.
Västra Hisingen är industrins och hamnar: Western Hisingen is the realm of industry and ports. A little way from here is the Preemraff oil refinery, which buys its crude oil mostly from the North Sea. In the neighbouring district of Arendal, the Arendal shipyard operated between 1963 and 1989, and today it is home to, among other things, the headquarters of Volvo Buses. Arendal is such a purely industrial area that only 90 people lived there in 2012.
Vålberga, en bit härifrån, är ett bostad: Vålberga, a little way from here, is a residential area built around 1963 that consists mostly of rows of terraced houses. It is in Barkarby-Skälby, Järfälla's southernmost district. Nearby is also the manor Skälby gård, between four burial grounds. And the old Barkarby parish merged into a re-formed Järfälla parish in 2010.
Vårberg centrum invigdes i september 196: Vårberg centre opened in September 1968, just under a year after the metro station in the same building complex, and has been praised for its international modernist architecture. According to the City Museum, it is an early and well-preserved example of an indoor square. Nearby is the Kummelholmen art gallery, whose name simply comes from the building's property designation.
Vårberg sträcker sig hela vägen ner till: Vårberg stretches all the way down to Lake Mälaren in the north-west, and 65 hectares of the district's area is water. The homes in the Bergholmen block on Rönnholmsgränd were built in the late 1960s and are green-listed by the City Museum. The same goes for Vårbergsskolan, which was built from 1968 to 1972 as a lower secondary school and today houses an adult education college and an independent school.
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation invigdes den: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967, and just under a year later Vårberg Centre opened in the same building complex. The centre has been praised for its international modernist architecture and is an early example of an indoor square. Nearby is Vårberg nursing home from the late 1960s, which for a long time was Vårberg's only major workplace, and the Kummelholmen art gallery.
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation öppnade den 2: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967 and has an outdoor platform, 12.6 kilometres from Slussen. Less than a year later, in September 1968, Vårberg centrum opened in the same building complex. It is an indoor square that the City Museum has green-listed for its value in urban planning history and its international modernist architecture.
Vårfrukyrkan: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady
Vårfrukyrkan i Fruängen fick vänta länge: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady in Fruängen, had to wait a long time for its church hall. The red-brick church centre opened in 1963, but without the worship space shown on the plans. It wasn't until 2004 that construction began, in cast-in-place concrete, and on the first Sunday of Advent 2005 the church could be consecrated and given the name Vårfrukyrkan.
Vårväderstorget ritades av arkitekten He: Vårväderstorget was designed by the architect Helge Zimdal and completed in 1958, built in Italian style with terraces and arches. The name, meaning Spring Weather Square, is one of Biskopsgården's many on the theme of weather and meteorology. The square has its own tram stop, and here you'll find, among other things, Göteborgs folkhögskola, a folk high school, and Biskopsgården library, one of the city's most visited.
Waldemarsudde var konstnären prins Eugen: Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen. He was the son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his time. Today his villa and garden are an art museum by the water.
Wendelsbergs folkhögskola: Wendelsbergs folkhögskola, the Wendelsberg folk high school
Willy Brandts park: Willy Brandts park, Willy Brandt Park
Ytterby har gamla anor, bygden har varit: Ytterby has a long history; the area has been settled since the Iron Age and is full of ancient remains. A little way from here stands the ruin of Ytterby's old church, built in Romanesque style in the 1100s on what was then Norwegian land. Legend attributes the building to Saint Olaf, and perhaps the stone church was preceded by an even older wooden church from the 1000s.
Äggelundastenen, en runsten som ursprung: The Äggelunda Stone, a runestone that originally stood at Äggelunda gård in Veddesta, was moved in 2014 to the Fruns backe burial ground when building work started around Barkarby commuter train station. Another runestone in Veddesta has had worse luck: it was mentioned in 1728 by Olof Celsius the Elder and has been missing ever since.
Äggelundastenen, runstenen U 84, stod ur: The Äggelunda stone, runestone U 84, originally stood at Äggelunda farm in Veddesta. When the area around Barkarby commuter train station was to be developed in 2014, the stone was moved to the burial-ground area Fruns backe, south-west of Veddesta gård. Not far from there stand two more Viking Age runestones, known as the runestones on Häradsvägen.
Äldreboendet Danvikshem har en historia: The Danvikshem care home has a history going back to Danvik's Hospital, which was founded in 1551 and didn't close until 1915. Nearby was also the Danvik asylum, a mental hospital that existed between 1788 and 1861, and along Kvarnholmsvägen lies an abandoned cemetery, Danvikens begravningsplats. Happier memories belong to the Goman Building, Gomanhuset, where the Swedish Cooperative Union, Kooperativa Förbundet, had its charcuterie laboratory.
Älta är en av Nackas fyra kommundelar, o: Älta is one of Nacka's four districts, and nearby is Stensö, where around 2,600 people live. It is named after the peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip is the Stensö swimming spot. A couple of minutes away, next to Ältavägen, is Älta Church.
Ältavägen är 8,1 kilometer lång och fick: Ältavägen is 8.1 kilometres long and got its route in 1934. It runs mostly through undeveloped countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. In the Flaten nature reserve there is an unusual attraction: a racing track for radio-controlled model cars. It is at Ältavägen 301 in the Flaten district.
Älvestaån rinner från sjön Aspen till Tu: The Älvestaån stream flows from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön and drops 17 metres over only about 2.5 kilometres. Part of it runs in a culvert under Hågelby manor and the Hågelbyleden road. In Hågelby's park the stream has been reshaped into a canal and become part of the park's design. The name comes from Elvesta farm by Lake Tullingesjön, which is also spelled Älvesta.
Älvsborgs kyrka hette tidigare Hagens ka: Älvsborg church used to be called Hagen's chapel and has belonged to Älvsborg parish since 1967. A little further away rises Stora Billingen, a 40-metre-high hill by Nya Varvet. Spaces for military use were blasted into the rock beneath it, but in the 2000s HSB was allowed to build 50 small houses in the area after all appeals had been rejected.
Älvsjö gård har mycket gamla anor, med k: Älvsjö gård has very old roots, with known owners since the mid-15th century. One and the same family held the farm for almost two centuries, right up to 1968. For a long time the area was sparsely built up. Around the turn of the 20th century, the population consisted mostly of people who worked on the farm and at the station.
Älvsjövägen har en imponerande trafikmän: Älvsjövägen carries an impressive amount of traffic. With 22,000 vehicles a day, it equals all the daily border traffic between Norway and Sweden along the E6 and E18 combined. A calmer spot is Solbergaskogen, a little way off, a forest classified as a key habitat in 2009 that holds ancient remains such as the Solberga burial ground.
Ändhållplatsen ligger vid Östra sjukhuse: The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset hospital. From here it is a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes, forest and swimming spots, where many Gothenburgers spend their weekends.

The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset hospital. From here it is a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes, forest and swimming spots, where many Gothenburgers spend their weekends. Thanks for riding with us!
Ängarna en kort promenad härifrån är sed: Since 2026, the meadows a short walk from here have been protected as the Rissne ängar nature reserve, about 21 hectares where Rissne, Hallonbergen and Duvbo meet. Open meadows are surrounded by wooded slopes with pine, and several red-listed beetles thrive here. A little further away is Duvbo Church, which stands on a steep rocky slope among the villas.
Ängen Svartlöten, alldeles i närheten, ä: The meadow Svartlöten, right nearby, is an ancient monument and gave its name to Svarta Löt, a medieval assembly site mentioned in several documents from the 1400s. The assembly site itself is thought to have been at the croft Eriksberg by Kumla gård, partly where the E4/E20 motorway runs today. All around, the Botkyrka town grew up in the late 1960s and early 1970s, as part of the so-called Million Programme, Sweden's large-scale housing drive. Alby centrum opened in 1972, and on the square just outside, fresh fruit and vegetables are sold.
Ärvinge är ett informellt område i södra: Ärvinge is an informal area in southern Kista, and from here it's not far to Kista Galleria. It has not only 180 shops and restaurants but also a bowling alley, a multiplex cinema and a go-kart track covering a full 4,000 square metres. Students also live in the mall's two towers, so some people have the shopping right under their beds.
Ät eller handla i Kville saluhall: Eat or shop at Kville saluhall food hall
Åbyvägen har fått sitt namn efter byn Åb: Åbyvägen is named after the village of Åby, which lay between Brunnby and Ersta gård and is believed to have existed as early as the Viking Age, right up to the early 1500s. The road has also been called Fabian Wredes väg. Ersta is a vanished farm too; it lay on the south-western part of Årstafältet. On the same field is the Årstafältet allotment area, which in 2018 was counted as Stockholm's newest allotment garden.
Ågesta gårds stora stenbyggnad från 1600: The large 17th-century stone building of Ågesta farm is right next to us and got its present appearance around 1800. Since 1945 the farm has been owned by the City of Stockholm. Below it lies Lake Ågestasjön, and the name is a little riddle. 'Åg' is an old word for bulrush and reed, but the local heritage society thinks the name comes from 'Åkes sta', Åke's place. The lake is part of the Orlången nature reserve.
Ågestaverket: Ågestaverket, the old nuclear power plant
Åkermyntans centrum är ett litet köpcent: Åkermyntans centrum is a small shopping centre that opened in November 1977, but it has earned a place in comedy history. In one of the sketches by the comedy group Killinggänget, the character Fred Asp, known for partying with his ferret Göran, lives near Åkermyntan. A little way off is the Hässelby garden and local history museum, and outside it stands a grey granite runestone that was found in Riddersvik in the early 19th century.
Åkeshovs slott var en gång centrum för e: Åkeshov Castle was once the centre of a large estate, where districts such as Nockeby, Nockebyhov and Åkeslund were later built. Baroness Agneta Wrede lived at the castle for more than fifty years, from 1747 to 1800, and has a room named after her. In the castle park stands an orangery in elegant Rococo style, designed by Carl Hårleman in 1749, and next to it is an arboretum planted during Stockholm's year as European Capital of Culture in 1998.
Åkeshovshallen invigdes 1959 och öppnade: Åkeshovshallen swimming hall opened in 1959 and reopened in 2018 after more than two years of renovation. In the big pools the water is kept at 27 degrees, and in the children's area at 29. A little way from here is the Linnéa allotment area, also called Kortenslund after the old boatswain's croft that once stood on the site. A little further on you can glimpse Åkeshov's orangery from 1749.
Ålkistan kallas trakten där Brunnsviken: Ålkistan is the name for the area where Brunnsviken bay connects to Saltsjön, and the canal here was blasted out in 1863 to 1864. On Roslagsvägen, on the north side, there was once the Ålkistan inn, which was built in the early 18th century and demolished in the 1880s. The residential area Sfären itself is also called Himlabacken and was built from 1989 to 1991.
Ångloksnördar, se hit! En kort promenad: Steam engine fans, look this way! A short walk away is the home of Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap, a non-profit society formed in 1972 to preserve locomotives, mainly from the Bergslagen Railways. They have around a hundred vehicles, among them working restored steam, electric and diesel locomotives. The Rex cinema was also nearby, showing films from 1959 to 1973.
År 1645, under Hannibalsfejdens slutsked: In 1645, during the final stage of the Hannibal Controversy war, Hannibal Sehested tried to attack Gothenburg. Norwegian troops threw a temporary bridge across the Göta älv river, and on Hisingen the Fredrikshamn redoubt was built to protect the bridgehead. The redoubt is right nearby, a reminder that this riverbank was once a battlefield.
År 1926 fick Farstanäsbron en filmroll:: In 1926 the Farstanäs bridge got a film role: it played the bridge defended by the soldier Sven Dufva in the film Fänrik Ståls sägner, The Tales of Ensign Stål. The bridge over Lake Magelungen was originally built by the armed forces and is therefore also called Militärbron, the Military Bridge. Today's 200-metre-long footbridge and cycle bridge dates from 1998. At Farsta gård, a little way off, stands Farstastenen, the Farsta Stone, the only surviving runestone in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Årsta centrum var det första förortscent: Årsta centrum was the first suburban centre built in Sweden, completed in 1953 and inspired by English community centres. The Forum cinema on the square opened as early as 1951. Just south of Årsta church, designed by Johan Celsing and consecrated in 2011, is a burial ground from the late Iron Age with ten burial mounds and 35 stone settings, two of them ship-shaped.
Årstadal har tillsammans med Sundbyberg: Together with Sundbyberg, Årstadal has been described as Stockholm's first suburb. Close by, the Nyboda tunnels run through the rock, and the oldest of them became Sweden's first railway tunnel when the Western Main Line reached the city in 1860. Up on the hill above Liljeholmskajen is Årstabergsparken, a park that opened in 2018 and was even nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year.
Årstafruns park fick sitt namn 2010 efte: Årstafruns park got its name in 2010 after Årstafrun, the Lady of Årsta, Märta Helena Reenstierna, diarist and manor owner at Årsta gård. Right next to it stand the EPA houses, among the first deck-access apartment buildings in Sweden and today protected under the Cultural Environment Act. A little way off is Snigelparken, the Snail Park, where children play in a sandpit shaped like a concrete snail.
Årstalänken bjuder på en ovanlig syn: de: Årstalänken offers an unusual sight: the eastern part of this motorway section has been closed since 2004 and is a so-called ruin motorway, where homes are now being planned. Årstaberg commuter train station has around 8,300 boarding passengers on an ordinary winter weekday, and the Tvärbanan light rail has stopped here since 2000. On Årstaskogs väg rise the Årstahusen, three residential tower blocks built from 2017 to 2020.
Årstaskolan byggdes 1946 efter ritningar: Årsta school was built in 1946 to designs by Stig Åkermark and today has just over 900 pupils, from the preschool class to year nine. Many streets in Årsta are named after lakes, and Hjälmarsvägen was named after Lake Hjälmaren in 1941. Nearby also runs Södra länken, whose longest tunnel, at 3.8 kilometres, is Sweden's longest road tunnel.
Årstidstorget kallas av många kort och g: Many people simply call Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, 'Norra' or 'Norra centrum', and it is the little meeting place of northern Kortedala. There's a health centre, a pizzeria, tobacconists and a pastry shop for anyone in need of a fika, a coffee break, and there's a restaurant nearby. Local clubs also have their premises by the square. The square is on tram line six, by its terminus.
Åt Järfällahållet breder Viksjö ut sig,: Towards Järfälla spreads Viksjö, a district of about 11 square kilometres with mostly small houses from the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s and plenty of natural areas. On the Stockholm side is Backlura, where all the streets are named after flowers and plants. The Hässelby district administration area, by the way, existed for only two years, 1997 and 1998.
Åva gymnasium: Åva upper secondary school, Åva gymnasium
Åva gymnasium invigdes 1972 där Roslagsb: Åva upper secondary school opened in 1972 where the Roslagsbanan railway splits. The school magazine Cumulus has won the Lilla journalistpriset award twice and been named Sweden's best school magazine. In 2018 the school was given an industrial robot from AGA's research, and the students brought it back to life themselves. A little way off stands Tibble church, which has been called the cathedral of Roslagen.
Ö-varvet en bit bort är en riktig familj: The Ö-varvet shipyard a little way off is a true family saga. Ernst Backman founded it in 1916 as a repair yard for fishing boats, his sons Gösta and Hugo took over in 1945, and since then two more generations of Backmans have been in charge. Today the yard can service ships of up to 900 tonnes. Nearby is Öckerö old church, also called Mariakyrkan.
Ö-varvet grundades 1916 av Ernst Backman: Ö-varvet, the shipyard, was founded in 1916 by Ernst Backman as a repair yard for fishing boats, and since then it has been passed down through several generations of the Backman family. Today the yard builds and repairs vessels of up to 900 tonnes and also makes trawls and fishing winches. The sea also shapes Öckerö seglande gymnasieskola, the sailing upper secondary school a little further away, where around 300 students take programmes with a maritime element.
Ö-varvet på Öckerö grundades 1916 av Ern: Ö-varvet, the shipyard on Öckerö, was founded in 1916 by Ernst Backman as a repair yard for fishing boats and has since been passed down through several generations of Backmans. In 1997 to 1998 a branch yard was set up here on Hönö. Today the yard builds ships and makes trawls and fishing winches.
Öckerö har inte bara en sockenkyrka utan: Öckerö has not just one parish church but two, close to each other: Öckerö Old Church, also called Mariakyrkan, St Mary's, and Öckerö New Church, which these days is usually just called Öckerö Church. The parish covers the whole municipality, and the old parish includes places such as Hönö, Fotö, Hälsö, Björkö, Kalvsund, Källö-Knippla and Rörö.
Öckerö kommun är unik på sitt sätt: tio: Öckerö Municipality is unique in its way: ten inhabited islands and no fixed link to the mainland at all, so everything depends on the ferries. The only other example in Sweden is Gotland. Nature offers a species-rich flora and abundant birdlife, but the municipality also struggles with problems from marine litter. The main town is called, unsurprisingly, Öckerö.
Öckerö är en av de centrala öarna i Göte: Öckerö is one of the central islands in Gothenburg's northern archipelago and has given its name to the whole municipality. The island is barely four square kilometres in size but had 3,570 permanent residents in 2020, and it is home to the municipality's administrative centre. The houses have grown so close together that since 2018 it has been counted together with its neighbour Hönö, in the urban area Hönö-Öckerö.
Öjersjö ligger högt, cirka 110 till 120: Öjersjö lies high up, about 110 to 120 metres above sea level, so the winters here are sometimes a little snowier than in the lower parts of the municipality. The village lies by Stora Kåsjön, the largest lake in Partille Municipality, which is 32 metres deep and also the municipality's drinking-water source. All around, nature takes over, with the Knipeflågsbergen nature reserve bordering the Delsjö area.
Ölet började flöda här 1857, i lokaler s: The beer started flowing here in 1857, in premises that had previously been a cloth factory, and the brewery kept going all the way until 1971. After a big fire in 1893 it was quickly rebuilt in Renaissance style, and the façade facing Riddarfjärden bay is today a well-known part of the cityscape. Up on Skinnarviksberget hill, Villa Ludvigsberg sits enthroned with its lookout tower, and at the quay lies Kronprinsesse Märtha, a Norwegian ship built in 1929 in Danzig that is now a restaurant.
Ön Kungshatt har fått sitt namn efter sa: The island of Kungshatt, "King's Hat", is named after the legendary king Erik Väderhatt, Erik Weather-Hat, who lost his hat here while fleeing. According to the legend he could control the winds by turning his hat, so it was probably a costly loss. In the 1500s the island was probably called Serszöön, and on its eastern part today is the holiday home area Kungshättan.
Ön Trälen, även kallad Lilla Fjellsholme: The island of Trälen, also called Lilla Fjellsholmen, was bought by Volvo in the late 1940s. A holiday resort for employees was built there, with a cabin village, restaurant, kiosk and swimming spots, run by three trade unions within the group until 1990. In 2006 the island became the backdrop for TV4's reality show Trälen, and in 2014 all the old buildings were demolished.
Örbyskolan har två riktiga veteraner bla: Örbyskolan has two real veterans among its school buildings: Röda skolan, the Red School, from 1903 and Stenskolan, the Stone School, from 1915. Both are marked blue by the City Museum, which judges them to have exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Gamla Huddingevägen, which runs past, was incidentally the main road until traffic was rerouted north of the district in 1971.
Örgryte gamla kyrkogård har anor från 12: Örgryte Old Cemetery dates back to the 13th century, and many well-known Gothenburg figures are buried here, among them three bishops. The old church is one of the city's most popular churches for ceremonies, with around sixty weddings a year. By the main entrance stands the bronze statue Genomkämpat, 'The Struggle Is Over', whose original is in a cemetery in Berlin. And where the old ossuary once stood, the wholesale merchant Julius Lindström was granted a family grave in 1870, in return for paying for a new ossuary.
Örnsberg har fått sitt namn från en fast: Örnsberg takes its name from a property bought by Nils Öhrn in the 1740s, so the eagle, 'örn', in the name is really a gentleman called Öhrn. The area also includes the Hägersten industrial area, where about a hundred companies were based in 2007. A little further away, at Fågeltorget, was the neighbourhood cinema Tärnan, which opened in 1952 and closed in 1970.
Östermalms IP invigdes den 30 september: Östermalms IP, the sports ground, was opened on 30 September 1906 by King Oscar II. Next to it stands Tennispaviljongen, a listed tennis hall from 1896 that was moved about a hundred metres to its current spot in 1911. Djurgården's football team has long dreamed of a new arena here, but the Royal Djurgården Administration, which manages the land, has said no to the proposals.
Östra Balltorp ligger alldeles intill oc: Östra Balltorp is right next to us and has had a slightly confused identity: some years it counts as a separate built-up area, others as part of Gothenburg. Its neighbour Balltorp was built up in the 1980s but has been inhabited for 10,000 years. A little further away is the Pepparred nature reserve, protected since 1925.
Östra Rudboda radhusområde byggdes i mit: The Östra Rudboda terraced-house area was built in the mid-1970s, with just over 450 terraced and linked houses grouped around shared courtyards known as "tun", and today it counts as part of the municipality's culturally and historically valuable buildings. The neighbouring district of Yttringe got its name from the large meadows that have been there for a very long time. A little further away is Gråviken, an important site for seabirds with natural values of national interest.
Östra Yttringe gård är känd sedan medelt: Östra Yttringe gård has been known since the Middle Ages, then under the name Östra yttre ängen, the Eastern Outer Meadow. With its austere form, the main building from 1801 is a typical example of the smaller manor houses of its time, and the farm lies in an old cultural landscape within the Långängen-Elfvik nature reserve. Further away is Långnäs gård, which has its origins in a larger farm from the mid-14th century.
Östra gymnasiet: Östra gymnasiet, the Östra upper secondary school
Östra gymnasiet alldeles intill invigdes: Östra gymnasiet, the upper secondary school right next to us, opened in 2005 and was named one of the buildings of the year by the magazine Byggindustrin that same year. A little further away is a more unexpected neighbour, the Beateberg prison. It became known from the TV series FC Z, in which the inmates' football team played a match against FC Z itself.
Över Svindersviken spänner Svindersviksb: Spanning Svindersviken bay is Svindersviksbron, an arch bridge completed in 2016 that links central Nacka with Kvarnholmen. On Mjölnarvägen stands Silo III, a grain silo from 1912 that was converted into flats. It was a complicated project, and for a while only the outer walls were left standing. Its neighbour, the Old Mill Office from the same period, was the head office of Kvarnen Tre Kronor, the Three Crowns mill.
Över bron når vi Djurgården, som i flera: Across the bridge we reach Djurgården, which for several hundred years was the king's hunting park. Today the island is part of the Royal National City Park, with museums, an amusement park and large green spaces.
Över sundet, centralt på Öckerö, ligger: Across the strait, in central Öckerö, is Öckerö old church, also called Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church. Hönö and Öckerö have grown ever closer in recent years: in 2018 the two towns merged into a single urban area called Hönö-Öckerö. Even so, Hönö is the island with the most inhabitants in the municipality.
Över Årstafältet gick Göta landsväg, den: Göta landsväg, the medieval road from Stockholm towards Götaland, ran across Årstafältet. It is mentioned in the city's land register in 1494, and a preserved stretch is classed as an ancient monument. Årsta also has Snigelparken, the Snail Park, named after a sandpit shaped like a concrete snail. The statue Melodi, Melody, by Nils Sjögren also stands there.
